chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 1 基本动词 BREAK

words.tr: phrase. 祝你好运！（常用于表演前鼓励演员）
words.ex: Break a leg before your performance!
words.ex_cn: 演出前祝你好运！
words.en: A phrase used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance.

words.tr: phrase. 停止运转；出故障；分解；感情失控
words.ex: The machine broke down yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器昨天坏了。
words.en: If a machine or vehicle breaks down, it stops working. If a discussion, relationship, or system breaks down, it fails because of a problem or disagreement.

words.tr: phrase. 打成平手；得失相当
words.ex: After selling 100 tickets, the theater broke even.
words.ex_cn: 卖了100张票后，剧院打成了平手。
words.en: To reach a point in a business where the costs and the revenue are equal, so that there is neither profit nor loss.

words.tr: 短语动词. 为某事破土动工；开始进行（某项目或计划）
words.ex: They will break ground for a new school next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将为新学校破土动工。
words.en: To begin construction on a new building or project.

words.tr: phrase. 开始动工；破土动工；开创先例
words.ex: They will break ground next Monday for the new school.
words.ex_cn: 他们将在下周一为新学校破土动工。
words.en: To start digging the ground for a new building or to start a new project or activity that has not been done before.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 打扰；突然闯入；中断
words.ex: He broke in on the meeting without knocking.
words.ex_cn: 他没敲门就闯进了会议。
words.en: To interrupt or disturb someone or something, especially when they are engaged in a private activity or conversation.

words.tr: phrase. 闯入；打断；（使）逐渐适用
words.ex: Thieves broke in through the back door.
words.ex_cn: 小偷从后门闯入。
words.en: To enter a building by force, especially in order to steal something; to interrupt a conversation or activity.

words.tr: phrase. 闯入；打断；突然…
words.ex: The thief tried to break into the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 小偷试图在夜里闯入房子。
words.en: To enter a building or car using force, in order to steal something; to suddenly start doing something.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 强行进入；打断；使某人适应（新工作、新鞋等）
words.ex: He broke in the new shoes by wearing them around the house.
words.ex_cn: 他通过在家里穿新鞋来磨合。
words.en: To train or accustom someone or something to a new situation or routine.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 摆脱……的束缚；从……中挣脱出来
words.ex: He wants to break loose from his routine.
words.ex_cn: 他想摆脱他的日常惯例。
words.en: To escape or get free from a restraint or control.

words.tr: phrase. 脱离；挣脱；突然发生
words.ex: The dog broke loose from its chain and ran away.
words.ex_cn: 狗挣脱了链子跑掉了。
words.en: To escape from confinement or control; to start suddenly and forcefully.

words.tr: phrase. 开创先河；取得突破性进展；开辟新领域
words.ex: The scientist's research breaks new ground in medicine.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家的研究在医学上开辟了新领域。
words.en: To do something innovative that has not been done before.

words.tr: phrase. 中断；突然停止；断绝（关系）；休息一会
words.ex: He broke off the conversation when the phone rang.
words.ex_cn: 电话响时，他中断了对话。
words.en: To suddenly stop doing something, especially speaking.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 中止某事；突然停止做某事；中断
words.ex: He broke off the conversation when the phone rang.
words.ex_cn: 电话响时，他中断了对话。
words.en: To end a relationship or association abruptly.

words.tr: phrase. 拼命做某事；竭尽全力（常用于口语，带有夸张意味）
words.ex: He broke his neck trying to finish the work on time.
words.ex_cn: 他为了按时完成工作累得筋疲力尽。
words.en: To try extremely hard to do something.

words.tr: phrase. 拼命工作；累断腰；竭尽全力
words.ex: He is breaking his back to support his family.
words.ex_cn: 他拼命工作来养家糊口。
words.en: To work extremely hard or to make a great effort to achieve something.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人心碎；令某人极度悲伤
words.ex: His lies broke her heart.
words.ex_cn: 他的谎言让她心碎。
words.en: To cause someone to feel extreme sadness or grief.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 将……分开；结束（关系）；使（集会）解散
words.ex: They will break the fight up.
words.ex_cn: 他们会把这场打斗分开。
words.en: To separate something into pieces or to disperse a group.

words.tr: phrase. 打碎；分裂；解体；结束；期终放假
words.ex: He broke up the ice with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子把冰打碎了。
words.en: To end a relationship or to disintegrate into pieces.

words.tr: phrase. 打破僵局；缓解紧张气氛；使初次见面的人放松
words.ex: He told a joke to break the ice at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上讲了个笑话来打破僵局。
words.en: To do or say something to relieve tension or get conversation going in a strained situation or when strangers meet.

words.tr: 短语动词. 向某人透露（坏消息或令人震惊的消息）
words.ex: He will break the news to his parents tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会把这个消息告诉他的父母。
words.en: To inform someone about some important news, especially bad news.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词BREAK补充词组

words.tr: phrase. 脱离；摆脱
words.ex: He tried to break away from his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他试图摆脱旧习惯。
words.en: To leave or escape from a group, place, or situation, especially in order to start something new or different.

words.tr: phrase. 突然离开； 突然挣脱；决裂； 退出
words.ex: He broke away from the group and ran home.
words.ex_cn: 他突然离开团队，跑回家了。
words.en: To leave or escape from a person, group, or situation that controls or restricts you.

words.tr: phrase. 拆除营地；收拾营地；结束露营
words.ex: They break camp early in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他们一大早就收拾营地出发。
words.en: To pack up and leave a campsite; to dismantle a camp.

words.tr: phrase. 突发；爆发；越狱
words.ex: The fire broke out in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 火在厨房里突然烧了起来。
words.en: If something such as war, fighting, or disease breaks out, it begins suddenly.

words.tr: 短语动词。突然出现某种皮肤反应，如皮疹、汗等；常用于描述因紧张、疾病或过敏等原因身体突然出现某种状况
words.ex_cn: 他吃完坚果后身上起了皮疹。
words.en: If you break out in a rash or a sweat, a rash or sweat suddenly appears on your skin.

words.tr: 短语动词. 突然哭起来； burst into tears 的同义表达
words.ex: The little boy broke out into tears when he lost his toy.
words.ex_cn: 当小男孩丢了玩具时，他突然哭了起来。
words.en: To suddenly start crying, often because of strong emotions.

words.tr: 短语动词. 突然哭起来；忍不住流泪
words.ex: The little boy broke into tears when he lost his toy.
words.ex_cn: 当小男孩弄丢了玩具时，他突然哭了起来。
words.en: To suddenly start crying.

words.tr: 短语动词。突然哭起来；忍不住流泪
words.ex: The little girl broke out in tears when she lost her toy.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩一丢了玩具就突然哭了起来。
words.en: To start crying suddenly and uncontrollably.

words.tr: phrase. v. 逃脱；摆脱；突然发生
words.ex: The prisoner tried to break out of jail.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯试图越狱。
words.en: To escape from a place or a situation, especially one that limits or restrains you.

words.tr: phrase. 减缓某人跌落的冲击；防止某人重重摔下
words.ex: The mat helps break one's fall during gymnastics.
words.ex_cn: 垫子有助于在体操运动中减缓摔倒的冲击。
words.en: To reduce the impact of someone's fall, often by providing a cushioning or support.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 中止某事；中断某事；折断某物
words.ex: He broke off the conversation suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 他突然中断了对话。
words.en: To end something suddenly or to separate a part from something by breaking it.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 中止某事；突然停止做某事；中断
words.ex: He broke off the conversation when the phone rang.
words.ex_cn: 电话响时，他中断了对话。
words.en: To end a relationship or association abruptly.

words.tr: phrase. v. 把某物打成碎片；彻底摧毁某物
words.ex: He broke the glass to pieces with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子把玻璃砸成了碎片。
words.en: To smash or destroy something completely.

words.tr: 短语动词. 完成某项困难任务中最艰难的部分；攻克主要难题
words.ex: We broke the back of the work yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨天完成了大部分工作。
words.en: To complete the most difficult part of a task.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 突破某物；取得重大进展或成功
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家突破了沉默的壁垒。
words.en: To make a way through a barrier or a difficult situation, often after a period of effort.

words.tr: phrase. 突围；突破
words.ex: He broke through the wall with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用手打破了墙壁。
words.en: To break through means to make a way through a barrier or to achieve success in spite of difficulties.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 2 基本动词 BRING

words.tr: 短语动词. 赚钱养家；成功地获得经济收入以维持家庭生计
words.ex: He works two jobs to bring home the bacon.
words.ex_cn: 他做两份工作来养家糊口。
words.en: To earn the income needed to support one's family; to successfully complete a task or achieve a goal.

words.tr: phrase. v. 使某人恢复知觉；说服某人改变主意；使某人逐渐接受某种观点
words.ex: He fainted, but the smell of vinegar brought him around.
words.ex_cn: 他晕倒了，但醋的气味让他恢复了知觉。
words.en: To persuade someone to agree with you or to do what you want; to cause someone to regain consciousness.

words.tr: phrase. 带回；回忆；使恢复
words.ex: The song brings back happy memories.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了快乐的回忆。
words.en: To bring something back means to return it to the place where it was before, or to make it exist or happen again.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 使显现；激发；出版；生产
words.ex: Music brings out her talent.
words.ex_cn: 音乐使她的才华显现出来。
words.en: To make something visible or available; to publish or reveal.

words.tr: phrase. 使表现出；说出；呈出；出版
words.ex: The new lighting really brings out the colors in the painting.
words.ex_cn: 新灯光让画中的颜色更加突出。
words.en: To cause something to be seen or known; to publish something.

words.tr: phrase. 提出；教育；养育；呕出
words.ex: He brought up an important point in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上提出了一个重要的观点。
words.en: To mention a subject or start to talk about it; to care for a child until they are an adult, often giving them particular beliefs; to educate someone; to vomit.

words.tr: phrase. v. 使某人承担责任；追究某人的责任
words.ex: The boss will bring him to account for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 老板会让他为这个错误负责。
words.en: To make someone explain or justify their actions, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.tr: phrase. v. 要求某人对某事负责；追究某人的责任
words.ex: The manager called him to account for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 经理要求他为这个错误负责。
words.en: To demand that someone explains or takes responsibility for their actions or decisions.

words.w: bring sb. up to date on ...
words.tr: phrase. 向某人通报最新情况；使某人了解最新的进展
words.uk: brɪŋ sʌmˈbɒdi ʌp tə dɪt ɒn
words.us: brɪŋ sʌmˈbɑːdi ʌp tə dɪt ɑːn
words.ex_cn: 我会让你了解这个项目的最新情况。
words.en: To inform someone of the latest information about a topic.

words.tr: phrase. v. 使某人了解最新情况；向某人通报最新进展
words.ex: I will bring you up to date on the project.
words.ex_cn: 我会让你了解这个项目的最新情况。
words.en: To inform someone about the latest information or developments.

words.tr: phrase. 带来；引起
words.ex: Hard work can bring about success.
words.ex_cn: 努力工作可以带来成功。
words.en: To cause something to happen.

words.tr: phrase. v. 导致；引起；促成（某事的发生）
words.ex: Hard work can bring about success.
words.ex_cn: 努力工作可以带来成功。
words.en: To cause something to happen.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事提出质疑；使某事受到怀疑
words.ex: His mistake brings the plan into question.
words.ex_cn: 他的错误让这个计划受到了质疑。
words.en: To cause something to be doubted or reconsidered.

words.tr: 使某事停止；使某事突然中止
words.ex: The accident brought traffic to a halt.
words.ex_cn: 事故使交通完全停顿。
words.en: To cause something to stop.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词BRING补充词组

words.tr: phrase. 把某人带到（某地）；使某人恢复知觉或达到某种状态
words.ex: The teacher brought the students to the museum.
words.ex_cn: 老师带学生们去了博物馆。
words.en: To cause someone to faint or become unconscious.

words.w: bring sth. crashing down around sb.
words.tr: phrase. v. 使某物突然崩溃或倒塌在某人周围，通常比喻彻底破坏某人的计划、安全感或处境
words.uk: brɪŋ sʌmθɪŋ ˈkræʃɪŋ daʊn əˈraʊnd sʌmbədi
words.ex: His lies brought his career crashing down around him.
words.ex_cn: 他的谎言让他的事业瞬间崩塌。
words.en: To cause something to collapse or fail dramatically in someone's vicinity, often leading to significant consequences for them.

words.tr: phrase. v. 使某物轰然倒塌；彻底摧毁某事物
words.ex: The storm brought the old tree crashing down.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把那棵老树砸倒了。
words.en: To cause something to collapse or fail suddenly and dramatically.

words.tr: phrase. v. 成功完成（困难的事情）；把某事办成
words.ex: He brought the plan off with hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过努力把计划实现了。
words.en: To successfully achieve something difficult.

words.tr: phrase. v. 成功完成（困难的事情）
words.ex: He brought off the magic show with great skill.
words.ex_cn: 他以高超的技巧完成了这场魔术表演。
words.en: To succeed in doing something difficult.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 3 基本动词 CALL

words.tr: 短语动词. 宣布停止某事；叫停某事
words.ex: The government decided to call a halt to the new project.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定停止这个新项目。
words.en: To decide that something should stop.

words.tr: 短语动词. 宣布停止；叫停
words.ex: The teacher called a halt to the game because it was getting too noisy.
words.ex_cn: 老师叫停了游戏，因为太吵了。
words.en: To decide that something should stop.

words.tr: phrase. 召集会议
words.ex: The manager will call a meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将召开一次会议。
words.en: To arrange for a meeting to take place, especially in a formal or official context.

words.tr: phrase. 直言不讳；是什么说什么
words.ex: He always calls a spade a spade, even if it makes people uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他总是实话实说，即使这会让别人不舒服。
words.en: To speak plainly and directly, without euphemism or evasion.

words.tr: 短语动词. 到此为止，收工，停止工作
words.ex: After working all afternoon, they decided to call it a day.
words.ex_cn: 工作了整个下午后，他们决定收工了。
words.en: If you call it a day, you decide to stop what you are doing because you are tired of it or because it is not successful.

words.tr: 短语动词. 决定停止做某事，通常指放弃或结束一项活动、工作或争论；认输；收工
words.ex: After several failed attempts, he decided to call it quits.
words.ex_cn: 在几次尝试失败后，他决定放弃。
words.en: To decide to stop doing something, especially to end a relationship or to stop working.

words.tr: phrase. 回电话；回访；召回
words.ex: He will call back after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后会回电话。
words.en: To telephone someone again, especially in order to give them some information or because they were not available when you telephoned before.

words.tr: n. 回叫信号；
words.ex: He received a callback after the interview.
words.ex_cn: 面试后他收到了回叫信号。
words.en: A callback is a telephone call that you make to someone who has called you, or a function that is passed as an argument to another function and is executed after some event has occurred.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人辱骂、骂脏话、出言侮辱
words.ex: He was calling her names in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前辱骂她。
words.en: To use offensive or insulting words to describe someone.

words.tr: phrase. adj. 严厉训斥某人；责备某人
words.ex: The manager called him on the carpet for his poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 经理因他表现不佳而严厉批评了他。
words.en: To reprimand or scold someone, especially in a formal setting.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对……表示怀疑；质疑……的可靠性或真实性
words.ex: The new evidence calls the witness's story into question.
words.ex_cn: 新的证据使证人的说法受到质疑。
words.en: To express doubt about the truth or validity of something.

words.tr: phrase. 取消；转移；叫走；依次叫名
words.ex: They decided to call off the meeting because of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为风暴决定取消会议。
words.en: To cancel or abandon something that was planned.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 给某人打电话
words.ex: I need to call her up to discuss the details.
words.ex_cn: 我需要给她打电话讨论细节。
words.en: To telephone someone.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 给某个地方打电话
words.ex: You can call a place up to make a reservation.
words.ex_cn: 你可以打电话给某地预订。
words.en: To telephone a place.

words.tr: 短语动词. 提醒某人注意某事；使某人关注某事
words.ex: He called my attention to the broken window.
words.ex_cn: 他让我注意到了那扇破了的窗户。
words.en: To draw or direct someone's notice or awareness to something.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 提醒某人注意某事；使某人关注某物
words.ex: The teacher called the student's tardiness to her attention.
words.ex_cn: 老师指出了学生迟到的问题。
words.en: To direct someone's focus or awareness to something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 揭穿某人的虚张声势；考验某人是否言出必行
words.ex: He said he would quit the job, but she called his bluff and said, 'Okay, leave.'
words.ex_cn: 他说他要辞职，但她揭穿了他的虚张声势，说：‘好啊，那就走吧。’
words.en: To challenge someone to carry out a threat or prove a claim, in order to test if they are being truthful or just bluffing.

words.tr: phrase. 让狗停止攻击；比喻停止对某人或某事的攻击或指责
words.ex: The farmer had to call the dogs off when the sheep ran away.
words.ex_cn: 当羊跑掉时，农夫不得不把狗叫回来。
words.en: To stop a pursuit or aggressive action; to call off a hunt.

words.tr: 短语动词. 负责；掌权；决定事情的人
words.ex: He calls the shots in his company.
words.ex_cn: 他在他的公司里说了算。
words.en: To be in charge; to make the important decisions.

words.tr: 短语动词. 决定事情的进行方式；掌握控制权；说了算
words.ex: He is the one who calls the tune in the band.
words.ex_cn: 他是乐队里决定方向的人。
words.en: If you say that someone calls the tune, you mean that they are in a position of power or control and can make decisions about what happens.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词CALL补充词组

words.tr: phrase. 呼吁；号召；要求；接（人）
words.ex: The situation calls for immediate action.
words.ex_cn: 这种情况需要立即采取行动。
words.en: If you call for something, you demand that it should happen.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 拜访某人；号召某人；请求某人做某事
words.ex: During his campaign, the candidate called on many voters to support him.
words.ex_cn: 在竞选期间，候选人拜访了许多选民以争取他们的支持。
words.en: To visit someone; to ask someone to do something.

words.tr: phrase. v. 要求某人做某事；拜访某人；号召某人
words.ex: The president called upon the nation to unite in the face of adversity.
words.ex_cn: 总统号召全国人民在逆境面前团结起来。
words.en: To formally ask someone to do something.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 责备某人；训斥某人
words.ex: The teacher called the student down for not paying attention in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生上课不专心而训斥了他。
words.en: To reprimand or scold someone.

words.tr: phrase. 叫（某人）进来；召来；来访
words.ex: He called in a doctor for his sick son.
words.ex_cn: 他为生病的儿子请了一位医生。
words.en: To request someone's presence or participation, especially by telephone.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 公开指责或挑战某人；叫某人出来面对问题或解释行为
words.ex: She called him out for his inappropriate behavior at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 她公开批评他在会议上的不当行为。
words.en: To publicly criticize or accuse someone of something.

words.tr: phrase v. 要求恢复秩序；宣布会议开始并要求大家遵守规则
words.ex: The chairman called the meeting to order.
words.ex_cn: 主席宣布会议开始。
words.en: To request or demand that a group of people become quiet and orderly, especially in a formal meeting or assembly.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 4 基本动词 COME

words.tr: phrase. 发生；造成
words.ex: How did this mistake come about?
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是怎么发生的？
words.en: If you ask how something came about, you want to know how it happened or started.

words.tr: phrase. 偶遇；偶然发现；使产生…印象
words.ex: I came across an old photo while cleaning my room.
words.ex_cn: 我在打扫房间时发现了一张旧照片。
words.en: If you come across something or someone, you find them or meet them by chance.

words.tr: phrase. 偶然碰见；撞见
words.ex: I run across my old friend at the market.
words.ex_cn: 我在市场遇到了我的老朋友。
words.en: To meet or find someone or something by chance.

words.tr: 短语动词. 彻底崩溃；分崩离析；从接缝处裂开（比喻事物或局面完全失控或瓦解）
words.ex: The old bag came apart at the seams after years of use.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧包用了几年后裂开了。
words.en: To fall apart or fail suddenly and completely, often because of internal problems.

words.tr: phrase. 空手而归；一无所获
words.ex: He went to the store but came away empty-handed.
words.ex_cn: 他去了商店，但空手而归。
words.en: To leave a place without achieving what one wanted or without taking anything with one.

words.w: come between sb. and sb. else
words.tr: phrase. 介入某人与另一人之间，通常指破坏或影响两人之间的关系
words.uk: kʌm bɪˈtwiːn sʌmˈbɒdi ənd sʌmˈbɒdi ɛls
words.us: kʌm bɪˈtwin ˈsʌmˌbɑdi ənd ˈsʌmˌbɑdi ɛls
words.ex: She tried to come between him and his wife, but failed.
words.ex_cn: 她试图介入他和他的妻子之间，但失败了。
words.en: To interfere in the relationship between two people, causing problems or difficulties.

words.tr: phrase. v. 严厉对待；严惩；对……采取强硬措施
words.ex: The teacher will come down hard on students who cheat.
words.ex_cn: 老师会对作弊的学生严厉惩罚。
words.en: To criticize or punish someone severely.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 严厉对待……；对……采取强硬措施
words.ex: The teacher will come down on you hard if you cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 如果你考试作弊，老师会严厉地惩罚你。
words.en: To criticize or punish someone severely.

words.tr: phrase. v. 地位或经济状况下降；变得不如从前富裕或有地位
words.ex: He used to be rich, but now he has come down in the world.
words.ex_cn: 他曾经很富有，但现在他已经今不如昔了。
words.en: To decline in social status or financial situation.

words.tr: phrase. v. 回到现实中；从幻想中清醒过来；脚踏实地
words.ex: After the holiday, we have to come down to earth and go back to work.
words.ex_cn: 假期结束后，我们得回到现实，回去工作。
words.en: To stop imagining or dreaming and start dealing with practical matters.

words.tr: phrase. v. 归结为某事；最终取决于某事
words.ex: The whole debate comes down to money.
words.ex_cn: 整个争论归根结底就是钱的问题。
words.en: If a problem or decision comes down to a particular thing, that is the most important thing involved.

words.tr: phrase. v. 患上（疾病）；感染（某病）
words.ex: He came down with the flu last week.
words.ex_cn: v. 他上周染上了流感。
words.en: To become ill with a particular disease.

words.tr: 短语动词. 从四面八方来；从遥远的地方聚集而来
words.ex: People come from far and wide to see the festival.
words.ex_cn: 人们从四面八方赶来参加这个节日。
words.en: To originate from many different places, especially in a large group.

words.tr: phrase. 无论如何；不管发生什么（都要坚持做某事）
words.ex: I'll finish this project come hell or high water.
words.ex_cn: 无论如何，我都会完成这个项目。
words.en: No matter what difficulties or obstacles arise, one is determined to do something.

words.tr: phrase. （不良行为或错误决定的后果）反噬自身，自食其果
words.ex: His bad habits have come home to roost.
words.ex_cn: 他的坏习惯终于带来恶果了。
words.en: If a problem or situation comes home to roost, it starts to cause problems for the person who is responsible for it, often after a period of time.

words.tr: phrase. 回家
words.ex: He comes home after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后回家。
words.en: To return to one's home.

words.tr: 短语动词。集体到来；成群结队地出现
words.ex: The students came in a body to protest the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 学生们集体前来抗议新规定。
words.en: To arrive or appear together as a group.

words.tr: 短语动词. 成群结队地到达；集体到达
words.ex: They arrive in a body to support their team.
words.ex_cn: 他们集体到达来支持他们的队伍。
words.en: To arrive somewhere as a group, especially in a way that shows unity or solidarity.

words.tr: phrase. v. 派上用场；变得有用
words.ex: This tool will come in handy when you fix the bike.
words.ex_cn: 当你修自行车时，这个工具会派上用场。
words.en: If an object or skill comes in handy, it is useful in a particular situation.

words.w: come in out of the rain
words.tr: 短语动词. 从雨中进来；比喻脱离困境或危险；引申义为回到安全或舒适的地方
words.uk: kʌm ɪn aʊt əv ðə reɪn
words.us: kʌm ɪn aʊt əv ðə reɪn
words.ex: You should come in out of the rain before you catch a cold.
words.ex_cn: 你应该进屋避雨，以免感冒。
words.en: To enter a place to avoid bad weather, especially rain.

words.tr: phrase. 充分发挥才能；开始受到重视；真正显现出自己的价值
words.ex: He comes into his own when he plays basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他打篮球时才真正展现自己的能力。
words.en: To begin to show one's true ability or to start to be successful in a way that makes people recognize one's true value.

words.tr: phrase. 达到法定年龄；到了成年
words.ex: He came of age last year and now he can vote.
words.ex_cn: 他去年成年了，现在可以投票了。
words.en: To reach the age at which one is legally recognized as an adult.

words.tr: phrase. 别胡扯了；别装了；醒醒吧（用于表示不相信或不耐烦）
words.ex: Come off it, you know that's not true.
words.ex_cn: 别骗人了，你知道那不是真的。
words.en: Used to tell someone to stop pretending or to stop saying something that is not true.

words.tr: phrase. 处于下风；落于次要地位；在比较中失败
words.ex: He came off second best in the competition.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中落于下风。
words.en: To be the loser in a competition or argument; to be less successful than someone else.

words.tr: phrase. 加油；快点；拜托；来吧；开始
words.ex: Come on, you can finish this race!
words.ex_cn: 加油，你能跑完这场比赛的！
words.en: Used to encourage someone to do something or to hurry up, or to express disbelief or skepticism.

words.tr: 短语动词. 最终获得成功或优势；在竞争或困难中取得有利结果
words.ex: After all the expenses, we managed to come out ahead.
words.ex_cn: phr. 在支付了所有费用后，我们最终处于有利位置。
words.en: To end up in a better position or condition than one was in before, especially after some kind of competition, conflict, or financial transaction.

words.tr: 短语动词. 最终会解决的；到最后会显现出来的（指问题或真相终会水落石出）
words.ex: Don't worry about the small mistakes in the project; they'll come out in the wash.
words.ex_cn: 别担心项目中的小错误；它们最终会得到解决的。
words.en: If you say that something will come out in the wash, you mean that it will become known or be resolved in the future, often implying that it is not necessary to worry about it now.

words.tr: phrase. v. （人）变得开朗起来，不再害羞或拘谨
words.ex: He is coming out of his shell at school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校里正变得开朗起来。
words.en: To become less shy and more confident and willing to engage with others.

words.tr: 短语动词. 公开自己的性取向（尤指同性恋身份）；出柜
words.ex: She decided to come out of the closet and share her true identity with the world.
words.ex_cn: 她决定公开自己的真实身份，向世界展示她的真实自我。
words.en: To publicly acknowledge one's homosexuality, which was previously kept secret.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 推出或发布某物；说出某事；突然提出某事
words.ex: He came out with a surprising statement at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上提出了一个令人惊讶的声明。
words.en: To introduce or make something known to the public, especially something new or innovative.

words.tr: 短语动词. 走到死胡同；陷入绝境；没有进展
words.ex: Our project has come to a dead end due to lack of funding.
words.ex_cn: 由于缺乏资金，我们的项目已走投无路。
words.en: To reach a point where no further progress is possible; to be unable to proceed further.

words.tr: 短语动词。指问题或紧张局势发展到必须立即解决的关键阶段；爆发，达到顶点
words.ex: The problem came to a head when the teacher found out.
words.ex_cn: 当老师发现时，问题爆发了。
words.en: If a situation or problem comes to a head, it reaches a point where action must be taken to resolve it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 完全停止；陷入停顿
words.ex: The traffic came to a standstill during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨期间，交通陷入了停滞。
words.en: If something such as a process or activity comes to a standstill, it stops completely.

words.tr: 短语动词. 因某事而发生肢体冲突；因某事争吵到动手打架
words.ex: The two men came to blows over the parking space.
words.ex_cn: 那两个人因为停车位而打了起来。
words.en: If two people come to blows, they start hitting each other, usually because they have been arguing.

words.tr: phrase. 打起来；发生肢体冲突
words.ex: The two boys came to blows over a toy.
words.ex_cn: 两个男孩因为一个玩具打了起来。
words.en: If two or more people come to blows, they start fighting.

words.tr: phrase. 开始认真对待并努力解决某事；着手处理某事
words.ex: It took her a while to come to grips with the new reality.
words.ex_cn: 她花了一些时间才适应了新的现实。
words.en: To begin to deal with or understand a difficult problem or situation.

words.tr: phrase. 苏醒过来；变得活跃；显得逼真
words.ex: The painting seems to come to life in the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画在月光下似乎活了过来。
words.en: To become active or lively; to start to function or operate.

words.tr: phrase. 真相大白；为人所知
words.ex: The truth came to light after the investigation.
words.ex_cn: 调查之后，真相大白了。
words.en: If something comes to light, it becomes known or is discovered, often after being hidden or secret.

words.tr: phrase. 想起
words.ex: A good idea comes to mind when I walk in the park.
words.ex_cn: 当我散步时，一个好主意浮现在脑海中。
words.en: If something comes to mind, you suddenly remember it or think of it.

words.tr: phrase. 完全失败；终成泡影； 化为乌有
words.ex: Their plans for a trip came to nothing because of the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他们的旅行计划因为下雨而落空了。
words.en: If something comes to nothing, it fails or does not achieve anything.

words.tr: phrase. 归于无效；落空；白费
words.ex: His efforts came to naught because he gave up too soon.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力白费了，因为他放弃得太早了。
words.en: If something comes to naught, it fails completely or has no effect.

words.tr: phrase. 恢复理智；清醒过来；醒悟
words.ex: After the argument, he came to his senses and said sorry.
words.ex_cn: 争吵之后，他醒悟过来并道了歉。
words.en: To start to think clearly and behave sensibly again after a period of confusion or irrationality.

words.tr: phrase. v. 接受（现实、情况等）；与……达成协议；妥协
words.ex: He finally came to terms with his failure.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了失败。
words.en: To accept something that one cannot change, especially a difficult or unpleasant situation.

words.tr: phrase. 达成协议；和解；接受（现实、条件等）
words.ex: He could not come to terms with the loss of his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他无法接受朋友的去世。
words.en: If you come to terms with something difficult or unpleasant, you learn to accept and deal with it.

words.tr: phrase. 涌现； 惹人注意
words.ex: During the crisis, brave leaders come to the fore.
words.ex_cn: 在危机中，勇敢的领导者会脱颖而出。
words.en: If someone or something comes to the fore, they become important or noticeable.

words.tr: 短语动词. 进入正题；谈主要问题；切中要点
words.ex: He finally came to the point and told us the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他终于直截了当地告诉我们真相。
words.en: To directly address the main issue or topic without unnecessary details.

words.tr: 短语动词. 进入正题；说重点；直截了当地说出主要问题
words.ex: Please get to the point; we don't have much time.
words.ex_cn: 请直奔主题，我们没有太多时间。
words.en: To speak or write directly and clearly about the most important part of a subject, without including unnecessary details.

words.tr: phrase. 想起来；仔细想想
words.ex: Come to think of it, we haven't had lunch yet.
words.ex_cn: 仔细想想，我们还没有吃午饭呢。
words.en: used when you suddenly remember or realize something

words.tr: phrase. 发生；上来；提到
words.ex: A problem came up during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议期间发生了一个问题。
words.en: To arise or occur, especially unexpectedly or as a subject of discussion.

words.tr: 短语动词。从后面接近或赶上；在比赛或竞争中后来居上
words.ex: He managed to come up from behind and win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他设法从后面赶上并赢得了比赛。
words.en: To approach or reach someone or something from a position that is behind.

words.tr: 短语动词。地位或经济状况上升；发迹，出人头地
words.ex: He used to be poor, but now he has come up in the world.
words.ex_cn: 他曾经很穷，但现在他发迹了。
words.en: To achieve success or a higher social status, especially after starting from a low position.

words.tr: phrase. 赶上；提出；想出
words.ex: He ran fast to come up with the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得很快，以便赶上公交车。
words.en: If you come up with a plan, idea, or solution, you think of it and suggest it.

words.tr: phrase. 无论如何；不管发生什么
words.ex: Come what may, we will always be friends.
words.ex_cn: 不管发生什么，我们永远是朋友。
words.en: Regardless of what happens; whatever may occur.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词COME补充词组

words.tr: phrase. v. 摔跤；失败；遭遇挫折
words.ex: He tried to ride the bike too fast and came a cropper.
words.ex_cn: 他试图骑自行车太快，结果摔了一跤。
words.en: To fail or suffer a defeat, especially in an unexpected or sudden way.

words.tr: phrase. 请再说一遍；再来
words.ex: I didn't catch that, could you come again?
words.ex_cn: 我没听清，你能再说一遍吗？
words.en: Used to ask someone to repeat something because you did not hear or understand it.

words.tr: phrase. 和某人一起来；跟随某人
words.ex: Why don't you come along with us to the party?
words.ex_cn: 你为什么不和我们一起去参加派对呢？
words.en: To accompany someone to a place or event.

words.tr: phrase. 出现；跟随；进步；（催促）赶快
words.ex: I didn't see him, but he came along later.
words.ex_cn: 我没看到他，但他后来出现了。
words.en: To appear or arrive, often unexpectedly; to make progress or improve.

words.tr: 短语. 来拿吧！常用于招呼别人来享用食物或抓住机会
words.ex: Dinner is ready, come and get it!
words.ex_cn: 晚餐准备好了，来拿吧！
words.en: A phrase used to announce that food is ready or to call someone to take something.

words.tr: phrase. v. （观点或态度）改变，回心转意；顺便来访，顺道拜访；苏醒，恢复知觉
words.ex: At first he refused, but later he came around and agreed to help.
words.ex_cn: 他一开始拒绝了，但后来回心转意，同意帮忙。
words.en: To change one's opinion or decision; to regain consciousness; to visit someone casually.

words.tr: phrasal verb. （观点或态度）转变，改变主意；（身体或情绪上）恢复；顺便来访，过来
words.ex: He didn't want to help at first, but he came round after we talked.
words.ex_cn: 他一开始不想帮忙，但经过交谈后改变了主意。
words.en: To regain consciousness; to change one's opinion or position; to visit someone casually.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 向…扑来；攻击；指责；接近（某事物）
words.ex: The dog came at me with barking.
words.ex_cn: 那只狗冲我扑过来，边叫边冲。
words.en: To move towards someone or something in a threatening way; to reach or achieve something.

words.tr: phrase. 回来；记起；复原；恢复；重新流行
words.ex: He promised to come back soon.
words.ex_cn: 他答应很快就会回来。
words.en: To return to a place or to a previous activity or condition.

words.tr: phrase. v. 获得某物；设法得到某物
words.ex: It's not easy to come by a job in this economy.
words.ex_cn: 在这种经济环境下，得到一份工作并不容易。
words.en: To obtain something, especially something that is rare or difficult to get.

words.tr: 短语动词. 正当地获得某物；通过正当手段得到某物
words.ex: He came by his wealth honestly, through years of hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他的财富是通过多年的辛勤工作正当获得的。
words.en: To obtain something through honest means or effort.

words.tr: phrase. 向某人坦白；向某人说出真相
words.ex: You need to come clean with your parents about what happened.
words.ex_cn: 你需要向你的父母坦白发生了什么。
words.en: To admit or confess something that one has been hiding or lying about, especially to someone they have a close relationship with.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 下来；下降；流传；病倒
words.ex: The price of apples came down last week.
words.ex_cn: 上周苹果的价格降了。
words.en: To move or travel from a higher to a lower level or position; to descend.

words.tr: phrase. 回家
words.ex: He comes home after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后回家。
words.en: To return to one's home.

words.tr: phrase. 进来
words.ex: He comes in every morning at 8 o'clock.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上8点进来。
words.en: To enter a place, especially a building or room.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 遭受（批评、指责等）；得到（关注、赞扬等）
words.ex: He came in for a lot of criticism after the project failed.
words.ex_cn: 项目失败后，他受到了很多批评。
words.en: To receive something, especially criticism or praise.

words.tr: phrase. 参加（某项活动）；集合以参加（某事）
words.ex: The soldiers quickly fell in for the drill.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们迅速集合准备训练。
words.en: To be assigned or chosen to do something, often a duty or task.

words.tr: phrase. 进入；得到；继承
words.ex: The sun comes into the room in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 太阳早上照进房间里。
words.en: To enter a place, state, or condition; to inherit something; to begin to be involved in something.

words.tr: phrase. 离开；举行；实现；成功；从…掉下
words.ex: He will come off the train at the next station.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下一站下车。
words.en: To happen or occur, especially in a particular way; to be successful or effective.

words.tr: phrase. 某事发生在某人身上；来到某人身边（常指机会、好运或困难等）
words.ex: Good opportunities will come your way if you wait and try.
words.ex_cn: 如果你等待并尝试，好机会就会来到你身边。
words.en: If something comes your way, it happens to you or you get it, often without expecting it.

words.tr: phrase. 出现；出来；出版
words.ex: The sun comes out after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨停后太阳出来了。
words.en: If something comes out, it becomes known, especially after it has been kept secret or it has been unknown.

words.tr: phrase. v. 公开支持；为……而出面；参加（某项活动）
words.ex: She decided to come out for the marathon this year.
words.ex_cn: 她决定今年参加马拉松比赛。
words.en: To publicly declare one's support for someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 突然出现，毫无预兆地到来
words.ex: The cat came out of nowhere and scared me.
words.ex_cn: 那只猫突然冒出来，吓了我一跳。
words.en: To appear or happen suddenly and unexpectedly.

words.tr: phrase. 过来；顺便来访；改变立场；突然感觉；显得
words.ex: Come over to my house after school.
words.ex_cn: 放学后到我家来。
words.en: To move or travel towards someone or something, especially in order to visit them.

words.tr: phrase. 到达；显现；实现；成功地完成；（健康）恢复；渡过
words.ex: The package will come through tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 包裹明天会到达。
words.en: To successfully deal with a difficult situation or to do what is needed or expected.

words.tr: phrase. 苏醒；到达；总计；突然想起
words.ex: He came to after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后他醒了过来。
words.en: If someone comes to, they regain consciousness after being unconscious. It can also mean to reach a particular state or condition, or to be involved in something.

words.tr: phrase. 落得悲惨下场；遭遇不幸的结局
words.ex: If you don't change your ways, you'll come to a bad end.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不改变你的方式，你将会以不好的结局结束。
words.en: To end in a bad or unfortunate way, often as a result of one's actions.

words.tr: phrase. 结束；终止
words.ex: The movie comes to an end at nine o'clock.
words.ex_cn: 电影在九点结束。
words.en: To reach a point where something stops or finishes.

words.tr: phrase. 不幸早逝；意外地过早结束
words.ex: The old building came to an untimely end in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 那座老建筑在风暴中过早地倒塌了。
words.en: To die or to stop existing before the expected or usual time.

words.tr: phrase. 遭难；吃亏；出事；失败
words.ex: He didn't study for the exam and came to grief.
words.ex_cn: 他没有为考试学习，结果失败了。
words.en: To experience failure, misfortune, or an accident.

words.tr: phrase. 实现；发生；成为事实
words.ex: Many things have come to pass since we last met.
words.ex_cn: 自从我们上次见面以来，发生了很多事情。
words.en: To happen or occur, especially in a way that seems inevitable or as the result of a series of events.

words.tr: 短语动词. 停止移动，静止下来；安顿下来
words.ex: The ball rolled down the hill and came to rest in the grass.
words.ex_cn: 球从山上滚下来，最后停在了草地上。
words.en: If something comes to rest, it stops moving.

words.tr: phrase. 实现；成真
words.ex: Her dream will come true next year.
words.ex_cn: 她的梦想明年将会实现。
words.en: If a dream, hope, or prediction comes true, it actually happens.

words.tr: phrase. v. 变得激动或失控；崩溃；发狂
words.ex: He came unglued when he saw the mess in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到厨房里的混乱时，他崩溃了。
words.en: If something comes unglued, it becomes disorganized or fails to work as planned.

words.tr: phrase. 突然产生；要求；成为...负担；偶遇
words.ex: A good idea came upon her while she was walking.
words.ex_cn: 她在散步时突然产生了一个好主意。
words.en: To meet or find someone or something by chance; to suddenly have a thought or feeling.

words.tr: phrase. 加油；快点；拜托；来吧；开始
words.ex: Come on, you can finish this race!
words.ex_cn: 加油，你能跑完这场比赛的！
words.en: Used to encourage someone to do something or to hurry up, or to express disbelief or skepticism.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 5 基本动词 DO

words.tr: phrase. v. （因惊讶或震惊）猛地回头再看一眼，表示突然意识到某事
words.ex: He did a double-take when he saw his friend at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到朋友在机场时，他愣了一下，再看了一眼。
words.en: If you do a double-take, you look at something or someone again because you find it hard to believe what you saw or heard the first time.

words.tr: v. 向后转; 大改变; 倒转; 彻底改变 n. 突然改变（看法，立场等）; 向后转（的动作）
words.ex: The soldier stopped and did an about-face.
words.ex_cn: 士兵停下并向后转。
words.en: An about-face is a complete change in attitude or direction.

words.tr: n. 夹趾拖鞋；吧嗒吧嗒声；突然转变
words.ex: He was wearing a pair of colorful flip-flops to the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着一双彩色的人字拖去海滩。
words.en: A flip-flop is a type of open-toed sandal typically worn as a form of casual wear. It consists of a flat sole held loosely on the foot by a Y-shaped strap that passes between the first and second toes and around both sides of the foot. In another sense, flip-flop refers to a sudden reversal of policy or opinion.

words.tr: phrase. 对……进行修理或处理；有时含贬义，指对某人或某物进行严厉的打击或破坏
words.ex: He did a job on the broken chair and fixed it.
words.ex_cn: 他修理了那把坏椅子，把它修好了。
words.en: To cause damage or harm to someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 生意兴隆，非常繁忙（源于19世纪美国土地办公室业务火爆的景象）
words.ex: The ice cream shop is doing a land office business on hot days.
words.ex_cn: 这家冰淇淋店在热天生意非常兴隆。
words.en: To do a very large amount of business, especially in a short period of time.

words.tr: phrase. 对……进行严厉批评或打击；对……施加不利影响
words.ex: The bad news really did a number on his mood.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息真的严重影响了他的情绪。
words.en: To cause damage or have a significant impact on someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 消除；终止；废除；杀死；干掉
words.ex: They want to do away with the old rules.
words.ex_cn: 他们想废除旧规则。
words.en: To do away with something means to get rid of it or to stop using it.

words.tr: phrase. 对待某人
words.ex: The work was done by him.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作是他做的。
words.en: To treat someone in a particular way.

words.tr: 短语动词. 为某人增光；使某人显得体面；证明某人有良好教养或能力
words.ex: Her performance did credit to her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现证明了她的努力没有白费。
words.en: To bring honor or respect to someone; to make someone worthy of praise.

words.tr: 短语动词，对某人有好评；使某人感到光荣；证明某人品德良好
words.ex: Her success does her family credit.
words.ex_cn: 她的成功为她的家庭增光。
words.en: To make someone feel proud or to bring honor to someone.

words.tr: phrase. 充分体现…的价值；公正地对待；如实评价
words.ex: This painting does justice to the beauty of nature.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画充分展现了自然的美。
words.en: To treat or represent someone or something in a way that is fair and shows their true qualities.

words.tr: phrase. 公正地对待；充分展现……的价值或优点
words.ex: This movie does justice to the book.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影忠实地还原了这本书。
words.en: To treat someone or something in a fair or appropriate way; to be adequate or sufficient for something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 按自己的方式行事；做自己想做的事
words.ex: He likes to do his own thing and never follows others.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢做自己的事，从不跟随别人。
words.en: To act independently and according to one's own preferences or interests.

words.tr: 短语动词. 做自己擅长的事；按自己的方式行事
words.ex: He likes to do his thing without any help.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢自己做自己的事，不需要任何帮助。
words.en: To do what one enjoys or is interested in, often in one's own unique way.

words.tr: phrase. 对...有益
words.ex: Eating vegetables does you good.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜对你有好处。
words.en: To be beneficial or advantageous to someone.

words.tr: phrasal verb. （用某种方式）杀死，击垮；使精疲力竭（尤指疾病或压力）
words.ex: He does his homework in the evening.
words.ex_cn: 他晚上做作业。
words.en: To make someone extremely tired or exhausted.

words.tr: phrase. 使精疲力竭；杀死
words.ex: The old coat was done in by the rain and wind.
words.ex_cn: 那件旧外套被风雨毁坏了。
words.en: To kill someone or to make someone very tired.

words.tr: phrase. v. 欺骗某人，使某人失去应得的东西
words.ex: He was accused of trying to do his partner out of his share of the profits.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控试图骗取其合伙人的利润份额。
words.en: To cheat someone out of something that they should have or were expecting to get.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人感到骄傲；为某人争光
words.ex: The team's performance did the coach proud.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队的表现让教练感到骄傲。
words.en: To make someone feel proud of you because of your achievements or behavior.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 扣好；整理好；修缮；包装
words.ex: She will do up her dress for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她会把裙子整理好去参加派对。
words.en: To fasten, close, or tidy something, or to repair or renovate it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某人有极大的心理安慰；使某人感到愉快和欣慰
words.ex: Spending time with family does my heart good.
words.ex_cn: 和家人在一起让我的心情变好。
words.en: If something does your heart good, it makes you feel happy or improves your mood.

words.tr: phrase. 再做一次某事；重新做某事
words.ex: If you're not satisfied with the result, you can do something over again.
words.ex_cn: 如果你对结果不满意，你可以重新做一遍。
words.en: To repeat an action or process.

words.tr: phrase. 重新做某事；把某事再做一遍
words.ex: I did my homework over because it was wrong.
words.ex_cn: 我把作业重做了一遍，因为之前做错了。
words.en: To repeat an action or process, often with the implication of starting over.

words.tr: phrase. 以艰难的方式做某事；不走捷径，靠辛苦努力完成
words.ex: He learned English by doing it the hard way, without any formal lessons.
words.ex_cn: 他通过没有正式课程的艰难方式学习英语。
words.en: To learn or achieve something through difficult or unpleasant experience.

words.tr: 短语动词. 负责做某项荣誉性任务，如主持仪式、切蛋糕、宣布消息等
words.ex: Can you do the honors and introduce the speaker?
words.ex_cn: 你能主持仪式并介绍演讲者吗？
words.en: To perform a task or duty that is considered a privilege or a special honor, especially in a social context.

words.tr: 短语动词. 起作用；奏效；解决问题
words.ex: A simple fix can do the trick.
words.ex_cn: 一个简单的解决办法就能奏效。
words.en: If something does the trick, it achieves what you wanted.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词DO补充词组

words.w: do a snow job on sb.
words.tr: 短语动词. 对某人花言巧语蒙骗；通过夸大或虚假的言辞使某人信服或迷惑
words.uk: duː ə snəʊ dʒɒb ɒn sʌmbədi
words.us: duː ə snoʊ dʒɑːb ɑːn ˈsʌmbədi
words.ex: He tried to do a snow job on her, but she wasn't fooled.
words.ex_cn: 他试图对她花言巧语，但她没有上当。
words.en: To deceive or mislead someone, often by using flattery or elaborate lies.

words.tr:
n. 损害；破损；
v. 损害；破坏；
words.ex: The storm caused serious damage to the house.
words.ex_cn: 风暴对房屋造成了严重损害。
words.en: Damage is physical harm that is caused to something which makes it less attractive, useful, or valuable.

words.tr: phrase. 尽全力
words.ex: He did his best in the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试中尽了最大努力。
words.en: To try as hard as one can to achieve something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 尽自己的责任；履行义务
words.ex: He does his duty every day at work.
words.ex_cn: 他每天在工作中尽职尽责。
words.en: To perform the tasks or responsibilities that one is expected or required to do.

words.tr: 短语动词. 尽自己的一份责任；做自己应做的事
words.ex: Everyone should do one's part to keep the classroom clean.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都应该尽自己的一份力来保持教室的清洁。
words.en: To fulfill one's responsibilities or contribute to a collective effort.

words.tr: phrase. 尽自己的一份力量；做自己该做的事
words.ex: Everyone can do one's bit to help the environment.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都可以尽自己的一份力来帮助环境。
words.en: To do one's bit means to contribute one's share of effort towards a common goal.

words.tr: phrase. 重新做；重做一次
words.ex: The teacher asked the student to do over the assignment to improve its quality.
words.ex_cn: 老师要求学生重做作业以提高其质量。
words.en: To do something again, especially because it was not done correctly the first time.

words.tr: phrase. 翻新；改造；转让；移交
words.ex: He decided to make over his property to his children.
words.ex_cn: 他决定将他的财产转让给他的孩子们。
words.en: To change something completely, often so that it is better, or to transfer the legal possession of property to someone else.

words.tr: phrase. 用手做某事；手工完成某事
words.ex: She prefers to do her knitting by hand rather than using a machine.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢手工编织，而不是使用机器。
words.en: To perform a task manually, without the use of machines.

words.tr: phrase. v. 把某事彻底做好，通常指把某人或某物打扮得非常整洁或漂亮；有时也用于讽刺，表示把事情搞得一团糟
words.ex: She did the project up brown, leaving no detail unchecked.
words.ex_cn: 她彻底完成了这个项目，没有遗漏任何细节。
words.en: To do something thoroughly or completely, especially to ensure that it is done to a high standard.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 6 基本动词 GET

words.tr: 短语动词. 得到黑眼圈；受挫，丢脸
words.ex: He got a black eye after falling off his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来后眼睛乌青了。
words.en: To receive a bruise around the eye from being hit, or to suffer damage to one's reputation.

words.tr: phrase. 黑眼圈；被打青的眼睛；耻辱，丢脸
words.ex: He has a black eye from playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他踢足球时弄出了个黑眼圈。
words.en: A black eye is a bruise around the eye, typically caused by a blow to the face, which results in discoloration and swelling.

words.tr: 短语动词. 得到一次机会；获得喘息的机会；走运一次
words.ex: He just needs to get a break to find a job.
words.ex_cn: 他只需要一个机会就能找到工作。
words.en: To have an opportunity or a rest.

words.tr: 短语动词. 休息一下；暂停一会儿
words.ex: Let's have a break and get some coffee.
words.ex_cn: 让我们休息一下，去喝点咖啡。
words.en: To take a short rest or pause from work or an activity.

words.tr: phrase. 想出一个绝妙的主意；突然有了好点子
words.ex: He gets a bright idea during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时想到了一个好主意。
words.en: To have a sudden, clever, or innovative thought.

words.tr: 短语动词. 想出一个绝妙的主意；突然有了聪明的想法
words.ex: Tom has a bright idea for the school project.
words.ex_cn: 汤姆对学校项目有了一个绝妙的主意。
words.en: To suddenly think of a good or clever idea.

words.tr: phrase. 从……中获得乐趣；因……而兴奋
words.ex: He gets a charge out of telling funny stories.
words.ex_cn: 他讲有趣的故事时感到非常兴奋。
words.en: To derive pleasure or excitement from something.

words.tr: phrase. 从……中获得极大的乐趣；对……感到兴奋或有趣
words.ex: I get a kick out of watching funny videos.
words.ex_cn: 我从看有趣的视频中获得乐趣。
words.en: To derive great pleasure or enjoyment from something.

words.tr: phrase. 非常享受做某事；从……中获得极大乐趣
words.ex: He gets a bang out of watching funny videos.
words.ex_cn: 他看搞笑视频时感到非常开心。
words.en: To derive great pleasure or enjoyment from something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 进行体检；做健康检查
words.ex: He will get a check-up next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周要去做体检。
words.en: To undergo a medical examination to assess one's health.

words.tr: n. 检查；体格检查
words.ex: He had a check-up at the hospital last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周在医院做了体检。
words.en: A check-up is a medical examination by your doctor to make sure that there is nothing wrong with your health.

words.w: get a clean bill of health
words.tr: 短语动词. 获得健康证明；被确认健康；通过检查或评估而被认为没有问题
words.uk: ɡet ə klen bɪl əv helθ
words.us: ɡet ə klen bɪl əv helθ
words.ex: The doctor said he got a clean bill of health after the check-up.
words.ex_cn: 医生说他体检后得到了健康证明。
words.en: To be declared healthy or in good condition after a check-up or inspection.

words.w: have a clean bill of health
words.tr: 短语动词. 身体健康状况良好；无健康问题
words.uk: hæv ə kliːn bɪl ɒv helθ
words.us: hæv ə klin bɪl əv hɛlθ
words.ex: The doctor said I have a clean bill of health.
words.ex_cn: 医生说我的健康状况良好。
words.en: To be declared healthy or free from problems after an examination or review.

words.w: get a dirty look from sb.
words.tr: 短语动词. 从某人那里得到一个不满或责备的眼神；遭到某人的白眼
words.uk: ɡet ə ˈdɪrti lʊk frɒm sʌmbədi
words.us: ɡet ə ˈdɜːrti lʊk frəm ˈsʌmbədi
words.ex: She got a dirty look from her boss when she arrived late.
words.ex_cn: 她迟到时从老板那里得到了一个厌恶的眼神。
words.en: To receive an unfriendly or disapproving glance from someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 得到一个厌恶或责备的眼神；被人怒目而视
words.ex: He got a dirty look for cutting in line.
words.ex_cn: 他因为插队而被人狠狠瞪了一眼。
words.en: To receive a disapproving or unfriendly glance from someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 得到公平的对待；获得公正的机会
words.ex: He wants to get a fair shake in court.
words.ex_cn: 他想在法庭上得到公平的对待。
words.en: To be treated fairly and without prejudice.

words.w: get a free hand with sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 在某事上获得完全的自主权或自由处理的权力
words.uk: ɡet ə friː hænd wɪð sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡet ə fri hænd wɪð sʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: The manager gave him a free hand with the project, allowing him to make all the decisions.
words.ex_cn: 经理给了他对这个项目的完全自主权，允许他做出所有决定。
words.en: To be given complete freedom or authority to do something as one sees fit.

words.w: have a free hand with sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 在某事上有完全的自主权或自由处理的权力
words.uk: hæv ə friː hænd wɪð ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv ə fri hænd wɪð ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: The manager has a free hand with the project budget.
words.ex_cn: 经理对项目预算有完全的自由处理权。
words.en: To have complete freedom or authority to do something as one sees fit.

words.tr: 短语动词. 获得充分的自主权；被放手让其自由行事
words.ex: The manager gave him a free hand to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 经理让他放手去完成这个项目。
words.en: To be given freedom to act independently without interference.

words.tr: 短语动词. 意为被给予充分的自由去做某事，不受限制地处理事务
words.ex: The manager gave him a free hand to plan the project.
words.ex_cn: 经理让他全权负责计划这个项目。
words.en: To have the freedom or authority to do something as one sees fit, without needing to seek approval from others.

words.tr: 短语动词. 理解某事；掌握某事
words.ex: It took me a while to get a grasp of the new software.
words.ex_cn: 我花了一段时间才掌握了新软件的使用方法。
words.en: To understand or become familiar with a concept, idea, or skill.

words.tr: 短语动词，对某事有理解或掌握
words.ex: It's important to have a grasp of the basics before moving on to more advanced topics.
words.ex_cn: 在进入更高级的主题之前，掌握基础知识是很重要的。
words.en: To understand a subject or situation well.

words.tr: 短语动词. 为某事鼓掌；表示支持或赞赏
words.ex: She got a hand for her presentation from her colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 她的同事们帮助她完成了演示。
words.en: To receive applause or praise for something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 得到帮助；获得支持（尤指鼓掌）
words.ex: He managed to get a hand from his neighbor to move the heavy furniture.
words.ex_cn: 他设法从邻居那里得到了帮助，搬动了沉重的家具。
words.en: To receive assistance or help from someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 在某事上得到帮助
words.ex: I need to get a hand with moving these boxes.
words.ex_cn: 我需要请人帮忙搬这些箱子。
words.en: To receive assistance with a task or problem.

words.tr: 短语动词. 参与某事；在某事中起作用
words.ex: She had a hand in organizing the event.
words.ex_cn: 她在组织这次活动中起到了作用。
words.en: If you have a hand in something, you are involved in it or have influence over it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 理解并开始控制某事物；对某事有把握
words.ex: It took me a while to get a handle on the new software.
words.ex_cn: 我花了一段时间才掌握了这个新软件。
words.en: To understand or gain control over something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事有控制力或理解；掌握某事
words.ex: She finally has a handle on the new software.
words.ex_cn: 她终于掌握了新软件。
words.en: To understand or be in control of something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比别人早一步开始做某事，抢先着手
words.ex: He gets a head start on his homework every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都提前开始做作业。
words.en: To begin something earlier than others in order to gain an advantage.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比别人早一步开始；在竞争中领先
words.ex: They have a head start on the project because they began early.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为开始得早，在项目上有了领先优势。
words.en: To have an advantage that makes you more likely to succeed in something, especially because you start doing it before other people.

words.tr: 短语动词. 获得领先；抢先一步；提前开始
words.ex: By studying the material before the class, I was able to get a head start on the project.
words.ex_cn: 通过在课前学习材料，我能够在项目上获得先机。
words.en: To get a head start means to begin something before others do, or to have an advantage at the beginning of a competition or task.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比别人早开始；领先一步
words.ex: Tom has a head start in the race because he began running early.
words.ex_cn: 汤姆在比赛中领先，因为他开始跑得早。
words.en: To have an advantage that makes success more likely, especially by starting before others.

words.tr: phrase. 快点；赶快行动
words.ex: Get a move on, or we will miss the bus.
words.ex_cn: 快点走，不然我们会错过公交车。
words.en: If you tell someone to get a move on, you are telling them to hurry.

words.tr:
n. 匆忙；
v. 赶快；
words.ex: He left in a hurry without saying goodbye.
words.ex_cn: 他匆忙离开，连再见都没说。
words.en: If you hurry somewhere, you go there quickly. If you hurry to do something, you start doing it quickly or do it more quickly than usual.

words.tr: 短语动词. 以...而闻名；获得作为...的名声
words.ex: He gets a reputation as a kind person.
words.ex_cn: 他得到了一个善良的人的名声。
words.en: To become known or regarded as having a particular quality or characteristic.

words.tr: 短语动词，以……而闻名；被认为是……的人或事物
words.ex: He has a reputation as a kind person.
words.ex_cn: 他以善良著称。
words.en: To be known or thought of by people in a particular way.

words.tr: 短语动词. 获得名声；树立声誉
words.ex: He got a reputation for being kind to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他因对每个人都友善而获得了好名声。
words.en: To become known or famous for something, especially something bad or good.

words.w: get a reputation for doing sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 因做某事而获得名声或声誉
words.uk: ɡet ə ˌrepju(ː)ˈteɪʃən fə ˈduːɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡet ə ˌrɛpjuˈteɪʃən fər ˈduːɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: She quickly got a reputation for being a hard worker.
words.ex_cn: 她很快因工作努力而获得了声誉。
words.en: To become known or famous for a particular quality or achievement, especially something bad.

words.w: have a reputation for doing sth.
words.tr: 短语. 因做某事而享有某种声誉；以做某事而出名
words.uk: hæv ə ˌrepjuˈteɪʃən fɔː ˈduːɪŋ sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv ə ˌrɛpjuˈteɪʃən fɔr ˈduɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: She has a reputation for being a tough negotiator.
words.ex_cn: 她以强硬的谈判者而闻名。
words.en: To be known or famous for a particular quality or achievement.

words.w: get a rise out of sb.
words.tr: phrase. v. 故意惹某人发怒或激动；使某人产生强烈反应
words.uk: gɛt ə raɪz aʊt ʌv ˈsʌmˌbɒdi
words.us: ɡɛt ə raɪz aʊt ʌv ˈsʌmˌbɑdi
words.ex: He enjoys getting a rise out of his colleagues by making sarcastic comments.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢通过发表讽刺评论来激怒同事。
words.en: To provoke or annoy someone, often intentionally.

words.w: get a rough idea of sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事有个大致的了解；粗略地知道某事
words.uk: ɡet ə rʌf ˈaɪdɪə əv ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡet ə rʌf ˈaɪdiə əv ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: After reading the summary, I got a rough idea of what the book is about.
words.ex_cn: 读完摘要后，我对这本书的内容有了个大概的了解。
words.en: To understand the basic or general aspects of something without knowing all the details.

words.w: get a rough idea about something
words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事有个大致的了解
words.uk: ɡet ə rʌf aɪˈdɪə əˈbaʊt ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡet ə rʌf aɪˈdiə əˈbaʊt ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: Before making a decision, it's important to get a rough idea about something.
words.ex_cn: 在做决定之前，对某事有个大致的了解是很重要的。
words.en: To have a general understanding or estimate about something without knowing all the details.

words.w: have a rough idea of something
words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事有个大致的了解或粗略的概念
words.uk: hæv ə rʌf ˈaɪdiə ɒv ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv ə rʌf ˈaɪdiə ʌv ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: I have a rough idea of how to fix the bike.
words.ex_cn: 我对如何修理自行车有个大概的想法。
words.en: To have a general understanding or knowledge about something, without knowing all the details.

words.w: have a rough idea about sth.
words.tr: 短语. 对某事有个大致的了解；对某事有粗略的概念
words.ex: I have a rough idea about the project, but I need more details.
words.ex_cn: 我对这个项目有个大概的了解，但我需要更多细节。
words.en: To have a general, not detailed, understanding of something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对……有个大致的了解；粗略地理解某事
words.ex: I just want to get a rough idea of how much it will cost.
words.ex_cn: 我只想大致了解一下它会花多少钱。
words.en: To understand the basic or general aspects of something without knowing all the details.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对……有个大致的概念；对……有粗略的想法
words.ex: I have a rough idea of what you mean, but could you clarify it?
words.ex_cn: 我大致了解你的意思，但你能澄清一下吗？
words.en: To have a general understanding or concept of something, without knowing all the details.

words.w: get a run for one's money
words.tr: phrase. 获得与对手势均力敌的竞争；使某人付出相当的努力才能获胜
words.uk: ɡet ə rʌn fə wʌnz ˈmʌni
words.us: ɡet ə rʌn fər wʌnz ˈmʌni
words.ex: The new team will get a run for their money in the competition.
words.ex_cn: 新团队在比赛中将会遇到强劲的对手。
words.en: To have a strong competition or to receive value for the money spent.

words.w: get a slap on the wrist
words.tr: 短语动词. 受到轻微的惩罚或口头警告，而没有严重的后果
words.uk: ɡet ə slæp ɒn ðə rɪst
words.us: ɡet ə slæp ɑːn ðə rɪst
words.ex: He got a slap on the wrist for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迟到只被轻描淡写地批评了一下。
words.en: To receive a mild punishment or reprimand.

words.tr: phrase. 变得傲慢自大；变得自以为了不起
words.ex: After winning the award, he started to get a swelled head and ignored his friends.
words.ex_cn: 获奖后，他开始自以为了不起，忽视了朋友。
words.en: To become conceited or vain.

words.tr: phrase. adj. 自负的；傲慢的；自以为了不起的
words.ex: He won one game and now he has a swelled head.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了一场比赛，现在就得意洋洋。
words.en: To be conceited or overly proud of oneself, often due to success or recognition.

words.tr: n. 谴责；斥责
words.ex: He received a severe tongue-lashing from his boss for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因为自己的错误受到了老板的严厉斥责。
words.en: A severe scolding or reprimand.

words.tr: 短语动词. （在别人不停说话时）插得上话，说上话
words.ex: I couldn't get a word in edgewise with my chatty friend.
words.ex_cn: 我那个健谈的朋友让我很难插上话。
words.en: To manage to say something in a conversation where others are talking a lot and it is difficult to be heard.

words.tr: adv. 以刃向外；沿边
words.ex: She pushed the box edgeways through the narrow opening.
words.ex_cn: 她把箱子沿边推过狭窄的开口。
words.en: If you say something edgeways, you say it with the edge rather than the flat side facing outwards or forwards.

words.tr: phrasal verb. （消息等）传开；（人）走动，外出活动
words.ex: The news about the party got about quickly.
words.ex_cn: 关于派对的消息很快传开了。
words.en: To move around or travel, especially within a community or area.

words.tr: phrase. 避免；绕开；说服；顺利应付
words.ex: He tried to get around the rules by using a loophole.
words.ex_cn: 他试图利用一个漏洞来规避规则。
words.en: To find a way to deal with or avoid a problem; to move or travel from place to place; to become known by many people.

words.tr: phrase. v. 督促某人；责备某人；追着某人要求其做某事
words.ex: She always gets after her kids for not cleaning their rooms.
words.ex_cn: 她总是因为孩子们不打扫房间而训斥他们。
words.en: To criticize or urge someone to do something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 勉强维持生计；靠极少的钱过日子
words.ex: They managed to get along on a shoestring after losing their jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他们在失业后设法靠极少的钱勉强维持生计。
words.en: To manage to live or operate with a very small amount of money.

words.tr: phrase. 相处
words.ex: They get along well with each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们相处得很好。
words.en: If people get along, they like each other and are friendly to each other.

words.tr: 短语动词. 与某人相处融洽；与某人和睦相处
words.ex: She gets along with everyone in the office.
words.ex_cn: 她与办公室里的每个人都相处得很好。
words.en: To have a good relationship with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人相处融洽；继续与某人交往
words.ex: I get on with my brother even when we argue.
words.ex_cn: 即使我们吵架，我和我哥哥还是相处得很好。
words.en: If you get on with someone, you are friendly and have a good relationship with them.

words.tr: phrase. 进展；相处；上车
words.ex: How is your project getting on?
words.ex_cn: 你的项目进展如何？
words.en: If you get on with someone, you have a friendly relationship with them. If you get on with something, you continue doing it or start doing it.

words.tr: phrase. 在没有…的情况下生活或应付过去；设法继续
words.ex: She managed to get along without her phone for a week.
words.ex_cn: 她设法在没有手机的情况下度过了一周。
words.en: To manage or survive without something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 忍不住激动或焦躁不安；坐立不安
words.ex: He always gets ants in his pants before a test.
words.ex_cn: 他每次考试前都坐立不安。
words.en: To become extremely restless or excited and unable to stay still.

words.tr: phrase. 形容某人非常焦躁不安或坐立不安
words.ex: He has ants in his pants and can't sit still.
words.ex_cn: 他坐立不安，好像屁股下有蚂蚁。
words.en: If someone has ants in their pants, they are very restless or excited about something and cannot keep still.

words.tr: adj. 坐立不安的；焦虑的
words.ex: The waiting made her feel antsy.
words.ex_cn: 等待让她感到坐立不安。
words.en: If someone is antsy, they are nervous or impatient.

words.tr: phrase. 领会；贿赂；查明；够到
words.ex: I don't know what you are getting at.
words.ex_cn: 我不明白你到底想表达什么。
words.en: If you ask someone what they are getting at, you are asking them to explain what they mean, usually because you think they are being unpleasant or are suggesting something that is untrue.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始用力做某事；向…发起攻击；着手对付
words.ex: They have at the problem with new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他们用新想法应对这个问题。
words.en: To attempt to do something; to attack someone or something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 远离一切烦恼；彻底放松；摆脱日常琐事
words.ex: He went to the mountains to get away from it all.
words.ex_cn: 他去山里远离一切烦恼。
words.en: To escape from one's usual environment or daily routine, often for relaxation or to avoid stress.

words.tr: phrase. 逃脱；离开；度假
words.ex: The thief tried to get away from the police.
words.ex_cn: 小偷试图逃脱警察。
words.en: If you get away, you succeed in leaving a place or a person's company. If you get away with something, you succeed in doing it without being caught or punished.

words.tr: phrase. v. （做坏事而）逃脱惩罚，侥幸成功
words.ex: He stole the money but got away with it.
words.ex_cn: 他偷了钱，但没有被发现。
words.en: To avoid being punished for something wrong that one has done.

words.tr: phrase. v. 报复某人；对某人进行反击
words.ex: He decided to get back at his boss for the unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他决定报复老板的不公平对待。
words.en: To take revenge on someone for something they have done to you.

words.tr: phrase. v. 恢复正常生活；重新自立；从困境中恢复过来
words.ex: After the illness, he worked hard to get back on his feet.
words.ex_cn: 生病后，他努力恢复健康。
words.en: To recover from a setback or illness and return to a normal state of health, happiness, or success.

words.tr: 短语动词. 恢复健康；恢复经济独立；重新站稳脚跟；恢复正常状态
words.ex: He broke his leg, but he is back on his feet now.
words.ex_cn: 他摔断了腿，但现在已康复了。
words.en: To recover from an illness or setback and return to a normal state of health or operation.

words.tr: phrase. v. 回复某人；稍后给某人答复
words.ex: I'll get back to you with the details tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天会给你具体细节的回复。
words.en: To return to someone, especially in order to give them information or to respond to a request or question.

words.tr: phrase. 回来；取回；恢复；报复
words.ex: He will get back tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会回来。
words.en: To return to a place, condition, or activity; to recover something lost or taken away; to retaliate.

words.tr: 短语动词. 变得更好；改善；康复
words.ex: He practices every day to get better at English.
words.ex_cn: 他每天练习，为了让英语变得更好。
words.en: To become better in health, condition, or quality.

words.tr: phrase. 感到紧张或焦虑，通常是因为即将发生的重要或令人期待的事情
words.ex: I get butterflies in my stomach before speaking in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 我在全班面前讲话前会紧张得胃里发紧。
words.en: To feel nervous or excited about something that is going to happen.

words.tr: 短语动词. 感到紧张或焦虑，通常是因为即将发生的重要或令人紧张的事情
words.ex: I have butterflies in my stomach before the test.
words.ex_cn: 考试前我紧张得心里七上八下。
words.en: To feel very nervous or excited about something that you are going to do or that is going to happen.

words.tr: phrase. 凭某物勉强应付；靠某物过活
words.ex: She manages to get by with the old computer.
words.ex_cn: 她用那台旧电脑勉强应付。
words.en: To manage to live or do something with the help of something, especially when this is not ideal or sufficient.

words.tr: phrase. v. 度过难关；勉强应付；勉强维持生活
words.ex: He gets by with little money.
words.ex_cn: 他靠很少的钱维持生活。
words.en: To manage to live or do a particular thing using the money, knowledge, equipment, etc. that you have.

words.tr: phrase. v. 变得过于兴奋或激动而失去控制；忘乎所以；得意忘形
words.ex: He got carried away with the game and forgot to eat dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他玩游戏玩得忘了吃晚饭。
words.en: If you get carried away, you are so excited or involved in something that you do something hasty or foolish.

words.tr: phrase. 接近
words.ex: The cat tries to get close to the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猫试图靠近那只鸟。
words.en: To move or come near to someone or something in distance or time.

words.tr: 短语动词. 靠近；接近；变得亲密
words.ex: The cat gets close to the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猫靠近鸟。
words.en: To move or come nearer to someone or something in distance.

words.tr: phrase. 感到胆怯或临阵退缩
words.ex: He got cold feet before the speech and ran away.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲前临阵退缩，跑掉了。
words.en: If you get cold feet about something, you suddenly become too frightened to do something that you had planned to do.

words.tr: phrase. （因害怕或犹豫而）临阵退缩，胆怯，不敢行动
words.ex: He has cold feet about the trip because he is afraid of flying.
words.ex_cn: 他对这次旅行感到害怕，因为他害怕坐飞机。
words.en: to suddenly become too frightened to do something you had planned to do, especially something important such as getting married

words.tr: 短语动词. 因某事获得认可或赞誉；因某事得到学分或功劳
words.ex: He got credit for helping his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他因为帮助朋友而得到了认可。
words.en: To receive recognition or praise for something.

words.tr: phrase. 获得信用；得到认可；获得学分
words.ex: She worked hard to get credit for her work.
words.ex_cn: 她努力工作以获得对其工作的认可。
words.en: To receive recognition or acknowledgment for something done or achieved; in an educational context, to receive a unit of value towards a degree or qualification.

words.tr: 短语动词. 切入正题；认真讨论实质问题；着手处理事情的核心部分
words.ex: Let's get down to brass tacks and discuss the budget.
words.ex_cn: 让我们开始讨论预算这个最重要的细节。
words.en: If you get down to brass tacks, you start to discuss the most important and practical details of a situation.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始认真做正事；着手处理重要事务
words.ex: We need to get down to business if we want to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: v. 我们需要开始认真工作，如果我们想按时完成项目。
words.en: To start doing what needs to be done, especially in a serious or determined way.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始认真工作；着手做正事
words.ex: After the meeting, we need to get down to work immediately.
words.ex_cn: 会议结束后，我们需要立即开始认真工作。
words.en: To begin to work seriously or with determination.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始认真处理问题；进入正题；着手解决实质问题
words.ex: We need to get down to cases and solve this problem.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要开始认真处理这个问题并解决它。
words.en: To begin to deal with something seriously.

words.tr: phrase. 进入正题；讨论实质内容；着手处理关键细节
words.uk: get daʊn tə ðə ˈnɪti ˈɡrɪti
words.us: get daʊn tə ðə ˈnɪti ˈɡrɪti
words.ex: Let's get down to the nitty-gritty of the project and discuss the budget.
words.ex_cn: 让我们深入讨论项目的实质，谈谈预算。
words.en: To begin to deal with the most important aspects or details of something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 起鸡皮疙瘩；感到毛骨悚然或激动
words.ex: He gets goose bumps when he hears that song.
words.ex_cn: 他听到那首歌时就会起鸡皮疙瘩。
words.en: To develop goosebumps due to cold, fear, or excitement.

words.tr: phrase. 起鸡皮疙瘩；感到毛骨悚然或激动
words.ex: I have goose bumps when I hear that song.
words.ex_cn: 当我听到那首歌时，我起了鸡皮疙瘩。
words.en: To have goosebumps on one's skin.

words.tr: phrase. 鸡皮疙瘩；因寒冷或恐惧等引起的皮肤上的小突起
words.ex: The sudden chill gave him goose pimples.
words.ex_cn: 突如其来的寒意让他起了鸡皮疙瘩。
words.en: Small raised areas that appear on the skin because of cold, fear, or excitement.

words.tr: 短语动词. 起鸡皮疙瘩；感到毛骨悚然
words.ex: I have goose pimples when the cold wind blows.
words.ex_cn: 当冷风吹来时，我起了鸡皮疙瘩。
words.en: An alternative term for having goosebumps.

words.tr: phrase. 白发；灰发
words.ex: He noticed the first signs of gray hair.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了第一缕白发的迹象。
words.en: Hair that has turned white or gray, typically as a result of aging.

words.tr: 短语动词. 变得焦虑或担忧而长出白发；因压力或烦恼而变老
words.ex: He started to get gray hairs when he was thirty.
words.ex_cn: 他三十岁时开始长白头发了。
words.en: To become worried or stressed, often causing one's hair to turn gray.

words.tr: phrase. 抓住；掌握；得到；找到某人
words.ex: He tried to get hold of the rope.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抓住那根绳子。
words.en: To obtain something or to contact someone.

words.tr: phrase. v. 抓住；握住；掌握
words.ex: He has hold of the rope and won't let go.
words.ex_cn: 他抓住了绳子，不肯松手。
words.en: To grasp or hold something firmly.

words.w: get in on the ground floor
words.tr: 短语动词. 在初期就参与进来，通常指在项目、企业或机会刚开始时就加入，以获得最大利益
words.uk: ɡet ɪn ɒn ðə ɡraʊnd flɔː(r)
words.us: ɡet ɪn ɑːn ðə ɡraʊnd flɔːr
words.ex: He got in on the ground floor of the new tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他早早加入了这家新科技公司。
words.en: To become involved in something at the beginning, especially when it is likely to be successful.

words.tr: phrase. 进入；到达；插话；收割；当选
words.ex: He gets in the car every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上上车。
words.en: To arrive at a place, especially after a journey.

words.tr: phrase. v. 惹人烦扰；使人心烦意乱；让人感到恼火
words.ex: Stop getting in my hair and let me work.
words.ex_cn: 别再烦我了，让我工作吧。
words.en: To annoy or bother someone, especially by being too close to them or by interfering with what they are doing.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 妨碍某人；挡住某人的路
words.ex: Please move the box, it is getting in my way.
words.ex_cn: 请把箱子移开，它挡了我的路。
words.en: To prevent someone from doing something or moving freely.

words.tr: 与某人联系或接触
words.ex: I will get in touch with my friend tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天会联系我的朋友。
words.en: To communicate with someone, especially after a period of not communicating.

words.tr: 短语动词. 取得联系；与...联络
words.ex: Please get in touch if you need help.
words.ex_cn: 如果你需要帮助，请联系我。
words.en: To communicate with someone, especially by phone or email, in order to give or receive information.

words.tr: phrase. v. 陷入混乱；惹上麻烦；把事情搞糟
words.ex: He gets into a mess when he doesn't plan his work.
words.ex_cn: 当他不规划工作时，就会陷入混乱。
words.en: If you get into a mess, you find yourself in a difficult or confusing situation that is hard to resolve.

words.tr: 短语. 处于混乱状态；处境糟糕
words.ex: His room is in a mess.
words.ex_cn: 他的房间乱七八糟。
words.en: To be in a state of disorder, confusion, or trouble.

words.tr: 短语动词. 进入全面活跃状态；全面展开；开始充分运转
words.ex: The party got into full swing at eight o'clock.
words.ex_cn: 派对在八点钟进入高潮。
words.en: When an event or activity gets into full swing, it reaches its highest level of activity or excitement.

words.tr: 短语动词. 进入高速运转状态；加快行动；开始积极行动
words.ex: We need to get into high gear to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要加快速度，按时完成项目。
words.en: To start working or operating at a very fast and efficient rate.

words.tr: phrase. 进入；陷入；染上（坏习惯）
words.ex: He wants to get into a good university.
words.ex_cn: 他想进入一所好大学。
words.en: To enter or become involved in a particular activity, situation, or state.

words.w: get into the swing of things
words.tr: 短语动词. 开始适应某事的节奏或状态；逐渐习惯并顺利进行
words.uk: ɡet ˈɪntə ðə swɪŋ əv θɪŋz
words.us: ɡet ˈɪntu ðə swɪŋ əv θɪŋz
words.ex: After a few days, he got into the swing of things at his new job.
words.ex_cn: 几天后，他适应了新工作。
words.en: To become accustomed to a new environment or situation and start to participate fully in it.

words.tr: phrase. v. 走开，消失；迷路
words.ex: He told the noisy boy to get lost.
words.ex_cn: 他让那个吵闹的男孩走开。
words.en: If you tell someone to get lost, you are telling them in a rude way to go away.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 混淆；搞混；卷入（麻烦或复杂情况）
words.ex: I get mixed up when I hear two people talking at once.
words.ex_cn: 当两个人同时说话时，我会搞混。
words.en: Become confused or mistaken; mix things up incorrectly.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始行动；赶快动起来
words.ex: It's late, so get moving now.
words.ex_cn: 天晚了，现在快点动身吧。
words.en: If you get moving, you start taking action or start going somewhere.

words.tr: phrase. 得到不公平的待遇；受到不公正的对待
words.ex: He got a raw deal when his boss blamed him for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他的老板把错误归咎于他，他受到了不公平的对待。
words.en: To be treated unfairly, especially in a business deal or agreement.

words.tr: phrase. 不公平的待遇；苛刻的交易；吃亏的买卖
words.ex: He got a raw deal when he lost his job without any warning.
words.ex_cn: 他毫无预警地丢了工作，受到了不公平的对待。
words.en: If someone says that they have had a raw deal, they mean that they have been treated unfairly.

words.tr: phrase. 下车；离开
words.ex: He gets off the bus at the school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校下车。
words.en: To leave a place, especially in order to start a journey; to remove something, especially clothing.

words.tr: 短语动词. 轻易脱身；受到从轻处理；侥幸过关
words.ex: He got off easy after the teacher only gave him a warning.
words.ex_cn: 老师只给了他一个警告，他算是逃过一劫了。
words.en: To escape punishment or a difficult situation with little or no trouble.

words.tr: 短语动词. 从轻发落；受到较轻的惩罚
words.ex: He got off lightly after breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他违反规则后却得到了从轻处理。
words.en: To escape or receive a less severe punishment or consequence than might have been expected.

words.w: get off on the wrong foot
words.tr: phrase. 一开始就出错；一开始就关系不佳
words.uk: ɡet ɒf ɒn ðə rɒŋ fʊt
words.us: ɡɛt ɔf ɒn ðə rɔŋ fʊt
words.ex: They got off on the wrong foot when they first met.
words.ex_cn: 他们第一次见面时就产生了误会。
words.en: To start a relationship or project badly, often because of a misunderstanding or mistake.

words.w: get off to a bad start
words.tr: phrase. 开始就不顺利；有一个糟糕的开端
words.uk: ɡet ɒf tə ə bæd stɑːt
words.us: ɡet ɔːf tə ə bæd stɑːrt
words.ex: They get off to a bad start on their trip because the flight is delayed.
words.ex_cn: 他们的旅行因为航班延误而有了一个糟糕的开端。
words.en: To begin something in an unfavorable or unsuccessful manner.

words.tr: phrase. 别再烦我！别再挑剔我！
words.ex: Can you get off my case? I already said I'm sorry!
words.ex_cn: 你能别再责备我了吗？我已经说对不起了！
words.en: Stop criticizing or harassing someone.

words.tr: phrase. 别再烦我！别再管我！
words.ex: Please get off my back! I will do it soon.
words.ex_cn: 别再烦我了！我很快就会做的。
words.en: Stop bothering or nagging someone.

words.tr: phrase. v. 别再紧逼某人；别再纠缠；让某人清静一下
words.ex: Get off my tail! I'm doing the work as fast as I can.
words.ex_cn: 别紧跟着我！我在尽快完成工作了。
words.en: Stop following or pressuring someone closely.

words.tr: phrase. 让某人感到烦躁；使某人恼火
words.ex: The loud music next door gets on my nerves.
words.ex_cn: 隔壁的吵闹音乐让我很烦。
words.en: To irritate or annoy someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 跟风；随大流；加入潮流
words.ex: Many people get on the bandwagon when a new trend becomes popular.
words.ex_cn: 当一种新潮流变得流行时，许多人就会跟风。
words.en: Join a popular activity or trend that others are already doing.

words.tr: 短语动词. 支持某人或加入某个潮流、运动，尤其是当其开始成功时
words.ex: He started to get on his friend's bandwagon when the team began to win.
words.ex_cn: 当球队开始赢球时，他开始支持他朋友的球队了。
words.en: To join or support a popular trend, activity, or cause.

words.tr: phrase. 赶时髦；跟风；随大流；加入声势日隆的活动或潮流
words.ex: Many people jump on the bandwagon when a new trend becomes popular.
words.ex_cn: 当一种新潮流变得流行时，许多人会跟风。
words.en: To join others in doing something that is becoming fashionable or popular.

words.tr: phrase. 加入某人的阵营；赶时髦地支持某人（或某事）；随大流
words.ex: He did not have his own idea, so he just jump on one's bandwagon.
words.ex_cn: 他没有自己的想法，所以只是随大流。
words.en: To join or support a cause, movement, or activity that is already successful or popular.

words.tr: 短语动词. 感到喉咙哽咽，因情绪激动而喉咙发紧
words.ex: I get lump in my throat when I hear that song.
words.ex_cn: 当我听到那首歌时，我喉咙哽咽。
words.en: Feel a tight, emotional sensation in the throat, often from sadness or gratitude.

words.w: have a lump in one's throat
words.tr: 短语动词. 喉咙里像有东西堵着一样，形容因情绪激动（如悲伤、感动）而感到喉咙发紧
words.uk: hæv ə lʌmp ɪn wʌnz θrəʊt
words.us: hæv ə lʌmp ɪn wʌnz θroʊt
words.ex: I had a lump in my throat when I said goodbye to my mom.
words.ex_cn: 当我向妈妈道别时，我喉咙哽咽了。
words.en: To feel a tightness in the throat because of strong emotion, especially sadness or the effort not to cry.

words.w: get on the good side of sb.
words.tr: 短语动词. 赢得某人的好感；与某人搞好关系
words.uk: ɡet ɒn ðə ɡʊd saɪd əv ˈsʌmwʌn
words.us: ɡet ɑːn ðə ɡʊd saɪd əv ˈsʌmwʌn
words.ex: He helped his boss with the report to get on the good side of him.
words.ex_cn: 他帮老板写报告，以讨好他。
words.en: To make someone like you or approve of you by doing things that they like or agree with.

words.tr: phrase. 相处融洽
words.ex: I get on with my brother very well.
words.ex_cn: 我和我哥哥相处得很好。
words.en: To continue doing something, especially after an interruption, or to have a good relationship with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 相处；进展
words.ex: I get along with my neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 我和我的邻居相处得很好。
words.en: If you get along with someone, you have a friendly relationship with them.

words.tr: phrase. 得到应得的报应；受到应有的惩罚
words.ex: He lied to everyone and finally got his comeuppance.
words.ex_cn: 他骗了所有人，最终得到了应得的报应。
words.en: Receive the punishment or consequences one deserves.

words.w: get one's ducks in a row
words.tr: phrase. 把事情安排得井井有条；做好充分准备
words.uk: ɡet wʌnz dʌks ɪn ə rəʊ
words.us: ɡet wʌnz dʌks ɪn ə roʊ
words.ex: He needs to get his ducks in a row before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他需要在会议前把事情安排妥当。
words.en: To organize one's tasks or affairs in order to be prepared for what is coming.

words.w: get one's feet on the ground
words.tr: phrase. v. 站稳脚跟；适应新环境；务实起来
words.uk: ɡet wʌnz fiːt ɒn ðə ɡraʊnd
words.us: ɡet wʌnz fit ɑːn ðə ɡraʊnd
words.ex: It takes time to get one's feet on the ground in a new job.
words.ex_cn: 在一份新工作中站稳脚跟需要时间。
words.en: Become practical, realistic, or established in life.

words.w: have one's feet on the ground
words.tr: phrase. 脚踏实地的；务实的；现实的
words.uk: hæv wʌnz fiːt ɒn ðə ɡraʊnd
words.us: hæv wʌnz fit ɑːn ðə ɡraʊnd
words.ex: He has his feet on the ground and always thinks about the future.
words.ex_cn: 他脚踏实地，总是考虑未来。
words.en: To be sensible and practical, especially in the way you deal with everyday life.

words.tr: phrase. 开始尝试某事，通常指初次尝试某项新活动或任务，以熟悉情况
words.ex: He wants to get his feet wet in cooking by making a simple meal.
words.ex_cn: 他想通过做一顿简单的饭来开始学做饭。
words.en: To begin to do something new, especially something that one has not done before.

words.tr: phrase. 因某事而遭受损失或痛苦，通常指因插手不该管的事或冒险而受到惩罚或伤害
words.ex: He got his fingers burned when the pot was too hot.
words.ex_cn: 当锅太烫时，他把手烫伤了。
words.en: If you get your fingers burned, you suffer as a result of an unsuccessful or risky action.

words.w: get one's foot in the door
words.tr: 短语动词. 比喻获得初步的机会或进入某个组织、行业等，以便将来有更好的发展
words.uk: ɡet wʌnz fʊt ɪn ðə dɔː
words.us: ɡet wʌnz fʊt ɪn ðə dɔːr
words.ex: He got his foot in the door with a small job at the company.
words.ex_cn: 他通过在公司做一份小工作而获得了入门的机会。
words.en: To achieve a first step toward a goal by gaining entry into an organization, a career, etc.

words.w: have one's foot in the door
words.tr: phrase. 已经获得初步成功或进入某个机会的门槛，通常指在工作或社交场合中取得了初步立足点
words.uk: hæv wʌnz fʊt ɪn ðə dɔː
words.us: hæv wʌnz fʊt ɪn ðə dɔr
words.ex: He got a part-time job at the company, so now he has his foot in the door.
words.ex_cn: 他在那家公司找到了一份兼职工作，所以现在算是站稳了脚跟。
words.en: To achieve an initial stage of progress or acceptance in a particular area or field.

words.tr: phrase. 弄脏自己的手；参与实际工作，尤指做艰苦或不愉快的事情
words.ex: He doesn't mind getting his hands dirty when helping in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园里帮忙时不怕弄脏手。
words.en: To involve oneself in work that is considered menial or unpleasant, often to achieve a goal or to help out.

words.tr: phrase. 弄脏自己的手；比喻参与不道德或卑鄙的事情
words.ex: He doesn't want to dirty his hands with that bad job.
words.ex_cn: 他不想把手弄脏去做那份糟糕的工作。
words.en: Become involved in something disreputable or morally questionable.

words.tr: phrase. 弄脏自己的手；比喻做不道德或卑劣的事
words.ex: He soiled his hands while working in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园里干活时弄脏了手。
words.en: To involve oneself in dishonest or immoral activities.

words.tr: phrase. v. 把手拿开；不要碰
words.ex: The teacher said, "Get your hands off that machine!"
words.ex_cn: 老师说：“把你的手从那台机器上拿开！”
words.en: To remove one's hands from something or someone, often used as a command to stop touching or interfering.

words.tr: phrase. 不干涉的；禁止插手的
words.ex: Hands off! That's my lunch.
words.ex_cn: 不要碰！那是我的午餐。
words.en: If you say 'hands off' something, you are telling someone not to touch it or interfere with it.

words.tr: phrase. 放开某人的手；停止干预或控制某人/某事
words.ex: The teacher said, "Take your hands off the computer!"
words.ex_cn: 老师说：“把你的手从电脑上拿开！”
words.en: To stop holding or touching something, or to stop being involved in something, allowing others to take control.

words.tr: phrase. v. 得到；弄到（某物）
words.ex: He wants to get his hands on the new phone.
words.ex_cn: 他想弄到那部新手机。
words.en: To obtain something, especially something that is difficult to get.

words.tr: phrase. 找到；得到；抓到；对…动手
words.ex: He finally laid his hands on the book he wanted.
words.ex_cn: 他终于找到了他想要的那本书。
words.en: To find or obtain something, especially after some effort.

words.tr: phrase. v. 摆脱困境；渡过难关；开始摆脱财务或情绪上的压力
words.ex: After months of hard work, he finally gets his head above water.
words.ex_cn: 经过几个月的努力工作，他终于摆脱了困境。
words.en: To manage to deal with a difficult situation, especially one in which you have financial problems.

words.tr: phrase. 比喻处境困难时仍能勉强维持，不致陷入绝境；经济上或情绪上能够应付，不至于崩溃
words.ex: After getting a new job, he finally has his head above water.
words.ex_cn: 找到新工作后，他终于摆脱了困境。
