words.en: To manage to deal with a difficult situation, especially one in which you have financial problems, and just avoid going under.

words.tr: phrase. 得到某人应得的报应或奖赏（通常指因恶行而受到惩罚）
words.ex: He lied to everyone, so when he got his just desserts, no one felt sorry for him.
words.ex_cn: 他向所有人撒了谎，所以当他得到应有报应时，没有人同情他。
words.en: To receive the appropriate reward or punishment for one's actions.

words.tr: 短语动词. 所付的钱物有所值；得到应得的东西
words.ex: We got our money's worth from the concert.
words.ex_cn: 我们从那场音乐会中得到了应得的价值。
words.en: To receive good value for the money one has spent.

words.w: get one's nose out of one's business
words.tr: phrase. v. 不要多管闲事；让某人别干涉他人的私事
words.uk: ɡet wʌnz nəʊz aʊt əv wʌnz ˈbɪznəs
words.us: ɡet wʌnz noʊz aʊt əv wʌnz ˈbɪznəs
words.ex: He always gets his nose out of other people's business.
words.ex_cn: 他总是管别人闲事。
words.en: To stop interfering in someone else's affairs.

words.tr: 短语动词. 恢复精力，重新振作（尤指在感到疲倦后突然恢复体力或精神）
words.ex: After resting a few minutes, he got his second wind and ran faster.
words.ex_cn: 休息了几分钟后，他恢复了体力，跑得更快了。
words.en: To get one's second wind means to feel energetic again after being tired, especially during physical activity.

words.tr: 短语动词. 恢复精力，重新振作（通常指在感到疲倦后突然又有了力气）
words.ex: After resting a while, he had his second wind and kept running.
words.ex_cn: 休息了一会儿后，他恢复了体力，继续跑步。
words.en: To regain energy or strength after feeling tired, especially during physical activity.

words.tr: phrase. 开始；起步；获得开端
words.ex: He got his start as a cook in a small restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 他是在一家小餐馆当厨师开始起步的。
words.en: To begin one's career or involvement in a particular field or activity.

words.tr: phrase. 开始属于某人；某人开始起步
words.ex: The show has its start at 8 PM.
words.ex_cn: 演出晚上8点开始。
words.en: To begin one's career in a particular field or profession.

words.tr: phrase. 开始认真处理或深入研究某事；全身心投入某事
words.ex: He got his teeth into the new project last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周开始认真投入这个新项目。
words.en: To start doing something with enthusiasm and determination.

words.tr: phrase. 全力投入某事；认真着手处理某事（尤指令人兴奋或具挑战性的事）
words.ex: She was eager to sink her teeth into the new project.
words.ex_cn: 她渴望着手处理这个新项目。
words.en: To start doing something with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr: phrase. v. 摆脱困境；从……下面出来；摆脱压力或负担
words.ex: He worked hard to get out from under his debt.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以摆脱债务。
words.en: To escape from a difficult situation or problem.

words.tr: phrase. v. 摆脱困境；从混乱中脱身
words.ex: He tried to get out of a mess after breaking the vase.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在打碎花瓶后摆脱困境。
words.en: To extricate oneself from a difficult or troublesome situation.

words.tr: phrase. 克服；恢复；原谅
words.ex: He got over his cold last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周康复了。
words.en: To recover from something, such as an illness or a shock; to overcome a problem or difficulty.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 对某人采取肢体行动；与某人发生身体接触（常指暴力或亲密行为）
words.ex: He got physical with his brother during the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他在打架时对弟弟动了手。
words.en: To engage in physical contact or sexual activity with someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 进行体力活动；动手动脚；变得暴力或具有攻击性
words.ex: He gets physical when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 他生气时会动粗。
words.en: If a situation gets physical, it becomes violent, with people hitting or fighting each other.

words.tr: 短语动词。开始认真对待道德或宗教问题；突然变得有责任感或行为端正
words.ex: He used to be lazy, but he got religion and now works hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他以前很懒，但后来幡然醒悟，现在每天都努力工作。
words.en: To suddenly become very interested in or enthusiastic about a particular subject or activity, often in a way that is surprising to others.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始行动；启动；开始进行
words.ex: Let's get rolling on the project tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天开始推进这个项目吧。
words.en: To start or begin something, especially a process or activity.

words.tr: phrase. 对……产生疑虑；重新考虑；改变主意
words.ex: He gets second thoughts about the job after the interview.
words.ex_cn: 面试后他对这份工作产生了犹豫。
words.en: To reconsider a decision or plan, especially because you are now not sure if it is the best one.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对……重新考虑；对……产生疑虑
words.ex: He had second thoughts about quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他对于辞职有了犹豫。
words.en: To reconsider a decision or opinion, often because of doubts or concerns.

words.tr: 短语动词. 准备好；做好准备（常用于命令或鼓励语气，如 'Get set, go!'）
words.ex: He gets set for the race quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快做好了赛跑的准备。
words.en: Get ready; prepare for a race or event by assuming a starting position.

words.tr: phrase. 准备就绪；安排妥当；处于某种状态
words.ex: The meeting is set for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 会议定在明天。
words.en: To be placed or fixed in a specified position or condition; to be ready or prepared for something.

words.tr: phrase. 生病
words.ex: He gets sick when he eats too much candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多糖果会生病。
words.en: To become ill or to start to feel ill.

words.tr: phrase. v. 意识到；看透；识破（某人或某事的真相）
words.ex: He quickly got wise to the trick.
words.ex_cn: 他很快识破了这个把戏。
words.en: To become aware of or informed about something, especially something that someone is trying to keep secret.

words.tr: phrase. 变得聪明；明白过来；了解真相
words.ex: He got wise to the trick after two days.
words.ex_cn: 两天后，他明白了这个把戏。
words.en: To become aware or knowledgeable about something, especially something that was previously unknown or misunderstood.

words.tr: phrase. v. 使某人摆脱困境；使某人免于承担责任
words.ex: The teacher let him off the hook because he apologized.
words.ex_cn: 老师让他过关了，因为他道歉了。
words.en: To free someone from a difficult situation or from blame.

words.tr: phrase. 脱身；摆脱困境或责任；侥幸逃脱
words.ex: He managed to get off the hook by proving his alibi.
words.ex_cn: 他通过证明自己的不在场证明成功摆脱了困境。
words.en: To escape from a difficult situation or avoid responsibility.

words.tr: 短语动词. 听取某人的意见；获得某人的关注
words.ex: He always tries to get my ear before class.
words.ex_cn: 他总是在课前找我说话。
words.en: To succeed in getting someone to listen to you.

words.tr: phrase. v. 深受某人信任，能影响某人；得到某人的注意或倾听
words.ex: The teacher has my ear when she speaks.
words.ex_cn: 老师说话时，我在认真听。
words.en: To be listened to with attention and respect, especially by someone in authority.

words.tr: phrase. v. 把……从脑海中排除；不再想某事
words.ex: I can't get that song out of my mind.
words.ex_cn: 我无法把那首歌从脑子里赶出去。
words.en: To stop thinking about something or someone; to forget something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 控制住
words.ex: We need to get the fire under control quickly.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要迅速把火势控制住。
words.en: To manage to bring something under control, especially something that is difficult to manage or that has been out of control.

words.tr: 短语动词. 完全掌控……；使……处于控制之下
words.ex: Don't worry, I have the situation under control.
words.ex_cn: 别担心，我已把情况控制住了。
words.en: To have a situation or problem under control means to have it managed or dealt with successfully so that it is no longer a cause for concern.

words.w: get sb. out of a jam
words.tr: phrase. 帮某人摆脱困境
words.uk: ɡet ˈsʌmˌbɒd.i ˈaʊt ɒv ə dʒæm
words.us: ɡet ˈsʌmˌbɑd.i ˈaʊt əv ə dʒæm
words.ex: He got his friend out of a jam by lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他借钱给朋友，帮朋友摆脱了困境。
words.en: To help someone escape from a difficult situation.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人处于无助或受制于人的境地；迫使某人屈服
words.ex: They got him over a barrel when he stole the money.
words.ex_cn: 当他偷了钱时，他们让他陷入了困境。
words.en: To put someone in a situation where they have no choice but to agree to your demands, because they are in a very difficult position and you have all the power.

words.tr: phrase. 完全控制某人，使某人处于无法反抗或无助的境地
words.ex: They have him over a barrel because he stole the money.
words.ex_cn: 他偷了钱，所以他们抓住了他的把柄。
words.en: To have someone in a situation where they are at a disadvantage and cannot escape.

words.tr: phrase. 完全控制某人，使某人唯命是从
words.uk: ɡet sʌm wʌn ˈʌndə wʌnz θʌm
words.us: ɡet sʌm wʌn ˈʌndər wʌnz θʌm
words.ex: He got his little brother under his thumb.
words.ex_cn: 他让弟弟听他的话。
words.en: To have someone completely under one's control or influence.

words.tr: 短语动词. 使某事被某人理解；把某事清楚地传达给某人
words.ex: He tried to get his idea across to the class.
words.ex_cn: 他试图让全班理解他的想法。
words.en: To successfully communicate an idea or message to someone.

words.tr: phrase. v. 使某事被理解；清楚地传达某事
words.ex: He tried to get his idea across to the class.
words.ex_cn: 他试图向全班传达他的想法。
words.en: To successfully communicate an idea or piece of information to someone, especially in a way that is clear and understandable.

words.tr: 短语动词. 把心里的烦恼或秘密说出来，以减轻心理负担；倾诉
words.ex: He talked to his friend to get the worry off his chest.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友倾诉，把心中的担忧说出来。
words.en: To talk about something that has been worrying you for a long time so that you feel less anxious.

words.tr: 短语动词. 把心里的话说出来；倾诉心中的烦恼或不满
words.ex: He has something off his chest and wants to tell his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他心里有件事想说出来，想告诉他的朋友。
words.en: To confess or talk about something that has been worrying you or making you feel guilty.

words.tr: phrase. v. 使某事开始成功；使某项目启动
words.ex: They want to get their business off the ground.
words.ex_cn: 他们想让他们的生意起步。
words.en: To get something off the ground means to start a project or venture successfully.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 成功摆脱（负担、责任等）；把某物从某处取下；（尤指通过表达而）释放心中的情绪
words.ex: I need to get this letter off today.
words.ex_cn: 我需要今天把这封信寄出去。
words.en: To remove something from a surface or to start a journey.

words.w: get sth. out in the open
words.tr: 短语动词. 把某事公开化，坦率地谈出隐藏的问题或情感
words.uk: ɡet ˈsʌmθɪŋ aʊt ɪn ði ˈəʊpən
words.us: ɡet ˈsʌmθɪŋ aʊt ɪn ði ˈoʊpən
words.ex: He finally got the truth out in the open.
words.ex_cn: 他终于把真相公之于众。
words.en: To make something known to the public or to a group of people, especially something that was previously hidden or kept secret.

words.w: get sth. out of one's system
words.tr: phrase. v. 通过做某事来彻底释放或排解内心的某种情绪或冲动，从而不再受其困扰
words.uk: ɡet ˈsʌmθɪŋ aʊt əv wʌnz ˈsɪstəm
words.us: ɡet ˈsʌmθɪŋ aʊt əv wʌnz ˈsɪstəm
words.ex: He ran five miles to get the stress out of his system.
words.ex_cn: 他跑了五英里，把压力释放掉。
words.en: To rid oneself of a strong emotion or desire, typically by expressing it in some way.

words.tr: 短语动词. 从某物中获得某物；从某事中获益或提取出有价值的东西
words.ex: I get a lot of good ideas out of reading books.
words.ex_cn: 我从读书中得到了很多好想法。
words.en: To obtain or derive something from something else, often implying effort or a process to achieve the desired result.

words.tr: 短语动词. 把某事弄清楚；明确某事；澄清误解
words.ex: Let me get one thing straight: I did not break the window.
words.ex_cn: 让我把一件事说清楚：我没有打破窗户。
words.en: To make sure that one understands something correctly or that something is clearly understood.

words.tr: 短语动词. 把某事说清楚；明确表态
words.ex: I want to have something straight: this is my book, not yours.
words.ex_cn: 我要说清楚一点：这是我的书，不是你的。
words.en: To understand something clearly and correctly, often after confusion.

words.w: get something through one's thick skull
words.tr: phrase. 终于让某人明白某事（尤指经过多次解释）；使某人意识到
words.uk: ɡet ˈsʌmθɪŋ θruː wʌnz θrɪk skʌl
words.us: ɡet ˈsʌmθɪŋ θruː wʌnz θrɪk skʌl
words.ex: He finally got it through his thick skull that he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他终于意识到自己考试没及格。
words.en: To make someone understand something, especially something that is difficult to understand.

words.w: get sth. into one's thick head
words.tr: phrase. 让某人终于明白某事（尤指经过反复解释）；使某人理解（常含不耐烦语气）
words.uk: ɡet ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈɪntuː wʌnz θɪk hed
words.us: ɡet ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈɪntuː wʌnz θɪk hɛd
words.ex: I tried to get the idea into his thick head, but he still didn't understand.
words.ex_cn: 我试图让他明白这个想法，但他还是不懂。
words.en: To make someone understand something, especially something that is difficult to understand or accept.

words.tr: 短语动词。开始进行；启动（通常指活动、计划或旅程等）
words.ex: The project will get underway next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目下周一将正式启动。
words.en: If a process or event gets underway, it begins.

words.tr: adj. 正在进行中的；航行中的；
words.ex: The project is underway.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: If something is underway, it is happening now.

words.tr: 短语动词. 得到新鲜空气；外出透气
words.ex: Let's open the window to get the air fresh.
words.ex_cn: 让我们打开窗户，让空气变得新鲜。
words.en: To be dismissed or fired from a job.

words.tr: phrase. 启动；开始
words.ex: Let's get the ball rolling on this project.
words.ex_cn: 让我们开始这个项目的规划。
words.en: To start something, especially something that involves a group of people.

words.tr: 短语动词. 使事情开始进行；让进程启动
words.ex: Let's have the ball rolling by starting the meeting now.
words.ex_cn: 让我们现在开始会议，把事情推动起来。
words.en: To start something, especially a process or activity.

words.tr: phrase. 开始某事；启动进程；使事情运转起来
words.ex: He made the first call to set the ball rolling.
words.ex_cn: 他打了第一个电话来启动这件事。
words.en: To start something happening or to initiate an activity.

words.tr: phrase. 开始某事；启动某个过程或活动
words.ex: He started the ball rolling by asking the first question.
words.ex_cn: 他通过第一个问题开启了讨论。
words.en: To start the ball rolling means to begin an activity or process.

words.tr: 短语动词. 战胜某人；占上风；使某人处于劣势
words.ex: The stress got the better of him.
words.ex_cn: 压力战胜了他。
words.en: To defeat or gain an advantage over someone in a competition, argument, or struggle.

words.tr: 短语动词. 在与某人的竞争或对抗中占据上风；胜过某人
words.ex: He have the better of his brother in math.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上比他弟弟强。
words.en: To defeat someone in a competition or argument.

words.tr: 短语动词. 战胜某人；在竞争中胜过某人；使某人处于下风
words.ex: He always gets the best of his little brother in games.
words.ex_cn: 他在游戏中总是胜过他的弟弟。
words.en: To gain an advantage over someone; to defeat or overcome someone in a competition or conflict.

words.tr: phrase. 感到忧郁或悲伤；情绪低落
words.ex: He gets the blues when it rains.
words.ex_cn: 天下雨时，他就会感到忧郁。
words.en: To feel sad or depressed.

words.tr: phrase. 感到忧郁或悲伤；情绪低落
words.ex: He has the blues because his friend left.
words.ex_cn: 他感到忧郁，因为他的朋友离开了。
words.en: To feel sad or depressed.

words.tr: phrase. 被解雇；被赶走
words.ex: He got the boot from his job because he was always late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为总是迟到而被解雇了。
words.en: To be dismissed from employment.

words.tr: phrase. v. 冷遇某人；受到冷淡对待
words.ex: He got the cold shoulder when he came to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他到派对时受到了冷遇。
words.en: To be treated in an unfriendly way and ignored by someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 请一天假；休息一天
words.ex: He got a day off because he was sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病休了一天假。
words.en: To take a day off from work or other obligations to rest or attend to personal matters.

words.tr: 短语动词. 请一天假；休息一天
words.ex: He got the day off because he was sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病而请了一天假。
words.en: To take a day off from work or school, typically for rest or personal reasons.

words.tr: phrase. 休假一天
words.ex: I have a day off tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天放假。
words.en: To take a day off from work or other duties to rest or do something else.

words.tr: 短语动词. 请一天假；休息一天
words.ex: I have the day off tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天放假。
words.en: To take a day off from work or school, usually for rest or personal matters.

words.tr: 短语动词. 激怒某人；惹恼某人；使某人发疯
words.ex: He will get the devil if he breaks the rules again.
words.ex_cn: 如果他再违反规则，他会受到严厉惩罚。
words.en: To be severely scolded or punished.

words.tr: 短语动词. 捉住魔鬼；常用于口语中表示惹上大麻烦或受到严厉惩罚
words.ex: He tries to catch the devil in the story.
words.ex_cn: 他在故事中试图抓住魔鬼。
words.en: To be severely scolded or to get into big trouble.

words.tr: v. 得到；获得；使；变得；收到；
words.ex: I got a new book from the library.
words.ex_cn: 我从图书馆得到了一本新书。
words.en: To come into possession of something; to receive or be given something.

words.tr: phrase. 遭受严厉批评或惩罚；惹上大麻烦
words.ex: He will catch hell for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因为违反规则会遭到严厉责骂。
words.en: To receive severe criticism or punishment.

words.tr: 短语动词. 熟悉某事物的感觉；体会某事物的特性
words.ex: She needs to get the feel of the new job before she can perform well.
words.ex_cn: 她需要先熟悉这份新工作，才能表现出色。
words.en: To begin to understand or become familiar with something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 具有某种感觉或氛围；让人感觉到某事物的存在或特质
words.ex: The room has the feel of a cozy home.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有家的温馨感觉。
words.en: To give the impression or sensation of being a particular thing.

words.tr: 短语动词。获得发言权；站起来讲话（尤指在会议或辩论中）
words.ex: He wants to get the floor to speak.
words.ex_cn: 他想发言。
words.en: To be given the opportunity to speak in a discussion or meeting.

words.tr: 短语动词. 受到热情接待；被友好地对待（通常带有虚伪或敷衍的意味）
words.ex: He got the glad hand from the boss after finishing the project.
words.ex_cn: 他完成项目后得到了老板的热情接待。
words.en: To be given an enthusiastic but often insincere welcome.

words.tr: phrase. 得到许可；获得批准（去做某事）
words.ex: We got the go-ahead to start the project yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨天得到了开始项目的批准。
words.en: If you get the go-ahead for something, you receive permission to start doing it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 获得批准；被允许进行某事
words.ex: The project got the green light from the manager.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目得到了经理的批准。
words.en: To receive permission or approval to proceed with a plan or action.

words.tr: phrase. 掌握某事的窍门；熟悉某事的做法
words.ex: It took her a few weeks to get the hang of driving a manual car.
words.ex_cn: 她花了几个星期才掌握了手动挡汽车的驾驶技巧。
words.en: To learn how to do something well or to become familiar with how something works.

words.tr: 短语动词. 掌握某事的诀窍；熟悉某事的做法
words.ex: After a few lessons, she finally had the hang of skiing.
words.ex_cn: 经过几节课后，她终于掌握了滑雪的技巧。
words.en: To understand how to do something or use something after a period of learning or practice.

words.tr: phrase. 强行推销
words.ex: The car salesman used a hard sell approach to close the deal.
words.ex_cn: 汽车销售员采用了强力推销的方法来达成交易。
words.en: A hard sell is a method of selling in which the seller is very forceful and persistent in trying to persuade someone to buy something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 获得内部消息或优势；比别人更早或更详细地了解情况
words.ex: He got the inside track on the new job by talking to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他通过和朋友交谈，获得了这份新工作的内部消息。
words.en: To gain an advantage over others, especially through special information or connections.

words.tr: phrase. 占有内部消息或优势；处于有利地位；比别人更了解内情
words.ex: He has the inside track to get the job because he knows the manager.
words.ex_cn: 他有内部消息，可能得到这份工作，因为他认识经理。
words.en: To have an advantage or special information that makes success more likely.

words.tr: phrase. 最终获得胜利或报复成功，让先前嘲笑自己的人无话可说；最后笑的人才是笑得最好的
words.ex: He was laughed at in school, but now he gets the last laugh with his successful company.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校时被人嘲笑，但现在他靠着成功的公司笑到了最后。
words.en: To ultimately succeed or be proven right after a period of difficulty or doubt.

words.tr: 短语动词. 最后笑的人笑得最好；指最终取得胜利或成功，尤其是在别人曾嘲笑或怀疑之后
words.ex: He laughed at my idea, but I will have the last laugh when it succeeds.
words.ex_cn: 他嘲笑我的想法，但当它成功时，我将笑到最后。
words.en: To ultimately prove successful or correct after a period of doubt or criticism.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人抢先一步；先发制人；在某人之前采取行动
words.ex: If you can get the jump on your competitors, you'll have a better chance of success.
words.ex_cn: 如果你能抢在竞争对手之前行动，你就有更大的成功机会。
words.en: To gain an advantage over someone by acting before they do.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人抢先一步；占据优势；比别人更快采取行动
words.ex: By arriving early, we had the jump on the other companies that were bidding for the contract.
words.ex_cn: 由于我们早到，我们比其他竞标合同的公司占了优势。
words.en: To have an advantage over someone by acting before they do.

words.tr: 短语动词. 争得最后发言权；在争论中最后取胜
words.ex: He always gets the last word in arguments.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中总是最后发言。
words.en: To make the final, decisive remark in an argument or discussion.

words.tr: phrase. 强辩到底；说出最终意见；最后决定
words.ex: In the heated debate, she always manages to have the last word.
words.ex_cn: 在激烈的辩论中，她总能说出最后一句话。
words.en: To be the person who makes the final decision or gives the final opinion in a discussion or argument.

words.tr: 短语动词. 得到最后发言权；在争论中最后说了算
words.ex: He always wants to get the final word in every argument.
words.ex_cn: 他总想在每次争论中说最后一句话。
words.en: To make the final, decisive remark in an argument or discussion.

words.tr: 短语动词. 拥有最后发言权；做出最终决定
words.ex: In the end, the manager will have the final word on the decision.
words.ex_cn: 最后，经理将对这个决定有最终发言权。
words.en: To have the final word means to have the ultimate authority to decide or conclude something.

words.tr: phrase. 得到许可；被选中
words.ex: He got the nod for the job after the interview.
words.ex_cn: 面试后他得到了这份工作。
words.en: To receive approval or permission to do something.

words.tr: phrase. 占优势；获得认可；被选中
words.ex: He has the nod for the job because he is experienced.
words.ex_cn: 他因为有经验而得到了这份工作的优先考虑。
words.en: To receive approval or consent, often in a formal or official context.

words.tr: phrase. 明白情况；理解意思
words.ex: Do you get the picture now?
words.ex_cn: 你现在明白了吗？
words.en: To understand or comprehend the situation or what is being communicated.

words.tr: 短语. 受到隆重的欢迎或特别优待，享受贵宾待遇
words.ex: The movie star gets the red carpet treatment at the film festival.
words.ex_cn: 这位电影明星在电影节上受到了隆重的接待。
words.en: To be treated with great hospitality and luxury, as if one were a very important guest.

words.tr: phrase. v. 被敷衍；被支来支去；得不到明确答复
words.ex: He called the office three times but just got the runaround.
words.ex_cn: 他给办公室打了三次电话，但每次都被人敷衍。
words.en: To be given the runaround, i.e., to be kept waiting or sent from person to person without getting a direct answer or help.

words.tr: phrase. 被解雇；被开除
words.ex: He got the sack because he was always late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为总是迟到而被解雇了。
words.en: If you get the sack, you are dismissed from your job.

words.tr: phrase. 被解雇；被开除；被辞退
words.ex: He got the ax because he was late every day.
words.ex_cn: 他因为每天迟到而被解雇了。
words.en: To be dismissed from employment, especially suddenly or unexpectedly.

words.w: get a load off one's mind
words.tr: 短语动词. 把心事说出来以减轻心理负担；倾诉以释放心中的压力
words.uk: ɡet ə ləʊd ɒf wʌnz maɪnd
words.us: ɡet ə loʊd ɔːf wʌnz maɪnd
words.ex: He told his friend about his problems to get a load off his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他把问题告诉朋友，以减轻心里的负担。
words.en: To relieve one's worries or anxieties; to feel less stressed or burdened after sharing or resolving a concern.

words.w: get the short end of the stick
words.tr: phrase. 吃亏；处于不利地位；得到较差的待遇
words.uk: /ɡet ðə ʃɔːt end əv ðə stɪk/
words.us: /ɡɛt ðə ʃɔrt ɛnd əv ðə stɪk/
words.ex: In the negotiation, she always seemed to get the short end of the stick.
words.ex_cn: 在谈判中，她似乎总是吃亏。
words.en: To receive less or suffer more than others in a particular situation.

words.w: have the short end of the stick
words.tr: phrase. 处于不利地位；吃大亏；得到较差的一方
words.uk: /hæv ðə ʃɔːt ɛnd ɒv ðə stɪk/
words.us: /hæv ðə ʃɔrt ɛnd ʌv ðə stɪk/
words.ex: He always has the short end of the stick in the family, getting the old clothes and hand-me-down toys.
words.ex_cn: 他在家里总是吃亏，只能穿旧衣服和玩别人用过的玩具。
words.en: To be in a less advantageous position or to receive less than one is due in a situation.

words.w: end up with the short end of the stick
words.tr: phrase. 最终吃亏；处于不利地位；得到较差的结果
words.uk: /end ʌp wɪð ðə ʃɔːt end ɒv ðə stɪk/
words.us: /end ʌp wɪð ðə ʃɔːrt end ʌv ðə stɪk/
words.ex: He worked hard but ended up with the short end of the stick.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，但最后却吃了亏。
words.en: To be in a less advantageous position or to receive less benefit than others in a situation.

words.w: get the show on the road
words.tr: phrase. 开始行动；启动计划；让事情运转起来
words.uk: ɡet ðə ʃəʊ ɒn ðə rəʊd
words.us: ɡet ðə ʃoʊ ɑːn ðə roʊd
words.ex: Let's get the show on the road and start the project.
words.ex_cn: 让我们开始行动，启动这个项目。
words.en: To start doing something or to begin a journey.

words.tr: 短语动词. 受到严厉的审问或盘问
words.ex: He got the third degree from his parents when he came home late.
words.ex_cn: 他回家晚了，被父母严厉盘问了一番。
words.en: To be interrogated intensely or harshly, especially by police or in a formal setting.

words.w: get the upper hand on sb.
words.tr: 短语动词. 在某人之上占优势；战胜某人；取得对某人的控制权
words.uk: ɡet ði ˈʌpə hænd ɒn sʌmbədi
words.us: ɡet ði ˈʌpər hænd ɑn ˈsʌmbədi
words.ex: By staying calm, she managed to get the upper hand on her opponent in the negotiation.
words.ex_cn: 通过保持冷静，她在谈判中成功地胜过了对手。
words.en: To gain control or an advantage over someone.

words.w: have the upper hand on sb.
words.tr: 短语动词. 在某人之上占优势；对某人处于有利地位
words.uk: hæv ði ˈʌpə hænd ɒn səmˈbədi
words.us: hæv ði ˈʌpər hænd ɑn ˈsʌmˌbɑdi
words.ex: By using his negotiation skills, he managed to have the upper hand on his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 通过运用他的谈判技巧，他成功地对对手占了上风。
words.en: To have an advantage or more control in a situation than someone else.

words.tr: 短语动词. 占上风；取得优势
words.ex: By studying the opponent's strategies, they managed to get the upper hand in the negotiations.
words.ex_cn: 通过研究对手的策略，他们在谈判中获得了优势。
words.en: To gain a position of advantage or control over someone or something.

words.tr: v. 有；得到；吃；
words.ex: I have a book.
words.ex_cn: 我有一本书。
words.en: To possess, own, or hold something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 理解暗示或言外之意；明白某事的含义或意图
words.ex: He got the message when his friend stopped talking.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友不再说话时，他明白了意思。
words.en: To understand an implicit warning or hint; to realize what is being suggested without explicit words.

words.tr: phrase. 通过；（电话）打通；度过；做完；用完
words.ex: He got through the exam with help from his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在朋友的帮助下通过了考试。
words.en: To succeed in reaching a place or a stage in a process, or to make someone understand or accept something.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 使某人理解；与某人取得联系；让信息被某人接受
words.ex: I tried to explain the situation, but I just couldn't get through to her.
words.ex_cn: 我试图解释情况，但我就是无法让她理解。
words.en: If you get through to someone, you succeed in making them understand something that you are trying to tell them.

words.tr: phrase. v. 完成某事；结束某事；把某事处理完
words.ex: I finally got through with all my homework.
words.ex_cn: 我终于完成了所有的家庭作业。
words.en: To complete or finish something, especially something that is difficult or takes a long time.

words.tr: 短语动词. 为……腾出时间；设法抽出时间做某事
words.ex: I need to get time for a vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我需要抽出时间去度假。
words.en: To find or make time to do something.

words.tr: 短语动词，有时间做某事；愿意花时间处理或关注某人或某事
words.ex: Do you have time for a quick meeting?
words.ex_cn: 你有时间开个短会吗？
words.en: If you have time for something, you are willing to spend time doing it or thinking about it.

words.tr: phrase. 找时间做某事；抽出时间做某事
words.ex: I cannot find time for exercise every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天找不到时间锻炼。
words.en: To make time available in one's schedule for a particular activity or person.

words.tr: 短语动词. 请到假；获得休息时间；获准休假
words.ex: He wants to get time off next week.
words.ex_cn: 他想下周请假。
words.en: To be granted a period of leave from work or other obligations.

words.tr: 短语动词. 有空闲时间；休假；休息
words.ex: I will have time off next week to visit my family.
words.ex_cn: phrase. 我下周将休假去看望我的家人。
words.en: To take a period of time away from work or duty, typically for rest or recreation.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 站起来；恢复过来（尤指经历困难后重新振作）
words.ex: After the fall, he tried to get to his feet.
words.ex_cn: 摔倒后，他试图站起来。
words.en: To stand up, especially after sitting or lying down.

words.w: get to the bottom of sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 彻底查清楚某事；查明某事的真相
words.uk: ɡet tə ðə ˈbɒtəm əv stəʊ
words.us: ɡɛt tə ðə ˈbɑtəm əv stoʊ
words.ex: The detective was determined to get to the bottom of the mystery.
words.ex_cn: 侦探决心要彻底查明这个谜团。
words.en: To discover the real but sometimes hidden reason why something happens.

words.w: get time to catch one's breath
words.tr: 短语动词. 有时间喘口气；有片刻休息
words.uk: ɡet taɪm tə kætʃ wʌnz breθ
words.us: ɡet taɪm tə kætʃ wʌnz breθ
words.ex: After the race, he finally got time to catch his breath.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于有时间喘口气了。
words.en: To have a brief pause to rest and recover one's energy or composure.

words.w: have time to catch one's breath
words.tr: 短语动词. 有时间喘口气；有片刻休息或放松的机会
words.uk: hæv taɪm tə kætʃ wʌnz breθ
words.us: hæv taɪm tə kætʃ wʌnz breθ
words.ex: After running, I need a moment to have time to catch my breath.
words.ex_cn: 跑完步后，我需要一点时间喘口气。
words.en: To have a moment to rest or recover, especially after a period of intense activity.

words.w: get to the heart of the matter
words.tr: phrase. 抓住问题的核心/实质
words.uk: ɡet tuː ðə hɑːt əv ðə ˈmætə(r)
words.us: ɡet tuː ðə hɑːrt əv ðə ˈmætər
words.ex: Let's get to the heart of the matter and discuss the main issue.
words.ex_cn: 让我们直截了当地讨论主要问题。
words.en: To understand or deal with the most important part of a problem or issue.

words.w: get at the heart of the matter
words.tr: 短语动词. 触及问题的实质；抓住问题的核心
words.uk: ɡet æt ðə hɑːt əv ðə ˈmætə(r)
words.us: ɡet æt ðə hɑrt əv ðə ˈmætər
words.ex: By asking the right questions, she was able to get at the heart of the matter.
words.ex_cn: 通过问对问题，她能够触及问题的核心。
words.en: To reach the most important or central part of an issue or problem.

words.tr: phrase. 聚会；聚集
words.ex: We get together every weekend to play basketball.
words.ex_cn: 我们每周末聚在一起打篮球。
words.en: If people get together, they meet in order to spend time with each other.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某人采取强硬态度；对某人严厉起来
words.ex: The manager decided to get tough with the employees who were consistently late.
words.ex_cn: 经理决定对那些经常迟到的员工采取强硬态度。
words.en: To adopt a strict or severe attitude towards someone, often in order to make them behave better.

words.tr: 短语动词. 变得强硬起来；采取严厉措施
words.ex: When negotiations stalled, the government decided to get tough.
words.ex_cn: 当谈判陷入僵局时，政府决定采取强硬措施。
words.en: To become strict or severe in dealing with a situation or people.

words.tr: phrase. 惹恼某人；使某人烦躁不安；对某人产生强烈影响（通常指负面情绪）
words.ex: His rude words really get under my skin.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话真的让我很不舒服。
words.en: To irritate or annoy someone.

words.w: get up enough nerve to do sth.
words.tr: phrase. 鼓起足够的勇气做某事
words.uk: ɡet ʌp ɪˈnʌf nɜː(r) tuː duː ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡet ʌp ɪˈnʌf nɜːr tuː duː ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: She finally got up enough nerve to ask her boss for a raise.
words.ex_cn: 她终于鼓起勇气向老板要求加薪。
words.en: To gather enough courage to do something that one is afraid or hesitant to do.

words.tr: phrase. 鼓起足够的勇气；下定决心做某事
words.ex: He could not get up enough nerve to speak in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他没能鼓起足够的勇气在全班面前讲话。
words.en: To summon the courage needed to do something difficult or frightening.

words.tr: 短语动词. 痊愈；恢复健康
words.ex: I hope you get well soon.
words.ex_cn: 我希望你早日康复。
words.en: To recover from an illness or injury.

words.tr: phrase. 得到某人应得的（通常指报应或惩罚）
words.ex: He lied to everyone, so he will get what's coming to him.
words.ex_cn: 他对每个人都撒了谎，所以他将得到应有的报应。
words.en: To receive the outcome, especially punishment, that one deserves.

words.tr: phrase. v. 听说某事；得知某事的风声
words.ex: He managed to get wind of the secret meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他设法听到了这次秘密会议的风声。
words.en: To hear or learn about something secret or private.

words.tr: phrase. 对某事感到激动、焦虑或生气
words.ex: She got worked up over the smallest details.
words.ex_cn: 她对最小的细节都感到非常激动。
words.en: To become very excited or upset about something.

words.tr: phrase. 对…激动；特别生气；不开心
words.ex: She tends to get worked up over small issues.
words.ex_cn: 她往往会因为小事而变得激动。
words.en: To become very upset, angry, or excited about something.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词GET补充词组

words.tr: 短语动词. 举行盛大的欢送仪式；隆重地送别
words.ex: The team will get a big send-off from the fans before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 球队在出发前会得到球迷们的热烈欢送。
words.en: To receive an elaborate farewell celebration or send-off, often for someone leaving a job or place.

words.tr: n. 送行，送别
words.ex: We gave him a big send-off at the train station.
words.ex_cn: 我们在火车站为他举行了盛大的送别。
words.en: A send-off is a party or other occasion when people come together to say goodbye to someone who is leaving.

words.tr: 短语动词. 得到腿抽筋；腿部肌肉突然痉挛
words.ex: He gets a charley horse when he runs too fast.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得太快时会抽筋。
words.en: To experience a painful muscle cramp, typically in the calf or thigh.

words.tr: phrase. 得到腿抽筋（通常指小腿肌肉突然痉挛）
words.ex: He had a charley horse in his leg during the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛时腿抽筋了。
words.en: To experience a sudden, involuntary muscle cramp, typically in the leg.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人产生短暂的爱慕或暗恋之情
words.ex: She got a crush on her new teacher.
words.ex_cn: 她对新来的老师产生了好感。
words.en: To develop a romantic infatuation or strong liking for someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某人有好感；暗恋某人
words.ex: She had a crush on her English teacher in high school.
words.ex_cn: 她在高中时对她的英语老师有好感。
words.en: To have a romantic infatuation with someone, especially without knowing them very well.

words.tr: 短语动词. 确定某事物的位置或性质；对某事有清晰的了解或控制
words.ex: The satellite was able to get a fix on the missing plane.
words.ex_cn: 卫星能够确定失踪飞机的位置。
words.en: To determine the exact position or location of something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事有明确的掌握或定位；了解某事的确切情况或位置
words.ex: The police have a fix on the suspect's location.
words.ex_cn: 警方已经确定了嫌疑人的位置。
words.en: To have a clear understanding or precise location of something.

words.tr: phrase. 遭受严厉对待；被苛责；受苦
words.ex: He gets a hard time from his classmates because he is new.
words.ex_cn: 他因为是新来的，所以受到同学的为难。
words.en: To be treated severely or to face difficulties.

words.tr: phrase. 遭遇困难；经历艰难的时光
words.ex: I have a hard time understanding this chapter.
words.ex_cn: v. 我在理解这一章时遇到了困难。
words.en: To experience difficulty or struggle with something.

words.tr: phrase. 被打一顿；遭到痛击；受到严厉批评
words.ex: He got a licking for breaking the window.
words.ex_cn: 他因为打破了窗户而被打了一顿。
words.en: To receive severe criticism or punishment.

words.tr: phrase. 承受打击；遭受严厉批评或挫折（常用于口语，原义为‘被打’，引申为‘经受困难或失败’）
words.ex: The boxer took a licking but still smiled.
words.ex_cn: 那个拳击手挨了一顿打，但仍然微笑着。
words.en: To suffer a defeat or loss, often used in the context of sports or financial markets.

words.tr: 短语动词. 过一种更充实或有意义的生活；常用于讽刺或劝告别人不要过于沉迷琐事或过于严肃
words.ex: Stop complaining all the time and get a life!
words.ex_cn: 别再总是抱怨了，过有意义的生活吧！
words.en: An expression used to tell someone to stop being boring or to start doing something more interesting or valuable.

words.tr: 短语动词. 脸红；感到羞愧或尴尬而面部发红
words.ex: He gets a red face when he is embarrassed.
words.ex_cn: 他感到尴尬时会脸红。
words.en: To become red in the face, typically as a result of embarrassment, shame, or physical exertion.

words.tr: 短语动词. 脸红；面红耳赤（通常由于尴尬、羞愧或生气）
words.ex: He has a red face because he is shy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为害羞而脸红。
words.en: To feel embarrassed or ashamed, often resulting in a visible blush.

words.tr: n. 殴打；彻底击败
words.ex: The team took a shellacking in the final game.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在决赛中遭到了彻底的失败。
words.en: A severe defeat or criticism.

words.tr: phrase. 遭受惨败；被痛打；被严厉批评
words.ex: The team will take a shellacking in the game.
words.ex_cn: 这支球队会在比赛中惨败。
words.en: To suffer a severe defeat or criticism.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始；获得起步机会
words.ex: She managed to get a start on her project despite the difficulties.
words.ex_cn: 尽管困难重重，她还是成功地开始了她的项目。
words.en: To begin something; to initiate an action or process.

words.tr: 短语动词。开始；着手；起步
words.ex: We have a start at 8 a.m. tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天早上8点开始。
words.en: To be startled or surprised by something unexpected.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 超过，领先于；在……之前采取行动
words.ex: By starting early, she managed to get ahead of her competitors.
words.ex_cn: 通过提前开始，她成功地超越了她的竞争对手。
words.en: To surpass someone in achievement, progress, or advantage; to be in a leading position.

words.tr: phrase. v. 取得成功；进步；超越他人
words.ex: He works hard to get ahead in his job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以在工作中取得进步。
words.en: To make progress or become successful in one's career or life.

words.tr: phrase. 相处
words.ex: They get along well with each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们相处得很好。
words.en: If people get along, they like each other and are friendly to each other.

words.tr: phrase. 年纪渐长；上了岁数
words.ex: My grandfather is getting along in years and needs more rest.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖父年纪大了，需要更多的休息。
words.en: To grow older; to age.

words.tr: phrase. v. 最终找到时间做某事；抽空做某事
words.ex: I finally got around to cleaning the garage last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我终于在上周末抽出时间清理了车库。
words.en: If you get around to doing something that you have delayed doing or have been too busy to do, you finally manage to do it.

words.tr: phrase. v. 逃离；摆脱；离开
words.ex: He wants to get away from the noisy city.
words.ex_cn: 他想逃离喧闹的城市。
words.en: To escape from a place or a situation.

words.tr: phrase. 逃脱；离开；度假
words.ex: The thief tried to get away from the police.
words.ex_cn: 小偷试图逃脱警察。
words.en: If you get away, you succeed in leaving a place or a person's company. If you get away with something, you succeed in doing it without being caught or punished.

words.tr: phrase. v. 报复某人；对某人进行反击
words.ex: He decided to get back at his boss for the unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他决定报复老板的不公平对待。
words.en: To take revenge on someone for something they have done to you.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人彻底摊牌；与某人把事情说清楚或激烈地争论
words.ex: They decided to have it out with each other after months of unresolved tension.
words.ex_cn: 经过几个月的未解紧张关系后，他们决定彻底解决彼此之间的问题。
words.en: To discuss a problem or disagreement with someone in order to resolve it.

words.tr: phrase. 回来；取回；恢复；报复
words.ex: He will get back tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会回来。
words.en: To return to a place, condition, or activity; to recover something lost or taken away; to retaliate.

words.tr: phrase. 开始忙起来；投入工作；忙碌起来
words.ex: After the break, it's time to get busy.
words.ex_cn: 休息之后，是时候开始工作了。
words.en: To start doing something with a lot of energy and effort.

words.tr: phrase. 凭某物勉强维持生活或应付过去
words.ex: He manages to get by on a small salary.
words.ex_cn: 他靠微薄的薪水勉强过活。
words.en: To manage to live or do something with the limited money, resources, etc. that you have.

words.tr: phrase. v. 度过难关；勉强应付；勉强维持生活
words.ex: He gets by with little money.
words.ex_cn: 他靠很少的钱维持生活。
words.en: To manage to live or do a particular thing using the money, knowledge, equipment, etc. that you have.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始认真工作；赶快行动；立即着手做某事
words.ex: We need to get cracking on this project if we want to meet the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 如果我们想赶上截止日期，我们需要立即开始这个项目。
words.en: To start doing something quickly and with energy.

words.tr: phrase. 打扮得漂亮；精心装扮
words.ex: She gets dolled up for the party every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 她每周末都会打扮得漂漂亮亮去参加派对。
words.en: To dress up smartly or elaborately, especially for a special occasion.

words.tr: phrase. 精心打扮，盛装打扮（通常指为了特殊场合而穿得漂亮）
words.ex: She gets all dolled up for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对精心打扮。
words.en: To make oneself look very attractive, especially by putting on nice clothes and makeup.

words.tr: phrase. 开始认真处理某事；着手做某事
words.ex: He got down to his homework after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后开始做作业。
words.en: If you get down to something, especially something that requires a lot of attention, you begin doing it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始认真讨论或处理事实；不再绕弯子，直奔主题
words.ex: It's time to get down to the facts and solve this problem.
words.ex_cn: 是时候认真处理这个问题并解决了。
words.en: To begin to deal with something in a serious and determined way.

words.tr: phrase. v. 向某人报复；向某人讨回公道
words.ex: He swore he would get even with the person who betrayed him.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓要向背叛他的人报复。
words.en: To take revenge on someone for something they have done to you.

words.tr: phrase. v. 报复；扯平；一报还一报
words.ex: He wanted to get even after being treated unfairly.
words.ex_cn: 在被不公平对待后，他想报复。
words.en: To take revenge or retaliate against someone.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人无礼或轻薄；对某人过分亲昵或放肆
words.ex: He was warned not to get fresh with the ladies at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他被警告不要在派对上对女士们无礼。
words.en: To behave disrespectfully or inappropriately towards someone.

words.tr: adj. 新鲜的；新的；刚发生的；
words.ex: She bought fresh apples from the market.
words.ex_cn: 她从市场买了新鲜的苹果。
words.en: Fresh food has been picked or produced recently, and has not been preserved, for example by being frozen or put in a tin.

words.tr: phrase. 参与某事；加入某事；分享某事的机会或利益
words.ex: He managed to get in on the deal at the last minute.
words.ex_cn: 他在最后一刻设法参与了这笔交易。
words.en: To become involved in or take part in an activity or opportunity.

words.tr: 短语动词，参与某事；了解某事的内情
words.ex: She was in on the secret from the beginning.
words.ex_cn: 她从一开始就知情。
words.en: To be involved in or aware of something, especially something secret or planned.

words.w: get into an argument with sb
words.tr: 短语动词. 与某人发生争执；和某人争吵
words.uk: ɡet ˈɪntuː ən ˈɑːɡjʊmənt wɪð sʌmbədi
words.us: ɡet ˈɪntu ən ˈɑːɡjəmənt wɪð ˈsʌmbɑːdi
words.ex: He got into an argument with his friend about the homework.
words.ex_cn: 他因为作业和朋友发生了争吵。
words.en: To become involved in a disagreement or dispute with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 参与；卷入；与……有牵连
words.ex: He wants to get involved with the school club.
words.ex_cn: 他想加入学校的俱乐部。
words.en: To become associated with someone or something in a way that requires time, effort, or attention.

words.tr: 短语动词. 参与其中；卷入；介入
words.ex: He got involved in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他参加了学校的戏剧表演。
words.en: To become connected or concerned with something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. v. 使一切恢复正常；整理好自己的生活或情绪；变得有条理
words.ex: She finally managed to get it all together after weeks of chaos.
words.ex_cn: 在几周的混乱之后，她终于把一切都整理好了。
words.en: To organize one's thoughts or life; to become calm and able to deal with things effectively.

words.tr: phrase. 形容一个人生活井然有序，做事有条理，各方面都处理得很成功
words.ex: He seems to have it all together at work and at home.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作和家庭方面似乎都处理得很好。
words.en: To be in complete control of one's life or situation, with everything organized and functioning well.

words.tr: phrase. v. 振作起来；使自己镇定；整理好状态
words.ex: You need to get it together if you want to pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 如果你想通过考试，你需要振作起来。
words.en: To organize oneself or one's thoughts; to become composed or focused.

words.tr: phrase. 受到严厉批评或惩罚；倒霉；遭殃
words.ex: He was late again and got it in the neck from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他又迟到了，结果被老板狠狠批评了一顿。
words.en: To receive severe punishment or criticism.

words.tr: phrase. 对……生气，对……发怒
words.ex: Don't get mad at me for telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为我讲真话而对我生气。
words.en: To become angry with someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 变得生气；发怒
words.ex: He gets mad when he sees people littering.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到人们乱扔垃圾时，他会生气。
words.en: To become very angry or lose one's temper.

words.tr: phrase. 别胡说！别开玩笑了！（用于表示不耐烦或不相信）
words.ex: Get off it! That's not true.
words.ex_cn: 别胡说！那不是真的。
words.en: used to tell someone to stop doing something, especially because it is annoying or not true

words.tr: phrase. 进展；相处；上车
words.ex: How is your project getting on?
words.ex_cn: 你的项目进展如何？
words.en: If you get on with someone, you have a friendly relationship with them. If you get on with something, you continue doing it or start doing it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 尽某人最大的努力攻击或尝试；拿出某人最强的一击
words.ex: He gave the exam his best shot.
words.ex_cn: 他为考试尽了最大努力。
words.en: To try as hard as one can to achieve something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 尽力一试；全力以赴尝试做某事
words.ex: He will have his best shot at winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他会尽力赢得这场比赛。
words.en: To try as hard as one can to achieve something.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人发怒；激怒某人
words.ex: He gets his dander up when people are late.
words.ex_cn: 当别人迟到时，他就生气了。
words.en: To make someone very angry or annoyed.

words.tr: phrase. 激怒某人；使某人感到恼火或防御性
words.ex: He gets his back up when someone criticizes his work.
words.ex_cn: 当有人批评他的工作时，他就会生气。
words.en: To make someone feel angry or defensive.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人感到愤怒或激动，激起某人的敌意或防御心理
words.ex: He gets his hackles up when someone criticizes his work.
words.ex_cn: 当有人批评他的工作时，他就会生气。
words.en: To make someone very angry or annoyed.

words.tr: phrase. 变得愤怒或激动（尤指因受挫或生气）；发脾气
words.ex: He got his Irish up when he saw the dog hurt.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到狗受伤时，他激动起来。
words.en: To make someone angry or annoyed.

words.tr: phrase. adj. 愤怒的，生气的，发火的（指某人非常恼怒或激动）
words.ex: He has his dander up because someone took his seat.
words.ex_cn: 他很生气，因为有人占了他的座位。
words.en: To become angry or annoyed.

words.tr: phrase. 感到愤怒或防御性的；生气地反抗；感到被冒犯而采取对抗态度
words.ex: Don't worry, I will have your back up if someone欺负 you.
words.ex_cn: 别担心，如果有人欺负你，我会支持你。
words.en: To make someone feel angry or alert.

words.tr: phrase. adj. 毛发竖起，形容人生气或戒备的状态；感到愤怒或敌意
words.ex: He has his hackles up when someone criticizes his work.
words.ex_cn: 当有人批评他的工作时，他就会竖起羽毛，变得愤怒或防御。
words.en: To become very angry or annoyed.

words.tr: phrase. 情绪激动的；生气的；烦躁的（尤指因不满或愤怒）
words.ex: He has his Irish up because someone took his seat.
words.ex_cn: 他生气了，因为有人占了他的座位。
words.en: To become angry or lose one's temper.

words.tr: phrase. 激怒某人；使某人恼火
words.ex: It really gets my goat when people are late.
words.ex_cn: 当人们迟到时，真的让我很生气。
words.en: To make someone annoyed or angry.

words.tr: phrase. v. 充分享受；吃腻；对……感到足够
words.ex: He got his fill of pizza at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上吃够了披萨。
words.en: To experience or enjoy something to the fullest extent.

words.tr: phrase. v. 吃饱；喝足；充分体验（某事物），通常指对某事感到足够或厌倦
words.ex: He has had his fill of junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他已经吃够了垃圾食品。
words.en: To experience or enjoy something to the extent that one is satisfied or has had enough.

words.tr: phrase. v. 看透某人的意图；识破某人；摸清某人的底细
words.ex: He tried to trick me, but I got his number right away.
words.ex_cn: 他想骗我，但我立刻识破了他的把戏。
words.en: To understand someone's true character or intentions, often with the implication of being able to predict or influence their behavior.

words.tr: phrase. 完全看透某人；知道某人的底细或真实面目；了解某人的伎俩
words.ex: If you try to cheat, she will have your number.
words.ex_cn: 如果你试图作弊，她会看穿你。
words.en: To understand someone's true motives, intentions, or character, often implying that one can predict or manipulate their actions.

words.tr: 短语动词. 有机会表达自己的意见或观点
words.ex: He wanted to get his say before the meeting ended.
words.ex_cn: 他想在会议结束前发表自己的意见。
words.en: To have the opportunity to express one's opinion or views.

words.tr: 短语动词. 说出自己的意见；发表看法
words.ex: Everyone will have their say in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都会在会议上发表自己的意见。
words.en: to express one's opinion or point of view

words.tr: phrase. v. 坚持己见，强行按自己的方式行事（通常指不顾他人反对）
words.ex: He always gets his way with the teacher because he is very polite.
words.ex_cn: 他总是能如愿以偿，因为他很有礼貌。
words.en: To achieve what one wants, especially by persuading others or overcoming opposition.

words.tr: phrase. v. 完全控制某人或某事；随心所欲地对待
words.ex: He always wants to have his way with the game rules.
words.ex_cn: 他总是想按自己的方式来玩游戏规则。
words.en: To do what one wants with someone or something, often without considering the wishes or needs of others.

words.tr: 短语动词. 按照某人自己的意愿行事；达到自己的目的
words.ex: He always cries until he gets his way.
words.ex_cn: 他总是哭，直到如愿以偿。
words.en: If someone gets their way or has their way, nobody stops them from doing what they want to do.

words.tr: phrase. v. 恢复冷静；振作精神；清醒过来
words.ex: After the shock, he finally got his wits about him and called for help.
words.ex_cn: 震惊过后，他终于清醒过来，赶紧呼救。
words.en: To remain calm and think clearly, especially in a difficult or dangerous situation.

words.tr: phrase. 保持清醒；头脑灵活；随机应变
words.ex: You need to have your wits about you when crossing the street.
words.ex_cn: 过马路时你需要保持清醒和警觉。
words.en: To be alert and able to think clearly, especially in a difficult or dangerous situation.

words.tr: phrase. 出去；离开
words.ex: He told the dog to get out.
words.ex_cn: 他让狗出去。
words.en: To leave or escape from a place or situation.

words.tr: phrase. 故意绕道；特地去做某事（通常指为了帮助别人）
words.uk: ɡet aʊt ɒv wʌn z weɪ
words.us: ɡet aʊt əv wʌn z weɪ
words.ex: He gets out of his way to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他特意帮助别人。
words.en: To move aside or avoid someone or something in order to not hinder or be hindered.

words.tr: phrase. 摆脱；逃避；从…出去
words.ex: He wants to get out of debt.
words.ex_cn: 他想摆脱债务。
words.en: To leave a place or situation; to avoid doing something that you do not want to do.

words.tr: 短语动词. 准备做某事
words.ex: We get ready to go to school at 7 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 我们早上7点准备去上学。
words.en: to prepare oneself to do something

words.tr: 短语动词. 准备好做某事
words.ex: We get ready to go to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我们每天早上都准备去上学。
words.en: To prepare oneself to undertake a particular action or task.

words.tr: 短语动词. 准备好；做好准备
words.ex: She needs some time to get ready for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她需要一些时间为聚会做准备。
words.en: To prepare oneself or something for a particular purpose or event.

words.tr: phrase. 下来；吞下；弯下；写下
words.ex: He got down from the chair slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地从椅子上下来。
words.en: To move from a higher to a lower position; to write something down; to cause someone to feel sad or depressed.

words.tr: phrase. v. 把……尽快完成或处理掉，以便腾出时间或空间做其他事；把……放到一边
words.ex: He got the chair out of the way so we could walk through.
words.ex_cn: 他把椅子挪开，这样我们就能走过去了。
words.en: To remove an obstacle or complete a task so that it is no longer a concern.

words.tr: 开始；着手进行
words.ex: He turned the key to get started.
words.ex_cn: 他转动钥匙发动了引擎。
words.en: To begin doing something.

words.tr: v. 开始；创立；创始；发动（机器）；开动；出发，启程（start 的过去式和过去分词）；
words.ex: He started his homework after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后开始做作业。
words.en: If you start to do something, you do something that you were not doing before and you continue doing it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 掌握某人的把柄；获得可以用来对付某人的证据或信息
words.ex: He got some dirt on his coworker and now he has something on him.
words.ex_cn: 他掌握了同事的把柄，现在有了能制住对方的东西。
words.en: To collect or obtain information that could be used against someone, often in a competitive or adversarial context.

words.tr: 短语动词. 掌握某人的把柄；拥有能用来要挟或揭露某人的秘密信息
words.ex: He has some dirt on his boss, which gives him leverage in the company.
words.ex_cn: 他掌握了他老板的一些丑闻，这让他在这家公司有了影响力。
words.en: To possess information about someone that could be used against them, especially in a way that forces them to do something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 形容某人突然充满幻想或对某事过于乐观，通常指对成功、财富或爱情产生不切实际的憧憬
words.ex: He gets stars in his eyes when he sees a new toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到新玩具时，他就眼前一亮。
words.en: To be overly impressed or dazzled by someone or something, often leading to unrealistic expectations.

words.tr: phrase. 形容某人充满憧憬或幻想，通常指对某事过于理想化或充满浪漫的期待
words.ex: He has stars in his eyes when he talks about becoming a movie star.
words.ex_cn: 当他谈论成为电影明星时，他眼中满是憧憬。
words.en: To be very hopeful or excited about something, often in a way that is not realistic.

words.tr: phrase. 得到某物；获得某物
words.ex: She managed to get something to eat before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 她在离开前设法弄到了一些吃的。
words.en: To obtain, acquire, or receive something.

words.tr: phrase. 理解；明白（某事）
words.ex: Do you get it now?
words.ex_cn: 你现在明白了吗？
words.en: To understand or comprehend something, often after an explanation.

words.tr: phrase. v. 把某物拿回来；恢复某物；重新获得某物
words.ex: I need to get my book back from the library.
words.ex_cn: 我需要从图书馆取回我的书。
words.en: To retrieve something that was previously owned, given, or lent.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 成功摆脱（负担、责任等）；把某物从某处取下；（尤指通过表达而）释放心中的情绪
words.ex: I need to get this letter off today.
words.ex_cn: 我需要今天把这封信寄出去。
words.en: To remove something from a surface or to start a journey.

words.tr: phrase. 下车；离开
words.ex: He gets off the bus at the school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校下车。
words.en: To leave a place, especially in order to start a journey; to remove something, especially clothing.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 尽快完成令人不愉快的事情；把某事尽快了结
words.ex: He wants to get his exam over with.
words.ex_cn: 他想尽快把考试结束掉。
words.en: If you want to get something over with, you want to do it or finish it quickly, especially because it is unpleasant.

words.tr: 短语动词. 此短语通常应为 'have something over' 或 'have something to discuss with someone'，可能意为对某人有某种优势，或有事要与某人谈。但 'have something over with' 并非常见或正确搭配，可能为误用。
words.ex: I want to have it over with the meeting now.
words.ex_cn: 我想现在就把会议结束掉。
words.en: To finish or conclude something, especially something that one does not enjoy or is eager to be done with.

words.tr: phrase. v. 完成某事；把某事结束掉（尤指令人不快的事）
words.ex: I just want to get this meeting over so I can go home.
words.ex_cn: 我只想赶快结束这个会议，然后回家。
words.en: To complete or deal with something, especially something unpleasant.

words.tr: phrase. v. 把某事彻底搞定；确保某事成功；包揽某事
words.ex: We need to get the contract sewed up before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要在会议前确保合同已经敲定。
words.en: To ensure that something is completely arranged or finished.

words.tr: phrase. 缝合；包办；确保成功
words.ex: He will sew up the torn shirt tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会缝好这件破了的衬衫。
words.en: To sew up means to mend or close by sewing, or to ensure the success of something.

words.tr: phrase. 掌握某事物；获得某项经验或成就
words.ex: After getting a few projects under his belt, he felt more confident in his abilities.
words.ex_cn: 在成功完成几个项目后，他对自己的能力感到更有信心。
words.en: To have successfully achieved or experienced something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 拥有某项经验或成就；掌握某项技能
words.ex: After years of hard work, she finally has a successful business under her belt.
words.ex_cn: phrase. 经过多年的努力，她终于拥有了一家成功的企业。
words.en: If you have something under your belt, you have already achieved it or have experience of it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 占某人的便宜；利用某人的弱点或处境获得好处
words.ex: He always tries to get the advantage of others in negotiations.
words.ex_cn: 他在谈判中总是试图占别人的便宜。
words.en: To gain a superior position over someone; to exploit someone for one's own benefit.

words.tr: 短语动词. 利用某人的弱点或处境来获得好处；占某人的便宜
words.ex: She tried to get an advantage of him by manipulating his emotions.
words.ex_cn: 她试图通过操纵他的情感来占他的便宜。
words.en: To take unfair or unethical advantage of someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人占优势；胜过某人
words.ex: By studying harder, she managed to get the advantage over her classmates in the exam.
words.ex_cn: 通过更努力地学习，她在考试中成功地胜过了她的同学们。
words.en: To gain a superior position or condition compared to someone else.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人占据优势；获得对某人的有利地位
words.ex: By studying harder, she was able to get an advantage over her classmates.
words.ex_cn: 通过更努力地学习，她能够胜过她的同学。
words.en: To gain a superior position or benefit over someone else.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人有优势；在某方面胜过某人
words.ex: She has the advantage of him in terms of experience.
words.ex_cn: 她在经验方面比他更有优势。
words.en: To be in a better position than someone else, especially in a competition or conflict.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人有优势；在某方面胜过某人
words.ex: She has an advantage over her competitors because of her extensive experience.
words.ex_cn: 由于她丰富的经验，她比竞争对手更有优势。
words.en: To have a better position or opportunity compared to someone else.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人有优势；在与某人的比较中处于有利地位
words.ex: She has the advantage over her opponent in terms of experience.
words.ex_cn: 她在经验方面比对手占优势。
words.en: To be in a better position than someone else, especially in a competition or contest.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人占优势；胜过某人
words.ex: By studying harder, she managed to get the edge on her competitors.
words.ex_cn: 通过更加努力学习，她设法在竞争中占据了优势。
words.en: To gain a slight advantage over someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人占优势；比别人抢先一步
words.ex: By starting early, she managed to get an edge on her competitors.
words.ex_cn: 通过提前开始，她成功地领先于她的竞争对手。
words.en: To gain a slight advantage over someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人略胜一筹；获得对某人的优势
words.ex: By studying harder, she managed to get the edge over her classmates in the exams.
words.ex_cn: 通过更努力地学习，她在考试中设法胜过了她的同学们。
words.en: To have a slight advantage over someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人占优势；胜过某人
words.ex: By studying harder, she managed to get an edge over her classmates.
words.ex_cn: 通过更加努力学习，她成功地比她的同学们占了优势。
words.en: To gain a slight advantage over someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人略胜一筹；在竞争中占有优势
words.ex: She has the edge on her competitors in terms of experience.
words.ex_cn: 在经验方面，她比她的竞争对手有优势。
words.en: To have a slight advantage over someone or something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人略胜一筹；在某方面占有优势
words.ex: He felt that he had an edge on his competitors because of his extensive experience.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得自己比竞争对手更有优势，因为他有丰富的经验。
words.en: To have an advantage over someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人略胜一筹；比某人更有优势
words.ex: She has the edge over her competitors in terms of experience.
words.ex_cn: 在经验方面，她比她的竞争对手略胜一筹。
words.en: To have a slight advantage over someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 比某人略胜一筹；比某人更有优势
words.ex: She has an edge over her competitors because of her extensive experience.
words.ex_cn: 由于她丰富的经验，她比竞争对手更有优势。
words.en: To have a slight advantage over someone else.

words.tr: n. 不予理睬，冷落；拒绝；刷掉，掸去；断然解雇
words.ex: He received a brushoff from the company after the interview.
words.ex_cn: 面试后，他被公司冷落了。
words.en: A blunt or abrupt rejection or dismissal.

words.tr: 短语动词. 得到好处；获得奖励；（非正式）被严厉对待或惩罚（视语境而定）
words.ex: If you don't finish your homework, you're going to get the business from your teacher.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不完成作业，你将会受到老师的批评。
words.en: To handle or deal with business matters; to engage in business activities.

words.tr: 短语动词. 感到毛骨悚然；感到不安或恐惧
words.ex: I get the creeps when I walk past that old house at night.
words.ex_cn: 我晚上走过那栋老房子时会感到毛骨悚然。
words.en: To feel a sensation of fear or unease, often described as a shiver or a feeling of something crawling on the skin.

words.tr: 短语动词. 感到毛骨悚然；感到不安或恐惧
words.ex: I have the creeps when I walk in the dark alone.
words.ex_cn: 我独自在黑暗中行走时感到毛骨悚然。
words.en: To feel a sensation of fear or disgust, often causing one's skin to crawl.

words.tr: phrase. 感到紧张不安；感到害怕或毛骨悚然
words.ex: He gets the willies when he sees a spider.
words.ex_cn: 他一看到蜘蛛就吓得毛骨悚然。
words.en: To feel a sudden, unpleasant sensation of fear, unease, or creepiness.

words.tr: phrase. 感到紧张不安；感到害怕或毛骨悚然
words.ex: He has the willies when he sees a big spider.
words.ex_cn: 他看到大蜘蛛时就感到害怕。
words.en: To feel nervous or frightened, especially in a situation that is eerie or unsettling.

words.tr: n. 门；大门；
words.ex: He closed the gate before it rained.
words.ex_cn: 下雨前他关上了门。
words.en: A gate is a structure like a door which is used at the entrance to a field, a garden, or the grounds of a building.

words.tr: n. 躲避，怠慢；结束（与某人的）恋爱关系；忽视
words.ex: She decided to give him the go-by after their heated argument.
words.ex_cn: 在激烈的争吵之后，她决定对他置之不理。
words.en: To be ignored or disregarded; to be passed over without notice.

words.tr: 短语动词. 掌握某人的把柄；获取某人的不利证据或秘密
words.ex: The detective was determined to get the goods on the corrupt official.
words.ex_cn: 侦探决心掌握这个腐败官员的不利证据。
words.en: To collect incriminating evidence against someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 掌握某人的把柄；拥有能证明某人做错事的证据
words.ex: He had the goods on the corrupt official.
words.ex_cn: 他掌握了那个腐败官员的罪证。
words.en: To have evidence or proof that someone has committed a crime or wrongdoing.

words.tr: phrase. 得到暗号；收到行动的信号（通常指秘密或非言语的指示）
words.ex: He got the high sign to leave the room quietly.
words.ex_cn: 他收到暗示，要悄悄地离开房间。
words.en: To receive a signal or sign indicating approval, permission, or a warning.

words.w: get the lead out of one's pants
words.tr: 短语动词. 加快速度，赶紧行动（俚语，常用于催促他人加快动作）
words.uk: ɡet ðə led aut əv wʌn(z) pænts
words.us: ɡet ðə lɛd aʊt əv wʌn(z) pænts
words.ex: Come on, get the lead out of your pants and hurry to school!
words.ex_cn: 快点，别磨蹭了，赶紧去上学！
words.en: To hurry up or move faster.

words.w: shake the lead out of one's pants
words.tr: phrase. （非正式）赶紧行动起来；别磨蹭了（字面意思是‘把裤子里的铅抖掉’，比喻摆脱懒散或迟钝）
words.uk: /ʃeɪk ðə liːd aʊt əv wʌnz pænts/
words.us: /ʃeɪk ðə lid aʊt əv wʌnz pænts/
words.ex: He ran so fast he could shake the lead out of his pants.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得太快了，都能把铅从裤子里抖出来了。
words.en: To hurry up or move faster.

words.tr: phrase. 了解某事的内情；获取某事的详细信息
words.ex: I need to get the lowdown on the company's financial situation before making a decision.
words.ex_cn: 在做出决定之前，我需要了解公司的财务状况内幕。
words.en: To obtain detailed information about something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 了解内情；获取详细情况或真实信息
words.ex: Can you get the lowdown on the new teacher?
words.ex_cn: 你能打听一下新老师的情况吗？
words.en: To obtain the essential facts, details, or inside information about a situation.

words.tr: phrase. 被解雇；被抛弃；被赶走
words.ex: He got the old heave-ho from his job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周被解雇了。
words.en: To be dismissed or fired from a job.

words.tr: int. 哼唷，嗨哟（尤指水手用力拉缆绳时的吆喝声）
words.ex: The sailors shouted 'heave-ho' as they pulled the anchor.
words.ex_cn: 水手们拉锚时喊着'哼唷，嗨哟'。
words.en: The act of dismissing someone from a job or position.

words.tr: phrase. 被解雇；被赶走；被抛弃
words.ex: He got the heave-ho from his job because he was always late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为总是迟到而被解雇了。
words.en: To be dismissed, rejected, or fired from a job or position.

words.tr: n. 浏览一遍；草率的工作；草草过目
words.ex: He gave the car a quick once-over before driving.
words.ex_cn: 他开车前快速检查了一下车子。
words.en: A quick inspection or examination.

words.tr: 短语动词. 摆脱；逃脱；溜走
words.ex: He got the slip and ran away from the police.
words.ex_cn: 他趁机溜走，逃开了警察。
words.en: To escape or avoid someone or something, especially by moving quickly or stealthily; to evade capture or pursuit.

words.tr: 短语动词. 得到全套服务；获得所有可用的项目或待遇（通常指在餐饮或服务中享受全面、完整的项目）
words.ex: He went to the mechanic and asked to get the works on his car.
words.ex_cn: 他去修车店，要求给他的车做个全面保养。
words.en: Receive the full set of services, goods, or information available; be given everything that is offered.

words.tr: 短语动词. 在某事中处于不利地位；在争执或竞争中遭受最大损失或最坏结果
words.ex: He got the worst of the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他在打斗中吃了亏。
words.en: To be in the least favorable position in a situation or conflict.

words.tr: 短语动词. 在某事中处于最不利的地位；遭受最大的损失或痛苦
words.ex: He had the worst of the storm while driving home.
words.ex_cn: 他在开车回家时遭遇了最糟糕的暴风雨。
words.en: To be in the least favorable position in a particular situation.

words.tr: phrase. v. 取得初步进展；开始成功（常用于比喻在某事上迈出第一步，尤其指在恋爱或谈判中）
words.ex: He got to first base with his new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他用他的新点子取得了初步进展。
words.en: Achieve the first stage of success in a venture, especially in a romantic or business context.

words.tr: phrase. v. （与某人）取得初步进展，建立初步关系（尤指恋爱或性关系）
words.ex: He couldn't get to first base with his science project.
words.ex_cn: 他连科学项目的第一步都没完成。
words.en: To make initial progress in a relationship or endeavor with someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. （棒球）上一垒；取得初步成功；迈出第一步；取得初步进展
words.ex: He reached first base with a single hit.
words.ex_cn: 他通过一记安打上了第一垒。
words.en: In baseball, to successfully hit the ball and run to first base without being put out; also used figuratively to mean achieving an initial stage of success or progress in a non-sporting context.

words.tr: phrase. （与某人）取得初步进展；初步成功；（尤指恋爱或求爱）迈出第一步
words.ex: He reached first base with his new friend during the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中和新朋友一起跑到了一垒。
words.en: To achieve the first stage of progress or agreement in a process or relationship.

words.tr: 短语动词. 在棒球规则中，对某人已有两次好球（不利局面）；引申为对某人已有两次严重过错或警告
words.ex: If you get two strikes against one, you must be careful not to make a third mistake.
words.ex_cn: 如果你已经两次犯错，就必须小心不要再犯第三个错误。
words.en: To be at a disadvantage or in a difficult position because of two mistakes or problems.

words.tr: phrase. 处于不利地位；有两项不利因素；已有两次失败或过错（常用于比喻处境艰难）
words.ex: He has two strikes against him because he was late twice this week.
words.ex_cn: 他这周迟到了两次，已经两次犯规了。
words.en: To be in a situation where one has two disadvantages or obstacles that make success less likely.

words.tr: 短语动词。开始进行；启动（通常指活动、计划或旅程等）
words.ex: The project will get underway next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目下周一将正式启动。
words.en: If a process or event gets underway, it begins.

words.tr: phrase. 正在进行中的；已开始的
words.ex: The project is underway.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: Currently in progress or happening now.

words.tr: phrase. 起床
words.ex: I get up at seven o'clock every morning.
words.ex_cn: 我每天早上七点起床。
words.en: To rise from bed after sleeping; to stand up; to increase in amount or level.

words.tr: phrase. 习惯于
words.ex: He is getting used to waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 他正在习惯早起。
words.en: To become familiar with something or someone, so that it/they no longer seem(s) new, strange, or difficult.

words.tr: phrase. 变湿；被弄湿
words.ex: If you go outside in the rain, you will get wet.
words.ex_cn: 如果你在雨中外出，你会淋湿的。
words.en: To become or make something become wet.

words.tr: phrase. 因某事受到责备或惩罚
words.ex: He will get what for breaking the window.
words.ex_cn: 他因为打碎窗户会挨骂。
words.en: To receive punishment or scolding for something done.

words.tr: phrase. v. 开始参与某事；适应某事；跟上某事物的节奏
words.ex: He needs to get with the program.
words.ex_cn: 他需要跟上形势。
words.en: To understand or accept a new idea, trend, or situation, especially after initial resistance.

words.tr: phrase. 与……在一起；支持；理解；陪伴
words.ex: I will be with my friend after school.
words.ex_cn: 我放学后会和我的朋友在一起。
words.en: To be in the company of someone; to stay with someone.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 7 基本动词 GIVE

words.tr: phrasal verb. 留意；倾听；听取（某人的意见或问题）
words.ex: He won't give an ear to his friend's advice.
words.ex_cn: 他不会听朋友的建议。
words.en: To listen to someone or something attentively.

words.tr: phrase. v. 留心倾听；专心听取
words.ex: He gives his ear to every word his teacher says.
words.ex_cn: 他认真听老师说的每一句话。
words.en: To listen to someone or something attentively.

words.w: give as good as one gets
words.tr: phrase. 以牙还牙，以眼还眼；以其人之道还治其人之身；给予对方同样强度的回击
words.uk: ɡɪv æz ɡʊd æz wʌn ɡets
words.us: ɡɪv æz ɡʊd æz wʌn ɡets
words.ex: He insults me, so I give as good as I get.
words.ex_cn: 他骂我，所以我也回骂他。
words.en: To respond to an attack or criticism with equal force or severity.

words.tr: phrase. 分娩；产生
words.ex: She will give birth to a baby next month.
words.ex_cn: 她下个月要生孩子。
words.en: To bring a baby or young animal into the world by birth.

words.tr: phrase. 出生；产生；引起
words.ex: She gave birth to a healthy baby last night.
words.ex_cn: 她昨晚生了一个健康的宝宝。
words.en: To produce a baby or young animal from your body.

words.tr: phrase. 相信某事；认为某事可信
words.ex: He gave credence to the rumor about the closure.
words.ex_cn: 他相信了关于关闭的谣言。
words.en: To believe that something is true or likely to be true, especially after considering evidence or arguments.

words.tr: 短语动词. 向某人叙述……的情况；向某人报告……的详情
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ən əˈkaʊnt əv
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ən əˈkaʊnt əv
words.ex: He gave me an account of what happened yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他向我描述了昨天发生的事情。
words.en: To describe or explain something to someone in detail.

words.w: give credit where credit is due
words.tr: phrase. 该表扬时就应表扬；有功即赏，公正地承认他人的贡献
words.uk: ɡɪv ˈkrɛdɪt weə(r) ˈkrɛdɪt ɪz djuː
words.us: ɡɪv ˈkrɛdɪt wer ˈkrɛdɪt ɪz duː
words.ex: He gave credit where credit is due for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他如实称赞了她的努力。
words.en: Acknowledge and praise someone for their contribution or achievement, especially when it is deserved or has been overlooked.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某人放任自流，给予某人充分自由（去做某事）
words.ex: The teacher gave free rein to the students to choose their projects.
words.ex_cn: 老师让学生们自由选择他们的项目。
words.en: Allow someone complete freedom to act or behave as they wish, without restriction or interference.

words.tr: 短语动词. 给某人充分的自由或权力去做他们想做的事
words.ex: The boss gave her free rein to design the new website.
words.ex_cn: 老板让她自由发挥来设计新网站。
words.en: To allow someone to do what they want or need to do, without trying to control them or restrict their freedom.

words.tr: phrase. 让步；退让；放弃立场
words.ex: He will not give ground in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中不会让步。
words.en: To concede or yield in a conflict or argument.

words.tr: phrase. 屈服于；向…让步；投降
words.ex: Don't give in to fear when you face a challenge.
words.ex_cn: 当你面对挑战时，不要向恐惧屈服。
words.en: To yield to someone or something, especially after resisting for a period of time.

words.tr: phrase. 投降；屈服；让步
words.ex: He will not give in to the bully.
words.ex_cn: 他不会向欺凌者屈服。
words.en: To agree to something that you had been opposing, especially because someone has forced or persuaded you to.

words.tr: phrase. 加大油门；加速前进；全力以赴（通常用于鼓励加快速度或增加动力）
words.ex: He gave it the gun and the car sped away.
words.ex_cn: 他加大油门，车就飞驰而去了。
words.en: To accelerate or increase speed, especially in a vehicle, by pressing the accelerator pedal firmly.

words.tr: 短语动词. 把枪交给她
words.ex: Give her the gun now.
words.ex_cn: 现在把枪给她。
words.en: To allow her to take the lead or make the decisive move in a situation.

words.tr: phrase. 直言不讳地告诉某人真相；坦率地对某人说出实情
words.ex: I will give it to you straight: you need to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 我会直接告诉你：你需要更努力。
words.en: To tell someone something in a direct and honest way, without trying to make it seem less serious or less unpleasant than it is.

words.tr: 短语动词. 把某物交给某人；有时引申为严厉地批评或惩罚某人
words.ex: He gave it to his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他把它给了他的弟弟。
words.en: To hand something over to someone.

words.w: give one an inch, and one will take a mile
words.tr: phrase. 得寸进尺；给一点就想要更多
words.uk: ɡɪv wʌn ən ɪntʃ , ænd wʌn wɪl teɪk ə maɪl
words.us: ɡɪv wʌn ən ɪntʃ , ænd wʌn wɪl teɪk ə maɪl
words.ex: He asked for a small break, but give him an inch, and he will take a mile.
words.ex_cn: 他只是要一小段休息时间，但你让他一步，他就会得寸进尺。
words.en: If you give someone a small amount of power or freedom to do something, they will try to take a lot more.

words.w: if you give one an inch, one will take a mile
words.tr: phrase. 得寸进尺；你若让步一寸，对方就会进逼一英里
words.uk: ɪf juː ɡɪv wʌn ən ɪntʃ wʌn wɪl teɪk ə maɪl
words.us: ɪf jə ɡɪv wʌn ən ɪntʃ wʌn wɪl teɪk ə maɪl
words.ex: If you give him an inch, he will take a mile.
words.ex_cn: 你给他一点好处，他就会得寸进尺。
words.en: This idiom means that if you allow someone a small amount of something, they will try to take much more. It's used to describe someone who takes advantage of a small opportunity to gain a lot.

words.tr: phrase. 解雇某人，让某人走人
words.ex: He gave her walking papers because she was late every day.
words.ex_cn: 他解雇了她，因为她每天都迟到。
words.en: To dismiss someone from their job or position, especially in a formal or abrupt manner.

words.tr: phrase. 愿意不惜一切代价得到某物或做某事
words.ex: I would give my right arm for a chance to meet my favorite singer.
words.ex_cn: 我愿意付出一切去见我最喜欢的歌手。
words.en: If you say that you would give your right arm to do or have something, you mean that you would like it very much.

words.tr: phrase. 愿意不惜一切代价得到某物或做某事
words.ex: He would give his right arm to play in the World Cup.
words.ex_cn: 他宁愿失去右臂也想参加世界杯。
words.en: If you say that you would give your right arm to do or have something, you mean that you would like it very much.

words.tr: phrase. v. 摆架子；装腔作势；自以为了不起
words.ex: He gives himself airs because he bought a new car.
words.ex_cn: 他因为买了新车就摆出一副了不起的样子。
words.en: To behave in a way that shows you think you are more important than you really are.

words.tr: phrase. 分发；发出；发表；用尽
words.ex: He gives out books to the students.
words.ex_cn: 他把书分发给学生们。
words.en: To distribute or hand out something; to emit or produce something such as a sound or smell; to announce or make something known publicly.

words.tr: phrase. v. 导致；引起；使发生
words.ex: His comments could give rise to controversy.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论可能引起争议。
words.en: If something gives rise to an event or situation, it causes that event or situation to happen.

words.tr: phrase. v. 给某人打电话；对某人说一套讨好或欺骗的话
words.ex: He gave me a line about being busy.
words.ex_cn: 他跟我说他很忙。
words.en: To call someone on the phone.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人说谎或编造借口；给某人灌输一套说辞
words.ex: He fed me a line about working late.
words.ex_cn: 他骗我说他在加班。
words.en: To tell someone something that is not true, especially as an excuse or explanation.

words.tr: 短语动词. 让某人感到疼痛；使某人烦恼或生气
words.ex: My little brother gives me a pain when he shouts loudly.
words.ex_cn: 我弟弟大声喊叫时让我很烦。
words.en: To cause someone to feel annoyed or in pain.

words.w: give sb. a piece of one's mind
words.tr: phrase. v. 向某人发泄不满；严厉斥责某人
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə piːs əv wʌnz maɪnd
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə pis əv wʌnz maɪnd
words.ex: She gave him a piece of her mind for being late.
words.ex_cn: 她因为他迟到而狠狠训了他一顿。
words.en: To express one's feelings or opinions to someone in a very direct and often angry way.

words.tr: phrase. 给某人打电话
words.ex: I'll give you a ring when I arrive.
words.ex_cn: 我到了就给你打电话。
words.en: To call someone on the telephone.

words.tr: phrase. 给某人打个电话；联系某人（通常指通过电话）
words.ex: I will give you a buzz tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天给你打电话。
words.en: To call someone on the telephone.

words.tr: phrase. 故意避开……；对……敬而远之
words.ex: The children give the angry dog a wide berth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们对那只生气的狗敬而远之。
words.en: To keep a safe distance from someone or something, often to avoid trouble or interference.

words.tr: phrase. 赠送；分发；背叛；泄露
words.ex: He will give away his old books to the library.
words.ex_cn: 他将把他的旧书捐给图书馆。
words.en: To give something to someone without asking for payment, or to reveal something secret or private.

words.tr: phrase. 放弃
words.ex: He gave up smoking last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年戒烟了。
words.en: If you give up something, you stop doing it or having it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 使某人犹豫；让某人停下来思考
words.ex: The loud noise gave him pause.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他停顿了一下。
words.en: To cause someone to stop and think carefully about something, often because it is surprising or worrying.

words.tr: 使某人犹豫；让某人停下来思考
words.ex: The teacher gave pause to the student.
words.ex_cn: 老师让那个学生停顿一下。
words.en: To cause someone to hesitate or think carefully about something, especially because of a possible problem or difficulty.

words.tr: phrase. 给某人使眼色；对某人抛媚眼（通常表示兴趣或挑逗）
words.ex: He gave her the eye at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上对她抛媚眼。
words.en: To look at someone in a way that shows you are attracted to them.

words.w: give sb. the shirt off one's back
words.tr: phrase. 愿意为某人牺牲一切，甚至不惜自己受苦；把贴身的衬衫都给某人
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ðə ʃɜːt ɒf wʌnz bæk
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ðə ʃɜːrt ɔːf wʌnz bæk
words.ex: He gave his brother the shirt off his back when he had no clothes.
words.ex_cn: 当他兄弟没衣服穿时，他把自己的衬衫脱下来给了他。
words.en: To be willing to do anything for someone, even at great personal cost.

words.tr: phrase. 以牙还牙；针锋相对的报复行为
words.ex: He insulted me, so I insulted him back — it's just tit for tat.
words.ex_cn: 他侮辱了我，所以我回敬了他——这就是以牙还牙。
words.en: If you say that someone is using a tit-for-tat strategy, you mean that they are doing the same thing that someone else has done to them, especially something bad, as a way of punishing them or getting revenge.

words.tr: phrase. v. 使某人丢脸；使某人名誉受损；使某人受到打击
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə blæk aɪ
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə blæk aɪ
words.ex: He gave his brother a black eye during the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他在打架时把弟弟打出了黑眼圈。
words.en: To cause someone to have a bruise around the eye, typically as a result of being hit; to cause someone to be embarrassed or to lose reputation.

words.tr: phrase. 给某人一个好主意；使某人灵光一现
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə braɪt aɪˈdɪə
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə braɪt aɪˈdiə
words.ex: He gave me a bright idea to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他给了我一个好主意来解决这个问题。
words.en: To suggest or inspire someone with a clever or innovative thought.

words.tr: 短语动词. 使某人理解某事；暗示或传达给某人某信息
words.ex: He gave me to understand that the meeting is canceled.
words.ex_cn: 他让我明白会议取消了。
words.en: To cause someone to believe or realize something, often indirectly.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 发出，释放（如气味、热量、光等）
words.ex: The light gives off a warm glow.
words.ex_cn: 灯发出温暖的光芒。
words.en: If something gives off or gives out a gas, heat, or a smell, it produces it and sends it out into the air.

words.tr: phrase. 发出（蒸汽、光等）
words.ex: The lamp gives off a warm light.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯发出温暖的光。
words.en: If something gives off or gives out a gas, heat, or a smell, it produces it and sends it out into the air.

words.tr: phrase. v. 分发某物；发出某物；公布某物
words.ex: The teacher gives out books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师把书分发给学生。
words.en: To distribute something; to emit light, heat, etc.; to announce or publish something.

words.tr: 短语动词。在婚礼上将新娘交给新郎，通常由新娘的父亲完成，象征将女儿托付给新郎
words.ex: The father will give the bride away at the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 父亲将在婚礼上把新娘交给新郎。
words.en: To formally present the bride to the groom at a wedding ceremony, traditionally done by her father.

words.tr: phrase. 即使对讨厌的人或对手，也应公正地承认其优点或应得之物
words.ex: He is rude, but I must give the devil his due—he works hard.
words.ex_cn: 他很粗鲁，但我必须承认，他工作很努力。
words.en: To acknowledge the good qualities or the value of someone or something, even if you generally dislike or disapprove of them.

words.tr: phrase. 尽管某人有很多缺点，但也要承认其应有的优点；公允地评价任何人，即使是敌人或不喜欢的人
words.ex: She gave the devil her due, even though she disliked him.
words.ex_cn: 尽管她不喜欢他，她还是承认了他的优点。
words.en: To acknowledge the positive qualities or achievements of someone, even if you generally dislike them.

words.tr: phrase. 泄露秘密；暴露真相；无意中透露关键信息
words.ex: He gave the game away by laughing when he was supposed to be serious.
words.ex_cn: 他本该严肃，却笑了出来，结果露了馅。
words.en: To reveal a secret or a hidden agenda, often unintentionally.

words.tr: phrase. 断气；死亡；（机器等）停止运转，彻底损坏
words.ex: The old car finally gave up the ghost yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 那辆旧车昨天终于报废了。
words.en: To die or to stop functioning, especially after a long period of use or existence.

words.tr: phrase. v. 发泄，表达（感情或情绪），如愤怒、不满等
words.ex: He gave vent to his anger after the fight.
words.ex_cn: 打完架后，他发泄了怒气。
words.en: To express a strong emotion, especially anger, in a way that makes it clear what you are feeling.

words.tr: 短语动词. 赋予……表达机会；说出；表达（某种情感或意见）
words.ex: He gave voice to his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他表达了内心的恐惧。
words.en: To express feelings or opinions.

words.tr: phrase. 让路；让步
words.ex: The old rules give way to new ones.
words.ex_cn: 旧规则让位于新规则。
words.en: If something gives way to something else, it is replaced by it.

words.tr: phrase. 撤退；让路；退让；屈服；垮塌
words.ex: The soldiers had to give way to the enemy.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们不得不向敌人撤退。
words.en: To yield or surrender; to collapse or fail under pressure.

words.tr: phrase. 别为难某人了；让某人歇会儿；对某人宽容一点
words.ex: Can you give me a break? I'm really trying my best.
words.ex_cn: 你能放过我吗？我真的在尽全力了。
words.en: To allow someone to have a rest or to stop being hard on someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 给某人一个厌恶或不满的眼神
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə ˈdɪrti lʊk
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə ˈdɜːrti lʊk
words.ex: He gave her a dirty look when she interrupted him.
words.ex_cn: 当她打断他时，他狠狠地瞪了她一眼。
words.en: To look at someone in a way that shows you are annoyed or do not approve of them.

words.w: give sb. a free hand with sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 给某人充分的自由或自主权去处理某事
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌmˈbɒdi ə friː hænd wɪð ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡɪv ˈsʌmbədi ə friː hænd wɪð ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: The teacher gave the students a free hand with their project.
words.ex_cn: 老师让学生们自由地做他们的项目。
words.en: To allow someone to do something in the way that they want, without giving them instructions or advice.

words.tr: phrase. 给某人充分的自由或自主权去做某事
words.ex: The boss gave her a free hand to design the new website.
words.ex_cn: 老板让她自由设计新网站。
words.en: To allow someone to do something in their own way without interference.

words.w: give sb. a hand for sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 因某事帮助某人；为某事向某人伸出援手
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə hænd fɔː sʌm θɪŋ
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə hænd fɔr sʌm θɪŋ
words.ex: Can you give me a hand for carrying these boxes?
words.ex_cn: 你能帮我搬这些箱子吗？
words.en: To help someone with something.

words.tr: phrase. 给予某人帮助
words.ex: Can you give me a hand with this box?
words.ex_cn: 你能帮我搬一下这个箱子吗？
words.en: To help someone with something.

words.w: give one a run for one's money
words.tr: phrase. 使某人全力以赴；给某人造成相当大的竞争或挑战，使其不得不竭尽全力
words.uk: ɡɪv wʌn ə rʌn fə(r) wʌnz ˈmʌni
words.us: ɡɪv wʌn ə rʌn fɔːr wʌnz ˈmʌni
words.ex: The new student can give the champion a run for his money in chess.
words.ex_cn: 这名新学生在国际象棋方面能和冠军一较高下。
words.en: To provide strong competition or challenge to someone, making them work hard to achieve success.

words.w: give sb. a hand with sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 帮助某人做某事；协助某人处理某事
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə hænd wɪð sʌm θɪŋ
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə hænd wɪð sʌm θɪŋ
words.ex: Can you give me a hand with my homework?
words.ex_cn: 你能帮我做作业吗？
words.en: To help someone with something.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人日子难过；严厉批评某人；刁难某人
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə hɑːd taɪm
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə hɑːrd taɪm
words.ex: My little brother gives me a hard time every day.
words.ex_cn: 我弟弟每天都让我难堪。
words.en: To cause someone difficulty or trouble; to make things hard for someone.

words.w: give sb. a rough idea of sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 向某人简要说明某事的大致情况
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə rʌf aɪˈdɪə əv sʌm θɪŋ
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə rʌf aɪˈdiə əv sʌm θɪŋ
words.ex: He gave me a rough idea of the cost.
words.ex_cn: 他给我大概说了下费用。
words.en: To provide someone with a general understanding or overview of something, without going into detailed specifics.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某人大发雷霆；严厉斥责某人
words.ex: He gave his brother the devil for breaking his toy.
words.ex_cn: 他因为弟弟弄坏了玩具而狠狠责备了他。
words.en: To scold or reprimand someone severely.

words.tr: phrase. v. 严厉责骂某人；使某人受苦；让某人日子不好过
words.ex: He gave his brother hell for breaking the window.
words.ex_cn: 他因为弟弟打碎了窗户而狠狠责骂了他。
words.en: To cause someone a lot of trouble or pain.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人不公平；给某人吃苦头；亏待某人
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə rɔː diːl
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə rɔː diːl
words.ex: He gave his coworker a raw deal by making him work overtime for free.
words.ex_cn: 他让同事免费加班，不公平地对待了他。
words.en: To treat someone unfairly or badly.

words.w: give sb. a reputation as a sb.
words.tr: 短语动词. 使某人获得某种身份或角色的名声；让某人被视为某类人
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌmˈbədi ə ˌrepjʊˈteɪʃən æz ə sʌmˈbədi
words.us: ɡɪv sʌmˈbɑːdi ə ˌrepjəˈteɪʃən æz ə sʌmˈbɑːdi
words.ex: He gave her a reputation as a hard worker.
words.ex_cn: 他让她获得了勤奋工作的名声。
words.en: To establish or cause someone to be known for a particular characteristic or role.

words.tr: phrase. 给某人带来名声；使某人获得声誉
words.ex: He gave his son a reputation for being honest.
