words.ex_cn: 他让儿子获得了诚实的名声。
words.en: To establish or cause someone to be known for a particular characteristic or role.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人冷淡；故意冷落某人
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ðə kəʊld ˈʃəʊldə(r)
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ðə koʊld ˈʃoʊldər
words.ex: He gave me the cold shoulder after our argument.
words.ex_cn: 我们争吵后，他对我冷淡不理。
words.en: To deliberately ignore someone or treat someone in an unfriendly way.

words.w: give sb. the red carpet treatment
words.tr: 短语动词. 以隆重的礼遇接待某人；给予某人贵宾般的待遇
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌmˈbədi ðə red ˈkɑːpet ˈtriːtmənt
words.us: ɡɪv ˈsʌmbədi ðə red ˈkɑːrpɪt ˈtriːtmənt
words.ex: They gave the celebrity the red carpet treatment at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他们在机场给这位名人最高规格的接待。
words.en: To treat someone with special honor or respect, often by providing luxurious or elaborate accommodations or services.

words.tr: phrase. 解雇某人；开除某人
words.ex: The boss gave him the ax because he was late too often.
words.ex_cn: 老板因为他经常迟到而解雇了他。
words.en: To dismiss someone from their job.

words.tr: phrase. 解雇某人；让某人离职
words.ex: The boss gave him the sack for being late every day.
words.ex_cn: 老板因为他每天迟到而把他解雇了。
words.en: To dismiss or fire someone from their job.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词GIVE补充词组

words.w: give a good account of oneself
words.tr: 短语动词. 表现良好；证明自己的能力；在某场合中表现得体或出色
words.uk: ɡɪv ə ɡʊd əˈkaʊnt ɒv wʌnˈself
words.us: ɡɪv ə ɡʊd əˈkaʊnt əv wʌnˈsɛlf
words.ex: He gave a good account of himself in the job interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作面试中表现得很好。
words.en: To perform well or to behave in a way that is admired or respected.

words.tr: phrase. v. 追赶；追击（某人或某物）
words.ex: The police gave chase to the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察追捕那个小偷。
words.en: To pursue or follow someone or something in order to catch or overtake them.

words.tr: phrase. 追赶；追击
words.ex: The police will give chase to the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察会追捕小偷。
words.en: To pursue someone or something in order to catch them.

words.tr: 短语动词. 无私地奉献自己；付出自己的时间、精力或情感帮助他人
words.ex: He always gives of himself to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他总是无私地帮助别人。
words.en: To devote oneself to a task or to helping others.

words.tr: phrase. 给予某人自由
words.ex: They gave him his freedom after many years in prison.
words.ex_cn: 在多年监禁后，他们给了他自由。
words.en: To release someone from captivity or obligation, restoring their liberty.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 沉迷于；专心致志于；听任自己陷入（某种状态或行为）
words.ex: He gives himself up to reading every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都专心阅读。
words.en: To devote oneself completely to something, often a feeling, activity, or way of life.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 投降；自首；放弃自己
words.ex: He decided to give himself up to the police.
words.ex_cn: 他决定向警察自首。
words.en: To surrender or submit oneself, especially to the authorities or to an emotion.

words.tr: phrase. v. （非正式）给出，分发某物；有时指不情愿地透露信息或表达情绪
words.ex: He gave out with a loud laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他大声笑了出来。
words.en: To express or emit something, such as an opinion, information, or sound.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人彻底摊牌；与某人把事情说清楚或激烈地争论
words.ex: They decided to have it out with each other after months of unresolved tension.
words.ex_cn: 经过几个月的未解紧张关系后，他们决定彻底解决彼此之间的问题。
words.en: To discuss a problem or disagreement with someone in order to resolve it.

words.tr: phrase. 隆重地为某人送行
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə bɪɡ send-ɒf
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə bɪɡ send-ɔːf
words.ex: They gave him a big send-off before he moved to New York.
words.ex_cn: 他在搬到纽约之前，大家为他举行了盛大的欢送会。
words.en: To organize a large farewell celebration for someone, especially when they are leaving a place or position.

words.w: give sth. a lick and a promise
words.tr: 短语动词. 匆匆忙忙地做某事，敷衍了事地完成某事
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌmθɪŋ ə lɪk ænd ə ˈprɒmɪs
words.us: ɡɪv sʌmθɪŋ ə lɪk ænd ə ˈprɑːmɪs
words.ex: He gave the wall a lick and a promise before the guests came.
words.ex_cn: 客人来之前，他随便刷了墙几下应付一下。
words.en: To do something quickly and carelessly, without putting in the necessary effort or attention to detail.

words.w: give sb. a reputation for doing sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 因做某事而使某人获得某种名声或声誉
words.uk: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə ˌreprɪˈteɪʃn fə ˈduːɪŋ sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡɪv sʌm wʌn ə ˌreprɪˈteɪʃn fɔr ˈduːɪŋ sʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: He gives his students a reputation for being hardworking.
words.ex_cn: 他让他的学生以勤奋著称。
words.en: To cause someone to be known or regarded in a particular way because of their actions or achievements.

words.tr: 短语动词. 在……方面给予……领先优势；让……在……上先走一步
words.ex: Good sleep gives you a head start on the day.
words.ex_cn: 充足的睡眠让你在一天开始时领先一步。
words.en: To provide someone with an advantage that makes them more likely to succeed at something before others have even started.

words.tr: phrase. v. 给……一个领先的机会；让……先开始
words.ex: The teacher gave the slower students a head start in the race.
words.ex_cn: 老师让速度较慢的学生在比赛中先出发。
words.en: To provide someone with an early advantage in a competition or endeavor.

words.tr: 短语动词. 与某人击掌庆祝或打招呼，表示友好或庆祝成功
words.ex: He gave me some skin after I won the game.
words.ex_cn: 我赢了比赛后，他给了我一些皮（击掌）。
words.en: To slap someone's hand in a celebratory gesture of greeting or agreement.

words.tr: phrase. 击掌庆祝；与某人击掌表示庆祝或鼓励
words.ex: After scoring the winning goal, he ran to his teammates to give them five.
words.ex_cn: 在踢进制胜一球后，他跑向队友与他们击掌庆祝。
words.en: To slap palms with someone as a gesture of greeting, celebration, or agreement.

words.tr: phrase. 悄悄给某人五块钱（或五单位货币）
words.ex: He slipped me five dollars for the coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他给了我五美元买咖啡。
words.en: To secretly give someone five dollars.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人感到毛骨悚然；让某人起鸡皮疙瘩
words.ex: That old house gives me the creeps.
words.ex_cn: 那栋老房子让我毛骨悚然。
words.en: To make someone feel frightened or uneasy, often because of something strange or unpleasant.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人感到毛骨悚然；让某人感到害怕或不安
words.ex: That spooky movie gives me the willies.
words.ex_cn: 那部恐怖电影让我毛骨悚然。
words.en: To make someone feel nervous or scared.

words.tr: phrase. 给某人批准或允许开始做某事
words.ex: The boss gave her the go-ahead to start the project.
words.ex_cn: 老板批准她开始这个项目。
words.en: To give someone permission or approval to proceed with something.

words.tr: phrase. 给某人放行，批准某人做某事
words.ex: The boss gave me the green light to start the project.
words.ex_cn: 老板批准我开始这个项目。
words.en: To give someone permission or approval to proceed with a plan or action.

words.tr: phrase. 将某人解雇；把某人赶走；让某人滚蛋
words.uk: gɪv ɛnz ði əʊld hiːv həʊ
words.us: ɡɪv ɛnz ði oʊld hiːv hoʊ
words.ex: The boss gave him the old heave-ho after he was late too many times.
words.ex_cn: 老板因为他多次迟到把他赶走了。
words.en: To dismiss someone from a job or to end a romantic relationship with someone.

words.tr: phrase. v. 让某人走人；解雇某人；把某人赶走
words.ex: The boss gave him the heave-ho after he was late three times.
words.ex_cn: 老板因为他迟到了三次，把他赶走了。
words.en: To dismiss or break up with someone.

words.tr: phrase. adj. 上下打量某人；粗略地检查或评估某人
words.ex: He gave the stranger the once-over before speaking.
words.ex_cn: 他在说话前打量了那个陌生人一眼。
words.en: To quickly examine or look at someone or something.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 8 基本动词 GO

words.w: go a long way toward doing sth.
words.tr: 短语. 对做某事大有帮助；在很大程度上促成某事
words.uk: ɡəʊ ə lɒŋ weɪ təˈwɔːd ˈduːɪŋ sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡoʊ ə lɔːŋ weɪ təˈwɔːrd ˈduːɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: Exercise can go a long way toward improving your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以大大改善你的健康。
words.en: To contribute significantly toward achieving a particular goal or outcome.

words.w: go a long way in doing sth.
words.tr: 短语. 在做某事方面起很大作用；对实现某事有很大帮助
words.uk: ɡəʊ ə lɒŋ weɪ ɪn ˈduːɪŋ sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡoʊ ə lɔːŋ weɪ ɪn ˈduːɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: Practice can go a long way in improving your English.
words.ex_cn: 练习能大大帮助你提高英语。
words.en: To be very helpful in achieving something or making something happen.

words.tr: phrase. 开始做某事；着手处理某事
words.ex: It's time to go about doing the chores.
words.ex_cn: 是时候开始做家务了。
words.en: To begin to deal with something or to start doing something.

words.tr: phrase. 继续做自己的事；忙自己的事务
words.ex: After the noise stopped, everyone went about their business.
words.ex_cn: 噪音停止后，每个人都继续做自己的事。
words.en: To continue with one's usual activities or duties without being distracted or disturbed.

words.tr: phrase. 格格不入；违反意愿
words.ex: It goes against the grain to lie, even if it helps.
words.ex_cn: 即使撒谎有帮助，这也违背我的本性。
words.en: If something goes against the grain, you would not normally do it because it would be unusual or unnatural.

words.tr: phrase. 开始做某事；继续进行某事
words.ex: They decided to go ahead with the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定继续执行这个计划。
words.en: To proceed with something; to continue with a plan or activity, especially after considering it carefully.

words.tr: phrase. v. 全力以赴；竭尽全力；拿出全部力量去做某事
words.ex: He went all out to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他全力以赴赢得了比赛。
words.en: To make a very great effort to achieve something.

words.w: go all the way with sb.
words.tr: phrase. 与某人完全合作；与某人发生性关系（视语境而定）
words.uk: ɡəʊ ɔːl ðə weɪ wɪð səmˈbədi
words.us: ɡoʊ ɔːl ðə weɪ wɪð ˈsʌmbədi
words.ex: He decided to go all the way with her after knowing her for a long time.
words.ex_cn: 在认识她很久之后，他决定和她发生性关系。
words.en: To have sexual intercourse with someone; to fully cooperate or commit to a project with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 完全参与到底；坚持到最后；（俚语）发生性关系
words.ex: He decided to go all the way and run for president.
words.ex_cn: 他决定全力以赴，竞选总统。
words.en: To proceed or continue to the ultimate conclusion or the farthest possible point.

words.tr: 短语动词. 与某人同床睡觉；常指发生性关系
words.ex: She was accused of going to bed with her boss.
words.ex_cn: 她被指控与她的老板发生性关系。
words.en: To have sexual intercourse with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 上床睡觉
words.ex: He goes to bed at nine every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上九点上床睡觉。
words.en: To go to bed means to lie down in a bed in order to sleep.

words.tr: phrase. 对…疯狂着迷；为…激动得发狂
words.ex: They go ape over every new phone release.
words.ex_cn: 他们对每次新手机发布都疯狂追捧。
words.en: To become extremely excited or angry about something.

words.tr: phrase. v. 发狂；发疯；极度兴奋或愤怒
words.ex: The kids went ape when they saw the clown at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在派对上看到小丑时兴奋得不得了。
words.en: To become extremely excited or angry.

words.tr: 短语动词. 原地打转；徒劳无功地忙碌；绕圈子
words.ex: We talked for hours but went around in circles and solved nothing.
words.ex_cn: 我们谈了几个小时，但只是原地打转，什么也没解决。
words.en: If you say that someone is going around in circles, you mean that they are not achieving anything because they keep coming back to the same point or problem.

words.tr: 短语动词. 原地打转；徒劳无功地忙碌；没有取得进展
words.ex: We keep going in circles and never solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 我们一直在原地打转，从没解决问题。
words.en: To move around in a circular path without making progress or reaching a destination.

words.tr: phrase. 走入歧途；堕落；丢失；被盗
words.ex: He went astray after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后走上了歧途。
words.en: If someone goes astray, they no longer follow the right course of action or the right way of life.

words.tr: phrase. 空手而归；一无所获地离开
words.ex: He went to the store but came away empty-handed.
words.ex_cn: 他去了商店，但空手而归。
words.en: To leave without achieving what one wanted or without taking anything with one.

words.tr: phrase. 违背诺言；食言
words.uk: ɡəʊ bæk ɒn wʌn z wɜːd
words.us: ɡoʊ bæk ɑːn wʌn z wɜːrd
words.ex: He promised to help, but he went back on his word.
words.ex_cn: 他答应帮忙，但却食言了。
words.en: If you go back on your word, you do not do what you have promised to do.

words.tr: phrase. 坏掉；腐败；变质
words.ex: The milk will go bad if you leave it out of the fridge.
words.ex_cn: 如果你把牛奶放在冰箱外面，它会变质的。
words.en: If food goes bad, it is no longer fresh or good to eat.

words.tr: phrase. v. 变得疯狂；失去理智；激动得失控
words.ex: The kids go bananas when they see the clown.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到小丑时都疯狂了。
words.en: To become very excited or to act in a wild or crazy manner.

words.tr: 短语动词. 被拒之门外；无人理会；得不到所需的东西
words.ex: The job offer went begging because no one wanted to work night shifts.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作无人问津，因为没有人愿意上夜班。
words.en: If something goes begging, it is not taken or used by anyone, even though it is available.

words.tr: phrase. v. 破产；身无分文；没钱了
words.ex: He went broke after buying a new car.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆新车后破产了。
words.en: To become completely without money; to go bankrupt.

words.tr: phrase. 彻底戒除（尤指突然停止使用毒品或戒除不良习惯）
words.ex: He decided to go cold turkey and quit smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他决定突然戒烟，彻底停止吸烟。
words.en: To abruptly stop using an addictive substance, especially drugs or alcohol, without tapering off.

words.tr: 短语动词. 奋力抗争到底；即使失败也不轻易放弃
words.ex: The team decided to go down fighting rather than give up easily.
words.ex_cn: 团队决定奋力抵抗到底，而不是轻易放弃。
words.en: To continue to fight or struggle, even when it seems that defeat is certain.

words.tr: 短语动词. 被载入史册；留名青史
words.ex: The event is sure to go down in history as one of the most significant moments of the century.
words.ex_cn: 这一事件必将作为本世纪最重要的时刻之一载入史册。
words.en: To be remembered or recorded in history as important or significant.

words.tr: 动词短语. 走下坡路；情况恶化；衰退
words.ex: After he stopped exercising, his health began to go downhill.
words.ex_cn: 他停止锻炼后，健康状况开始恶化。
words.en: To deteriorate or become worse in condition, quality, or performance.

words.tr: 短语动词. 各自付账；各付各的（尤指用餐时）
words.ex: We decided to go dutch for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定吃饭时AA制。
words.en: If two or more people go dutch, each person pays for their own meal, drink, or entertainment instead of one person paying for everything.

words.tr: phrase. 对……宽容一些；对……手下留情；不要对……太严厉
words.ex: Please go easy on him, he's new to the job.
words.ex_cn: 请对他温和一些，他是新来的。
words.en: To treat someone gently or leniently, especially when they have done something wrong or are in a vulnerable position.

words.tr: phrase. 放轻松；别太紧张；慢慢来
words.ex: Go easy on yourself; it's not the end of the world.
words.ex_cn: 对自己放松点，这不是世界末日。
words.en: To behave in a gentle, lenient, or non-strict manner.

words.tr: phrase. 全力以赴；孤注一掷；冒险一搏
words.ex: He went for broke and invested all his money in the business.
words.ex_cn: 他孤注一掷，把所有钱都投资到了生意上。
words.en: To risk everything in an all-out effort.

words.tr: 短语动词. 去争取吧；努力争取；勇敢尝试
words.ex: You can do it, so go for it!
words.ex_cn: 你可以做到，所以去干吧！
words.en: If you say 'go for it' to someone, you are encouraging them to increase their efforts to achieve or obtain something.

words.tr: phrase. 情况变得越来越糟；每况愈下
words.ex: Things went from bad to worse when it started to rain.
words.ex_cn: 情况本来已经不好，下雨后变得更糟了。
words.en: If a situation goes from bad to worse, it becomes even more unpleasant or unsatisfactory.

words.tr: phrase. 失去控制；出故障；变得混乱
words.ex: The computer went haywire when I opened the file.
words.ex_cn: 我打开文件时，电脑出问题了。
words.en: If a machine or a piece of equipment goes haywire, it stops working properly and starts to behave in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: phrase. 放纵狂欢；疯狂行事；尽情享受
words.ex: They go hog wild at the party every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他们每个星期五在派对上都疯狂起来。
words.en: To behave in a very excited and uncontrolled way, often in celebration or enjoyment.

words.w: go in one ear and out the other
words.tr: phrase. （信息）左耳进右耳出，听过后立刻忘记
words.uk: ɡəʊ ɪn wʌn ɪər ənd aʊt ði ˈʌðər
words.us: ɡoʊ ɪn wʌn ɪr ənd aʊt ði ˈʌðər
words.ex: When I tell him to clean his room, it goes in one ear and out the other.
words.ex_cn: 当我让他打扫房间时，他左耳进右耳出。
words.en: If something you hear goes in one ear and out the other, you do not remember it because you were not really listening or thinking about it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 急剧下降；骤然下跌（如经济、价格、情绪等）
words.ex: The plane went into a nose dive.
words.ex_cn: 飞机突然俯冲下去。
words.en: To go into a nose dive means to drop suddenly and steeply, or to deteriorate rapidly. It can be used both literally, as in the case of an aircraft, and figuratively, to describe situations or conditions that worsen quickly.

words.tr: phrase. （价格、数量等）急剧下降；猛跌；（飞机）俯冲
words.ex: The plane started to take a nose dive.
words.ex_cn: 飞机开始急剧下降。
words.en: To fall or drop suddenly and sharply.

words.tr: phrase. v. 失去控制；陷入混乱或恐慌状态
words.ex: When he saw the big dog, he went into a tailspin.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到那只大狗时，他慌了神。
words.en: To go into a tailspin means to lose control and become very confused or chaotic.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始生效；正式实施
words.ex: The new rule will go into effect next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新规则将于下周一生效。
words.en: To become active or start to be used.

words.tr: phrase. 生效；开始起作用
words.ex: The new rule will take effect next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新规则将在下周一生效。
words.en: If something takes effect, it begins to produce results or to work.

words.tr: phrase. 进入；加入；探究
words.ex: He goes into the room quietly.
words.ex_cn: 他悄悄地进入房间。
words.en: To enter a place, to start doing something as a job or activity, to investigate or examine something, or to discuss something in detail.

words.tr: phrase. 独自行动；单干；不依赖他人
words.ex: He decided to go it alone and start his own business.
words.ex_cn: 他决定独自一人创业。
words.en: To do something without help from anyone else.

words.tr: phrase. v. 进展顺利，有条不紊地进行，像时钟一样精确运转
words.ex: The party went like clockwork.
words.ex_cn: 聚会进行得非常顺利。
words.en: If a process or an event goes like clockwork, it happens exactly as it was planned, without any problems.

words.tr: phrase. v. 情绪失控；发狂；做出极端反应
words.ex: He went off the deep end when he heard the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到那个坏消息时，他情绪失控了。
words.en: To suddenly become very angry or lose control of one's emotions.

words.tr: phrase. 突然情绪失控；鲁莽行事；失去理智
words.ex: He jumped off the deep end when he quit his job to travel the world.
words.ex_cn: 他辞掉工作去环游世界，这举动太冲动了。
words.en: To do something suddenly and without thinking carefully about the consequences.

words.tr: 短语动词. 进行一次放纵行为，通常指大量饮酒或暴饮暴食
words.ex: He likes to go on a binge and watch all episodes of a TV show in one night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢连续看一整部电视剧的所有集，一晚上就看完了。
words.en: If someone goes on a binge, they do too much of something, such as drinking alcohol or eating, usually for a short period of time.

words.tr: phrase. 继续做某事
words.ex: Despite the difficulties, he decided to go on doing something to improve the situation.
words.ex_cn: 尽管困难重重，他决定继续做些事情来改善局面。
words.en: To continue an activity or task without stopping.

words.tr: phrase. 继续做
words.ex: She decided to go on with her studies despite the difficulties.
words.ex_cn: 尽管困难重重，她决定继续她的学业。
words.en: To continue doing something, especially after a pause or interruption.

words.tr: phrase. 继续下去；进行
words.ex: He goes on talking even when no one listens.
words.ex_cn: 即使没人听，他还是继续说。
words.en: To continue an activity or process, especially after a pause or interruption.

words.tr: 短语动词. 为获得某物而外出；参加…的选拔；追求某事物
words.ex: He often goes out for a walk after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他经常在晚饭后出去散步。
words.en: To leave your home or usual place to do something, especially for leisure or a specific purpose.

words.tr: phrase. 外出（娱乐）；熄灭
words.ex: They go out to watch a movie on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他们周末外出看电影。
words.en: To leave a place, especially one's home, for a short time, usually for a specific purpose such as entertainment or socializing.

words.w: go out of one's way to do sth.
words.tr: phrase. 特意做某事；不辞辛劳地去做某事
words.uk: ɡəʊ aʊt ɒv wʌns weɪ tə duː sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡoʊ aʊt əv wʌnz weɪ tə duː sʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: She went out of her way to help me with my project.
words.ex_cn: 她特意费力帮助我完成项目。
words.en: If you go out of your way to do something, you make a special effort to do it, especially something that is not convenient or that involves extra work.

words.tr: phrase. 特意；不辞辛劳地做某事
words.ex: He goes out of his way to help his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他特意去帮助他的朋友们。
words.en: To make a special effort to do something; to inconvenience oneself in order to do something for someone else.

words.w: go over like a lead balloon
words.tr: phrase. 彻底失败；不受欢迎；引起负面反应（通常指讲话或提议被冷遇或嘲笑）
words.ex: His joke went over like a lead balloon at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话在会议上反响很差。
words.en: If something goes over like a lead balloon, it is completely unsuccessful or unpopular.

words.tr: phrase. 超出某人的理解范围；被某人忽略；从某人头上越过
words.ex: The math problem went over his head.
words.ex_cn: 这道数学题他听不懂。
words.en: If something such as a joke or a piece of information goes over someone's head, it is too difficult for them to understand.

words.tr: phrase. 仔细检查；复习；重做；转向；受欢迎
words.ex: I will go over my homework tonight.
words.ex_cn: 我今晚会复习我的家庭作业。
words.en: To examine or review something carefully; to cross over something.

words.w: go over sth. with a fine-tooth comb
words.tr: 短语动词. 彻底检查某事；仔细审查每一个细节
words.uk: ɡəʊ ˈəʊvə θɪŋ ˈwɪð ə faɪn-tuːθ kəʊm
words.us: ɡoʊ ˈoʊvər θɪŋ ˈwɪð ə faɪn-tuːθ kəm
words.ex: She went over the report with a fine-tooth comb to ensure there were no errors.
words.ex_cn: 她仔细检查了报告，以确保没有错误。
words.en: To examine something very carefully and thoroughly.

words.w: search sth. with a fine-tooth comb
words.tr: phrase. 用细齿梳子搜寻某物；比喻极其仔细、彻底地搜查或检查某事物
words.uk: sɜːtʃ sʌmθɪŋ wɪð ə faɪn-tuːθ kəʊm
words.us: sɝːtʃ sʌmθɪŋ wɪð ə faɪn-tuːθ koʊm
words.ex: The police searched the house with a fine-tooth comb, but found no clues.
words.ex_cn: 警方彻底搜查了房子，但没有发现任何线索。
words.en: To examine something very thoroughly and meticulously for details or errors.

words.tr: 短语动词. 给人留下深刻印象；大获成功；以引人注目的方式完成
words.ex: They want to go over with a bang at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他们想在派对上大出风头。
words.en: To be very successful or popular.

words.tr: phrase. v. 过分；做得太过分；全力以赴
words.ex: He went overboard with the decorations for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对装饰得太过分了。
words.en: To do something to an excessive or extreme degree, often beyond what is considered reasonable or necessary.

words.tr: 短语动词. 取得成功；有前途；有所作为
words.ex: With his talent and hard work, he's definitely going to go places.
words.ex_cn: 凭借他的才华和努力，他一定会取得成功。
words.en: To achieve success or to have a promising future.

words.tr: phrase. 逍遥法外；毫发无损地逃脱惩罚
words.ex: Despite the evidence against him, he managed to go scot-free.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有证据对他不利，他还是设法逃避了惩罚。
words.en: To escape punishment or avoid paying a penalty.

words.tr: phrase. v. 无惩罚地逃脱；毫发无损地脱身
words.ex: He got off scot-free after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后毫发无损地逃脱了。
words.en: To escape punishment or avoid the consequences of one's actions.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 迅速上升；猛涨；飙升
words.ex: The balloons go sky high in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 气球在风中飞得很高。
words.en: To rise to an extremely high level, often dramatically or unexpectedly.

words.tr: 短语动词. 坚持到底；完成全程；不放弃直到成功
words.ex: Despite the tough conditions, the marathon runner was determined to go the distance.
words.ex_cn: 尽管条件艰苦，马拉松选手决心坚持到底。
words.en: To continue doing something until it is finished, especially something that is difficult or takes a long time.

words.tr: phrase. 经历；仔细检查；完成；通过；穿过
words.ex: He went through a hard time last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年经历了一段艰难的时光。
words.en: To experience something, often something difficult or unpleasant, or to examine or discuss something in detail.

words.tr: phrase. v. 通过正规途径办理；经由正常渠道进行
words.ex: If you want to get approval for your project, you'll need to go through channels.
words.ex_cn: 如果你想获得项目的批准，你需要按程序办理。
words.en: To follow the official and proper procedures to achieve something, especially in a bureaucratic or organizational context.

words.tr: 短语动词. 做表面功夫；敷衍了事；机械地完成动作（而没有真正投入感情或兴趣）
words.ex: He just goes through the motions at work because he doesn't like his job.
words.ex_cn: 他上班只是走个过场，因为他不喜欢他的工作。
words.en: If you say that someone is going through the motions, you mean that they are doing something because they have to or because they are expected to, but without any real interest, enthusiasm, or effort.

words.tr: 短语动词. （价格、情绪等）急剧上升，飙升
words.ex: When the team won, prices went through the roof.
words.ex_cn: 当球队获胜时，价格飞涨。
words.en: To increase very quickly or to become very angry.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 坚持做完某事；完成（困难或不愉快的事）
words.ex: She decided to go through with the surgery despite the risks.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有风险，她还是决定做手术。
words.en: To complete or carry out something, especially something that is difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr: 短语动词. 不惜一切代价；尽一切努力；用尽各种手段
words.ex: He will go to any length to protect his family.
words.ex_cn: 他会不遗余力地保护他的家人。
words.en: If someone is willing to go to any length, they are willing to do anything, no matter how extreme, to achieve their goal.

words.tr: 短语动词. 为某人挺身而出；支持或捍卫某人
words.ex: She always goes to bat for her colleagues when they are in trouble.
words.ex_cn: 每当同事们遇到麻烦时，她总是为他们出头。
words.en: To support or defend someone, especially in a difficult situation.

words.w: go to bed with the chickens
words.tr: phrase. 比喻很早就上床睡觉，像鸡一样早睡（鸡天黑就归巢）
words.uk: ɡəʊ tuː bed wɪð ðə ˈtʃɪkɪnz
words.us: ɡoʊ tuː bed wɪð ðə ˈtʃɪkɪnz
words.ex: In the village, she goes to bed with the chickens.
words.ex_cn: 在村里，她和鸡一起睡觉。
words.en: To go to bed very early, at the same time as chickens go to roost.

words.tr: phrase. 去死吧；见鬼去吧；滚蛋
words.ex: If you don't like it, you can go to hell!
words.ex_cn: 如果你不喜欢，你可以去死！
words.en: An expression of anger or contempt, used to tell someone to go away or that you do not care about them.

words.tr: phrase. 见鬼去吧；下地狱去；完蛋吧（用于表达愤怒或轻蔑）
words.ex: I told him to go to the devil when he asked for more money.
words.ex_cn: 当他要更多钱时，我叫他去见鬼。
words.en: An expression used to tell someone to go away or to express anger or frustration towards someone.

words.w: go to hell in a handbasket
words.tr: phrase. 迅速恶化或走向灾难；每况愈下
words.uk: ɡəʊ tu hel ɪn ə ˈhændbɑːskɪt
words.us: ɡoʊ tu hɛl ɪn ə ˈhændbæskɪt
words.ex: If we don't fix the problems, things will go to hell in a handbasket.
words.ex_cn: 如果我们不解决问题，事情就会迅速变糟。
words.en: To deteriorate or decline rapidly and uncontrollably.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 情绪崩溃；失去控制；瓦解
words.ex: He goes to pieces when he sees a spider.
words.ex_cn: 他一看到蜘蛛就崩溃了。
words.en: To become so upset or nervous that you cannot control yourself or think clearly.

words.tr: phrase. v. （指成功、赞美或酒精等）使人变得骄傲、轻狂或头晕；使某人头脑发热
words.ex: Success can sometimes go to one's head and make them lose sight of their goals.
words.ex_cn: 成功有时会使人骄傲自满，让他们忘记了自己的目标。
words.en: If something such as success or praise goes to someone's head, it makes them feel proud and confident in a way that makes them less pleasant or less effective.

words.tr: phrase. 糟蹋；毁掉；荒废（指事物变坏或被浪费）
words.ex: If no one takes care of the garden, it will go to pot.
words.ex_cn: 如果没人照料这个花园，它就会荒废掉。
words.en: If something goes to pot, it becomes much worse than it was, often because it has not been properly looked after.

words.tr: phrase. 走向衰败；变得糟糕；每况愈下
words.ex: The garden went to the dogs after no one took care of it.
words.ex_cn: 花园在无人照料后就荒废了。
words.en: To deteriorate or decline in condition, quality, or character.

words.w: go to the expense of doing sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 花费代价做某事；不惜花钱或付出努力做某事
words.uk: ɡəʊ tə ðə ɪkˈspens əv ˈduːɪŋ sth.
words.us: ɡoʊ tə ðə ɪkˈspɛns əv ˈduɪŋ sth.
words.ex: He went to the expense of buying a new car just to impress his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他为了给朋友们留下深刻印象，不惜花费买了一辆新车。
words.en: To incur the cost or financial burden of doing something, often reluctantly.

words.tr: 短语动词. 花费金钱；承担费用
words.ex: They decided to go to the expense of hiring a professional photographer for the event.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定为这次活动花费聘请一位专业摄影师。
words.en: To spend money on something, especially when it is considered a lot of money.

words.tr: 短语动词. 坚持到极限；尽最大努力；做到极致
words.ex: He decided to go to the limit in his next project to prove his abilities.
words.ex_cn: 他决定在下一个项目中尽力而为，以证明自己的能力。
words.en: To push oneself or something to the maximum possible extent or degree.

words.w: go to the trouble of doing sth.
words.tr: phrase. 不辞劳苦做某事；费心做某事
words.uk: ɡəʊ tuː ðə ˈtrʌbl əv ˈduːɪŋ sɒmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡoʊ tu ðə ˈtrʌbl əv ˈduːɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: She went to the trouble of preparing a special meal for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 她不辞辛劳地为他生日准备了一顿特别的饭菜。
words.en: If you go to the trouble of doing something, you make a special effort to do it, even though it involves some work or difficulty.

words.w: go to the trouble to do sth.
words.tr: phrase. 特意费心做某事；不辞劳苦地去做某事
words.uk: ɡəʊ tuː ðə ˈtrʌbl tuː duː ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡoʊ tu ðə ˈtrʌbl tu du ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: She went to the trouble to organize a surprise party for him.
words.ex_cn: 她费心为他组织了一个惊喜派对。
words.en: If you go to the trouble to do something, you make a special effort to do it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 不辞劳苦做某事；费心做某事
words.ex: He went to the trouble to help his friend fix the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他费心帮朋友修自行车。
words.en: To make a considerable effort to do something, especially when inconvenient.

words.tr: phrase. v. 破产；失败；垮台
words.ex: If the business keeps losing money, it will go to the wall.
words.ex_cn: 如果企业继续亏钱，它就会倒闭。
words.en: To be defeated or ruined, especially in a financial or competitive context.

words.tr: phrase. 尽情地做某事；大力地进行；全力以赴地处理
words.ex: We will go to town to buy some food.
words.ex_cn: 我们将去镇上买些食物。
words.en: To do something with great energy, enthusiasm, or thoroughness.

words.tr: phrase. v. 一起发生；相配；协调；共同行动
words.ex: These colors really go together well.
words.ex_cn: 这些颜色真的很相配。
words.en: If two things go together, they are suitable or harmonious when used or put together.

words.tr: phrase. v. 走得太远；做得过分
words.ex: He went too far when he broke his sister's toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他弄坏他妹妹的玩具时，他做得太过分了。
words.en: To go beyond what is reasonable or acceptable.

words.tr: phrase. 沉没；死；屈服；失败；破产
words.ex: The boat went under after hitting the rock.
words.ex_cn: 船撞上岩石后沉没了。
words.en: To fail, collapse, or be defeated; to sink or submerge.

words.tr: 短语动词. 用来表明或证明某事；显示
words.ex: The results go to show that practice helps.
words.ex_cn: 结果表明，练习是有帮助的。
words.en: To demonstrate or prove something; to serve as evidence.

words.tr: phrase. 接受手术；动手术
words.ex: She had to go under the knife for a serious knee injury.
words.ex_cn: 她因严重的膝盖受伤不得不接受手术。
words.en: To undergo a surgical operation.

words.tr: phrase. v. 彻底失败；付之一炬；突然爆发（通常指灾难性地失败或毁灭）
words.ex: The old house went up in flames last night.
words.ex_cn: 那栋老房子昨晚烧毁了。
words.en: If something goes up in flames, it is destroyed by fire or fails completely.

words.tr: phrase. 化为乌有；付之一炬；失败或落空（通常指计划、努力等）
words.ex: All his plans went up in smoke when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失去工作后，所有的计划都化为泡影了。
words.en: If something goes up in smoke, it fails or ends without achieving anything, often in a way that is sudden or unexpected.

words.tr: phrase. 完全投入；全力以赴；彻底地做某事
words.ex: When it comes to planning his daughter's wedding, he decided to go whole hog and hire the best caterer in town.
words.ex_cn: 当涉及到计划他女儿的婚礼时，他决定全力以赴，并聘请了镇上最好的餐饮服务。
words.en: To do something as completely or thoroughly as possible, without holding back.

words.tr: phrase. 不言而喻；无需多说
words.ex: It goes without saying that water is important for life.
words.ex_cn: 不言而喻，水对生命很重要。
words.en: If something goes without saying, it is generally accepted or understood without needing to be stated.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词GO补充词组

words.tr: phrase. 继续；进行（go on 的过去分词形式）
words.ex: The project has gone on for months without any progress.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目已经进行了几个月，但没有任何进展。
words.en: To continue doing something, especially after a pause or interruption.

words.tr: phrase. 对……着迷；热衷于……（通常指对某人或某事物非常喜爱或迷恋）
words.ex: She's really gone on him, you can see it in her eyes.
words.ex_cn: 她真的非常喜欢他，你从她的眼神里就能看出来。
words.en: To be very fond of or infatuated with someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 追逐；追求
words.ex: He goes after his dreams every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天追求自己的梦想。
words.en: To pursue or chase someone or something, often with the intention of catching or achieving them.

words.w: go all the way to sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 完全支持某事；做到最后；一直做到某事的终点或极限
words.uk: ɡəʊ ɔːl ðə weɪ tuː ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡoʊ ɔːl ðə weɪ tuː ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: They decided to go all the way to the top of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定一直走到山顶。
words.en: To continue to a particular destination or to achieve a particular goal, despite difficulties.

words.tr: phrase. 完全参与到底；坚持到最后；（俚语）发生性关系
words.ex: He decided to go all the way and run for president.
words.ex_cn: 他决定全力以赴，竞选总统。
words.en: To proceed or continue to the ultimate conclusion or the farthest possible point.

words.tr: 短语动词. 陪同前往；随行；参与某事而不主动主导
words.ex: He didn't want to plan anything, so he just decided to go along for the ride.
words.ex_cn: 他不想做任何计划，所以就决定随大流了。
words.en: To participate in an activity without taking an active role or without having a strong interest in it.

words.tr: phrase. 一起去；赞同；附和
words.ex: I will go along with you to the park.
words.ex_cn: 我会和你一起去公园。
words.en: To agree with or support someone or something; to accompany someone.

words.tr: phrase. 前进； 进行；赞同
words.ex: The car went along the road slowly.
words.ex_cn: 汽车缓慢地沿着路前进。
words.en: To proceed or continue with something, especially a plan or activity; to agree with or support an idea, proposal, etc.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 向…扑去；攻击；着手处理
words.ex: The dog went at the mailman with barking.
words.ex_cn: 那只狗朝邮递员扑了过去。
words.en: To attack or to start doing something with energy.

words.tr: phrase. 回去
words.ex: He will go back to his hometown next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会回他的家乡。
words.en: To return to a place or situation that you were in before.

words.tr: phrase. v. （计划、想法等）彻底失败，被抛弃；作废
words.ex: The old rules went by the board when the new manager arrived.
words.ex_cn: 新经理一到，旧规则就被抛弃了。
words.en: To be abandoned or ignored, especially as a result of changing circumstances.

words.tr: phrase. 被忽视；被放弃；被遗忘；失去机会
words.ex: He will pass by the board on his way to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在去开会的路上会经过这块板。
words.en: To be abandoned, ignored, or to fail.

words.tr: 短语动词. （非正式，常带讽刺或愤怒）去干点别的事吧，别烦我；滚开
words.ex: I'm busy right now, so go chase yourself!
words.ex_cn: v. 我现在很忙，所以走开，别烦我！
words.en: An informal, often rude way to tell someone to go away or leave you alone.

words.tr: 习语. 去做不可能的事吧；滚开吧（用于表达不耐烦或拒绝）
words.ex: Why don't you go fly a kite instead of bothering me?
words.ex_cn: v. 你为什么不走开去放风筝，而不是烦我？
words.en: An informal way to tell someone to go away or stop bothering you, often used in a playful or joking manner.

words.tr: phrase. 选择；追求；努力争取
words.ex: I want to go for the blue shirt.
words.ex_cn: 我对那件蓝色的衬衫感兴趣。
words.en: If you go for something, you choose it or try to achieve it.

words.tr: 短语动词. 进展迅速；全力推进；非常成功地进行
words.ex: He went great guns at his new job and finished all tasks in one day.
words.ex_cn: 他在新工作中干劲十足，一天内就完成了所有任务。
words.en: To proceed or perform with great speed, energy, or success.

words.tr: 短语动词. 成群结队地去；集体前往
words.ex: The employees decided to go in a body to ask for a raise.
words.ex_cn: 员工们决定全体出动去要求加薪。
words.en: To go somewhere together as a group or collectively.

words.tr: phrase. v. 喜欢；参加（某项活动）；从事
words.ex: He decided to go in for the marathon.
words.ex_cn: 他决定参加马拉松比赛。
words.en: If you go in for a particular activity, you decide to do it as a hobby or interest.

words.tr: 短语动词. 开始行动；投入行动；开始发挥作用
words.ex: The army will go into action at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 军队将在黎明时分投入战斗。
words.en: To begin to act or operate; to start doing something.

words.tr: phrase. 迅速开始行动；立即采取行动
words.ex: When the fire alarm rang, the firefighters swung into action.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，消防员立即行动起来。
words.en: To start doing something quickly and energetically, especially in response to a situation that requires immediate action.

words.w: go into one's song and dance about sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事老调重弹地大谈特谈，通常指令人厌烦的解释或借口
words.uk: ɡəʊ ˈɪntuː wʌnz sɒŋ ənd dɑːns əˈbaʊt sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡoʊ ˈɪntuː wʌnz sɔːŋ ənd dæns əˈbaʊt sʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: Whenever we ask him about his project, he goes into his song and dance about the details.
words.ex_cn: 每当我们问他关于他的项目时，他就开始详细解释其中的细节。
words.en: To explain or describe something in great detail, often in a way that is intended to impress or persuade.

words.tr: 短语动词. 进入轨道；（引申义）极度兴奋或愤怒
words.ex: The satellite will go into orbit around Earth.
words.ex_cn: 这颗卫星将进入地球轨道。
words.en: To enter into a state of great success or popularity, or literally, to enter into the path around a celestial body.

words.tr: phrase. 爆炸；离去；响起
words.ex: The firework went off at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 烟花在午夜爆炸了。
words.en: If a device or alarm goes off, it starts to ring loudly or make a loud noise. To leave a place, especially in order to do something. To happen in a particular way. To stop liking someone or something. To explode or fire. To decay or become rotten.

words.tr: phrase. adj. 草率行事的；未准备充分就行动的
words.ex: He went off half-cocked without checking the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他没有核实事实就匆忙行动了。
words.en: To act without proper preparation or thought, often leading to mistakes or failure.

words.tr: phrase. 继续下去；进行
words.ex: He goes on talking even when no one listens.
words.ex_cn: 即使没人听，他还是继续说。
words.en: To continue an activity or process, especially after a pause or interruption.

words.tr: 短语动词. 进行无明确目标的搜查或调查，通常指在没有充分证据的情况下试图找出问题或错误；引申为试图套取信息
words.ex: The journalist decided to go on a fishing expedition to uncover more details about the scandal.
words.ex_cn: 记者决定进行试探性调查，以揭露更多关于丑闻的细节。
words.en: To engage in a search or investigation with the hope of discovering information, often without a clear idea of what one is looking for.

words.tr: phrase. v. 不停地继续；喋喋不休；冗长地持续
words.ex: He goes on and on about his dog.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地讲他的狗。
words.en: To continue doing or saying something for a long time, often in a way that is annoying or boring.

words.tr: phrase. 进行罢工
words.ex: The workers go on strike to ask for higher pay.
words.ex_cn: 工人们罢工以要求加薪。
words.en: To stop work as a form of protest, typically in an attempt to gain a particular concession or concessions from their employer.

words.tr: 短语动词. 罢工；举行罢工行动
words.ex: The workers decided to go out on strike to demand better wages.
words.ex_cn: 工人们决定罢工，以要求提高工资。
words.en: To stop working as a form of protest, typically to achieve better pay or conditions.

words.tr: 短语动词. 做得更进一步；比某人做得更好；胜人一筹
words.ex: She decided to go one better and won the competition.
words.ex_cn: 她决定做得更好，并赢得了比赛。
words.en: To do something better than someone else, especially in a competitive way.

words.tr: 短语动词. 胜过某人；做得比某人更好；超越
words.ex: He baked a cake, and she did him one better by making a three-layer chocolate cake.
words.ex_cn: 他烤了一个蛋糕，她更进一步，做了一个三层巧克力蛋糕。
words.en: To surpass someone or something by doing something in a superior way.

words.tr: 短语动词. 出去寻找；外出搜寻
words.ex: They decided to go out in search of food after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨过后，他们决定外出寻找食物。
words.en: To venture out to find or look for something.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人约会；和某人一起外出
words.ex: She decided to go out with him after he asked her on a date.
words.ex_cn: 他在约她出去后，她决定和他约会。
words.en: To go out with someone means to have a romantic relationship with them.

words.tr: phrase. v. 彻底穿透某人；给某人带来强烈的感受（如恐惧或寒意）
words.ex: The news went right through him and left him feeling numb.
words.ex_cn: 这个消息对他产生了强烈影响，让他感到麻木。
words.en: To be fully understood or comprehended by someone.

words.tr: phrase. adj. 变得疯狂或失去理智；精神错乱
words.ex: If you keep pushing him, he's going to go round the bend.
words.ex_cn: 如果你继续逼他，他会发疯的。
words.en: To become very angry or to go crazy.

words.tr: phrase. v. 发疯；精神失常；变得疯狂
words.ex: If you have to work with him any longer, you'll go around the bend.
words.ex_cn: 如果你还要和他一起工作更长时间，你会发疯的。
words.en: To become extremely angry or to lose one's sanity.

words.w: go so far as to say sth.
words.tr: 短语动词，意为‘甚至说出……’，用于强调某人说了某件出人意料或极端的话
words.uk: ɡəʊ səʊ fɑːr əz tuː seɪ
words.us: ɡoʊ soʊ fɑr əz tu seɪ
words.ex: He went so far as to say that the project was a complete failure.
words.ex_cn: 他甚至说这个项目完全失败了。
words.en: To express an opinion or make a statement that is very strong or extreme.

words.tr: phrase. 独自参加社交活动（尤指舞会或聚会），不带伴侣
words.ex: He decided to go stag to the party because he didn't have a date.
words.ex_cn: 他决定独自参加派对，因为他没有约会对象。
words.en: To attend a social event, especially a party or dance, without a companion, typically used for men not bringing a female partner.

words.tr: phrase. v. 与某人正式交往；与某人保持稳定的恋爱关系
words.ex: She decided to go steady with him after dating for a year.
words.ex_cn: 在约会一年后，她决定与他保持稳定的恋爱关系。
words.en: To have a steady romantic relationship with someone.

words.tr: phrase. v. （情侣）正式交往，稳定约会
words.ex: They have gone steady for three months.
words.ex_cn: 他们已经稳定交往三个月了。
words.en: To maintain a stable and exclusive romantic relationship with someone.

words.tr: phrase. v. 变得因被监禁或困在狭小空间而烦躁不安或发疯
words.ex: After being stuck at home for weeks due to the pandemic, many people started to go stir crazy.
words.ex_cn: 由于疫情被困在家中数周后，许多人开始变得极度烦躁不安。
words.en: To become extremely restless or anxious due to confinement or lack of activity.

words.tr: phrase. v. 直走；改过自新，走上正路
words.ex: Go straight to the park.
words.ex_cn: 直走到公园。
words.en: To move forward in a straight line without turning.

words.tr: 短语动词. 竭尽全力；做到极限；坚持到最后
words.ex: He will go the limit to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他会全力以赴赢得比赛。
words.en: To do something to the fullest extent; to give one's maximum effort.

words.tr: phrase. 经历；仔细检查；完成；通过；穿过
words.ex: He went through a hard time last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年经历了一段艰难的时光。
words.en: To experience something, often something difficult or unpleasant, or to examine or discuss something in detail.

words.tr: 短语动词. 经历变化；仔细检查变更内容
words.ex: We will go through the changes step by step.
words.ex_cn: 我们将一步一步地经历这些变化。
words.en: To experience a series of difficult or transformative events.

words.tr: phrase. 去见阎王；沉入海底（常用于形容船只沉没或人溺亡）
words.ex: The old ship went to Davy Jones's locker after sinking in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船在暴风雨中沉没后去了戴维·琼斯的 locker。
words.en: To be lost at sea; to sink to the bottom of the ocean.

words.tr: phrase. 毁灭；衰败；陷入混乱
words.ex: The old house will go to rack and ruin if no one repairs it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没有人修理，这栋老房子就会变得破败不堪。
words.en: To deteriorate or decay, especially through neglect.

words.tr: phrase. 破产；衰败；毁坏；陷入混乱
words.ex: The old house will go to wrack and ruin if no one fixes it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没有人修理，这栋老房子将会破败不堪。
words.en: To deteriorate or collapse into a state of disrepair or destruction.

words.tr: 短语动词. 去上厕所；去洗手间
words.ex: He excused himself to go to the bathroom.
words.ex_cn: 他借口去上厕所。
words.en: To use the toilet for urination or defecation.

words.tr: phrase. 被浪费；白费；徒劳
words.ex: Don't let all your efforts go to waste.
words.ex_cn: 不要让你的所有努力都白费。
words.en: If something goes to waste, it is not used and is therefore wasted.

words.tr: phrase. 上升；增长；升起
words.ex: The price of apples will go up next week.
words.ex_cn: 苹果的价格将在下周上涨。
words.en: If a price, amount, or level goes up, it becomes higher or greater than it was.

words.tr: phrase. 伴随；与...相配；同…一致
words.ex: I will go with you to the market.
words.ex_cn: 我会和你一起去市场。
words.en: To be suitable or appropriate with something; to accompany something; to exist or occur together with something.

words.tr: phrase. v. 没有……也勉强过；在缺乏某物的情况下生活或继续
words.ex: He went without breakfast to save time.
words.ex_cn: 他为了节省时间没吃早餐。
words.en: If you go without something that you need or usually have, you do not get it or have it.

words.tr: phrase. 出错； 发生故障；误入歧途
words.ex: Things can go wrong if you don't follow the instructions.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不按照说明做，事情可能会出错。
words.en: If a situation or event goes wrong, it does not happen in the way you intended or expected, and often has a bad result.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 9 基本动词 HAVE

words.tr: phrase. 过得愉快，玩得开心
words.ex: We have a ball at the party every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我们每周末在派对上玩得很开心。
words.en: If you have a ball, you enjoy yourself very much.

words.tr: phrase. v. 多嘴的；爱说闲话的；管不住嘴的
words.ex: He has a big mouth, so everyone knows his secrets.
words.ex_cn: 他嘴巴不严，所以大家都知道他的秘密。
words.en: To talk too much or to reveal secrets, especially when one should not.

words.w: have a bone to pick with sb.
words.tr: phrase. 对某人有意见要理论；对某人有不满要讨个说法
words.uk: hæv ə bəʊn tə pɪk wɪð sʌmbədi
words.us: hæv ə boʊn tə pɪk wɪð ˈsʌmbədi
words.ex: I have a bone to pick with you about the late delivery.
words.ex_cn: 关于延迟交货的事，我有话要对你说。
words.en: To have a disagreement or complaint that one wants to discuss with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 有意见要提出；有怨言要申诉（通常指对某事感到不满并想争论）
words.ex: I have a bone to pick with you about the project deadline.
words.ex_cn: 关于项目截止日期，我有话要和你讨论。
words.en: To have a reason to disagree or be annoyed with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 与……有短暂或轻微的接触；侥幸逃脱（危险或麻烦）
words.ex: He had a brush with the law when he was young.
words.ex_cn: 他年轻时曾与法律有过一次小冲突。
words.en: To have a brief encounter or conflict with someone or something.

words.w: have a chip on one's shoulder
words.tr: phrase. 怀有怨恨或不满，常指因过去受到不公对待而对他人抱有敌意或容易生气
words.uk: hæv ə tʃɪp ɒn wʌnz ˈʃəʊldə(r)
words.us: hæv ə tʃɪp ɑːn wʌnz ˈʃoʊldər
words.ex: He has a chip on his shoulder because people laughed at him when he was young.
words.ex_cn: 他心里有怨气，因为小时候别人嘲笑过他。
words.en: To be habitually angry or resentful as a result of a perceived grievance or sense of inferiority.

words.tr: 短语动词. 刮得很干净的胡子；也有‘险些发生意外’的引申义，如‘九死一生’
words.ex: He had a close shave this morning and cut himself.
words.ex_cn: 他今天早上刮胡子刮得很仔细，结果划伤了自己。
words.en: To narrowly avoid an accident or disaster.

words.tr: 短语动词. 九死一生；侥幸脱险；差点发生意外
words.ex: He had a close call when the car almost hit him.
words.ex_cn: 他的车差点撞到他，真是千钧一发。
words.en: To narrowly avoid an accident or disaster.

words.tr: 短语动词. 九死一生；侥幸逃脱（危险或灾难）
words.ex: He had a narrow escape when the car almost hit him.
words.ex_cn: 当那辆车差点撞到他时，他死里逃生。
words.en: To narrowly avoid danger or an unpleasant situation.

words.tr: 短语. 听起来很熟悉；似曾相识
words.ex: That story has a familiar ring to me.
words.ex_cn: 那个故事听起来很熟悉。
words.en: To sound familiar or to seem like something one has heard before.

words.tr: phrase. 气得发疯；大动肝火；惊慌失措
words.ex: My mom will have a fit if she sees my messy room.
words.ex_cn: 如果我妈妈看到我乱糟糟的房间，她会大发脾气的。
words.en: To become very angry or upset about something.

words.tr: phrase. 大发脾气；歇斯底里地发作
words.ex: He throws a fit when he doesn't get his way.
words.ex_cn: 当他不能如愿时，他就会大发脾气。
words.en: To suddenly become very angry or upset.

words.tr: 短语动词. 尝试做某事；对某事进行尝试
words.ex: Why don't you have a go at solving the problem?
words.ex_cn: 你为什么不试试解决这个问题呢？
words.en: To attempt or try to do something, especially when it is something new or challenging.

words.tr: phrase. 尝试一下；试一试（做某事）
words.ex: I will have a go at solving this math problem.
words.ex_cn: 我会试着解这道数学题。
words.en: To attempt or try something.

words.w: have a good command of sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事物有很好的掌握或精通，通常用于语言或技能方面
words.uk: hæv ə ɡʊd kəˈmɑːnd əv sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv ə ɡʊd kəˈmænd əv sʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: She has a good command of English, which helps her in her international business dealings.
words.ex_cn: 她精通英语，这对她的国际商务交易很有帮助。
words.en: To have a good command of something means to be able to use, understand, or perform it very well.

words.w: have a good head on one's shoulders
words.tr: phrase. 形容某人头脑聪明、明智、有判断力
words.uk: hæv ə ɡʊd hed ɒn wʌnz ˈʃəʊldəz
words.us: hæv ə ɡʊd hɛd ɑn wʌnz ˈʃoʊldərz
words.ex: He has a good head on his shoulders and always makes smart choices.
words.ex_cn: 他头脑聪明，总是做出明智的选择。
words.en: To be sensible and able to make good decisions.

words.tr: phrase. 情况进展顺利；拥有正在成功发展的好局面
words.ex: You have a good thing going with your new business, keep it up!
words.ex_cn: 你的新生意发展得很好，继续保持！
words.en: To be in a successful or advantageous situation or arrangement.

words.tr: 短语动词. 有园艺天赋；擅长种植植物
words.ex: She must have a green thumb because her garden is always so beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 她一定擅长园艺，因为她的花园总是那么美丽。
words.en: To have a natural talent for gardening and the ability to make plants grow well.

words.tr: 短语动词，表示劝人发发慈悲、同情或善良一点，常用于恳求或劝说的语境中
words.ex: Have a heart and help the poor child.
words.ex_cn: 发发慈悲，帮帮那个可怜的孩子吧。
words.en: If you say 'Have a heart' to someone, you are asking them to be compassionate or sympathetic.

words.tr: phrase. 形容某人心地善良，非常慷慨和富有同情心
words.ex: My grandma is so kind; she has a heart of gold.
words.ex_cn: 我奶奶非常善良；她有一颗金子般的心。
words.en: To be very kind and generous.

words.tr: phrase. 心肠硬的；铁石心肠的
words.ex: He never helps anyone; he must have a heart of stone.
words.ex_cn: 他从不帮助别人；他一定铁石心肠。
words.en: To be very cold and unfeeling; to lack sympathy or compassion.

words.tr: adj. 率直的；诚实的; n. 谈心；坦诚的心里话
words.ex: We had a heart-to-heart conversation about our future plans.
words.ex_cn: 我们就未来的计划进行了一次坦诚的谈话。
words.en: A heart-to-heart is a conversation in which two people talk honestly and openly about their feelings and personal matters.

words.w: have a lot going for one
words.tr: 短语. 指某人拥有许多有利条件或优势，如才华、外貌、机会等，使他/她容易成功或受人喜爱
words.uk: hæv ə lɒt ˈɡəʊɪŋ fɔː wʌn
words.us: hæv ə lɑːt ˈɡoʊɪŋ fɔːr wʌn
words.ex: He has a lot going for him, like a good job and great friends.
words.ex_cn: 他有很多优势，比如一份好工作和很棒的朋友。
words.en: To possess many advantages or favorable qualities.

words.tr: 短语动词. 忙碌的；有很多事情在同时进行；生活或工作中充满各种活动或问题
words.ex: I can't make it to the meeting today; I have a lot going on.
words.ex_cn: 我今天不能参加会议了，我有很多事情要处理。
words.en: To be very busy or have many activities or responsibilities.

words.tr: 短语. 有很多潜力；很有前途
words.ex: The young athlete has a lot of promise.
words.ex_cn: 这名年轻运动员很有前途。
words.en: To show great potential or likelihood of future success.

words.w: have a lot on one's mind
words.tr: 短语动词. 心事重重；有很多事情在考虑中
words.uk: hæv ə lɒt ɒn wʌnz maɪnd
words.us: hæv ə lɑːt ɑːn wʌnz maɪnd
words.ex: He has a lot on his mind because of the exam tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 因为他明天有考试，所以心里有很多事。
words.en: To be preoccupied with many thoughts or concerns.

words.tr: 短语动词. 沸点低，指物质在较低温度下沸腾的性质
words.ex: The liquid has a low boiling point, so it turns to vapor quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种液体的沸点很低，所以很快就会变成蒸汽。
words.en: If someone has a low boiling point, they easily become angry.

words.tr: phrase. 侥幸脱险；几乎发生的意外；差点相撞；接近成功却最终失败
words.ex: The plane had a near miss with the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 飞机险些撞上山。
words.en: A near miss is an incident that might have resulted in an accident or injury but did not, often used to describe situations in aviation, military, and other contexts where precision and timing are critical.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事物有强烈的喜好或倾向；偏爱某事物
words.ex: She has a penchant for collecting rare books.
words.ex_cn: 她特别喜欢收藏珍本书。
words.en: If someone has a penchant for something, they have a special liking for it or a tendency to do it.

words.w: have a penchant for doing sth.
words.tr: phrase. 对做某事有强烈的偏好或倾向；热衷于做某事
words.uk: hæv ə ˈpentʃənt fə ˈduːɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv ə ˈpentʃənt fɔr ˈduːɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: She has a penchant for collecting rare stamps.
words.ex_cn: 她热衷于收集稀有邮票。
words.en: To have a strong liking or tendency to do a particular thing.

words.w: have a price on one's head
words.tr: 短语动词。指某人被悬赏捉拿或被追杀，通常因为犯罪或成为目标
words.ex: The criminal has a price on his head because the police want him caught.
words.ex_cn: 这个罪犯被通缉，因为警方想抓住他。
words.en: To be wanted by the authorities, with a reward offered for one's capture.

words.w: have a rough time of it
words.tr: 短语动词. 经历一段艰难的时期；过得不容易
words.ex: He has a rough time of it at school because he is new.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校过得不容易，因为他是新来的。
words.en: to experience a difficult period

words.tr: 短语动词. 经历一段艰难的时期；过得不容易
words.ex: He had a rough time at school last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年在学校过得很艰难。
words.en: To experience a period of difficulty or hardship.

words.tr: phrase. 有点疯疯癫癫的；头脑不正常；行为古怪
words.ex: He must have a screw loose to think that plan would work.
words.ex_cn: 他一定是疯了，才会认为那个计划可行。
words.en: To be slightly crazy or not thinking clearly.

words.tr: phrase. 头脑有问题的；有点疯疯癫癫的
words.ex: He must have a screw missing to think that was a good idea.
words.ex_cn: 他一定是有点精神不正常才会认为那是个好主意。
words.en: An idiom used to describe someone who behaves in a strange or irrational manner, suggesting they are not mentally sound.

words.w: have a snowball's chance in hell
words.tr: phrase. 毫无机会，绝对不可能成功（常用于否定句，表示某事完全不可能发生）
words.uk: hæv ə ˈsnəʊbɔːlz tʃɑːns ɪn hel
words.us: hæv ə ˈsnoʊbɔːlz tʃæns ɪn hel
words.ex: He has a snowball's chance in hell of winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛的机会微乎其微。
words.en: If you say that someone doesn't have a snowball's chance in hell of doing something, you are emphasizing that they have no chance at all of doing it.

words.w: have a soft spot in one's heart for ...
words.tr: phrase. 对……怀有温柔的情感；内心深处特别喜欢……
words.uk: hæv ə sɒft spɒt ɪn wʌnz hɑːt fɔː
words.us: hæv ə sɔːft spɑːt ɪn wʌnz hɑːrt fɔːr
words.ex: I have a soft spot in my heart for old movies.
words.ex_cn: 我对老电影有着特别的喜爱。
words.en: To have a particular fondness or affection for someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 爱吃甜品
words.ex: She has a sweet tooth and eats candy every day.
words.ex_cn: 她爱吃甜食，每天都要吃糖果。
words.en: If you have a sweet tooth, you like eating sweet foods, especially sweets and chocolate.

words.tr: phrase. 对……特别在意；对……有特殊感觉（通常指某种偏执或强烈情绪）
words.ex: He has a thing about keeping his room clean.
words.ex_cn: 他特别在意保持房间干净。
words.en: If you have a thing about something, you have a strong feeling or opinion about it, often one that is not shared by other people.

words.w: have a thing going with sb.
words.tr: 短语动词. 与某人有某种暧昧关系或正在发展某种特殊感情关系
words.uk: hæv ə θɪŋ ˈɡəʊɪŋ wɪð sʌmˈwʌn
words.us: hæv ə θɪŋ ˈɡoʊɪŋ wɪð ˈsʌmwʌn
words.ex: I heard she has a thing going with the new guy at work.
words.ex_cn: 我听说她和新来的同事有暧昧关系。
words.en: To be involved in a romantic or secret relationship with someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 与某人有某种关系（通常指恋爱或暧昧关系）
words.ex: He has something going with his coworker.
words.ex_cn: 他和同事有点关系。
words.en: To be involved in a romantic or sexual relationship with someone, or to be engaged in a particular activity or project with someone.

words.tr: 短语. 指两个人之间有某种隐秘或非正式的恋爱或亲密关系；在交往中
words.ex: They have a thing going, but it's not serious.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间有一段关系，但并不认真。
words.en: To be involved in a romantic or sexual relationship, or to be engaged in a particular activity or project.

words.tr: 短语动词. 有某种进展；在进行某事；指某人正在从事或拥有某种正在发展的状况或关系
words.ex: They have something going on between them, but they're not telling anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间有些什么正在进行，但他们没有告诉任何人。
words.en: If you have something going, you are involved in a particular activity or relationship, often one that is secret or not fully disclosed.

words.tr: 短语动词. 在某事中有发言权；能参与意见或决策
words.ex: Employees should have a voice in the decision-making process.
words.ex_cn: 员工应该在决策过程中有发言权。
words.en: To have the right or opportunity to express one's opinions or influence decisions in a particular matter.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事有发言权；参与某事的决策
words.ex: Employees should have a say in how their workplace is managed.
words.ex_cn: 员工应该对如何管理他们的工作场所有发言权。
words.en: To have a say in something means to have the right or opportunity to express your opinion or influence a decision about it.

words.tr: 短语动词，有发言权；能表达自己的意见；被倾听的权利
words.ex: In a democracy, every citizen should have a voice in the government's decisions.
words.ex_cn: 在民主国家，每个公民都应在政府的决策中有发言权。
words.en: To have the opportunity to express one's opinions or to have influence in decisions.

words.tr: 短语动词. 有发言权；能发表意见
words.ex: Every member should have a say in the decision-making process.
words.ex_cn: 每个成员在决策过程中都应该有发言权。
words.en: To have the right or opportunity to express one's opinion or influence decisions.

words.tr: 短语动词，善于应付（某类人或事物）；有处理……的技巧
words.ex: He has a way with words.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长用词。
words.en: To have a natural ability to deal with or handle a particular type of person or thing effectively.

words.tr: phrase. 对…有偏爱；对…缺乏抵抗力
words.ex: I have a weakness for chocolate.
words.ex_cn: 我对巧克力情有独钟。
words.en: If you have a weakness for something, you like it very much, even though it may not be good for you.

words.tr: 短语动词. 与某人谈一谈，通常指私下或严肃地交谈
words.ex: I need to have a word with you about the project.
words.ex_cn: 我需要和你谈谈关于这个项目的事情。
words.en: To speak to someone briefly, especially in order to give them advice or a warning.

words.tr: phrase. 有自己的目的或私怨要解决；有个人恩怨要清算
words.ex: He always seems to have an axe to grind when discussing company policies.
words.ex_cn: 他在讨论公司政策时似乎总是别有用心。
words.en: If someone has an axe to grind, they have a strong personal opinion about something and they want to persuade other people to share their opinion, often for personal gain.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对……有鉴赏力；善于发现……的美或价值
words.ex: She has an eye for beautiful clothes.
words.ex_cn: 她对漂亮的衣服很敏感。
words.en: If you have an eye for something, you are good at noticing it or you have a natural ability to appreciate it.

words.tr: phrase. 照看；密切注视
words.ex: Please keep an eye on the baby while I cook.
words.ex_cn: 我做饭时，请照看一下宝宝。
words.en: To watch or look after someone or something carefully.

words.tr: phrase. 密切关注；对……有意；看中了
words.ex: I have my eye on a new bike at the store.
words.ex_cn: 我一直在关注商店里的一辆新自行车。
words.en: To have a strong desire to obtain or achieve something.

words.tr: phrase. 密切注意；留意；照看
words.ex: Please keep your eye on the baby while I cook.
words.ex_cn: 我做饭时请照看一下宝宝。
words.en: To watch or monitor something or someone closely.

words.tr: phrase. 留意；密切注意；留心寻找
words.ex: Keep an eye out for the red bus at the corner.
words.ex_cn: 留意拐角处的红色公交车。
words.en: To watch carefully for someone or something to appear or to be careful about something.

words.tr: phrase. 留心寻找；密切注意
words.ex: I have my eye out for a good job.
words.ex_cn: 我正在留意一份好工作。
words.en: To be actively looking for something or someone, often with the implication of being alert or watchful for an opportunity or a potential threat.

words.tr: phrase. 留意；密切注意；留心寻找
words.ex: We are keeping our eyes out for a good deal on a used car.
words.ex_cn: 我们正在留意一辆便宜的二手车。
words.en: To watch carefully for someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 留心注意；密切留意
words.ex: You should have an eye out for any suspicious activity in your neighborhood.
words.ex_cn: 你应该留意你社区里的任何可疑活动。
words.en: To be vigilant or watchful for something.

words.tr: phrase. 留心注意；密切留意（某人或某事）
words.ex: He will have his eye out for good deals at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他会在市场上留意好的便宜货。
words.en: To be watchful or alert for something.

words.tr: phrase. 留意；密切注意；保持警惕
words.ex: Please keep an eye out for any suspicious activity.
words.ex_cn: 请留意任何可疑活动。
words.en: To remain alert or watchful for something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 留意；密切注意；保持警觉
words.ex: We are keeping our eyes out for a good deal on a used car.
words.ex_cn: 我们正在留意一辆便宜的二手车。
words.en: To watch carefully for someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 手心发痒（常用来形容渴望得到金钱或想要花钱）
words.ex: He has an itchy palm after holding money for too long.
words.ex_cn: 他长时间拿着钱后手心发痒。
words.en: To be eager for money, especially through bribery or dishonest means.

words.tr: phrase. 手痒（指贪财，渴望得到钱财）
words.ex: He has an itching palm and always wants more money.
words.ex_cn: 他贪财得很，总是想要更多的钱。
words.en: To have an itching palm means to be greedy for money, especially in a way that is considered unethical or immoral.

words.tr: phrase. 想错了；该重新想想了（用于表示某人对某事有错误的想法或期望）
words.ex: If you think I will lend you money again, you have another think coming.
words.ex_cn: 如果你认为我会再借给你钱，那你可就想错了。
words.en: If you say that someone has another think coming, you mean that they are completely wrong in their opinion or intention and they will soon realize this.

words.tr: 短语. 想法错误；打错算盘；如果这么想就大错特错了
words.ex: If you think he'll help you, you have another guess coming.
words.ex_cn: 如果你认为他会帮你，那你可就猜错了。
words.en: To be mistaken in one's assumption; to have another chance to guess incorrectly.

words.tr: phrase. v. 见识过世面的；经历丰富的；存在很久的
words.ex: This type of phone has been around for five years.
words.ex_cn: 这种手机已经存在五年了。
words.en: To be experienced, worldly, and knowledgeable about life.

words.tr: 短语动词. 指在某个领域或方面取得了很大进展或进步；经历了很长的发展过程
words.ex: We have come a long way since we started learning English.
words.ex_cn: 自从我们开始学英语以来，已经取得了很大进步。
words.en: To have made significant progress or improvement over time.

words.tr: phrase. 对……有野心；图谋得到（某物或某职位）
words.ex: He has designs on his friend's job.
words.ex_cn: 他图谋他朋友的工作。
words.en: To have plans or intentions to achieve something, often something that belongs to someone else or is not easily attainable.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某物有优先权或声称拥有权
words.ex: I have dibs on the front seat!
words.ex_cn: v. 我先要的前排座位！
words.en: To claim the right to have or do something before others.

words.tr: phrase. 声称对某物有优先权；预订某物；抢先占有某物
words.ex: He put dibs on the last slice of pizza.
words.ex_cn: 他抢先说最后那片披萨归他。
words.en: To claim the right to have or use something before others.

words.tr: phrase. 感到尴尬或难堪；出了丑；丢脸
words.ex: He made a big mistake in front of everyone and now he has egg on his face.
words.ex_cn: 他在大家面前犯了一个大错，现在很尴尬。
words.en: To be embarrassed or look foolish because of something one has done.

words.w: have eyes in the back of one's head
words.tr: phrase. 形容某人似乎能察觉到身后发生的事情，非常警觉或留意周围的情况
words.uk: /hæv aɪz ɪn ðə bæk əv wʌnz hɛd/
words.us: /hæv aɪz ɪn ðə bæk əv wʌnz hɛd/
words.ex: My mom seems to have eyes in the back of her head when I try to sneak candy.
words.ex_cn: 当我偷偷拿糖果时，我妈妈好像脑后有眼一样。
words.en: To be very aware of what is happening around you, especially things that are not in your direct line of sight.

words.tr: phrase. 有致命弱点；外表完美但内在有缺陷（原指看似强大或完美的人实际上有严重缺点）
words.ex: He thought his hero was perfect, but now he knows he has feet of clay.
words.ex_cn: 他原以为他的英雄是完美的，但现在他知道他也有缺点。
words.en: To have a weakness or fault that people do not realize at first.

words.tr: phrase. （非正式）言多必失症；说话不经思考而得罪人或造成尴尬的情况
words.ex: He has foot-in-mouth disease and always says the wrong thing.
words.ex_cn: 他有口无遮拦的毛病，总是说错话。
words.en: A humorous way of referring to the tendency of a person to say things that are embarrassing, inappropriate, or tactless.

words.tr: phrase. 成长的烦恼；发展中的困难（指儿童在发育过程中出现的间歇性肢体疼痛，或比喻个人、组织、社会等在发展过程中遇到的暂时性困难）
words.ex: The company is facing growing pains as it expands.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司扩张时正经历成长的阵痛。
words.en: The difficulties and problems that are experienced in the early stages of a project, business, or period of growth.

words.tr: phrase. 已经受够了；再也无法忍受
words.ex: I have had enough of this noise.
words.ex_cn: 我受够了这种噪音。
words.en: To no longer want to deal with a situation or person because it is unpleasant or annoying.

words.tr: phrase. 已经受够了；再也无法忍受；完了，结束了（通常指某人或某事已到极限或失败）
words.ex: I have had it with all this noise!
words.ex_cn: 我对所有这些噪音受够了！
words.en: To be unable or unwilling to tolerate something any longer.

words.w: have had it up to here
words.tr: phrase. 已经忍无可忍；受够了（表示极度不耐烦或愤怒）
words.uk: hæv hæd ɪt ʌp tə hɪə(r)
words.us: hæv hæd ɪt ʌp tə hɪr
words.ex: I have had it up to here with the noise.
words.ex_cn: 我受够了这噪音。
words.en: To be extremely annoyed or frustrated with a situation or person, to the point of not being able to tolerate it any longer.

words.w: have half a mind to do sth.
words.tr: phrase. 有做某事的念头；半心半意地想做某事
words.uk: hæv hɑːf ə maɪnd tuː duː ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv hæf ə maɪnd tu du ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: I have half a mind to quit my job.
words.ex_cn: 我真想辞职。
words.en: To be strongly inclined or tempted to do something, often something one shouldn't.

words.tr: phrase. 一点想法；模糊的念头
words.ex: He has half a notion to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他有点想辞掉工作。
words.en: An idea or plan that is not fully formed or thought out.

words.tr: 短语动词. 想两全其美；既想得到好处又不想承担后果
words.ex: You can't have it both ways—you can't work less and earn more.
words.ex_cn: 你不能两全其美——你不能工作更少却赚得更多。
words.en: To benefit from two different or opposite things at the same time.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人怀有恶意；故意与某人为难
words.ex: He has it in for his neighbor because of the loud music.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吵闹的音乐而针对他的邻居。
words.en: to be determined to to criticize, harm, or cause trouble for someone

words.tr: phrase. 对…感到矛盾的；对…有复杂情感的
words.ex: I have mixed feelings about the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 我对新校规感到矛盾。
words.en: To feel both positive and negative emotions about something.

words.tr: phrase. 有很多钱可以随意花；挥金如土
words.ex: He has money to burn, so he buys new shoes every week.
words.ex_cn: 他有的是钱，所以每周都买新鞋。
words.en: To have more money than one needs, allowing one to spend freely.

words.tr: phrase. 没有权利做某事；不该做某事
words.ex: You have no business telling me how to live my life.
words.ex_cn: 你没有权利告诉我如何生活。
words.en: If you say that someone has no business to do something, you mean that they have no right to do it.

words.tr: phrase. 对…毫无用处；不关心；不在乎
words.ex: He has no use for old phones.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得旧手机一点用都没有。
words.en: To not need or want something or someone, often because they are not useful or valuable.

words.tr: 短语动词. 没时间理会；对…不感兴趣；不愿浪费时间在…上
words.ex: He has no time for games after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后没有时间玩游戏。
words.en: If you have no time for someone or something, you have no patience with them or do not like them.

words.tr: phrase. 与...无关
words.ex: This problem has nothing to do with math.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题与数学无关。
words.en: If you say that something has nothing to do with a particular subject or situation, you mean that it is not connected with it in any way.

words.w: have one's back to the wall
words.tr: phrase. 处于困境中；背水一战；被迫采取最后手段
words.uk: hæv wʌnz bæk tuː ðə wɔːl
words.us: hæv wʌnz bæk tuː ðə wɔːl
words.ex: He has his back to the wall and cannot move.
words.ex_cn: 他被逼得走投无路，无法动弹。
words.en: To be in a difficult situation where one is forced to act defensively or from a position of disadvantage.

words.w: have one's cake and eat it too
words.tr: phrase. 想两全其美；既要……又要……（指想同时拥有两种互不相容的好处）
words.uk: hæv wʌnz keɪk ænd iːt ɪt tuː
words.us: hæv wʌnz keɪk ænd iːt ɪt tuː
words.ex: You can't have your cake and eat it too.
words.ex_cn: 你不能两全其美。
words.en: To want to have the benefits of two mutually exclusive options simultaneously.

words.w: eat one's cake and have it too
words.tr: phrase. 想两全其美；既想吃掉蛋糕又想保留它，比喻想同时拥有互相矛盾的好处
words.uk: iːt wʌnz keɪk ənd hæv ɪt tuː
words.us: iːt wʌnz keɪk ənd hæv ɪt tuː
words.ex: You can't eat your cake and have it too.
words.ex_cn: 你不能既吃蛋糕又留着蛋糕。
words.en: To want to have the benefits of two mutually exclusive options.

words.w: have one's ear to the ground
words.tr: phrase. 密切注意情况；随时了解最新动态；保持警觉以获取信息
words.uk: hæv wʌnz ɪə tə ðə ɡraʊnd
words.us: hæv wʌnz ɪr tə ðə ɡraʊnd
words.ex: He has his ear to the ground to hear about job openings.
words.ex_cn: 他密切关注着工作机会的消息。
words.en: To be well informed about current events and trends.

words.w: keep one's ear to the ground
words.tr: phrase. 保持警觉；留心观察；注意动向；打听消息
words.uk: kiːp wʌnz ɪə(r) tə ðə ɡraʊnd
words.us: kiːp wʌnz ɪr tə ðə ɡraʊnd
words.ex: He keeps his ear to the ground to know what people think.
words.ex_cn: 他密切关注人们的想法。
words.en: To keep one's ear to the ground means to stay well informed and up-to-date about what is happening or what is going to happen, especially by paying close attention to the news and to what people are saying.

words.w: have one's finger in the pie
words.tr: phrase. 参与某事；插手某事；介入某个活动或事务中
words.uk: hæv wʌnz ˈfɪŋɡər ɪn ðə paɪ
words.us: hæv wʌnz ˈfɪŋɡər ɪn ðə paɪ
words.ex: He always has his finger in the pie when people plan something.
words.ex_cn: 每当人们计划事情时，他总要插一手。
words.en: To be involved in or have an influence on a particular situation or activity.

words.tr: phrase. 忙于应付某事；被某事占据全部精力；有大量事情要处理
words.ex: She has her hands full with two jobs and a baby.
words.ex_cn: 她有两份工作还要带一个宝宝，忙得不可开交。
words.en: To be very busy with something; to have a lot of work or tasks to do.

words.tr: phrase. 忙得不可开交；应接不暇
words.ex: She has her hands full with three kids and a full-time job.
words.ex_cn: 她有三个孩子和一份全职工作，忙得不可开交。
words.en: If you have your hands full, you are extremely busy with something.

words.w: have one's heart in the right place
words.tr: phrase. 心地善良，出发点是好的（尽管做法可能欠妥）
words.uk: hæv wʌnz hɑːt ɪn ðə raɪt pleɪs
words.us: hæv wʌnz hɑrt ɪn ðə raɪt ples
words.ex: He always helps others; he has his heart in the right place.
words.ex_cn: 他总是帮助别人；他心地善良。
words.en: If you say that someone has their heart in the right place, you mean that they are kind and mean well, even if their actions sometimes seem to suggest otherwise.

words.w: have one's heart set on sth.
words.tr: phrase. 一心想要某物；决心要得到某物
words.uk: hæv wʌnz hɑːt set ɒn ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv wʌnz hɑːrt set ɑːn ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: He has his heart set on becoming a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他一心想要当医生。
words.en: To be determined to get something or to achieve something.

words.tr: phrase. 好运用尽；运气终结
words.ex: He kept gambling until his luck ran out.
words.ex_cn: 他一直赌博，直到运气用尽。
words.en: To have used up all one's good fortune; to be at the end of one's luck.

words.w: have one's nose in a book
words.tr: phrase. 专心读书；埋头看书
words.uk: hæv wʌnz nəʊz ɪn ə bʊk
words.us: hæv wʌnz noʊz ɪn ə bʊk
words.ex: He has his nose in a book every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都埋头看书。
words.en: To be reading a book with great interest or concentration, often to the exclusion of everything else.

words.w: have one's nose in the air
words.tr: phrase. 形容某人显得傲慢、自大或看不起别人
words.uk: hæv wʌnz nəʊz ɪn ði eə(r)
words.us: hæv wʌnz noʊz ɪn ði er
words.ex: He has his nose in the air and never talks to others.
words.ex_cn: 他趾高气扬，从不和别人说话。
words.en: To behave in a way that shows one thinks they are superior to others.

words.tr: phrase. 有繁重的工作要做；任务艰巨，不容易完成
words.ex: He has his work cut out to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他必须全力以赴才能按时完成这个项目。
words.en: To have a very difficult task or set of tasks to do.

words.tr: phrase. 有别的更重要的事情要处理；另有要事
words.ex: I can't talk now, I have other fish to fry.
words.ex_cn: 我现在不能聊天，我还有别的事要忙。
words.en: To have more important or interesting things to do.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某人有影响力；能通过关系影响某人
words.ex: He has a pull with the manager, so he gets extra days off.
words.ex_cn: 他和经理有关系，所以他能多休几天假。
words.en: To have influence or sway over someone, enabling one to achieve favors or preferential treatment.

words.tr: phrase. 完全控制某人；牵着某人的鼻子走
words.uk: hæv sʌm wʌn ɒn ðə strɪŋ
words.us: hæv sʌm wʌn ɑːn ðə strɪŋ
words.ex: The coach has the players on the string.
words.ex_cn: 教练牢牢掌控着队员们。
words.en: To control someone, making them do what you want.

words.tr: phrase. 过去比现在好；已显破旧或衰败；曾经辉煌但如今状况不佳
words.ex: That old car have seen better days.
words.ex_cn: 那辆旧车已经不如从前了。
words.en: To be in a worse condition than in the past; to be old or worn out.

words.tr: phrase. v. 手头上有（某事或某人需要处理）；负责照看；引起麻烦
words.ex: I have a big problem on my hands.
words.ex_cn: 我手上有一个大问题。
words.en: To have something that one needs to deal with or take care of.

words.tr: phrase. 把…留给某人处理（或照管）；使某人不得不应付某事
words.ex: If you start the project, you can't leave it on someone else's hands.
words.ex_cn: 如果你开始了这个项目，就不能把它留给别人不管。
words.en: To leave something for someone else to deal with or be responsible for.

words.tr: 短语动词，心里想着……；惦记着……
words.ex: I have my exam on my mind.
words.ex_cn: 我脑子里一直想着我的考试。
words.en: To be thinking about or worrying about something.

words.tr: 短语动词，对某人或某事有意见；反对；怀有成见
words.ex: I don't have anything against him, but I don't trust him.
words.ex_cn: 我并不反对他，但我不信任他。
words.en: To dislike or have a grievance about someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 把某物靠在…上；因某事对某人怀恨在心；保存某物以备对付…
words.ex: Don't keep anger against your friend.
words.ex_cn: 不要对你的朋友怀恨在心。
words.en: To remember or hold a grudge against someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某事了如指掌；能随时运用某事物
words.ex: He has all the answers at his fingertips during the test.
words.ex_cn: 考试时他所有答案都了如指掌。
words.en: To have something at one's fingertips means to have something readily available or to know something very well.

words.tr: phrase. 把某事牢记于心；随时可供使用；了如指掌
words.ex: He keeps the rules at his fingertips.
words.ex_cn: 他随时牢记这些规则。
words.en: To have immediate access to information or resources; to be fully prepared.

words.tr: 短语动词. 手头有某物；随时可用某物
words.ex: She has a dictionary at hand while writing.
words.ex_cn: 她写作时手边有一本字典。
words.en: To have something readily available or within easy reach.

words.tr: phrase. 活该；自作自受；应得某种结果（通常指负面结果）
words.ex: If you are unkind to others, you might have something coming.
words.ex_cn: 如果你对别人不友善，你可能会自食其果。
words.en: To deserve something, often something good, as a result of one's actions or efforts.

words.tr: phrase. 藏有秘密计划或保留未显露的手段；留有后招
words.ex: He always has something up his sleeve for the final exam.
words.ex_cn: 他为期末考试总是留有一手。
words.en: To have a secret plan or strategy that you are not revealing.

words.w: have sth. hanging over one's head
words.tr: phrase. 有某事悬而未决地压在心头，令人担忧或焦虑
words.uk: hæv ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈhæŋɪŋ ˈəʊvə wʌnz ˈhed
words.us: hæv ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈhæŋɪŋ ˈoʊvər wʌnz ˈhɛd
words.ex: He has a test hanging over his head.
words.ex_cn: 他有一场考试悬在头上。
words.en: To have something, especially a problem or responsibility, that causes worry or stress because it has not been dealt with.

words.tr: 短语动词，意思是心里有某个想法、计划或偏好；心中已有打算
words.ex: I have something in mind for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我脑子里有个晚餐的想法。
words.en: To be thinking of a particular plan or idea.

words.tr: 短语动词. 与某人彻底谈清楚某事，把问题或矛盾公开地讨论或解决
words.ex: I will have it out with my brother about the broken vase.
words.ex_cn: 我要和我弟弟谈谈那个打碎的花瓶。
words.en: To discuss or argue about a problem or disagreement with someone in order to resolve it.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 解决争端；把事情说清楚；摊牌
words.ex: They decided to have it out and solve their problem.
words.ex_cn: 他们决定把事情说清楚，解决他们的问题。
words.en: To resolve a dispute or argument; to finish discussing a topic.

words.tr: 短语动词. 具备成功所需的品质或能力；有本事，有能耐
words.ex: He works hard every day because he wants to have what it takes to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力学习，因为他想具备成为一名医生所需要的素质。
words.en: To have the necessary qualities or abilities to succeed in a particular endeavor.

words.w: have the cards stacked against sb.
words.tr: phrase. 处境不利；面临不公平的劣势（指某人因外部因素而处于不利地位）
words.uk: hæv ðə kɑːdz stækt əˈɡenst səmˈbədi
words.us: hæv ðə kɑːrdz stækt əˈɡenst ˈsʌmbədi
words.ex: He have the cards stacked against him because he is young and poor.
words.ex_cn: 因为他年轻又贫穷，所以形势对他不利。
words.en: If you say that the cards are stacked against someone, you mean that they are unlikely to succeed because the situation is unfair or difficult.

words.tr: phrase. 意为将有大麻烦要处理；会遇到严重的后果
words.ex: He have the devil to pay after breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他违反了规则，后果很严重。
words.en: to face serious consequences or trouble

words.tr: 短语动词. 意为某人将面临严重的后果或严厉的惩罚，通常因为做错了事或惹怒了别人
words.ex: He will have hell to pay for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他违反规则后将付出惨重代价。
words.en: To face severe consequences or punishment for one's actions.

words.w: have the shoe on the other foot
words.tr: phrase. 处于相反的境地；换位思考；处境完全相反
words.uk: hæv ðə ʃuː ɒn ði ˈʌðə fʊt
words.us: hæv ðə ʃuː ɑːn ði ˈʌðər fʊt
words.ex: He teased her, but now he has the shoe on the other foot.
words.ex_cn: 他曾经嘲笑她，但现在角色互换了。
words.en: If you say that the shoe is on the other foot, you mean that a situation has been reversed completely, so that someone who was in a position of power or advantage is now in a less favorable position.

words.w: have too many irons in the fire
words.tr: phrase. 同时忙于太多事情；同时参与多个计划或事务而导致难以兼顾
words.uk: hæv tuː ˈmeni ˈaɪənz ɪn ðə ˈfaɪə(r)
words.us: hæv tu ˈmeni ˈaɪrənz ɪn ðə ˈfaɪr
words.ex: He has too many irons in the fire, so he cannot focus on one thing.
words.ex_cn: 他同时忙于太多事情，所以无法专注于一件事。
words.en: To be involved in too many activities or projects at the same time, making it difficult to manage them all effectively.

words.tr: 短语动词. 已经好转；已经度过难关；情况开始向好的方向发展
words.ex: The patient has turned the corner and is getting better.
words.ex_cn: 病人已经好转，病情在好转了。
words.en: To pass a critical point and begin to improve or recover.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词HAVE补充词组

words.tr: phrase. 对……产生不良影响
words.ex: Smoking has a bad effect on your lungs.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的肺有害。
words.en: To cause a negative impact or influence on something or someone.

words.tr: 短语. 产生不良影响；对……有负面作用
words.ex: Smoking have a bad effect on your lungs.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的肺有不良影响。
words.en: To cause a negative impact or result.

words.w: have a bee in one's bonnet
words.tr: phrase. 固执地想着某事；对某事过分担忧或着迷（通常指不切实际的想法）
words.ex: He has a bee in his bonnet about cleaning the kitchen every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天总想着要打扫厨房。
words.en: To be obsessed or preoccupied with a particular idea or topic, often to the point of being irrational or impractical.

words.tr: n. 大餐；爆胎；突然上涨；骤升
words.ex: The team suffered a blowout in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍在决赛中惨败。
words.en: A sudden rupture or bursting of a tire, or a large and lavish party or event.

words.tr: 短语动词. 对某人有指控或有理由起诉；有证据或理由反对某人
words.uk: hæv ə keɪs əˈɡenst sʌm wʌn
words.us: hæv ə keɪs əˈɡenst sʌm wʌn
words.ex: They have a case against the driver for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他们对这位司机超速有指控。
words.en: If you have a case against someone, you have enough evidence or reasons to accuse them of something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 针对某人搜集证据以提出指控或进行控诉
words.ex: The police tried to build a case against the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图收集证据指控小偷。
words.en: To gather evidence and arguments to support a legal case against someone.

words.tr: 短语动词. 收集证据或信息来指控某人；为反对某人而搜集案情
words.ex: The police gathered a case against the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察收集了针对小偷的证据。
words.en: To collect evidence that can be used to accuse someone of a crime or wrongdoing.

words.tr: phrase. 为指控某人而收集证据或构建案件
words.ex: The police tried to assemble a case against the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图为这个小偷收集证据。
words.en: To gather evidence or arguments to accuse or prosecute someone.

words.tr: 短语. 问心无愧；良心清白
words.ex: He has a clear conscience because he told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因为说了实话而问心无愧。
words.en: To be free from guilt or the feeling of having done wrong.

words.tr: 短语. 对…问心无愧；对…感到良心清白
words.ex: He has a clear conscience about telling the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他对讲真话问心无愧。
words.en: To feel no guilt or remorse about something because you believe you have acted correctly.

words.tr: n. 歇斯底里；阵怒（等于 conniption fit）
words.ex: He had a conniption when he lost his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他丢钥匙时气得发疯。
words.en: A sudden fit of anger or panic; a tantrum.

words.tr: phrase. （因愤怒或震惊而）大发雷霆，激动得失去控制
words.ex: He had a conniption fit when he saw the mess in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到厨房里的混乱时，他气得发狂。
words.en: To have a conniption fit means to become very angry or upset, often in a way that is considered excessive or unreasonable.

words.tr: phrase. 比喻抗打击能力差，容易被击倒（尤指在批评或压力下无法承受）
words.ex: He has a glass jaw, so he gets knocked out easily.
words.ex_cn: 他有个玻璃下巴，所以很容易被击倒。
words.en: An expression used to describe someone who is easily hurt emotionally or physically, especially when facing criticism or challenges.

words.tr: n. 含酒精的饮料；提神的酒
words.ex: A cup of coffee is her favorite pick-me-up.
words.ex_cn: 一杯咖啡是她最喜欢的提神饮料。
words.en: Something that makes you feel better or more energetic when you are feeling tired or sad.

words.w: have a right to do sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 有权做某事
words.uk: hæv ə raɪt tuː duː ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv ə raɪt tu du ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: Every child has a right to get an education.
words.ex_cn: 每个孩子都有权接受教育。
words.en: To be entitled to do something; to have the legal or moral permission to do something.

words.w: have the right to do sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 有权利做某事
words.uk: hæv ðə raɪt tuː duː sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv ðə raɪt tu du sʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: Children have the right to go to school.
words.ex_cn: 儿童有权利上学。
words.en: To be entitled or permitted to do something.

words.tr:
v. 刮；擦；刮出刺耳声；勉强通过
n. 刮；擦；擦痕；刮擦声
words.ex: He scraped his knee on the rough ground.
words.ex_cn: 他在粗糙的地面上擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: To remove something from a surface using a sharp or rough edge, or to injure a part of the body by rubbing it against a rough surface.

words.tr: 短语动词. 抽烟；吸一支烟
words.ex: He has a smoke after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后抽一支烟。
words.en: To inhale and exhale the smoke of tobacco or a similar substance, especially from a cigarette, cigar, or pipe.

words.tr: phrase. 需要抽根烟；想抽烟
words.ex: He needs a smoke after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后需要吸一支烟。
words.en: To have a strong desire to smoke a cigarette or cigar.

words.tr: phrase. 想要抽一根烟（通常指香烟）
words.ex: He says he wants a smoke after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他说他晚饭后想抽根烟。
words.en: To have a strong desire to smoke a cigarette or cigar.

words.tr: phrase. （俚语）突然激动或失控；手忙脚乱；因紧张或兴奋而举止失常
words.ex: He had a spaz when the computer crashed.
words.ex_cn: 当电脑崩溃时，他突然发疯了。
words.en: To behave in a wild, uncontrolled, or exaggerated manner.

words.tr: n. 中风；划水动作；一击；
words.ex: He had a stroke last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年中风了。
words.en: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain results in cell death. It can also refer to an act of hitting or striking someone or something, or a gentle movement of the hand over a surface.

words.w: have a whale of a time
words.tr: 短语. 过得非常愉快；玩得尽兴
words.uk: hæv ə weɪl ɒv ə taɪm
words.us: hæv ə weɪl ʌv ə taɪm
words.ex: We had a whale of a time at the beach yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨天在海滩玩得非常开心。
words.en: To enjoy oneself greatly; to have a lot of fun.

words.tr: 短语动词. 发生意外；出事故
words.ex: He had an accident on his bike yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天骑自行车时出了事故。
words.en: To experience an unexpected and undesirable event, especially one causing injury or damage.

words.tr: n. 论点；争论；辩论；
