words.en: To check out means to leave a hotel after paying your bill, or to examine something or someone in order to be certain that everything is correct, safe, or satisfactory.

words.tr: phrase. 开支票；填写支票
words.uk: meɪk aʊt ə tʃɛk tuː ɛsb.
words.us: meɪk aʊt ə tʃɛk tu ɛsb.
words.ex: He makes out a check to pay the rent.
words.ex_cn: 他开了一张支票来支付房租。
words.en: To write a check for a specific amount of money.

words.w: make a day of doing sth.
words.tr: phrase. 花一整天做某事；把某事当作一整天的活动来享受
words.uk: meɪk ə deɪ əv ˈduːɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.us: meɪk ə deɪ əv ˈduɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: We made a day of going to the park.
words.ex_cn: 我们把去公园当作一整天的活动。
words.en: To spend the whole day doing a particular activity, especially as a way of enjoying yourself.

words.tr: phrase. 把一整天都用来好好享受；把活动安排成一整天；干脆玩上一整天
words.ex: Let's make a day of it and go to the park, have lunch, and watch a movie.
words.ex_cn: 我们把它当作一整天的活动吧，去公园、吃午饭，再看场电影。
words.en: To spend the whole day doing something, especially something enjoyable.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人做鬼脸；向某人扮怪相
words.ex: He made a face at his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他冲他弟弟做鬼脸。
words.en: To make a face at someone means to deliberately change the expression on your face to show that you dislike or are annoyed by them, or to amuse them.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人做鬼脸；向某人扮怪相
words.ex: The children make faces at their teacher.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们朝老师做鬼脸。
words.en: To make facial expressions at someone, often in a playful or mocking manner.

words.tr: phrase. 做鬼脸；扮怪相
words.ex: He made a face when he tasted the sour lemon.
words.ex_cn: 他尝到酸柠檬时皱起了脸。
words.en: To make a facial expression, often to show emotion or amusement.

words.tr: phrase. 做鬼脸；扮怪相
words.ex: The boy likes to make faces at his sister.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩喜欢对他的妹妹做鬼脸。
words.en: To make faces means to contort one's face in an exaggerated or comical way, often to express emotions or to amuse others.

words.w: make a fool out of sb.
words.tr: phrase. 使某人出丑；愚弄某人；让某人显得愚蠢
words.uk: meɪk ə fuːl aʊt əv ˈsʌmbədi
words.us: meɪk ə fuːl aʊt əv ˈsʌmbɑːdi
words.ex: He made a fool out of his brother by pretending to be a magician.
words.ex_cn: 他假装是魔术师，让他的兄弟出丑。
words.en: To make someone look stupid or foolish, especially by tricking them or making them appear ridiculous in front of others.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人出丑；让某人显得愚蠢
words.ex: He made an ass of himself at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上出丑了。
words.en: To cause someone to look foolish or to be humiliated.

words.tr: phrase. 记下某事；把某事记录下来
words.ex: Make a note of the time.
words.ex_cn: 把时间记下来。
words.en: To write something down so that you will remember it.

words.tr: phrase. 使自己成为令人讨厌的人；惹人嫌
words.ex: He was shouting and laughing loudly at the library, making a nuisance of himself.
words.ex_cn: 他在图书馆大声喧哗、大笑，惹人讨厌。
words.en: To behave in a way that is annoying or troublesome to others.

words.w: make a silk purse out of a sow's ear
words.tr: phrase. 把劣质材料变成精美之物；化腐朽为神奇；用拙劣原料造出精品
words.uk: meɪk ə sɪlk pɜːs aʊt əv ə saʊz ɪə(r)
words.us: meɪk ə sɪlk pɜːrs aʊt əv ə saʊz ɪr
words.ex: He tried to make a silk purse out of a sow's ear by turning old clothes into fancy dresses.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把旧衣服改成漂亮的裙子，这真是无中生有。
words.en: To make something of high quality from poor materials; to turn something of little value into something valuable.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人预约；与某人约定会面时间
words.ex: I will make an appointment with my doctor tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天要和我的医生预约。
words.en: To arrange a meeting with someone at a specific time.

words.tr: phrase. 预约；约会
words.ex: I will make an appointment with the doctor tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天要预约医生。
words.en: To arrange a meeting or consultation at a specific time.

words.tr: phrase. 为…做安排；为…做准备
words.ex: I will make arrangements for the meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我将为明天的会议做安排。
words.en: To organize or plan something in advance.

words.tr: phrase. 做安排；筹备；打点
words.ex: They make arrangements for the meeting next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们为下周的会议做安排。
words.en: To organize or plan something in advance.

words.tr: phrase. 安排做某事；为做某事做准备
words.ex: They made arrangements to meet tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们安排好了明天见面。
words.en: To organize or plan something in advance.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人做好安排；与某人商定计划
words.ex: I made arrangements with my friend to meet at the park.
words.ex_cn: 我和朋友约好在公园见面。
words.en: To organize or plan something with someone, especially to ensure that everything is ready and in place for a future event or situation.

words.tr: phrase. 偷走；携…潜逃；杀死；消灭
words.ex: The thief tried to make away with the bag.
words.ex_cn: 小偷试图带着包逃跑。
words.en: To steal something and escape with it; to take something away secretly or illegally.

words.tr: phrase. 携…逃跑；偷走；卷走
words.ex: The thief tried to make off with the bag.
words.ex_cn: 小偷试图拿着包逃跑。
words.en: To steal something and quickly leave the place.

words.tr: phrase. 对某事打赌；在某事上下赌注
words.ex: He made a book on football statistics.
words.ex_cn: 他编了一本关于足球统计数据的书。
words.en: To place a bet on something; to gamble on the outcome of an event.

words.tr: phrase. 闲聊；空谈；说闲话
words.ex: He likes to make chin music with his friends over tea.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢和朋友喝茶时聊天。
words.en: To engage in idle or trivial conversation.

words.tr: phrase. 向某人抛媚眼；向某人送秋波
words.ex: He makes eyes at the girl in the café.
words.ex_cn: 他在咖啡馆里对那个女孩抛媚眼。
words.en: To look at someone in a way that shows you are attracted to them.

words.tr: phrase. 抛媚眼；眉目传情；暗送秋波
words.ex: He makes eyes at her during class.
words.ex_cn: 他在上课时向她抛媚眼。
words.en: To look at someone in a way that shows you are attracted to them or trying to attract their attention.

words.tr: phrase. 走向；促进；有助于
words.ex: He made for the door when he heard the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 他听到警报后走向了门。
words.en: If something makes for a particular situation, it causes that situation to exist or develop.

words.tr: phrase. 擅自使用；随意动用；对…放肆无礼
words.ex: He makes free with my things without asking.
words.ex_cn: 他未经允许就随便动我的东西。
words.en: To use something without permission or restraint; to take liberties with.

words.tr: phrase. 使自由；释放；免除；使摆脱束缚
words.ex: The teacher will make free time for extra help after class.
words.ex_cn: 老师会在课后腾出时间为学生提供额外帮助。
words.en: To cause someone or something to be free; to liberate.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人交朋友；与某人建立友谊
words.ex: She easily makes friends with everyone she meets.
words.ex_cn: 她很容易与遇到的每个人交朋友。
words.en: To become friends with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 交朋友；建立友谊；与人结交
words.ex: He wants to make friends at school.
words.ex_cn: 他想在学校交朋友。
words.en: To establish a relationship of mutual affection with someone, typically one that is not a romantic or family relationship.

words.tr: phrase. 成功地成为某人；以某身份取得成就
words.ex: He tried to make good as a teacher, but it was hard.
words.ex_cn: 他努力当好一名老师，但这很难。
words.en: To succeed in becoming a particular type of person, especially after effort.

words.tr: phrase. 在某事上取得成功；擅长于某事
words.ex: He tries to make good at math.
words.ex_cn: 他努力把数学学好。
words.en: To become skilled or proficient in a particular subject or activity.

words.tr: phrase. 成功；履行诺言；补偿损失；实现目标
words.ex: He makes good progress in math.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上取得了良好的进步。
words.en: To succeed in doing something or to compensate for something.

words.tr: phrase. 把…打得稀烂；彻底击败
words.ex: They can make hamburger out of beef.
words.ex_cn: 他们可以用牛肉做汉堡。
words.en: To defeat or criticize someone or something severely and completely.

words.tr: phrase. 彻底击败；把…打得落花流水；把…驳得体无完肤
words.ex: The team made mincemeat out of their opponent in the game.
words.ex_cn: 这支球队在比赛中轻松击败了对手。
words.en: To defeat someone or something completely and easily.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人日子难过；给某人找麻烦；让某人处境艰难
words.ex: The spicy food makes it hot for him.
words.ex_cn: 这道辣菜让他感觉很热。
words.en: To cause someone to be in a difficult or uncomfortable situation, often by applying pressure or making things challenging.

words.tr: adj.  活泼的；明快的；时髦的；没好气的
words.ex: He gave a snappy reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了干脆利落的回答。
words.en: If someone is snappy, they speak to people in a sharp, unfriendly way.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人的生活痛苦；让某人日子难过
words.ex: The loud neighbors make life miserable for her.
words.ex_cn: 吵闹的邻居让她生活得很痛苦。
words.en: To cause someone to experience a lot of suffering or discomfort.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人做爱；与某人发生性关系
words.ex: They make love to each other every night.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天晚上都相爱。
words.en: To have sexual intercourse with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 做爱；发生性关系；示爱
words.ex: They make love every night before sleeping.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天晚上睡觉前相爱。
words.en: to engage in sexual activity, especially sexual intercourse, as an expression of love and intimacy.

words.tr: phrase. 费力地穿过（某地）；设法完成（困难或复杂的事情）；在（人群、障碍等）中前进
words.ex: He made his way through the crowded market.
words.ex_cn: 他穿过了拥挤的市场。
words.en: To move or progress through a particular place or situation, often with some difficulty.

words.tr: phrase. 前往；费力前进；取得成功；闯出一条路
words.ex: The boy makes his way to school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩每天早上步行去上学。
words.en: To move or travel towards a destination, especially when this is difficult or takes a long time.

words.tr: phrase. 使自己引人注目；故意引人注意；出风头
words.ex: He tried to make himself conspicuous by shouting in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他通过在人群中大喊来引起注意。
words.en: To make oneself conspicuous means to behave or dress in a way that is intended to attract attention.

words.tr: phrase. 使自己痛苦；让自己难受；自寻烦恼
words.ex: He makes himself miserable by thinking only about his problems.
words.ex_cn: 他因为只想着自己的问题而让自己痛苦。
words.en: To cause oneself to feel unhappy or to suffer.

words.tr: phrase. 迅速离开；悄悄溜走；躲起来
words.ex: When the teacher came in, the students made themselves scarce.
words.ex_cn: 当老师进来时，学生们都躲开了。
words.en: To leave or disappear, especially in order to avoid a difficult or unpleasant situation.

words.tr: phrase. 理解；辨认出；书写；进展；设法应付；亲热
words.ex: I can't make out the words in this small print.
words.ex_cn: 我看不清这些小字。
words.en: to manage to see, hear, or understand someone or something with difficulty

words.tr: phrase. 与某人和解；与某人言归于好
words.ex: He made peace with his brother after the fight.
words.ex_cn: 打架之后，他和弟弟和好了。
words.en: To end a disagreement or conflict with someone and become friendly again.

words.tr: phrase. 讲和；和解；休战；达成和平协议
words.ex: They make peace after a long fight.
words.ex_cn: 他们在长时间争吵后和好了。
words.en: To end a conflict or hostilities and establish friendly relations.

words.tr: phrase. 弥补某事；挽回某事；成功完成某事；使某事变好
words.ex: He made the cake good for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他把蛋糕做得很好，为了聚会。
words.en: To compensate for something or to fulfill a promise or obligation.

words.tr: phrase. 制作某物；使某事发生；把某物变成
words.ex: He made a cake for his sister.
words.ex_cn: 他为妹妹做了一个蛋糕。
words.en: To produce something, often using a particular material or substance.

words.tr: phrase. 充分利用某事；使某事变得重要；从某事中得出意义或结论
words.ex: He wants to make something of his life.
words.ex_cn: 他想让自己的人生有所成就。
words.en: To understand or derive benefit from something.

words.w: make sth. up out of whole cloth
words.tr: phrase. 凭空捏造；完全杜撰；毫无根据地编造某事
words.uk: meɪk ˈsʌmθɪŋ ʌp aʊt əv həʊl klɒθ
words.us: meɪk ˈsʌmθɪŋ ʌp aʊt əv hoʊl klɔːθ
words.ex: He made up the story out of whole cloth.
words.ex_cn: 他完全编造了这个故事。
words.en: To invent or fabricate something completely, without any basis in truth.

words.w: make up sth. out of whole cloth
words.tr: phrase. 凭空捏造某事；完全虚构某事
words.uk: meɪk ʌp ˈsʌmθɪŋ aʊt əv həʊl klɒθ
words.us: meɪk ʌp ˈsʌmθɪŋ aʊt əv hoʊl klɔːθ
words.ex: He made up a story out of whole cloth to avoid punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他编了一个完全虚构的故事来逃避惩罚。
words.en: To invent something completely, without any basis in truth.

words.tr: phrase. 整理床铺
words.ex: He makes the bed every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都整理床铺。
words.en: To arrange the sheets, blankets, and pillows on a bed neatly after it has been slept in.

words.tr: phrase. 铺床；整理床铺；自作自受（比喻意义）
words.ex: Every morning, he makes his bed before breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 每天早上，他在吃早餐前都会整理床铺。
words.en: To arrange the sheets, blankets, and pillows on a bed so that it is neat and ready for someone to sleep in. It can also mean to accept the consequences of one's actions.

words.tr: phrase. 到场；出席；露面；出现在某个社交场合
words.ex: He made the scene with a loud shout.
words.ex_cn: 他大喊一声，引起了轰动。
words.en: To arrive or appear at a particular place or event.

words.tr: phrase. （与某人）调情；与某人勾搭；与某人暧昧
words.ex: I make time with my brother every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 我每个星期天都抽时间和我兄弟在一起。
words.en: To spend time with someone, especially in a way that shows affection or interest.

words.tr: phrase. 腾出时间；抽空
words.ex: He makes time to call his parents every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每星期天都抽出时间给父母打电话。
words.en: If you make time for a particular activity or person, you arrange your schedule so that you are available to do the activity or spend time with the person.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 14 基本动词 PUT

words.tr: phrase. 结束某事；终止某事；使某事停止
words.ex: We need to put an end to this argument.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要结束这场争论。
words.en: To cause something to stop happening or existing.

words.tr: phrase. 制止某事；使某事停止
words.ex: The teacher put a stop to the noise in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师制止了课堂上的噪音。
words.en: To cause something to end or to prevent something from continuing.

words.w: put all one's eggs in one basket
words.tr: phrase. 孤注一掷；把所有希望或资源都押在一件事上
words.uk: pʊt ɔːl wʌnz eɡz ɪn wʌn ˈbɑːskɪt
words.us: pʊt ɔːl wʌnz eɡz ɪn wʌn ˈbæskɪt
words.ex: He put all his eggs in one basket by investing all his money in one company.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都投资到一家公司，把所有的鸡蛋都放在一个篮子里。
words.en: To risk everything on a single venture or idea.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人产生不切实际的想法；向某人灌输念头；让某人痴心妄想
words.ex: Don't put ideas into his head; he might start worrying for no reason.
words.ex_cn: 不要给他灌输想法，他可能会无缘无故地开始担心。
words.en: To suggest or implant thoughts or ideas in someone's mind, often influencing their behavior or decisions.

words.w: put in a good word for sb.
words.tr: phrase. 为某人美言；替某人说好话；帮某人推荐
words.uk: pʊt ɪn ə ɡʊd wɜːd fɔː(r) ˈsʌmbədi
words.us: pʊt ɪn ə ɡʊd wɜːrd fɔːr ˈsʌmbɑːdi
words.ex: My mom put in a good word for me with the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈向老师为我说了好话。
words.en: To say something good about someone to someone else, especially in order to help them get a job, position, etc.

words.tr: phrase. 为…美言；替…说好话；帮…说好话以求得到好处
words.ex: He put in a good word for his friend when applying for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他在朋友申请工作时帮他说了好话。
words.en: To say something good about someone, especially in order to help them get a job, position, etc.

words.tr: phrase. 露一下面；到场（短暂地）出现
words.ex: He put in an appearance at the meeting but left early.
words.ex_cn: 他出席了会议，但早早离开了。
words.en: To attend an event briefly, especially when one is expected or required to be there.

words.tr: 发表自己的看法：表示提供自己的观点或建议，尽管可能并不是很重要或有价值。
words.ex: He put in his two cents during the team meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在团队会议上发表了自己的意见。
words.en: To offer one's opinion or advice, often when it is not requested.

words.w: put in one's two cents worth
words.tr: phrase. 发表个人意见；插嘴；发表己见
words.ex: He put in his two cents worth during the team meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在团队会议上发表了自己的意见。
words.en: To offer one's opinion or advice, especially when it may not have been asked for.

words.tr: phrase. 发表个人意见；插嘴；发表一己之见
words.ex: He always puts his two cents in during team meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他总是在团队会议上发表自己的意见。
words.en: To offer one's opinion or advice, especially when it is not solicited.

words.tr: phrase. 穿上；戴上；上演；增加（体重、速度等）；假装；播放（音乐等）
words.ex: He put his hat on before going outside.
words.ex_cn: 他出门前把帽子戴上。
words.en: To place something on a surface or to wear something on your body. It can also mean to pretend to have a particular feeling or quality, to gain weight, or to start playing a record, tape, or CD.

words.tr: phrase. 摆架子；装腔作势；故作高傲
words.ex: He always puts on airs and acts like he is better than others.
words.ex_cn: 他总是装腔作势，表现得好像比别人高一等。
words.en: To behave in a way that is intended to impress others, often by pretending to be more important, intelligent, or cultured than one actually is.

words.tr: phrase. 装模作样；假装；故作姿态
words.ex: He puts on an act to make people laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他装模作样来逗人们笑。
words.en: To behave in a way that is not genuine or sincere, especially to deceive others or to make a particular impression.

words.tr: phrase. 开动脑筋；认真思考；绞尽脑汁
words.ex: Let's put on our thinking caps to solve this problem.
words.ex_cn: 让我们动动脑筋来解决这个问题。
words.en: To start thinking seriously about something, especially in order to solve a problem or make a decision.

words.tr: phrase. 体重增加；发胖；增重
words.ex: He put on weight after he stopped running.
words.ex_cn: 他停止跑步后长胖了。
words.en: To become heavier or fatter.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人安分；挫某人的傲气；让某人认清自己的地位
words.ex: He was so rude that she had to put him in his place.
words.ex_cn: 他非常无礼，她不得不让他认清自己的位置。
words.en: To make someone realize their position or status, often by showing them that they are not as important or powerful as they think they are.

words.tr: phrase. 全力以赴做某事；投入全部精力做某事
words.ex: He put his back into the work and finished it early.
words.ex_cn: 他全力以赴地工作，早早完成了。
words.en: To put a lot of effort into doing something.

words.tr: phrase. 全力以赴做某事；专心致志于某事；拼命干某事
words.ex: He put his back to the wall to push the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他背靠墙，用力推那个沉重的箱子。
words.en: To exert oneself fully in order to accomplish something.

words.tr: phrase. 全力以赴；给人留下最好印象；尽量表现得体
words.ex: He tries to put his best foot forward on the first day of work.
words.ex_cn: 他在上班的第一天努力表现得最好。
words.en: To try as hard as possible to make a good impression or to do something as well as possible.

words.w: put one's cards on the table
words.tr: phrase. 摊牌；把底牌亮出来；开诚布公；直言不讳
words.uk: pʊt wʌnz kɑːdz ɒn ðə ˈteɪbl
words.us: pʊt wʌnz kɑːrdz ɑːn ðə ˈteɪbl
words.ex: He decided to put his cards on the table and tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他决定坦诚相告，把事情都说出来。
words.en: To be honest about your intentions and reveal your plans or resources.

words.w: lay one's cards on the table
words.tr: phrase. 摊牌；把话挑明；开诚布公
words.uk: leɪ wʌnz kɑːdz ɒn ðə ˈteɪbl
words.us: leɪ wʌnz kɑːrdz ɑːn ðə ˈteɪbl
words.ex: He decided to lay his cards on the table and tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他决定坦诚相告，把一切都说出来。
words.en: To reveal one's plans or intentions openly.

words.tr: phrase. 明确指出（问题、原因等）；确切说出（症结所在）
words.ex: She couldn't quite put her finger on what was wrong with the picture.
words.ex_cn: 她不能确切地指出这幅画有什么问题。
words.en: To identify or describe something exactly.

words.tr: phrase. 坚决拒绝；采取坚定立场；果断制止
words.ex: When the child refused to do homework, the mother put her foot down.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子拒绝做作业时，母亲坚决地表明了态度。
words.en: To refuse to change a decision or to insist on something.

words.w: put one's foot down about sth.
words.tr: phrase. 坚决反对某事；对某事采取强硬立场；对某事断然拒绝
words.uk: pʊt wʌnz fʊt daʊn əˈbaʊt sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: pʊt wʌnz fʊt daʊn əˈbaʊt sʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: She finally put her foot down about the late nights, insisting that they must end.
words.ex_cn: 她终于对熬夜一事孤注一掷，坚持认为必须结束。
words.en: To assert one's authority or make a firm decision against something.

words.w: put one's foot in one's mouth
words.tr: phrase. （因说错话而）使人尴尬；说错话；祸从口出
words.uk: pʊt wʌnz fʊt ɪn wʌnz maʊθ
words.us: pʊt wʌnz fʊt ɪn wʌnz maʊθ
words.ex: He put his foot in his mouth when he called his teacher 'mom'.
words.ex_cn: 他把老师叫成“妈妈”时，说错了话。
words.en: To say something that is embarrassing, wrong, or foolish, especially in a social situation.

words.w: stick one's foot in one's mouth
words.tr: phrase. 说错话；失言；讲出令人尴尬或冒犯的话
words.ex: He stuck his foot in his mouth when he called his teacher by the wrong name.
words.ex_cn: 他叫错老师的名字时，说错了话。
words.en: To say something that is embarrassing, wrong, or tactless.

words.tr: phrase. 把自己的事情处理好；整顿好自己的事务；先管好自己的事
words.ex: He needs to put his house in order before starting a new job.
words.ex_cn: 他需要在开始新工作之前把事情安排好。
words.en: To organize or arrange one's personal affairs or the affairs of a group or organization in a proper or effective way.

words.w: put one's nose to the grindstone
words.tr: phrase. 埋头苦干；专心致志地工作
words.ex: He puts his nose to the grindstone every day to finish his work.
words.ex_cn: 他每天努力工作以完成任务。
words.en: To work very hard, especially for a long time.

words.w: have one's nose to the grindstone
words.tr: phrase. 埋头苦干，专心致志地工作
words.uk: hæv wʌnz nəʊz tə ðə ɡraɪndstəʊn
words.us: hæv wʌnz noʊz tə ðə ɡraɪndstoʊn
words.ex: He has his nose to the grindstone every day at work.
words.ex_cn: 他每天工作都埋头苦干。
words.en: To work very hard and diligently.

words.w: get one's nose to the grindstone
words.tr: phrase. v. 埋头苦干，专心致志地工作
words.uk: ɡet wʌnz nəʊz tə ðə ˈɡraɪndstəʊn
words.us: ɡet wʌnz noʊz tə ðə ˈɡraɪndstoʊn
words.ex: He gets his nose to the grindstone to finish the work.
words.ex_cn: 他埋头苦干以完成工作。
words.en: To work very hard, especially for a long time.

words.w: keep one's nose to the grindstone
words.tr: phrase. 埋头苦干；坚持不懈地工作；拼命努力
words.uk: kɛp wʌnz nəʊz tə ðə ˈɡrɪndstəʊn
words.us: kɛp wʌnz noʊz tə ðə ˈɡrɪndstoʊn
words.ex: He keeps his nose to the grindstone to finish his work on time.
words.ex_cn: 他埋头苦干，以便按时完成工作。
words.en: To continue to work hard without stopping.

words.w: hold one's nose to the grindstone
words.tr: phrase. 坚持不懈地努力工作；迫使某人持续努力，不松懈
words.uk: həʊld wʌnz nəʊz tuː ðə ɡraɪndstəʊn
words.us: hoʊld wʌnz noʊz tuː ðə ɡraɪndstoʊn
words.ex: My teacher holds my nose to the grindstone, so I study every day.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师严格督促我，所以我每天都学习。
words.en: To work very hard for a long period of time.

words.tr: phrase. 插手；干预；多管闲事
words.ex: He always puts his oar in when others are talking.
words.ex_cn: 当别人说话时，他总是插嘴。
words.en: To interfere or meddle in someone else's business.

words.tr: phrase. 多管闲事；插嘴（尤指在不被邀请或不需要的情况下发表意见）
words.ex: He always sticks his oar in when others are talking.
words.ex_cn: 当别人说话时，他总是插嘴。
words.en: To interfere or involve oneself in someone else's business without being asked.

words.tr: phrase. ph. 插嘴；干预；发表意见
words.ex: He always puts in his oar when we talk about plans.
words.ex_cn: 我们讨论计划时，他总是插嘴。
words.en: To interfere or offer an opinion without being asked.

words.w: put one's shoulder to the wheel
words.tr: phrase. 全力以赴；开始努力工作；奋力投入
words.uk: pʊt wʌnz ˈʃəʊldə tə ðə wiːl
words.us: pʊt wʌnz ˈʃoʊldər tə ðə wiːl
words.ex: He put his shoulder to the wheel to finish the job on time.
words.ex_cn: 他全力以赴按时完成了工作。
words.en: If someone puts their shoulder to the wheel, they start to work very hard at something.

words.w: set one's shoulder to the wheel
words.tr: phrase. 下定决心努力工作；全力以赴
words.uk: set wʌnz ˈʃəʊldə tu ðə wiːl
words.us: set wʌnz ˈʃoʊldər tu ðə wil
words.ex: He set his shoulder to the wheel and finished the job on time.
words.ex_cn: 他全力以赴，按时完成了工作。
words.en: To start working hard and with determination to achieve something.

words.tr: phrase. 放出试探性的信息；探口风；试探反应
words.ex: Before making a decision, it's wise to put out some feelers to gauge public opinion.
words.ex_cn: 在做决定之前，明智的做法是试探一下公众的意见。
words.en: to cautiously seek information or opinions from others; to test the waters

words.tr: phrase. 试探性地放出消息或暗示，以探测他人反应或兴趣
words.ex: Before making a decision, she decided to throw out some feelers to gauge public opinion.
words.ex_cn: 在做决定之前，她决定先试探一下公众的意见。
words.en: To tentatively suggest something or release information to gauge interest or reaction.

words.tr: phrase. 把某人视为/登记为某人；把某人看作某种身份
words.uk: pʊt ˈes biː daʊn æz ˈes biː
words.us: pʊt ˈes biː daʊn æz ˈes biː
words.ex: He put himself down as the leader even though he was not experienced.
words.ex_cn: 他虽然经验不足，但还是自告奋勇地担任了领导。
words.en: To record or list someone as a particular type of person or as having a particular role.

words.tr: phrase. 把某人奉若神明；过分崇拜某人；把某人理想化
words.ex: She always puts her father on a pedestal, thinking he can do no wrong.
words.ex_cn: 她总是把她的父亲奉若神明，认为他不会做错事。
words.en: To admire or love someone so much that you believe they have no faults.

words.tr: phrase. 把某人奉若神明；极度崇拜某人；把某人置于高不可攀的地位
words.ex: He always places his favorite team on a pedestal, believing they can do no wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他总是把他最喜欢的球队捧上天，认为他们不会犯错。
words.en: To admire or respect someone so much that you treat them as if they are perfect and cannot do anything wrong.

words.tr: phrase. 把某人捧上神坛；过分崇拜或理想化某人
words.ex: She set her mentor on a pedestal, believing he could do no wrong.
words.ex_cn: 她把她的导师捧得很高，认为他不可能做错事。
words.en: To admire someone so much that you think they are perfect.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人难堪；让某人当场出丑；使某人陷入尴尬境地
words.ex: The interviewer put the candidate on the spot with a tricky question.
words.ex_cn: 面试官用一个棘手的问题使候选人处于难堪地位。
words.en: To cause someone to be in a difficult or embarrassing situation where they are forced to answer a difficult question or make a decision.

words.tr: phrase. 把……交由某人支配；使……可供某人任意使用
words.ex: The library puts many books at students' disposal.
words.ex_cn: 图书馆为学生提供了大量书籍供其使用。
words.en: To make something available for someone to use as they wish.

words.tr: phrase. 收起来；杀死；关进监狱；放弃
words.ex: He put away his toys after playing.
words.ex_cn: 他玩完后把玩具收起来了。
words.en: To put something away means to place it in its proper storage location, to save or store it, to consume it, or to confine someone in prison.

words.tr: phrase. 放下；记下；镇压；贬低；削减；杀死
words.ex: He put down his pen and smiled.
words.ex_cn: 他放下笔，笑了。
words.en: To place something on a surface or in a particular position; to write something down; to suppress or end something by force; to criticize someone in a way that makes them seem stupid or unimportant.

words.tr: phrase. 延期；推迟
words.ex: He put off his homework until tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他把作业推迟到明天。
words.en: To delay something or to cause someone to feel dislike or lack of interest.

words.tr: phrase. 把…暂时搁置；推迟；使等待
words.ex: They put the project on hold because they need more money.
words.ex_cn: 他们把项目暂停了，因为需要更多资金。
words.en: To temporarily stop or delay something.

words.tr: phrase. 把…从脑海里抹去；刻意不去想；忘掉
words.ex: He tried to put the bad dream out of his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把那个噩梦从脑海中赶走。
words.en: To stop thinking about something; to forget about something.

words.tr: phrase. v. 把……从脑海中排除；不再想某事
words.ex: I can't get that song out of my mind.
words.ex_cn: 我无法把那首歌从脑子里赶出去。
words.en: To stop thinking about something or someone; to forget something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 把（人）打发退休；使（事物）退役；弃之不用
words.ex: They put the old cow out to pasture on the farm.
words.ex_cn: 他们把那头老牛放到农场去养老了。
words.en: To retire someone or something, especially because they are no longer effective or useful.

words.tr: phrase. 使…上床睡觉；把（孩子）安顿上床；把（稿件、项目等）最终完成并交付
words.ex: I put my little brother to bed at 8 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 我晚上8点让弟弟上床睡觉。
words.en: To make someone go to sleep or to resolve an issue.

words.w: put one's nose out of joint
words.tr: phrase. 使某人恼怒；使某人感到受冷落；使某人心里不痛快
words.uk: pʊt wʌnz nəʊz aʊt əv dʒɔɪnt
words.us: pʊt wʌnz noʊz aʊt əv dʒɔɪnt
words.ex: His plan to put one's nose out of joint failed miserably.
words.ex_cn: 他孤注一掷的计划惨败。
words.en: To make someone feel upset or jealous.

words.tr: phrase. 使入睡；使麻醉；使安乐死
words.ex: The doctor will put the patient to sleep before the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 医生会在手术前让病人睡着。
words.en: To cause someone or something to go to sleep, often used in the context of helping someone fall asleep or euthanizing an animal.

words.tr: phrase. 使……入睡；哄……睡觉
words.ex: The boring movie sent him to sleep.
words.ex_cn: 这部无聊的电影让他睡着了。
words.en: To cause someone to fall asleep.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人遭受极大折磨；让某人经历严峻考验
words.ex: The interview process really put me through the wringer.
words.ex_cn: 面试过程真的让我经历了一番严酷的考验。
words.en: To make someone undergo a very difficult or unpleasant experience.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人接受考验；检验某人的能力（或品质）
words.ex: The interviewer decided to put the candidate to the test with a challenging question.
words.ex_cn: 面试官决定用一个有挑战性的问题来考验候选人。
words.en: To cause someone to undergo a test or trial, especially to determine their abilities or the effectiveness of something.

words.tr: phrase. 怂恿某人做某事；唆使某人干某事
words.ex: He was accused of putting his friend up to stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控唆使他的朋友偷钱。
words.en: To encourage or persuade someone to do something, especially something mischievous or wrong.

words.tr: phrase. 提出（意见、计划、理论等）；将…提前；把（钟表）拨快
words.ex: He put forward a new proposal at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上提出了一个新的建议。
words.en: To suggest or propose something for consideration.

words.tr: phrase. 提出（想法、建议、理论等）；将…提前；推荐
words.ex: He decided to put forward his proposal at the last meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他决定在最后一次会议上提出他的建议。
words.en: To suggest or propose something for consideration.

words.tr: phrase. 把某物放在某人面前；给某人设置障碍；使某人遇到某事
words.ex: He tried to put obstacles in her way to prevent her from succeeding.
words.ex_cn: 他试图设置障碍阻止她成功。
words.en: to deliberately obstruct or hinder someone's progress or efforts

words.w: put sth. in the way of sb.
words.tr: phrase. 阻碍某人做某事；妨碍某人获得某物
words.uk: pʊt ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɪn ðə weɪ ɒv ˈsʌmbɒdi
words.us: pʊt ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɪn ðə weɪ əv ˈsʌmbɑːdi
words.ex: Don't put any obstacles in the way of your success.
words.ex_cn: 不要在你的成功道路上设置任何障碍。
words.en: To place an object in front of someone or something to block or hinder their movement.

words.tr: phrase. 把某物放在路上；用某物加以阻挡；设置障碍
words.ex: He tried to put something in the way of our plans.
words.ex_cn: 他试图妨碍我们的计划。
words.en: to deliberately obstruct or hinder someone's progress or efforts

words.tr: phrase. 整理；使有条理；把…收拾整齐
words.ex: She spent the afternoon putting her room in order.
words.ex_cn: 她花了一个下午的时间整理房间。
words.en: To arrange or organize things so that they are tidy or in the correct sequence.

words.tr: 短语动词. 把某事安排妥当；使某物井然有序
words.ex: I need to get my desk in order before the new semester starts.
words.ex_cn: v. 我需要在新学期开始前整理好我的书桌。
words.en: To arrange or organize something in a proper or desired sequence or condition.

words.tr: phrase. 将某事付诸实践；实施；实行
words.ex: He put his ideas into practice.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的想法付诸实践。
words.en: To apply a plan, idea, or method in a real situation.

words.tr: phrase. 用语言表达某事；把（想法、感受等）说出来
words.ex: He found it difficult to put his feelings into words.
words.ex_cn: 他发现很难用言语表达自己的感受。
words.en: To express something in language.

words.tr: phrase. 把某事写下来；将想法或计划付诸文字
words.ex: He decided to put his ideas on paper before discussing them with the team.
words.ex_cn: 他决定先把他的想法写下来，然后再和团队讨论。
words.en: To write something down, especially so that it becomes clear or official.

words.w: put sth. on the back burner
words.tr: phrase. 把某事搁置；把某事暂时放在次要位置
words.uk: pʊt ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɒn ðə bæk ˈbɜːnə
words.us: pʊt ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɑːn ðə bæk ˈbɜːrnər
words.ex: We decided to put the project on the back burner until we have more resources.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定把项目暂时搁置，直到我们有更多资源。
words.en: To postpone dealing with something.

words.tr: phrase. 把某事置于危险之中；拿某事冒险
words.ex: He was willing to put his reputation on the line to support the project.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意冒着名誉受损的风险来支持这个项目。
words.en: To risk something important, such as your job or reputation, in order to achieve something.

words.tr: phrase. 冒风险；把某事公开说出来；把某事摆到桌面上；豁出去
words.ex: He was willing to lay his career on the line to support the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意冒着职业生涯的风险来支持新政策。
words.en: To state something clearly and directly, often involving risk or frankness.

words.tr: phrase. 充分利用某物；把某物派上好用场
words.ex: He put his old tools to good use.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧工具好好利用了。
words.en: To use something in a way that is beneficial or effective.

words.tr: phrase. 把某物投入使用；利用某物
words.ex: She decided to put her knowledge to use and start her own business.
words.ex_cn: 她决定利用她的知识，开始自己的事业。
words.en: To make use of something; to utilize something for a purpose.

words.tr: phrase. 组装某物；把某物拼合起来；整理并准备（计划、报告等）
words.ex: He decided to put everything together and invest in the risky venture.
words.ex_cn: 他决定孤注一掷，投资于这个高风险的项目。
words.en: To assemble or compile something from various parts or elements.

words.tr: phrase. 组装某物；拼凑某物；把某物放在一起；整合某物
words.ex: He decided to put together his savings to start a new business.
words.ex_cn: 他决定把积蓄都拿出来，开始一项新业务。
words.en: to assemble or construct something; to organize or prepare something

words.tr: phrase. 把责任归咎于；把过错推到…身上
words.ex: He put the blame on his brother for the broken vase.
words.ex_cn: 他把责任推给了他弟弟，说是因为他打碎了花瓶。
words.en: To accuse someone of being responsible for something bad that has happened.

words.w: put the cart before the horse
words.tr: phrase. 本末倒置；主次颠倒；顺序错乱
words.uk: pʊt ðə kɑːt bɪˈfɔː ðə hɔːs
words.us: pʊt ðə kɑːrt bɪˈfɔːr ðə hɔːrs
words.ex: You are putting the cart before the horse by planning the party before getting an invitation.
words.ex_cn: 你还没收到邀请就计划派对，这是本末倒置。
words.en: To do things in the wrong order or to prioritize things incorrectly.

words.w: have the cart before the horse
words.tr: phrase. 把事情的顺序弄颠倒了；本末倒置
words.uk: hæv ðə kɑːt bɪˈfɔː ðə həʊs
words.us: hæv ðə kɑrt bɪˈfɔr ðə hoʊs
words.ex: You are having the cart before the horse by planning the party before the invitation.
words.ex_cn: 你计划派对却还没发邀请，这是本末倒置。
words.en: To do things in the wrong order or to prioritize incorrectly.

words.tr: phrase. 告发某人；指认某人（尤指向警方或权威）
words.ex: The witness was able to put the finger on the thief.
words.ex_cn: 证人能够指认出小偷。
words.en: To identify or accuse someone, especially of a crime.

words.tr: phrase. 告发某人；指认某人（尤指向警方揭发其罪行）
words.ex: No one could lay the finger on him for the crime.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能因为这起罪行而指控他。
words.en: to identify or blame someone for a fault or mistake

words.tr: phrase. 对某人施加压力；逼迫某人；迫使某人采取行动
words.ex: The police are really putting the heat on him to confess.
words.ex_cn: 警察正在对他施加巨大压力，迫使他认罪。
words.en: To apply pressure to someone, typically to make them do something or to achieve a desired outcome.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人施加压力；逼迫某人；向某人勒索
words.ex: The boss is putting the screws on the employees to meet the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 老板正在对员工施加压力，要求他们按时完成任务。
words.en: To apply pressure on someone, especially to make them do something.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人施加压力；逼迫某人；向某人勒索
words.ex: The boss is putting the squeeze on me to finish the project by Friday.
words.ex_cn: 老板正在逼我周五前完成这个项目。
words.en: To put pressure on someone to do something, often in a way that is unfair or difficult for them.

words.tr: phrase. 对…施加压力；逼迫；催逼
words.ex: The police decided to put the heat on the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 警方决定对嫌疑人施加压力。
words.en: To apply pressure or stress to someone, often to make them act in a certain way.

words.tr: phrase. 对…施加压力；逼迫；强迫
words.ex: The boss put the screws on the employees to meet the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 老板对员工施加压力，要求他们按时完成任务。
words.en: To apply pressure to someone, typically to force them to do something.

words.tr: phrase. 对…施加压力；逼迫；勒索
words.ex: The boss put the squeeze on the employees to meet the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 老板向员工施压，要求他们按时完成任务。
words.en: To apply pressure or influence on someone or something in order to achieve a desired outcome.

words.tr: phrase. 根据已知事实推断；综合线索得出结论
words.ex: She was able to put two and two together and figure out who the real culprit was.
words.ex_cn: 她能够根据所见所闻推断出真正的罪犯是谁。
words.en: If you put two and two together, you correctly guess the truth about something from the information that is available to you.

words.w: put one's money where one's mouth is
words.tr: phrase. 用行动证明；说到做到；拿出实际行动来支持自己的言论
words.uk: pʊt wʌnz ˈmʌni weə wʌnz maʊθ ɪz
words.us: pʊt wʌnz ˈmʌni wer wʌnz maʊθ ɪz
words.ex: He said he believed in the project, so he put his money where his mouth was.
words.ex_cn: 他说他相信这个项目，于是他用实际行动证明了自己的话。
words.en: To take action to support one's statements or opinions, especially by making a financial contribution.

words.tr: phrase. 强作镇定；装出一副勇敢的样子；故作坚强
words.ex: She put up a brave front during the interview, even though she was terrified.
words.ex_cn: 她在面试时表现得很勇敢，尽管她心里非常害怕。
words.en: To behave in a way that makes it seem as if one is not afraid or upset, even though one really is.

words.tr: phrase. 装门面；假装镇定；故作坚强
words.ex: She put up a front of confidence in front of her colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 她在同事面前装出自信的样子。
words.en: To behave in a way that is not sincere, especially to hide one's true feelings or intentions.

words.tr: phrase. 要么拿出行动来证明，要么闭嘴；要么就行动，否则就别废话
words.ex: If you keep making claims, it's time to put up or shut up.
words.ex_cn: 如果你一直提出主张，现在是时候要么行动，要么闭嘴了。
words.en: Used to tell someone to take action or stop talking about it.

words.tr: phrase. 忍受；容忍
words.ex: I can't put up with his loud noise every night.
words.ex_cn: 我无法忍受他每晚的噪音。
words.en: To tolerate or endure something unpleasant or annoying.

words.tr: phrase. 曲解某人的话；把话强加在某人嘴里；替某人乱说
words.ex: Don't put words into my mouth; I didn't say I hate him.
words.ex_cn: 不要曲解我的话；我没说讨厌他。
words.en: To suggest that someone has said something that they have not actually said.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词PUT补充词组

words.tr: phrase. 摆阔；装腔作势；故作高雅
words.ex: They really put on the dog for their daughter's wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他们为了女儿的婚礼真的摆阔了一番。
words.en: To make a showy display or effort, especially to impress others.

words.tr: phrase. 开始吃饭；准备用餐（口语幽默说法）
words.ex: We're going to put on the feedbag at the buffet tonight.
words.ex_cn: 我们今晚要在自助餐上大吃一顿。
words.en: To begin eating, especially heartily or eagerly.

words.tr: phrase. 找到某物；把某物拿在手里；把手放在某物上
words.ex: I finally managed to put my hand on the book I was looking for.
words.ex_cn: 我终于找到了我一直在找的那本书。
words.en: To place one's hand on something, either physically or metaphorically.

words.tr: phrase. 找到某物；拿到某物；把某物弄到手
words.ex: I'll put my hands on that book for you.
words.ex_cn: 我会帮你找到那本书。
words.en: to find or obtain something, often after searching

words.tr: phrase. 找到（某物）；拿到（某物）；占有（某物）
words.ex: If I can just lay my hand on that book, I'll be able to finish my report.
words.ex_cn: 如果我能找到那本书，我就能完成我的报告。
words.en: To find or obtain something, especially something that is difficult to find.

words.tr: phrase. 找到；得到；抓到；占有
words.ex: I wish I could lay my hands on that book.
words.ex_cn: 我希望我能找到那本书。
words.en: To find or obtain something, especially with some difficulty.

words.tr: phrase. 触摸或拿到某物；着手处理某事
words.ex: He set his hand on the doorknob and hesitated for a moment before turning it.
words.ex_cn: 他把手放在门把手上，犹豫了一会儿才转动它。
words.en: To find or obtain something, especially after searching.

words.tr: 短语动词。设法得到某物；找到某物
words.ex: He finally set his hands on the rare book he had been searching for.
words.ex_cn: 他终于找到了他一直在寻找的那本珍本书。
words.en: To manage to obtain something, especially something that is difficult to get.

words.w: put one's hand to the plow
words.tr: phrase. idiom. 着手工作；开始努力
words.ex: He put his hand to the plow and started working on the farm.
words.ex_cn: 他开始在农场干活，着手工作。
words.en: To begin a task with determination and commitment.

words.tr: phrase. 把某人登记为某事的参与者或捐款人；把某人列入（名单、课程、捐款等）
words.ex: Can I put you down for the charity run next weekend?
words.ex_cn: 我可以把你登记参加下周的慈善跑吗？
words.en: To register someone for a particular activity or event, often implying a commitment or reservation.

words.tr: phrase. 让某人充分展示自己的本领；对某人进行严格考验
words.ex: The coach decided to put the new player through his paces during the training session.
words.ex_cn: 教练决定在训练期间考验新球员的能力。
words.en: To test someone's abilities or skills, especially to see how well they perform under pressure or in different situations.

words.w: put sb. to bed with a shovel
words.tr: phrase. 【俚语】把某人打死（或埋葬）；把某人干掉
words.uk: pʊt ˈsʌmbədi tə bed wɪð ə ˈʃʌvl
words.us: pʊt ˈsʌmbədi tə bed wɪð ə ˈʃʌvl
words.ex: The critics really put that movie to bed with a shovel, saying it was one of the worst films of the year.
words.ex_cn: 评论家们真的把那部电影批得体无完肤，说它是今年最差的电影之一。
words.en: to bury someone (a humorous or euphemistic way of saying someone has died)

words.tr: phrase. 使某人相形见绌；使某人感到羞愧；让某人自愧不如
words.ex: Her dedication put the rest of us to shame.
words.ex_cn: 她的奉献精神让我们其他人自愧不如。
words.en: To make someone feel ashamed by outdoing them or by showing superior qualities.

words.tr: phrase. 向某人透露…的内情；使某人了解…的真相；把…的底细告诉某人
words.ex: He put me wise to the fact that the meeting had been postponed.
words.ex_cn: 他让我知道会议已经推迟了。
words.en: To inform someone about something, especially something they did not know before.

words.tr: phrase. 使被理解；把…讲清楚；成功地表达（想法、观点等）
words.ex: He tried to put across his idea clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他试图清楚地表达他的想法。
words.en: To communicate something clearly and effectively to someone.

words.tr: phrase. 被理解；讲清楚
words.ex: He tried to get across his idea simply.
words.ex_cn: 他试图简单地表达他的想法。
words.en: To succeed in communicating an idea or piece of information to someone, especially when this is difficult or complicated.

words.tr: phrase. 扑灭；熄掉；伸出；发表；恼怒
words.ex: He put out the fire with a blanket.
words.ex_cn: 他用毯子扑灭了火。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or light; to publish or produce something; to extend or stretch out something.

words.tr: phrase. 把…移到不碍事的地方；使…脱离危险；排除…的障碍；把…解决掉
words.ex: He put his toys out of the way before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他把玩具收起来，以免碍事，然后吃晚饭。
words.en: to remove or dispose of something; to deal with a problem or obstacle

words.tr: phrase. 举起；张贴；建造；进行；提供；推举；提供食宿
words.ex: He put up his hand to ask a question.
words.ex_cn: 他举起了手来提问。
words.en: To provide someone with a place to stay temporarily; to build or erect something; to raise or lift something; to propose or suggest something; to display or post something; to increase the price of something.

words.tr: phrase. 把某物存起来备用；储存；储蓄
words.ex: She always tries to put something by for a rainy day.
words.ex_cn: 她总是尽量存点钱以备不时之需。
words.en: to save or reserve something for future use

words.tr: phrase. 随机应变；见机行事；临场发挥
words.ex: He plays the song by ear.
words.ex_cn: 他凭耳朵演奏这首歌。
words.en: to improvise or perform something without prior preparation or rehearsal

words.tr: phrase. 把…归因于…；认为…是由…引起
words.ex: She put her success down to hard work and determination.
words.ex_cn: 她把自己的成功归因于勤奋和决心。
words.en: If you put something down to a particular thing, you believe that it is the cause of it.

words.tr: phrase. 把某事归因于某原因；认为某事是由某原因造成的
words.ex: He set his success down to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: To attribute something to a particular cause or reason.

words.tr: phrase. 投入；插入；安装；提交；花费（时间/精力）
words.ex: He puts his books in the bag.
words.ex_cn: 他把书放进包里。
words.en: To place or insert something into a particular location or position.

words.tr: phrase. 放进；插入；提出；提交；使就职；进港
words.ex: Put in the keys before you leave.
words.ex_cn: 离开前把钥匙放进去。
words.en: To place something inside or into a particular position or location.

words.tr: phrase. 把某物付印；将某事发表出版；使某事见诸印刷
words.ex: They decided to put the book into print last year.
words.ex_cn: 他们去年决定将这本书付印。
words.en: To publish something in writing or print.

words.tr: phrase. 赊账；先记账以后再付
words.ex: He asked if he could put the dinner on the cuff.
words.ex_cn: 他问是否可以把晚餐先赊账。
words.en: To buy something with the agreement that you will pay for it later.

words.tr: phrase. 使（想法、计划等）被理解或接受；成功实施；欺骗，蒙骗
words.ex: He put the hat over his head.
words.ex_cn: 他把帽子戴在头上。
words.en: To communicate or convey an idea effectively.

words.tr: phrase. 欺骗某人；把某事蒙混过关
words.ex: He tried to put one over on his boss by lying about his qualifications.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过谎报资格来欺骗他的老板。
words.en: To deceive someone; to trick someone into believing something that is not true.

words.tr: phrase. 直截了当地说某事；把某事说得简单明了
words.ex: He put the problem plainly so everyone could understand.
words.ex_cn: 他简单明了地说明了问题，所以每个人都能理解。
words.en: To express something in a clear and straightforward manner.

words.tr: phrase. 把某物摆正；澄清某事；纠正某事
words.ex: He put the picture straight on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把画在墙上摆正了。
words.en: To correct or make something right; to arrange something so that it is in the correct position or order.

words.tr: phrase. 把某事弄清楚；纠正某事；使某事恢复正常或正确状态
words.ex: He decided to set his finances straight and take a risk.
words.ex_cn: 他决定整顿财务，孤注一掷。
words.en: To clarify or correct something, especially a misunderstanding or misconception.

words.tr: phrase. 全面测试某物的性能；让某物接受严格考验
words.ex: We decided to put the new car through its paces on the test track.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定在测试赛道上全面检验这辆新车的性能。
words.en: To test something thoroughly to assess its performance or capabilities.

words.tr: phrase. 使某事平息；了结某事；彻底解决某问题
words.ex: The authorities finally managed to put the rumors to rest.
words.ex_cn: 当局终于设法平息了谣言。
words.en: To resolve or settle something, especially a controversy or a question, so that it is no longer a matter of concern or debate.

words.tr: phrase. 埋葬某物；使某事尘埃落定；彻底结束某事
words.ex: He decided to lay all his doubts to rest by asking her directly.
words.ex_cn: 他决定直接问她，以消除所有的疑虑。
words.en: To lay something to rest means to stop people from worrying about it or talking about it, by dealing with it effectively.

words.w: put that in one's pipe and smoke it
words.tr: phrase. 你就好好想想吧；你就接受这个事实吧；你好好掂量掂量（用来强调自己刚说的话不容置疑或必须被接受）
words.uk: pʊt ðæt ɪn wʌnz paɪp ənd sməʊk ɪt
words.us: pʊt ðæt ɪn wʌnz paɪp ənd smoʊk ɪt
words.ex: He told me to put that in my pipe and smoke it when I asked for a raise.
words.ex_cn: 当我要求加薪时，他让我把那话收起来好好想想。
words.en: Accept and consider something, especially an unpleasant fact or piece of advice, without complaint.

words.tr: phrase. 向某人强行索要钱财；向某人施压或勒索
words.ex: He decided to put the arm on his friend for a loan.
words.ex_cn: 他决定向朋友借钱，孤注一掷。
words.en: To pressure or threaten someone in order to obtain something.

words.tr: phrase. 向某人借钱；向某人索要钱财；向某人施加压力
words.ex: He tried to put the bite on his friend for a loan.
words.ex_cn: 他试图向他的朋友借钱。
words.en: To demand money from someone, often in a threatening manner.

words.tr: phrase. 向某人伸手要钱；向某人借钱或索要钱财
words.ex: He tried to put the touch on me for a loan.
words.ex_cn: 他试图向我借钱。
words.en: To ask someone for money, typically a loan.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人加以限制；严厉控制或制止某人
words.ex: The police put the clamps on the suspect to get him to confess.
words.ex_cn: 警察对嫌疑人施加压力，迫使他招供。
words.en: To restrict or exert pressure on someone.

words.tr: phrase. 施加限制；加以控制；制止
words.ex: The authorities decided to put the clamps on the protesters to maintain order.
words.ex_cn: 当局决定对抗议者施加压力以维持秩序。
words.en: To impose restrictions or limitations on something; to stop or control something.

words.tr: phrase. 施加压力；采取严厉措施；加以限制
words.ex: The mechanic put on the clamps to secure the engine in place.
words.ex_cn: 机械师夹紧了夹子以固定引擎的位置。
words.en: To apply brakes or stop something abruptly.

words.tr: phrase. 阻止某事；使某事彻底告吹；给某事泼冷水
words.ex: The bad weather put the kibosh on our plans for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 糟糕的天气打乱了我们野餐的计划。
words.en: To stop or prevent something from happening.

words.tr: phrase. 阻止某事；使某事停止；给某事泼冷水
words.ex: The police put the skids on the illegal street racing.
words.ex_cn: 警察阻止了非法街头赛车。
words.en: To bring something to a halt or cause it to fail.

words.tr: phrase. 使停止；阻止；使计划或进程受挫
words.ex: His plans were put the skids on by unexpected financial problems.
words.ex_cn: 他的计划因意外的财务问题而受阻。
words.en: To slow down or stop the progress of something.

words.tr: phrase. 使陷入困境；使面临困难；迫使（做某事）
words.ex: He was put to it to explain his actions.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不解释他的行为。
words.en: To cause someone to be in a difficult situation where they must do something.

words.tr: phrase. 感到为难；难以应付；不知如何是好
words.ex: When the power went out, we were really put to it to find a way to cook dinner.
words.ex_cn: 当停电时，我们真的陷入了困境，想办法做晚饭。
words.en: To be forced to do something; to be in a difficult situation.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 15 基本动词 RUN

words.tr: phrase. 发烧；发热
words.ex: He runs a fever when he gets sick.
words.ex_cn: 他生病时会发烧。
words.en: To have a higher body temperature than normal, often as a symptom of illness.

words.tr: phrase. 发烧；体温升高
words.ex: He runs a temperature every time he gets a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他每次感冒都会发烧。
words.en: To have a fever.

words.tr: phrase. 冒某事的风险；有遭受某事的危险
words.ex: He decided to run a risk of sth. in order to achieve his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他决定冒着某事的风险，以实现他的目标。
words.en: To be exposed to the possibility of something undesirable happening.

words.tr: phrase. 冒…的风险；有…的危险
words.ex: He was willing to run the risk of losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意冒失去工作的风险。
words.en: To be in a situation where there is a possibility of something bad happening.

words.tr: phrase. 冒…的风险；甘冒…的危险
words.ex: He decided to take a risk of investing in the startup.
words.ex_cn: 他决定冒险投资这家初创公司。
words.en: To undertake an action with the possibility of a negative outcome.

words.tr: phrase. 冒…的风险；甘冒…的危险
words.ex: He decided to take the risk of investing in the new technology.
words.ex_cn: 他决定冒险投资这项新技术。
words.en: To decide to do something even though you know it might have bad or dangerous results.

words.tr: phrase. 冒险；承担风险
words.ex: He runs a risk of failing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他有考试不及格的风险。
words.en: To do something that might result in loss, harm, or danger.

words.tr: phrase. 冒险；冒……的风险
words.ex: He decided to run the risk of losing everything.
words.ex_cn: 他决定冒险失去一切。
words.en: To expose oneself to the possibility of something bad happening.

words.tr: phrase. 严格管理；把…管理得井井有条
words.ex: The manager runs a tight ship at the small store.
words.ex_cn: 这位经理在小店里管理得非常严格。
words.en: To manage a group, organization, or system in a very strict and efficient way.

words.tr: phrase. 严格管理；把…管理得井井有条；维持纪律严明的组织
words.ex: The captain runs a taut ship on the navy boat.
words.ex_cn: 船长在军舰上实行严格管理。
words.en: To manage an organization or team in a strict and efficient manner, ensuring that everything runs smoothly and effectively.

words.tr: phrase. 跑腿；办差事；外出办件小事
words.ex: I need to run an errand to the post office before it closes.
words.ex_cn: v. 我需要在邮局关门之前去办件事。
words.en: To go somewhere to do something for someone, often involving a short trip.

words.tr: 短语动词. 去办差；去跑腿
words.ex: He goes on an errand to buy bread every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都去跑腿买面包。
words.en: To go somewhere to do a specific task, usually for someone else.

words.w: run around like a chicken with its head cut off
words.tr: phrase. （因慌乱或不知所措而）像无头苍蝇一样四处乱窜；手忙脚乱
words.uk: rʌn əˈraʊnd laɪk ə ˈtʃɪkɪn wɪð ɪts hed kʌt ɒf
words.us: rʌn əˈraʊnd laɪk ə ˈtʃɪkɪn wɪð ɪts hed kʌt ɔːf
words.ex: When the fire alarm rang, he ran around like a chicken with its head cut off.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，他像无头苍蝇一样乱跑。
words.en: To act in a frantic, disorganized manner.

words.tr: phrase. 原地打转；徒劳无功地忙碌；兜圈子
words.ex: When I don't know what to do, I feel like I run in circles.
words.ex_cn: 当我不知该做什么时，我感觉我在原地打转。
words.en: To engage in activity that is repetitive and unproductive, making no progress towards a goal.

words.tr: phrase. 原地打转；徒劳无功地忙碌；瞎忙
words.ex: We ran around in circles all day and got nothing done.
words.ex_cn: 我们整天原地打转，什么也没做成。
words.en: To spend a lot of time and energy doing something without achieving anything useful.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人厮混；常与某人混在一起（尤指结伴玩乐或交往）
words.ex: She likes to run around with her friends after school.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢放学后和朋友一起四处闲逛。
words.en: To spend time with someone, often in a social context, implying a casual or possibly frivolous relationship.

words.tr: phrase. 从…逃离
words.ex: She decided to run away from her problems instead of facing them.
words.ex_cn: 她决定逃离问题，而不是面对它们。
words.en: To leave a place or situation quickly in order to escape from something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 逃跑；出走；逃避
words.ex: The boy ran away from home.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩从家里跑走了。
words.en: To leave a place or person secretly and suddenly in order to escape from them or to avoid a difficult or unpleasant situation.

words.tr: phrase. 与某事相违背；与某事相反；背道而驰
words.ex: His actions run counter to his promises.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为与他的承诺背道而驰。
words.en: If something runs counter to something else, it is opposed to it or different from it.

words.tr: phrase. （特征、疾病或才能）世代相传；家族遗传
words.ex: Being good at singing runs in the family.
words.ex_cn: 擅长唱歌是我们家的家族特点。
words.en: If a quality, ability, disease, etc. runs in the family, many members of the family have it.

words.tr: phrase. 家族遗传；世代相传；与生俱来的特质
words.ex: The talent for music seems to run in the blood of this family.
words.ex_cn: 音乐天赋似乎是这个家族世代相传的。
words.en: To be an inherent or natural characteristic of a family or group.

words.tr: phrase. 遇到无法逾越的障碍；碰壁；遭遇顽固阻力
words.ex: We run into a stone wall when we try to find the answer.
words.ex_cn: 当我们试图找到答案时，遇到了无法克服的困难。
words.en: To encounter an obstacle that is very difficult or impossible to overcome.

words.tr: phrase. 遭遇无法逾越的障碍；碰壁；陷入僵局
words.ex: We tried to solve the problem, but we ran into a brick wall.
words.ex_cn: 我们试图解决这个问题，但却碰了壁。
words.en: To encounter an insurmountable difficulty or obstacle.

words.tr: phrase. 喋喋不休；信口开河；说个不停
words.ex: He tends to run off at the mouth whenever he gets nervous.
words.ex_cn: 每当他紧张时，他总是喋喋不休。
words.en: To talk incessantly or indiscreetly.

words.tr: phrase. 与…私奔；擅自带走；偷走；突然携…离开
words.ex: He run off with the money last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚带着钱跑了。
words.en: To leave a place or person suddenly and secretly, especially in order to get married or to steal something.

words.tr: phrase. 用完某物；耗尽某物
words.ex: We ran out of milk this morning.
words.ex_cn: 我们今天早上牛奶喝完了。
words.en: To have no more of something left because it has all been used.

words.tr: phrase. 用完；耗尽；跑出去；到期
words.ex: We run out of milk every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 我们每星期天都把牛奶喝光了。
words.en: If you run out of something, you have no more of it left.

words.tr: phrase. 碾过；溢出；匆匆浏览；超过（时间、数量等）
words.ex: The car ran over a small stone on the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车碾过了路上的一块小石头。
words.en: To hit someone or something with a vehicle and drive over them; to quickly look through or read something; to overflow.

words.tr: phrase. 失控；肆虐；放纵；任意滋长
words.ex: The children run riot in the playground every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们每天下午都在操场上乱跑乱闹。
words.en: If someone runs riot, they behave in a wild and uncontrolled way. If something runs riot, it spreads or develops in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr: phrase. 放肆；撒野；不受控制
words.ex: The children run wild in the park every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们每天下午在公园里疯跑。
words.en: If someone or something runs wild, they behave in a natural, free, or uncontrolled way.

words.tr: phrase. 撞倒；耗尽；贬低；追捕到；浏览；削弱；逐渐恶化
words.ex: The car ran down a pedestrian at the crossing.
words.ex_cn: 那辆车在十字路口撞倒了一名行人。
words.en: To criticize someone or something in a way that makes them seem less good or important; to hit someone with a vehicle and injure or kill them; to reduce the size or effectiveness of something gradually; to find someone or something after searching.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人精疲力竭；把某人折腾得疲惫不堪
words.ex: The demanding project ran the team ragged.
words.ex_cn: 这个要求很高的项目让团队筋疲力尽。
words.en: To make someone extremely tired by giving them too much work or by making them do too much.

words.tr: phrase. 因恐惧而退缩；战战兢兢地行事；害怕失败而提前撤退
words.ex: When the dog barked, the cat ran scared.
words.ex_cn: 当狗叫时，猫吓得跑了。
words.en: To flee in fear.

words.tr: phrase. 缺少某物；某物快用完了
words.ex: We ran short of food supplies during the long journey.
words.ex_cn: 在漫长的旅途中，我们的食物供应不足。
words.en: To not have enough of something that you need.

words.tr: phrase. 短缺；用尽；不够
words.ex: We run short of water in summer.
words.ex_cn: 我们在夏天缺水。
words.en: If you run short of something, you do not have enough of it.

words.tr: phrase. 把某事做过头；过度使用某事物直至其失去新鲜感或效用；因管理不善而弄垮某事物
words.ex: He ran the project into the ground by micromanaging every detail.
words.ex_cn: 他通过过分管理每个细节，把项目搞得一团糟。
words.en: To manage or use something so badly that it is almost destroyed or ruined.

words.tr: phrase. v. 把某物彻底毁掉；使某事彻底失败；过度使用某物直至报废
words.ex: He drove the project into the ground by insisting on unrealistic deadlines.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持不切实际的截止日期，把项目搞得一团糟。
words.en: To do something to an excessive or extreme degree, often leading to its failure or ruin.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词RUN补充词组

words.tr: phrase. 追赶；追求；追捕
words.ex: The dog runs after the ball every time.
words.ex_cn: 每次狗都追球跑。
words.en: To chase or pursue someone or something, often in a literal sense of running behind them to catch up.

words.tr: phrase. （感情、想象力等）失去控制；与…私奔；轻易赢得；偷走
words.ex: He might run away with the idea that you don't care.
words.ex_cn: 他可能会误以为你不在乎。
words.en: To leave a place or person secretly in order to marry or live with someone, especially when others do not approve; to steal something; to win something easily.

words.tr: phrase. 逃跑；出走；逃避
words.ex: The boy ran away from home.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩从家里跑走了。
words.en: To leave a place or person secretly and suddenly in order to escape from them or to avoid a difficult or unpleasant situation.

words.tr: phrase. 逃命；拼命逃跑；为保命而狂奔
words.ex: He runs for his life when the dog chases him.
words.ex_cn: 当狗追他时，他拼命逃跑。
words.en: To run as fast as possible to escape from a dangerous or life-threatening situation.

words.tr: phrase. v. 逮捕某人并带往警察局；把某人送进监狱
words.ex: The police ran him in for questioning.
words.ex_cn: 警察逮捕了他进行审问。
words.en: To arrest someone and take them to a police station.

words.tr: phrase. 偶遇某人；偶然碰见某人
words.ex: I ran into my old friend at the store.
words.ex_cn: 我在商店里碰到了我的老朋友。
words.en: If you run into someone, you meet them unexpectedly.

words.tr: phrase. 逃跑； 流掉；迅速离开
words.ex: The boy ran off with his brother's bike.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩骑着他哥哥的自行车跑掉了。
words.en: To leave a place or situation quickly and secretly, often to avoid a problem or responsibility; to produce copies of a document quickly; to discharge or release a liquid.

words.tr: phrase. v. 迅速制作；匆匆缝制；使（数量、债务等）迅速增加；升起（旗帜等）
words.ex: He decided to run up his credit card bills on the chance of a big win.
words.ex_cn: 他决定孤注一掷，用信用卡透支以期获得大赢。
words.en: To accumulate or increase something, especially debts or bills.

words.tr: phrase. 积欠（债务、账单等）；快速增加（数量、费用等）
words.ex: She managed to run up a large debt in a short time.
words.ex_cn: 她在短时间内成功地累积了一大笔债务。
words.en: To accumulate or increase something, typically a debt or bill, quickly or to a large extent.

words.tr: phrase. 跑着穿过；刺、戳；贯穿；匆匆处理；排练；划掉；挥霍
words.ex: The dog ran through the park quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗迅速跑过了公园。
words.en: To go over or examine something quickly; to be present in every part of something; to rehearse a play, piece of music, etc.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 16 基本动词 SEE

words.tr: phrase. v. 处理；安排；照料（某事）
words.ex: I will see about the meeting time.
words.ex_cn: 我会去确认一下会议时间。
words.en: To attend to or deal with something.

words.tr: phrase. （两人）看法一致；意见相同
words.ex: We don't always see eye to eye, but we respect each other's opinions.
words.ex_cn: 我们并不总是看法一致，但我们尊重彼此的意见。
words.en: If two people see eye to eye, they agree with each other.

words.w: see eye to eye about sth.
words.tr: phrase. （就某事）看法一致，意见相同
words.uk: siː aɪ tuː aɪ əˈbaʊt sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: siː aɪ tuː aɪ əˈbaʊt sʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: We don't see eye to eye about this issue.
words.ex_cn: 我们对这个问题的看法不一致。
words.en: To agree completely with someone about something.

words.w: see eye to eye on sth.
words.tr: phrase. 在某事上意见一致；看法相同
words.ex: They don't always see eye to eye on political issues.
words.ex_cn: 他们在政治问题上并不总是看法一致。
words.en: To agree with someone or have the same opinion as them about something.

words.tr: phrase. 护送某人回家；送某人到家
words.ex: He offered to see her home after the party.
words.ex_cn: 聚会结束后，他主动提出送她回家。
words.en: To accompany someone to their home to ensure they arrive safely.

words.tr: phrase. 为某人送行
words.ex: I will see my brother off at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 我会去机场为我哥哥送行。
words.en: To accompany someone to the point of departure, especially as a gesture of farewell.

words.tr: phrase. 为某人送行；送别某人
words.ex: I went to the airport to see off my friend.
words.ex_cn: 我去机场送我的朋友。
words.en: To accompany someone to the place where they are beginning a journey and say goodbye to them there.

words.tr: phrase. 坚持完成某事；把某事进行到底
words.ex: He decided to see his plan through despite the risks.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有风险，他决定孤注一掷，坚持执行他的计划。
words.en: To persevere with a task or situation until it is completed.

words.tr: phrase. 看到星星（通常指因撞击、眩晕或强烈刺激而眼前冒金星）
words.ex: When I spin around, I see stars.
words.ex_cn: 当我转圈时，我看到星星。
words.en: To see stars means to see flashes of light, usually as a result of being hit on the head.

words.tr: phrase. 产生幻觉；看到并不存在的事物
words.ex: Sometimes when I'm tired, I think I see things that aren't really there.
words.ex_cn: 有时候当我累的时候，我觉得我看见了并不存在的东西。
words.en: To perceive with the eyes; to understand or comprehend something.

words.w: see the color of one's money
words.tr: phrase. phr. 看到某人的钱；要求某人先付钱
words.ex: If you want a refund, you must see the color of one's money.
words.ex_cn: 如果你想退款，就必须看到对方的钱。
words.en: To confirm that someone has sufficient funds or to see evidence of their ability to pay before proceeding with a transaction or agreement.

words.w: see the handwriting on the wall
words.tr: phrase. 预见到不祥之兆；察觉到即将发生的厄运或失败
words.ex: He saw the handwriting on the wall and left the company before the layoffs.
words.ex_cn: 他察觉到了不祥之兆，于是在裁员前离开了公司。
words.en: To perceive signs or warnings of impending disaster or misfortune.

words.w: see the writing on the wall
words.tr: phrase. 察觉到不祥的征兆；预见到即将发生的厄运或失败
words.ex: He saw the writing on the wall and left the company before the layoffs.
words.ex_cn: 他看出了形势不妙，于是在裁员前离开了公司。
words.en: To perceive signs or indications that something bad is going to happen.

words.tr: phrase. 最后一次见到；彻底摆脱
words.ex: I hope I never have to see the last of him.
words.ex_cn: 我希望我再也不用见到他了。
words.en: If you see the last of someone or something, you see them for the last time, often because they are going away or disappearing.

words.tr: phrase. 顿悟；明白事理；看清真相
words.ex: After the teacher explained it, he finally saw the light.
words.ex_cn: 老师解释后，他终于明白了。
words.en: To understand or realize something after a period of confusion or ignorance.

words.w: see the light at the end of the tunnel
words.tr: phrase. 看到隧道尽头的光，比喻在困境中看到希望或问题即将解决
words.uk: /siː ðə laɪt æt ði end əv ðə ˈtʌnl/
words.us: /si ðə laɪt æt ði ɛnd əv ðə ˈtʌnl/
words.ex: After months of hard work, we can finally see the light at the end of the tunnel.
words.ex_cn: 经过几个月的辛勤工作，我们终于看到了成功的希望。
words.en: To begin to see that a difficult or unpleasant situation is improving or coming to an end.

words.tr: phrase. 参观名胜；游览观光
words.ex: When you visit Paris, make sure to see the sights like the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre.
words.ex_cn: 当你访问巴黎时，一定要去观光，比如埃菲尔铁塔和卢浮宫。
words.en: To visit and look at places of interest, especially as a tourist.

words.tr: phrase. 看穿；识破
words.ex: I can see through his lie.
words.ex_cn: 我看穿了他的谎言。
words.en: To perceive the true nature of someone or something, especially their deceitfulness or the real situation. Also, to support someone or something until the end of a difficult situation.

words.tr: phrase. 负责；注意；照料
words.ex: I will see to the children while you are away.
words.ex_cn: 你不在的时候，我会照看孩子们。
words.en: To attend to or take care of something.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词SEE补充词组

words.w: see a man about a dog
words.tr: phrase. （委婉语）去办点私事，通常指去上厕所、喝酒或处理其他不便明说的小事
words.uk: siː ə mæn əˈbaʊt ə dɒɡ
words.us: si ə mæn əˈbaʊt ə dɔɡ
words.ex: I can't stay long, I have to see a man about a dog.
words.ex_cn: 我不能久留，我得去处理点私事。
words.en: A polite, often humorous, way to excuse oneself from a situation, typically to leave without giving a specific reason.

words.tr: phrase. 认为合适做某事；觉得应当做某事
words.ex: She saw fit to change the meeting time.
words.ex_cn: 她认为合适更改会议时间。
words.en: To consider it appropriate or suitable to do something.

words.tr: phrase. 认为合适做某事；觉得应当做某事
words.ex: He thought fit to cancel the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他认为取消会议是合适的。
words.en: To consider it appropriate or suitable to do something.

words.tr: phrase. 认为合适；觉得应当（做某事）
words.ex: The company reserves the right to change the terms of the contract at any time, as they see fit.
words.ex_cn: 公司保留随时更改合同条款的权利，只要他们认为适当。
words.en: If someone sees fit to do something, they think it is good or necessary to do it.

words.tr: phrase. 认为合适；觉得恰当（常用于 think fit to do sth 结构）
words.ex: I think fit to go to the park today.
words.ex_cn: 我认为今天去公园合适。
words.en: To consider something to be appropriate or suitable for a particular purpose or situation.

words.tr: phrase. 不反对某事；认为某事没有问题
words.ex: She sees no objection to working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 她不反对加班。
words.en: To not have any reason to oppose or disapprove of something.

words.tr: 短语动词。不反对；认为没有异议
words.ex: I see no objection to your proposal.
words.ex_cn: 我不反对你的提议。
words.en: No objection is seen; the speaker does not oppose or disapprove of something.

words.w: see one's way clear to do sth.
words.tr: phrase. 觉得能够做某事；认为自己有理由或条件去做某事（常用于委婉表达同意或愿意）
words.uk: /siː wʌnz weɪ klɪə tə duː sʌmθɪŋ/
words.us: /si wʌnz weɪ klɪr tu du sʌmθɪŋ/
words.ex: He decided to see his way clear to invest in the risky venture.
words.ex_cn: 他决定孤注一掷，投资于这个高风险的项目。
words.en: If you see your way clear to doing something, you are able or willing to do it.

words.tr: phrase. （尤用于否定或疑问句）愿意做某事；觉得方便或合适去做某事
words.ex: He could not see his way clear to lending her the money.
words.ex_cn: 他无法同意借给她那笔钱。
words.en: To find a method or path to do something, especially after considering it carefully.

words.tr: phrase. 暴怒；勃然大怒（形容因愤怒而失去理智）
words.ex: He sees red when someone takes his things without asking.
words.ex_cn: 当有人未经允许拿他的东西时，他就会非常生气。
words.en: To become very angry suddenly.

words.tr: phrase. 得以问世；被公开；被实现（尤指长期被搁置的事物）
words.ex: The new book will finally see the light of day next month.
words.ex_cn: 这本书下个月终于要出版了。
words.en: If something sees the light of day, it becomes publicly known or available after being kept secret or hidden for a long time.

words.tr: phrase. 顿悟；明白事理；看清真相
words.ex: After the teacher explained it, he finally saw the light.
words.ex_cn: 老师解释后，他终于明白了。
words.en: To understand or realize something after a period of confusion or ignorance.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 17 基本动词 STAND

words.tr: phrase. 有获胜或成功的可能性；有机会
words.ex: If you study hard, you stand a chance of passing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 如果你努力学习，你就有可能通过考试。
words.en: To have a possibility of succeeding or achieving something.

words.tr: 短语动词。有可能（成功、获胜、被接受等）；有希望（做某事）
words.ex: If you study hard, you stand a chance of passing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 如果你努力学习，你就有可能通过考试。
words.en: To have a possibility of achieving something.

words.w: stand a chance of doing something
words.tr: phrase. 有做某事的可能性；有机会做成某事
words.ex: If you study hard, you stand a chance of passing the test.
words.ex_cn: 如果你努力学习，你就有通过考试的可能。
words.en: To have a possibility of achieving something or succeeding in something.

words.tr: phrase. 支持；站在……背后；为……撑腰
words.ex: I will stand behind my friend no matter what happens.
words.ex_cn: 无论发生什么事，我都会支持我的朋友。
words.en: To support or be in agreement with someone or something; to be ready to support or defend someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 支持；遵守；袖手旁观；准备行动
words.ex: I will stand by you when you face difficulties.
words.ex_cn: 当你遇到困难时，我会支持你。
words.en: To be ready to support or act if needed; to wait in a state of readiness.

words.tr: phrase. 代表某事物；象征某种意义；支持或主张某种理念
words.ex: We must stand for something, even if it is just honesty.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须坚持一些东西，即使只是诚实。
words.en: To tolerate or accept something one disagrees with; to represent an idea or principle.

words.tr: phrase. 替代某人；代替某人（尤指临时顶替）
words.ex: My brother will stand in for me at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 我弟弟将代替我去参加会议。
words.en: To temporarily perform the duties or responsibilities of someone else.

words.tr: phrase. 代替；代表；做替身；使花费
words.ex: Tom will stand in for the manager while she is away.
words.ex_cn: 当经理离开时，汤姆将代替她。
words.en: To temporarily take someone's place or perform their duties.

words.tr: phrase. 阻碍某人；挡某人的路
words.ex: Fear can stand in one's way of success.
words.ex_cn: 恐惧会阻碍一个人成功。
words.en: To prevent someone from doing something or achieving something.

words.w: stand on one's own two feet
words.tr: phrase. 独立自主；自立；不依赖他人
words.ex: When she got a job and rented her own room, she began to stand on her own two feet.
words.ex_cn: 当她找到工作并租了自己房间时，她开始自立了。
words.en: To be independent and able to take care of oneself without help from others.

words.tr: phrase. 坚持立场；不退让；坚决抵抗
words.ex: He stood his ground when the bully tried to take his lunch.
words.ex_cn: 当那个欺负人的孩子想拿走他的午餐时，他坚持了自己的立场。
words.en: To refuse to be forced to move backwards or to change your opinion, even when someone is opposing you or threatening you.

words.tr: phrase. 坚持立场；不退让；守住阵地
words.ex: He held his ground when the bully tried to take his lunch.
words.ex_cn: 当那个欺负人的孩子想拿走他的午餐时，他坚持不退让。
words.en: To maintain one's position or opinion despite opposition or pressure.

words.tr: phrase. 引人注目；突出；出色
words.ex: Her red hat makes her stand out in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 她的红帽子让她在人群中很显眼。
words.en: To be very noticeable or obvious, especially in comparison to others.

words.tr: phrase. 放某人鸽子；约定见面却故意不到场
words.ex: She stood her date up last night.
words.ex_cn: 她昨晚放了她约会的鸽子。
words.en: To fail to meet someone for a date or appointment without informing them in advance.

words.tr: phrase. 站起来
words.ex: The students stand up when the teacher enters the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 当老师走进教室时，学生们站起来。
words.en: If you stand up, you rise to your feet from a sitting or lying position.

words.tr: phrase. 合乎情理；顺理成章；是理所当然的
words.ex: It stands to reason that if you study hard, you will pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 你努力学习就会通过考试，这是合乎逻辑的。
words.en: If you say that something stands to reason, you mean that it is obvious or logical.

words.tr: phrase. 表明立场；挺身而出表明自己的态度或支持
words.ex: He must stand up and be counted for his beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他必须为自己的信念挺身而出，表明立场。
words.en: To declare one's support for or opposition to something publicly.

words.tr: phrase. 支持；捍卫；为…挺身而出
words.ex: He will stand up for his friend when others are mean.
words.ex_cn: 当别人对他的朋友刻薄时，他会为朋友挺身而出。
words.en: To support or defend someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. v. 抵抗；勇敢面对；经得起（考验或压力）
words.ex: He stood up to the bully and helped his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他勇敢地对抗欺负人的孩子，帮助了他的朋友。
words.en: To confront someone or something in a brave or determined way.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词STAND补充词组

words.tr: phrase. 对……感到敬畏；对……肃然起敬
words.ex: Children stand in awe of the big mountain.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们对这座大山充满敬畏。
words.en: To feel a mixture of respect, wonder, and fear towards someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 肃然起敬；敬畏地站立
words.ex: The children stand in awe of the big mountain.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们对这座大山感到敬畏。
words.en: To feel a mixture of respect, wonder, and fear towards someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 拘泥礼节；讲究形式
words.ex: They don't stand on ceremony at home.
words.ex_cn: 他们在家里不讲究繁文缛节。
words.en: To behave in a very formal or polite way, especially when this is not necessary.

words.tr: phrase. 监督某人；居高临下地盯着某人（常含威胁或压迫意味）
words.ex: The teacher stands over the student while he writes.
words.ex_cn: 老师站在学生旁边看他写字。
words.en: To watch or supervise someone closely, often in a way that makes them feel uncomfortable.

words.tr: phrase. 对某人有益；对某人有帮助
words.ex: His hard work stood him in good stead when he applied for the job.
words.ex_cn: 当他申请工作时，他的努力为他带来了好处。
words.en: If something stands you in good stead, it is helpful or useful to you.

words.tr: phrase. 请某人吃喝（或享受某种款待）
words.ex: He stood his friends to a treat at the ice cream shop.
words.ex_cn: 他请朋友们在冰淇淋店吃了一顿。
words.en: To pay for someone's entertainment or refreshment, typically as a gesture of generosity or celebration.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人一起站立；支持或陪伴某人（尤指在困难或正式场合中）
words.ex: I will stand up with my friend when he needs help.
words.ex_cn: 当我的朋友需要帮助时，我会站出来支持他。
words.en: To support or be present with someone, especially during a difficult time.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 18 基本动词 TAKE

words.tr: phrase. 让位于……；甘居次要地位；屈居……之后
words.ex: He always takes a back seat to his boss in meetings.
words.ex_cn: 在会议上他总是让老板出风头。
words.en: To be less important than something else and to receive less attention.

words.tr: phrase. 退居次要位置；不积极参与；让别人主导
words.ex: After the new manager arrived, John decided to take a back seat and let her lead the project.
words.ex_cn: 新经理到来后，约翰决定退居次要地位，让她来领导项目。
words.en: To take a less active or prominent role in something; to allow others to lead or take charge.

words.tr: phrase. 在某事上遭受重大损失；在某事上惨败（尤指投资或赌博）
words.ex: He takes a bath on his worries every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都为自己的烦恼洗个澡。
words.en: To suffer a significant financial loss on an investment or venture.

words.tr: phrase. 洗澡；沐浴
words.ex: He takes a bath every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上洗澡。
words.en: To wash oneself in a bathtub.

words.tr: phrase. （表演后）鞠躬致谢；接受掌声与赞美
words.ex: The singer takes a bow after the song.
words.ex_cn: 歌手在歌曲结束后鞠躬致意。
words.en: To acknowledge applause by bowing, especially at the end of a performance.

words.tr: phrase. 休息一下；暂停工作或活动
words.ex: He takes a break after working for two hours.
words.ex_cn: 他工作两小时后休息一下。
words.en: To stop doing something for a short period of time in order to rest or do something else.

words.tr: phrase. 冒险
words.ex: He decided to take a chance and apply for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他决定冒险申请这份工作。
words.en: To do something that involves risk or uncertainty, often with the hope of success.

words.tr: phrase. 冒险
words.ex: He took a risk and started his own business.
words.ex_cn: 他冒了一个险，开了自己的公司。
words.en: To do something that involves the possibility of danger, loss, or failure.

words.tr: phrase. 尝试做某事；试一试（尤指有挑战性的事）
words.ex: He decided to take a crack at solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他决定试着解决这个数学问题。
words.en: To attempt to do something, especially something difficult or challenging.

words.w: take a dim view of sth.
words.tr: phrase. 对某事持否定或不赞成的看法；对某事评价不高
words.ex: He takes a dim view of cheating in exams.
words.ex_cn: 他不赞成考试作弊。
words.en: To regard something with disapproval or pessimism.

words.tr: 看中; 看上; 对…喜欢起来; 结缘
words.ex: He takes a fancy to her because she is kind.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢上了她，因为她很善良。
words.en: To develop a liking or affection for someone or something, often suddenly.

words.tr: phrase. 开始喜欢（某人或某物）
words.ex: He takes a liking to his new teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢上了他的新老师。
words.en: To begin to like someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. （非正式）开始喜欢上（某人或某物）
words.ex: He takes a shine to his new teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢上了他的新老师。
words.en: If you take a shine to someone or something, you like them very much as soon as you meet them or see them.

words.tr: phrase. （俚语）看一看；瞧一瞧
words.ex: Can you take a gander at this picture?
words.ex_cn: 你能看一眼这张图片吗？
words.en: To take a quick look at something.

words.tr: phrase. phr. （俚语）看一看，瞧一瞧
words.ex: Take a gander at the new painting on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 看一下墙上的那幅新画。
words.en: To take a look at something, often casually or briefly.

words.tr: phrase. 采取强硬立场；持严厉态度
words.ex: The government decided to take a hard line against the protesters.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定对抗议者采取强硬立场。
words.en: To adopt an uncompromising or strict approach or policy in dealing with a situation or person.

words.w: take a hard line with sb.
words.tr: phrase. 对某人采取强硬态度；对某人毫不妥协
words.ex: The teacher takes a hard line with students who cheat.
words.ex_cn: 老师对作弊的学生采取严厉态度。
words.en: To adopt a strict or uncompromising approach in dealing with someone.

words.tr: phrase. 接受暗示；领会暗示；识趣（指能理解别人委婉的提示或暗示）
words.ex: He didn't take a hint when I closed the door.
words.ex_cn: 当我关上门时，他没有领会暗示。
words.en: To understand or realize what someone is suggesting indirectly.

words.w: take a leaf out of one's book
words.tr: phrase. 效仿某人的做法；借鉴某人的经验
words.uk: /teɪk ə liːf aʊt əv wʌnz bʊk/
words.us: /teɪk ə lif aʊt əv wʌnz bʊk/
words.ex: You should take a leaf out of her book and be more kind.
words.ex_cn: 你应该向她学习，变得更友善。
words.en: To copy or follow someone's example because they have been successful at something.

words.tr: phrase. 看一看；查看；审视
words.ex: Take a look at this picture.
words.ex_cn: 看一下这张图片。
words.en: To examine or inspect something briefly.

words.tr: phrase. 看一看；查看
words.ex: I will have a look at your homework.
words.ex_cn: 我会看一下你的作业。
words.en: To direct one's gaze towards something in order to see it.

words.tr: phrase. 看一下；瞧一眼
words.ex: Can you take a look at my homework?
words.ex_cn: 你能看一下我的作业吗？
words.en: To direct one's gaze in order to see someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 出现新的转机；转向新的方向
words.ex: The story will take a new turn tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 故事明天会有一个新的转折。
words.en: To undergo a significant change or development.

words.tr: phrase. 出现另一个新的转折；发生新的变化
words.ex: The story will take another new turn tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事明天会再次出现新的转折。
words.en: To change direction or approach in a new or different way.

words.tr: phrase. （俚语）悄悄溜走；偷偷离开；逃避责任或困境
words.ex: He took a powder when the police arrived.
words.ex_cn: 警察来的时候，他溜走了。
words.en: To leave suddenly or hastily, especially to avoid trouble or an unpleasant situation.

words.tr: phrase. 向某人挥拳；试图打某人一拳
words.ex: He took a punch at his brother during the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他在打架时朝他弟弟打了一拳。
words.en: To attempt to hit someone with a fist.

words.tr: phrase. 尝试做某事；试着处理某事（尤指不确定能否成功）
words.ex: He decided to take a stab at solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他决定试着解决这个数学问题。
words.en: To try to do something, especially something difficult or challenging.

words.tr: 短语动词. 尝试做某事，试着解决某事（通常指不太确定能否成功）
words.ex: I will have a stab at solving this math problem.
words.ex_cn: 我会试着解这道数学题。
words.en: To attempt or try to do something, especially when it is difficult or when you are not sure if you will succeed.

words.tr: phrase. 表明立场；明确立场
words.ex: He decided to take a stand on the controversial issue.
words.ex_cn: 他决定在这个有争议的问题上表明立场。
words.en: To take a stand means to adopt a firm position on a particular issue, often in a public or formal manner.

words.tr: phrase. 为某事采取立场；支持某事；公开表明支持某种观点或事业
words.ex: He takes a stand for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他为清洁用水而发声。
words.en: To publicly support or defend a particular set of beliefs or ideas.

words.tr: phrase. 试着做某事；尝试某事
words.ex: He wants to take a try at solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他想试着解这道数学题。
words.en: To attempt to do something.

words.tr: phrase. 尝试做某事；冒险一试
words.ex: He decided to take a shot at singing in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他决定在全班面前试一试唱歌。
words.en: To attempt to do something, especially something challenging or difficult.

words.tr: 短语动词. 尝试做某事
words.ex: I will have a try at solving this math problem.
words.ex_cn: 我会试着解这道数学题。
words.en: To attempt to do something, especially something new or challenging.

words.tr: 短语动词. 尝试做某事；争取某事的机会
words.ex: Why don't you have a shot at solving the problem?
words.ex_cn: 你为什么不试试解决这个问题呢？
words.en: To attempt to do something, especially something that is challenging or that you have not done before.

words.w: take a turn for the better
words.tr: 短语：情况开始好转；形势转好
words.ex: After being sick for a week, her health took a turn for the better.
words.ex_cn: 生病一周后，她的健康状况好转了。
words.en: If a situation takes a turn for the better, it improves.

words.w: take a turn for the worse
words.tr: 短语动词。情况恶化；转坏（尤指健康或局势）
words.ex: The weather took a turn for the worse in the afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 下午天气突然变坏了。
words.en: If a situation takes a turn for the worse, it suddenly becomes worse.

words.tr: phrase. 对…采取行动；针对…采取措施
words.ex: The school will take action against students who cheat.
words.ex_cn: 学校将对作弊的学生采取行动。
words.en: To take steps or measures to deal with a problem or situation, especially in a legal or official context.

words.tr: phrase. 利用；欺骗；占便宜
words.ex: He took advantage of the free tickets.
words.ex_cn: 他利用了免费的票。
words.en: To use a particular situation to do or get what you want.

words.tr: phrase. （在相貌、性格等方面）像（某人）， resemble (someone) in appearance or character
words.ex: Tom takes after his father in personality.
words.ex_cn: 汤姆在性格上像他父亲。
words.en: To resemble a family member, especially in appearance or character.

words.tr: phrase. 瞄准；针对；把…作为目标
words.ex: He takes aim at the target with a bow and arrow.
words.ex_cn: 他用弓箭瞄准目标。
words.en: To direct one's effort or attention towards a particular target or goal.

words.tr: phrase. 瞄准；对准目标
words.ex: He takes aim at the target with his toy gun.
words.ex_cn: 他用玩具枪对准目标。
words.en: To point or direct (a weapon or camera) at a target.

words.tr: phrase. 对...感兴趣
words.ex: He takes an interest in birds.
words.ex_cn: 他对鸟类感兴趣。
words.en: To become interested in something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 对……产生兴趣；关心
words.ex: He takes an interest in birds.
words.ex_cn: 他对鸟类感兴趣。
words.en: To become interested in something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 照顾；照料；处理；应付
words.ex: She takes care of her little brother after school.
words.ex_cn: 她放学后照顾她的弟弟。
words.en: To look after someone or something; to deal with something.

words.tr: phrase. 负责；看管
words.ex: He will take charge of the project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周将负责这个项目。
words.en: To assume control or responsibility for something.

words.tr: phrase. 负责；看管
words.ex: He will take charge of the project next week.
