words.ex_cn: 他下周将负责这个项目。
words.en: To assume control or responsibility over something.

words.tr: phrase. 对……表示反对；对……反感；对……提出异议
words.ex: He takes exception to people who are late.
words.ex_cn: 他看不惯迟到的人。
words.en: To object strongly to something; to be offended by something.

words.tr: phrase. 表示反对；提出异议；感到不满
words.ex: He took exception to the comment about his work.
words.ex_cn: 他对关于他工作的评论表示不满。
words.en: To object to something; to express disagreement with something.

words.tr: phrase. 休息五分钟（常用于工作或排练中短暂休息）
words.ex: He takes five minutes to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他休息五分钟。
words.en: To take a short break, typically of five minutes, from work or an activity.

words.tr: 短语动词。鼓起勇气；振作精神
words.ex: Take heart, things will get better.
words.ex_cn: 振作起来，事情会好起来的。
words.en: If you take heart from something, you are encouraged and made to feel optimistic by it.

words.tr: phrase. 留意；注意；当心
words.ex: Take heed of the warning sign.
words.ex_cn: 注意这个警告标志。
words.en: To pay attention to something, especially advice or a warning.

words.tr: phrase. 握住；控制住；掌握
words.ex: He takes hold of the rope to climb up.
words.ex_cn: 他抓住绳子往上爬。
words.en: To grasp or seize something with the hands; to gain control or influence over something.

words.tr: phrase. 抓住；掌握；得到；找到某人
words.ex: He tried to get hold of the rope.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抓住那根绳子。
words.en: To obtain something or to contact someone.

words.tr: phrase. 开始生效；扎根；占据主导地位
words.ex: The idea began to take hold among young people.
words.ex_cn: 这个想法开始在年轻人中流行起来。
words.en: To begin to have a strong effect; to start to control or influence someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 与...争论
words.ex: He takes issue with the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他不同意这个新规定。
words.en: To disagree with someone or something, especially publicly.

words.tr: phrase. 表示异议；提出反对；争论
words.ex: I have to take issue with your statement that all politicians are corrupt.
words.ex_cn: 我不得不对你的说法——所有政客都是腐败的——提出异议。
words.en: To disagree with or challenge a statement or opinion.

words.tr: phrase. 对…放松些；对…别太严厉；对…手下留情
words.ex: Take it easy on him, he is just a beginner.
words.ex_cn: 对他宽容点，他只是个新手。
words.en: To treat someone with leniency or not to be too harsh on someone.

words.tr: 习语。要么接受，要么放弃（表示提出的条件不可更改）
words.ex: I will give you $50 for the bike, take it or leave it.
words.ex_cn: 我给你50美元买这辆自行车，要就拿走，不要就算了。
words.en: If you say to someone 'take it or leave it', you are telling them that they can accept something or not accept it, but that you are not prepared to discuss any other alternatives.

words.tr: phrase. 别着急；慢慢来；放轻松
words.ex: Take it slow when you drive in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 下雨天开车时要慢一点。
words.en: To proceed at a leisurely or cautious pace.

words.tr: phrase. 对…有好感；欣然接受；不反感
words.ex: He does not take kindly to criticism.
words.ex_cn: 他不乐意接受批评。
words.en: If you take kindly to something, you accept it or agree to it willingly and with pleasure.

words.tr: phrase. 失去理智；发疯
words.ex: He must take leave of his senses to shout at the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他一定是失去理智了才会对老师大喊大叫。
words.en: To behave in a way that is not rational or sensible.

words.tr: phrase. 随意篡改；擅自改动；对…不拘礼节（常含贬义）
words.ex: He takes liberties with the rules to help his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他为了帮助朋友而随意违反规则。
words.en: To make changes to something in a way that is not strictly accurate or respectful, often adding one's own ideas or interpretations.

words.tr: phrase. 擅自使用；随意动用；对…放肆无礼
words.ex: He makes free with my things without asking.
words.ex_cn: 他未经允许就随便动我的东西。
words.en: To use something without permission or restraint; to take liberties with.

words.tr: phrase. 不相信；不重视；对……不以为然
words.ex: He take no stock in rumors about his neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会关于他邻居的谣言。
words.en: To not believe in or trust something or someone.

words.tr: phrase. 不相信某事；对某事持怀疑态度；不看重某事
words.ex: He does not take stock in rumors about the company.
words.ex_cn: 他不相信关于这家公司的谣言。
words.en: To not believe in or value something.

words.tr: phrase. 注意；留意；记下
words.ex: Please take note of the time.
words.ex_cn: 请记下时间。
words.en: To pay attention to something or someone because you think they are important.

words.tr: phrase. 注意；留意；记下
words.ex: Please take note of the time we start class.
words.ex_cn: 请注意我们上课的时间。
words.en: To pay attention to or to make a record of something.

words.tr: phrase. 注意到某事；留意某物
words.ex: He did not take notice of the sign.
words.ex_cn: 他没有注意到那个标志。
words.en: To become aware of something through observation or attention.

words.tr: phrase. 注意；留意；关注
words.ex: He did not take notice of the warning sign.
words.ex_cn: 他没有注意到那个警告标志。
words.en: To become aware of something or someone through observation or attention.

words.w: take off one's hat to sb.
words.tr: phrase. 对某人表示敬意；钦佩某人
words.ex: I take off my hat to her for winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 我佩服她赢得了比赛。
words.en: To show admiration or respect for someone.

words.tr: phrase. 脱帽致敬；表示钦佩或尊敬
words.ex: He takes off his hat when he sees the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他看到老师时会脱帽致意。
words.en: To remove one's hat, especially as a sign of respect or greeting.

words.w: take one's hat off to sb.
words.tr: phrase. 对某人表示钦佩或敬意；脱帽致敬某人
words.ex: I take my hat off to her for finishing the marathon.
words.ex_cn: 我向她脱帽致敬，因为她完成了马拉松。
words.en: To express admiration or respect for someone because of something they have done.

words.tr: phrase. 对……感到不快；因……而生气；对……觉得被冒犯
words.ex: He takes offense at small jokes.
words.ex_cn: 他对于小玩笑很敏感。
words.en: To feel upset or insulted by something that someone has said or done.

words.tr: phrase. 生气；不悦；被冒犯：对他人的言行感到生气或不悦，被冒犯。
words.ex: He took offense when she laughed at his joke.
words.ex_cn: 当她笑他的笑话时，他感到被冒犯了。
words.en: To feel upset or insulted by something said or done.

words.tr: phrase. 就职；上任；开始担任公职
words.ex: He took office last January.
words.ex_cn: 他去年一月上任。
words.en: To assume a position of authority or responsibility, especially in a formal or official capacity.

words.tr: phrase. 相信某人所说的话并据此行动；信以为真
words.ex: I take you at your word that you will help me tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我相信你明天会帮我。
words.en: To believe that what someone says is true and will be acted upon.

words.tr: phrase. 告别某人；向某人辞行
words.uk: teɪk wʌnz liːv əv ɛs biː
words.us: teɪk wʌnz liːv əv ɛs biː
words.ex: He took his leave of his friends before leaving town.
words.ex_cn: 他离开小镇前向朋友们告别了。
words.en: To say goodbye to someone, especially in a formal or polite way.

words.tr: phrase. 告辞；离开（某人或某地）
words.ex: He stood up and took his leave after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他站起来，在会议结束后告辞了。
words.en: To say goodbye and depart from someone or some place.

words.tr: phrase. 告别某人；辞别某人
words.ex: He took leave of his friend before leaving town.
words.ex_cn: 他离开城镇前向朋友告别。
words.en: To say goodbye to someone, often before a departure.

words.tr: phrase. 接受应得的惩罚或不愉快的后果；忍气吞声
words.ex: He made a mistake, so he had to take his medicine and accept the punishment.
words.ex_cn: 他犯了错误，所以只得认罚，接受后果。
words.en: To accept or endure something unpleasant, especially as a consequence of one's own actions.

words.tr: phrase. 自杀；结束自己的生命
words.ex: He felt so sad that he wanted to take his own life.
words.ex_cn: 他感到非常悲伤，想要结束自己的生命。
words.en: To commit suicide; to end one's own life intentionally.

words.tr: phrase. 慢慢来；不着急；从容不迫地做某事
words.ex: He takes his time to finish the homework.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢做作业，不着急。
words.en: To use as much time as one needs, without hurrying.

words.tr: phrase. 不辞辛劳地做某事；费心尽力做某事
words.ex: He takes pains to write every letter clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他努力把每个字母写得清晰。
words.en: To make a great effort to ensure that something is done well or correctly.

words.tr: phrase. 下苦功；费心尽力；认真努力做某事
words.ex: He takes pains to help his classmates with homework.
words.ex_cn: 他费尽心思帮助同学做作业。
words.en: If you take pains to do something or go to great pains to do something, you try hard to do it, because you think it is important to do it.

words.tr: phrase. 发生
words.ex: The meeting will take place tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 会议将在明天举行。
words.en: When something takes place, it happens, especially in a controlled or organized way.

words.tr: phrase. 生根；扎根；确立
words.ex: The idea began to take root in his mind.
words.ex_cn: 这个想法开始在他的脑海中扎根。
words.en: To begin to grow or develop; to become established or fixed.

words.tr: phrase. （尤指突然）生病，感到不适
words.ex: He has to take sick leave because he has a fever.
words.ex_cn: 他因为发烧不得不请病假。
words.en: To become ill.

words.tr: phrase. 突然生病；身体不适
words.ex: He took ill suddenly during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间突然生病了。
words.en: To become ill; to fall sick.

words.tr: phrase. 表态支持某一方；偏袒某一方
words.ex: He won't take sides in their argument.
words.ex_cn: 他不会在他们的争论中站队。
words.en: To support one person or group in an argument, fight, or competition against another.

words.w: take sb. down a peg or two
words.tr: phrase. 使某人谦虚一点；挫某人的傲气
words.uk: /teɪk ˌsʌmbɒdi daʊn ə ˈpɛɡ ɔː tuː/
words.us: /teɪk ˌsʌmbɑdi daʊn ə ˈpɛɡ ɔr tu/
words.ex: He was too proud, so his coach took him down a peg or two.
words.ex_cn: 他太骄傲了，所以教练给他泼了点冷水。
words.en: To make someone realize that they are not as important, skilled, or clever as they thought they were.

words.w: bring sb. down a peg or two
words.tr: phrase. 使某人受挫，让某人谦逊一些，降低某人的傲气
words.uk: brɪŋ səmˈbɒdi daʊn ə peɡ ɔː tuː
words.us: brɪŋ ˈsʌmbədi daʊn ə peɡ ɔr tuː
words.ex: He was too proud, so his coach brought him down a peg or two.
words.ex_cn: 他太骄傲了，所以教练给他打了点预防针。
words.en: To make someone realize that they are not as important or skilled as they think they are.

words.w: let sb. down a peg or two
words.tr: phrase. 杀某人的威风；挫某人的傲气；使某人收敛一些
words.uk: let ˈsʌmbədi daʊn ə pɛɡ ɔː tuː
words.us: let ˈsʌmbədi daʊn ə pɛɡ ɔːr tuː
words.ex: He failed the test, and it let him down a peg or two.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，这让他谦虚了一点。
words.en: To make someone less arrogant or self-confident by showing or proving that they are not as good as they think they are.

words.w: take sb. down a notch or two
words.tr: phrase. 使某人谦虚一点；挫一挫某人的傲气
words.uk: /teɪk sʌmˌbɒdi daʊn ə nɒtʃ ɔːr tuː/
words.us: /teɪk sʌmˌbɑːdi daʊn ə nɑːtʃ ɔːr tuː/
words.ex: He boasted too much, so his friend took him down a notch or two.
words.ex_cn: 他太自夸了，所以朋友给他泼了点冷水。
words.en: To reduce someone's pride or self-confidence; to humble someone.

words.tr: phrase. 误认为某人是…；把某人当作…（常用于否定或疑问句）
words.ex: He takes me for his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他把我当成他的兄弟。
words.en: To mistakenly believe someone is something they are not, especially a fool or a criminal.

words.tr: phrase. 拿走……；带走……；使……离开
words.ex: Please take the book away from the table.
words.ex_cn: 请把书从桌子上拿走。
words.en: To remove something or someone from a place.

words.tr: phrase. 拿走；取走；扣除
words.ex: He takes away the toys after playtime.
words.ex_cn: 他玩完后把玩具拿走。
words.en: To remove something from a place or to subtract a number or amount from another.

words.tr: phrase. （尤指在艺术、娱乐等领域）使……大获成功；使……大受欢迎；征服……
words.ex: The new song took the world by storm.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌风靡全球。
words.en: To achieve great and rapid success in a particular field or to captivate the public's imagination suddenly and overwhelmingly.

words.tr: phrase. 把…列入考虑中
words.ex: We must take the weather into account when planning the picnic.
words.ex_cn: 计划野餐时，我们必须把天气考虑进去。
words.en: If you take something into account, you consider it when you are thinking about a situation or deciding what to do.

words.tr: phrase. 使……措手不及；出其不意地袭击或惊吓
words.ex: The test results took her by surprise.
words.ex_cn: 测试结果让她大吃一惊。
words.en: To cause someone to feel surprised because they were not expecting something.

words.tr: phrase. 认为…理所当然；想当然
words.ex: He takes his health for granted.
words.ex_cn: 他把健康视为理所当然。
words.en: If you take something for granted, you believe it to be true or accept it as normal without thinking about it.

words.tr: phrase. 接管；接任；取代
words.ex: He will take over the business next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月将接管这家企业。
words.en: To take control of something, especially a company, by buying a majority of its shares or by getting a position of power within it.

words.tr: phrase. 误解；曲解（某人的话或行为）
words.ex: I took your words wrong, I thought you were angry.
words.ex_cn: 我误解了你的话，我以为你生气了。
words.en: To interpret or understand something in an incorrect or offensive way; to misunderstand or be offended by something said or done.

words.tr: phrase. 激动得说不出话来；使某人大为惊讶
words.ex: The view from the mountain takes my breath away.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色让我惊叹不已。
words.en: If something takes your breath away, it is so beautiful, amazing, or surprising that you feel unable to breathe for a moment.

words.tr: phrase. 责备某人；训斥某人
words.ex: The teacher took the student to task for not completing the homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为学生没有完成作业而责备了他。
words.en: To criticize or reprimand someone for something they have done wrong.

words.tr: phrase. 彻底击败某人；使某人破产；狠狠敲某人竹杠
words.ex: He took him to the cleaners in the poker game.
words.ex_cn: 他在扑克游戏中赢了他一大笔钱。
words.en: To cause someone to lose a lot of money, especially in a way that seems unfair.

words.tr: phrase. 收某人为门徒；庇护或照顾某人
words.ex: My teacher took me under her wing when I was new at school.
words.ex_cn: 当我刚到学校时，老师收留了我并照顾我。
words.en: To take someone under one's wing means to take care of and protect someone, especially someone who is younger or less experienced.

words.tr: phrase. 收某人为门徒；庇护或照顾某人
words.ex: The teacher took the new student under her wings.
words.ex_cn: 老师收留了这个新生，给予照顾。
words.en: To take someone under one's wing means to take care of them and protect them, often by providing guidance and support.

words.tr: phrase. 接受某人的提议或邀请；对某人的话采取行动
words.ex: He took me up on my offer to help with the project.
words.ex_cn: 他接受了我帮忙做这个项目的提议。
words.en: If you take someone up on their offer or suggestion, you accept it.

words.tr: phrase. v. 接受某人的建议、邀请或挑战；对某人的话作出回应（尤指接受提议或反驳）
words.ex: He took me up on my offer to help.
words.ex_cn: 他接受了我帮忙的提议。
words.en: To accept an offer or challenge from someone, especially one that involves doing something specific.

words.w: take a load off one's feet
words.tr: phrase. 休息一下，放松一下（尤指坐下歇脚）
words.uk: teɪk ə ləʊd ɒf wʌnz fiːt
words.us: teɪk ə loʊd ɔːf wʌnz fiːt
words.ex: After work, he sat down to take a load off his feet.
words.ex_cn: 下班后，他坐下歇歇脚。
words.en: To sit down and rest, especially after standing or walking for a long time.

words.tr: phrase. 表面理解某事物；不加怀疑地接受某事的表面价值或说法
words.ex: Don't take his words at face value.
words.ex_cn: 不要表面化地相信他的话。
words.en: To accept something as it appears to be without questioning its truth or validity.

words.tr: phrase. 对某事泰然处之；轻松应对某事（尤指困难或意外情况）
words.ex: He took the bad news in stride.
words.ex_cn: 他坦然接受了这个坏消息。
words.en: To deal with something difficult or unpleasant in a calm and accepting way.

words.tr: phrase. 逆来顺受；不加反抗地接受（尤指侮辱或挫折）
words.ex: He will not take that lie lying down.
words.ex_cn: 他不会顺从地接受那个谎言。
words.en: To accept something unpleasant without complaining or trying to fight against it.

words.tr: phrase. 误解某事；对某事产生错误的理解或反应
words.ex: He meant his comment as a joke, but she took it the wrong way.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论本意是开玩笑，但她误解了。
words.en: To misunderstand or misinterpret something that is said or done.

words.tr: phrase. 对某事感到不悦或误解；把某事当作冒犯
words.ex: He took my joke amiss.
words.ex_cn: 他把我的玩笑当真了。
words.en: To interpret something in a wrong way or to be offended by something that was not intended to offend.

words.tr: phrase. 盲目相信某事；不加验证地接受某事
words.ex: I take his words on faith because he is honest.
words.ex_cn: 我相信他的话，因为他很诚实。
words.en: To accept something as true without proof or evidence.

words.tr: phrase. 勇敢面对困难或打击；承受挫折或批评而不退缩
words.ex: He took the criticism on the chin and kept working.
words.ex_cn: 他接受了批评，继续工作。
words.en: To accept something unpleasant, such as criticism or a difficult situation, without complaining or trying to avoid it.

words.tr: phrase. 把……发泄在……身上；迁怒于……
words.ex: He took his stress out on his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他把压力发泄在弟弟身上。
words.en: To express one's negative feelings by treating someone else badly, often unfairly.

words.tr: phrase. 把某事放在心上；认真对待某事；因某事而感到难过或受伤
words.ex: He took her words to heart and changed his behavior.
words.ex_cn: 他把她的话放在心上，改变了行为。
words.en: To take something to heart means to be deeply affected or influenced by something, especially a remark, criticism, or advice, and to take it very seriously.

words.tr: phrase. 开始从事（某项活动、爱好等）；占用（时间、空间等）；继续（中断的事）
words.ex: He decided to take up gardening in his free time.
words.ex_cn: 他决定在空闲时间开始从事园艺。
words.en: To start doing something regularly as a habit, job, or interest; to fill or occupy time or space.

words.tr: phrase. 开始从事某事；占用（时间、空间等）；接受（提议、挑战等）
words.ex: He took up painting last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年开始学画画。
words.en: To begin to do or deal with something; to occupy or fill a space or period of time; to continue something that was stopped.

words.tr: phrase. v. （向某人）提出（问题、投诉等）商议或讨论
words.ex: I will take the problem up with my teacher.
words.ex_cn: 我会把这个问题跟老师说。
words.en: To discuss or bring up a matter with someone for consideration or action.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人讨论或处理某事；向某人提出某事
words.ex: He took up the problem with his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向老师反映了这个问题。
words.en: To discuss or bring a matter to someone's attention for consideration or resolution.

words.tr: phrase. 主动承担（责任、任务等）；自作主张做某事
words.ex: He took the blame upon himself.
words.ex_cn: 他把责任揽到了自己身上。
words.en: To accept a responsibility or task voluntarily.

words.tr: phrase. 主动承担某事；自告奋勇负责某事
words.ex: He took the blame on himself.
words.ex_cn: 他把责备揽到了自己身上。
words.en: To accept or begin to deal with a responsibility or task.

words.w: take sth. with a grain of salt
words.tr: phrase. 对某事持保留态度；对某事半信半疑
words.uk: /teɪk ˈsʌmθɪŋ wɪð ə ɡreɪn əv sɔːlt/
words.us: /teɪk ˈsʌmθɪŋ wɪð ə ɡreɪn əv sɔːlt/
words.ex: Take his advice with a grain of salt.
words.ex_cn: 对他的话要打点折扣。
words.en: To not completely believe something that you are told, because you think it is unlikely to be true.

words.w: take sth. with a pinch of salt
words.tr: phrase. 孤注一掷
words.ex: I took his promise with a pinch of salt.
words.ex_cn: 我对他的承诺持保留态度。
words.en: If you take something with a pinch of salt, you do not believe that it is completely accurate or true.

words.tr: phrase. 采取措施以防止某事发生
words.ex: They take steps to prevent pollution.
words.ex_cn: 他们采取措施防止污染。
words.en: Take measures or actions to stop something from happening or to avoid a problem.

words.tr: phrase. 采取措施；采取步骤
words.ex: We must take steps to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须采取措施保护环境。
words.en: To take steps means to begin a course of action intended to achieve a particular result.

words.tr: phrase. 评估某事物；盘点；审视（形势、资源、状况等）
words.ex: He took stock of his savings before buying a car.
words.ex_cn: 他在买车前盘点了自己的积蓄。
words.en: To take stock of something means to think carefully about a situation or event and form an opinion about it, so that you can decide what to do next.

words.tr: phrase. 评估形势；盘点库存；重新考虑或审视当前状况
words.ex: He took stock of his money before buying anything.
words.ex_cn: 他在买东西之前清点了钱。
words.en: To assess or review a situation or one's resources.

words.w: take the bitter with the sweet
words.tr: phrase. 甘苦与共；有苦有甜都要接受（比喻接受事物好的和坏的方面）
words.ex: He takes the bitter with the sweet when he works hard and still feels tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他努力工作却依然感到疲惫时，他坦然接受苦与乐。
words.en: To accept both the bad things and the good things that happen in life.

words.w: take the bull by the horns
words.tr: phrase. 迎难而上；果断处理棘手问题
words.ex: He took the bull by the horns and fixed the problem himself.
words.ex_cn: 他勇敢地直面问题，自己解决了它。
words.en: To deal with a difficult situation in a very direct or confident way.

words.tr: phrase. （尤用于负面语境）最糟糕；最离谱；拔得头筹（常含讽刺意味）
words.ex: His excuse was so silly, it really takes the cake.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口太可笑了，真是令人难以置信。
words.en: To be the most outstanding or egregious example of something, often used sarcastically to denote something surprisingly bad or good.

words.tr: phrase. 减轻某事物的强度或锋芒；缓解（压力、疼痛、紧张等）
words.ex: A hot cup of tea can take the edge off your hunger.
words.ex_cn: 一杯热茶可以减轻你的饥饿感。
words.en: To reduce the intensity or severity of something, making it less unpleasant or difficult to deal with.

words.tr: phrase. 减轻（压力、疼痛、紧张等）；缓和（情绪或强度）
words.ex: He drank tea to take the edge off his stress.
words.ex_cn: 他喝茶来缓解压力。
words.en: To reduce the intensity or severity of something, often making it more bearable.

words.tr: phrase. （尤指在法庭上）援引美国宪法第五修正案拒绝回答可能自证其罪的问题；保持沉默以避免自陷罪责
words.ex: When questioned by the police, he decided to take the Fifth.
words.ex_cn: 当被警察问讯时，他决定援引美国宪法第五修正案，拒绝作证。
words.en: To refuse to answer a question, especially in a legal setting, on the grounds that the answer might incriminate oneself.

words.w: take the law into one's own hands
words.tr: phrase. 擅自执法；私自执法（指不通过法律程序，自行采取报复或惩罚行动）
words.uk: /teɪk ðə lɔː ɪntuː wʌnz əʊn hændz/
words.us: /teɪk ðə lɔː ɪntuː wʌnz oʊn hændz/
words.ex: He took the law into his own hands when he chased the thief with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 当他拿着棍子追小偷时，他把法律掌握在了自己手中。
words.en: To take the law into one's own hands means to try to enforce the law or punish someone for a crime without involving the police or the legal system.

words.w: take the liberty of doing sth.
words.tr: 短语. 冒昧做某事；擅自做某事（常用于礼貌地为自己未经允许的行为道歉或解释）
words.ex: He took the liberty of using my pen without asking.
words.ex_cn: 他未经允许就用了我的笔。
words.en: If you take the liberty of doing something, you do it without asking for permission, often because you feel it is your right or duty to do so.

words.tr: phrase. 揭开某物的盖子；比喻揭露或公开某事
words.ex: The journalist took the lid off the scandal, revealing the extent of the corruption.
words.ex_cn: 记者揭开了丑闻的盖子，揭露了腐败的严重程度。
words.en: To remove the cover from something, often revealing its contents or causing a change.

words.tr: phrase. （尤指在法庭上）出庭作证；站上证人席
words.ex: He will take the stand to tell the truth in court.
words.ex_cn: 他将出庭作证说真话。
words.en: To take the stand means to go into the witness box in a court of law in order to give evidence.

words.w: take the trouble to do sth.
words.tr: phrase. 不辞辛劳地做某事；特意费心做某事
words.ex: He took the trouble to drive me to the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他不辞辛劳地开车送我去机场。
words.en: To make the effort to do something, especially when it is difficult or inconvenient.

words.tr: phrase. 不怕费事；特意花力气（做某事）
words.ex: He takes the trouble to help his classmates with homework.
words.ex_cn: 他不嫌麻烦地帮助同学做作业。
words.en: To make an effort to do something, especially when it is inconvenient or requires extra work.

words.tr: phrase. 承担过多（工作、责任等）；揽下太多事务
words.ex: He takes on too much work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天承担了太多工作。
words.en: To accept more tasks or responsibilities than one can handle.

words.w: take the wind out of one's sails
words.tr: phrase. 使某人泄气；挫败某人的锐气或计划
words.uk: /teɪk ðə wɪnd aʊt əv wʌnz seɪlz/
words.us: /teɪk ðə wɪnd aʊt əv wʌnz seɪlz/
words.ex: The bad news took the wind out of his sails.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息让他泄了气。
words.en: To make someone feel less confident or enthusiastic, especially by saying or doing something unexpected.

words.w: take the words out of one's mouth
words.tr: phrase. 抢先说出某人正想说的话；道出某人心中所想
words.uk: /teɪk ðə wɜːdz aʊt əv wʌnz maʊθ/
words.us: /teɪk ðə wɝːdz aʊt əv wʌnz maʊθ/
words.ex: You just said I was tired — that takes the words right out of my mouth!
words.ex_cn: 你刚说我觉得累了——这正是我想说的！
words.en: If you take the words out of someone's mouth, you say exactly what they were going to say.

words.tr: phrase. 请假；抽出时间休息；暂时离开工作或职责
words.ex: He will take time off to visit his family.
words.ex_cn: 他将请假去探望家人。
words.en: To take time off means to take a break from work or other duties, often for rest or to deal with personal matters.

words.tr: phrase. 逃跑；溜之大吉
words.ex: When the dog barked, the boy took to his heels.
words.ex_cn: 当狗叫的时候，男孩拔腿就跑。
words.en: To run away; to flee.

words.tr: phrase. 发起募捐；收集捐款
words.ex: They decided to take up a collection to help the family in need.
words.ex_cn: v. 他们决定募捐来帮助那个需要帮助的家庭。
words.en: To collect money or items from a group of people for a specific purpose, especially to help someone or to fund a project.

words.tr: phrase. 拿起武器反抗；武装起来对抗
words.ex: The villagers took up arms against the invaders.
words.ex_cn: 村民们拿起武器反抗入侵者。
words.en: To begin fighting or opposing someone or something, especially using weapons.

words.tr: phrase. 占用某人的时间
words.ex: Watching TV takes up his time every evening.
words.ex_cn: 看电视占用了他每天晚上的时间。
words.en: To occupy someone's time, often in a way that is considered unnecessary or excessive.

words.tr: phrase. 占用空间；占据地方
words.ex: The big box takes up room in the small house.
words.ex_cn: 这个大箱子在小房子里占了很多空间。
words.en: To occupy space or area.

words.tr: phrase. 占据空间；占用地方
words.ex: The big box takes up space in the room.
words.ex_cn: 这个大箱子占了房间里的空间。
words.en: To occupy or fill a particular area or volume.

words.tr: phrase. 占用时间；花费时间
words.ex: Watching TV can take up time you could use for studying.
words.ex_cn: 看电视会占用你本可以用来学习的时间。
words.en: To occupy or require time.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词TAKE补充词组

words.tr: phrase. 讽刺某人；挖苦某人
words.ex: He took a dig at his colleague during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议中对他的同事进行了讽刺。
words.en: To make a sarcastic or mocking remark about someone.

words.tr: phrase. （口语）讽刺或挖苦某人；对某人进行言语攻击
words.ex: She took digs at him for his lack of punctuality.
words.ex_cn: 她因为他不守时而挖苦他。
words.en: To make fun of or criticize someone in a teasing or sarcastic manner.

words.tr: phrase. 参与某事；插手某事
words.ex: She decided to take a hand in the project after realizing how important it was.
words.ex_cn: 在意识到这个项目的重要性后，她决定参与进来。
words.en: To become involved in or contribute to an activity or situation.

words.tr: 短语动词. 参与某事；在某事中起作用
words.ex: She had a hand in organizing the event.
words.ex_cn: 她在组织这次活动中起到了作用。
words.en: If you have a hand in something, you are involved in it or have influence over it.

words.tr: phrase. 尝试做某事；冒险一试
words.ex: He decided to take a shot at singing in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他决定在全班面前试一试唱歌。
words.en: To attempt to do something, especially something challenging or difficult.

words.tr: 短语动词. 尝试做某事；争取某事的机会
words.ex: Why don't you have a shot at solving the problem?
words.ex_cn: 你为什么不试试解决这个问题呢？
words.en: To attempt to do something, especially something that is challenging or that you have not done before.

words.tr: phrase. 摔倒；跌倒（尤指从坐骑或自行车上摔下）
words.ex: He took a spill while riding his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他骑自行车时摔了一跤。
words.en: To fall down or fall over, especially in a way that is unexpected or uncontrolled.

words.tr: 短语动词. 摔倒；跌倒（尤指从动物背上）；（非正式）意外洒出
words.ex: Be careful not to have a spill on the new carpet.
words.ex_cn: 小心不要把东西洒在新地毯上。
words.en: To have an accident where a liquid is accidentally poured or spilled.

words.tr: phrase. 散步
words.ex: He takes a walk after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后去散步。
words.en: To go for a walk, especially for pleasure or exercise.

words.tr: phrase. 走开；滚蛋（用于粗鲁地叫人离开）
words.ex: I told him to take a hike when he wouldn't stop bothering me.
words.ex_cn: 我告诉他走开，当他不停地打扰我时。
words.en: To go away; to leave. Often used as an imperative to tell someone to go away.

words.tr: phrase. 试着做某事；尝试一下（尤指不太有把握的事）
words.ex: I'm going to take a whack at solving this puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 我打算尝试解决这个谜题。
words.en: To make an attempt or try to do something, often something that one has not done before or is not skilled at.

words.tr: phrase. 尝试做某事；努力一试（通常指尝试某项任务或活动）
words.ex: Why don't you have a whack at solving the problem?
words.ex_cn: 你为什么不试试解决这个问题呢？
words.en: To attempt to do something, especially for the first time.

words.tr: phrase. v. 尝试做某事；试一试（某事）
words.ex: I will have a crack at solving this math problem.
words.ex_cn: 我会试着解这道数学题。
words.en: To attempt to do something, especially for the first time.

words.tr: phrase. 小睡片刻；打个盹儿
words.ex: After lunch, I usually take forty winks to recharge.
words.ex_cn: 午饭后，我通常会小睡片刻来充电。
words.en: To have a short sleep, especially during the day.

words.tr: phrase. （常用于表演开始前）开始吧；拿走它
words.ex: The band leader signaled the musicians to take it away.
words.ex_cn: 乐队指挥示意音乐家们开始演奏。
words.en: To begin something, especially a performance or presentation; to remove something from a place.

words.tr: phrase. v. 追赶；追随（某人）
words.ex: The plane will take off after the rain stops.
words.ex_cn: 飞机将在雨停后起飞。
words.en: To start chasing or following someone or something.

words.tr: 短语动词。模仿（某人）；在性格或行为上追随（尤指家庭成员）
words.ex: He takes out his anger on his little brother after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后把怒气发泄在弟弟身上。
words.en: To start chasing or pursuing someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 拿掉；离开；起飞；脱下；突然成功
words.ex: Please take off your hat before entering.
words.ex_cn: 进入前请把帽子拿掉。
words.en: If an aircraft, bird, or insect takes off, it leaves the ground and begins to fly.

words.tr: phrase. v. （非正式）突然开始谈论某事，尤指离题或夸张地谈论
words.ex: He decided to take off on the popular TV show for his next comedy routine.
words.ex_cn: 他决定以流行的电视节目为灵感，创作下一个喜剧节目。
words.en: To begin discussing or criticizing a topic, often in a negative way.

words.tr: phrase. 开始着手某事；着手进行某事；大胆地开始做某事
words.ex: He likes to launch forth on stories about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢开始讲述关于他旅行的故事。
words.en: To begin a journey or a new phase with enthusiasm or determination.

words.tr: phrase. 开始；着手；启程；出发
words.ex: The company decided to launch forth into the new market despite the risks.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有风险，公司决定孤注一掷进入新市场。
words.en: To start speaking or acting with great energy and confidence.

words.tr: phrase. 参加某事；参与某事
words.ex: He takes part in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他参加学校的戏剧表演。
words.en: To participate in an activity or event.

words.tr: phrase. 参与；参加（活动、事件等）
words.ex: He will take part in the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他将参加学校的戏剧表演。
words.en: To take part in something means to be involved in an activity or event.

words.tr: phrase. 同情
words.ex: Please take pity on the poor dog and give it some food.
words.ex_cn: 请可怜这只可怜的狗，给它一些食物。
words.en: To feel sympathy for someone because they are in a difficult or unpleasant situation.

words.tr: phrase. 对…表示怜悯；同情
words.ex: Please have pity on the poor dog.
words.ex_cn: 请可怜一下这只可怜的狗。
words.en: To feel sympathy or sorrow for someone's suffering or misfortune.

words.tr: phrase. 误把某人当作另一人
words.ex: I almost took him for his brother; they look so alike.
words.ex_cn: 我差点把他当成他哥哥了；他们长得太像了。
words.en: To mistakenly believe that someone is someone else because they look similar.

words.tr: phrase. 欺骗某人；收留某人；充分理解某人
words.ex: He was taken in by the con artist's elaborate story.
words.ex_cn: 他被骗子的精心编造的故事给骗了。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone into believing something that is not true.

words.tr: phrase. 拆开；拆卸；严厉批评
words.ex: He likes to take toys apart to see how they work.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢把玩具拆开看看它们是怎么工作的。
words.en: To disassemble something into its component parts; to analyze or criticize something in detail.

words.tr: phrase. 拆卸； 拆开
words.ex: He took apart the clock to see how it works.
words.ex_cn: 他把钟表拆开来看它是如何工作的。
words.en: To separate something into its different parts, especially in order to repair it or to understand how it works.

words.tr: phrase. 拿回；收回；取消；使回忆起
words.ex: I will take back my book from the library.
words.ex_cn: 我会从图书馆拿回我的书。
words.en: To take something back means to return something to the place it came from, or to admit that something you said was wrong.

words.tr: phrase. 吸收；领会；接待；接受
words.ex: Plants take in sunlight to make food.
words.ex_cn: 植物吸收阳光来制造食物。
words.en: To take something in means to understand it or to absorb it. It can also mean to deceive someone or to make clothes smaller.

words.tr: phrase. 呈现；承担；接受；较量；雇用
words.ex: The sky takes on a pink color at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空呈现出粉红色。
words.en: To undertake or begin to deal with a task or responsibility; to hire someone; to acquire a particular appearance or quality.

words.tr: phrase. 带某人外出（尤指吃饭、娱乐等）；使某人离开某处；（口语）击倒或杀死某人
words.ex: He often takes his girlfriend out for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他经常带女朋友出去吃饭。
words.en: To take someone out means to escort them somewhere, usually for entertainment or a meal, as a social activity.

words.tr: phrase. 拿出；取出；去掉；取得；领到
words.ex: He took out his keys to open the door.
words.ex_cn: 他拿出钥匙开门。
words.en: To remove something from a place or to take something with you when you go somewhere.

words.tr: phrase. 取出某物；带某人外出；移除；申请（如贷款、保险等）
words.ex: She took her keys out of her purse.
words.ex_cn: 她从钱包里拿出了钥匙。
words.en: To remove something from a place or to obtain something from a source.

words.tr: phrase. 脱下某物；摘掉某物；扣除某物
words.ex: He took his coat off when he entered the warm room.
words.ex_cn: 他进入温暖的房间后脱下了外套。
words.en: To remove something, especially a piece of clothing; to leave the ground and begin to fly; to become successful or popular very quickly.

words.tr: phrase. 请一天假；休息一天
words.ex: He will take a day off tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天要休息一天。
words.en: To take a day off means to decide not to go to work or school on a particular day, usually for rest or personal reasons.

words.tr: phrase. 为……承担责任；替……背黑锅
words.ex: He decided to take the rap for the accident to protect his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他决定为这次事故承担责任，以保护他的朋友。
words.en: To accept blame or punishment for something, especially to protect someone else.

words.tr: phrase. （替别人）承担责备或惩罚；代人受过
words.ex: He took the rap for breaking the window.
words.ex_cn: 他为打破窗户承担了责任。
words.en: To accept blame or punishment for something, especially something that someone else has done.

words.w: take the starch out of sb.
words.tr: phrase. 使某人泄气；挫败某人的锐气或傲气
words.uk: teɪk ðə stɑːrtʃ aʊt əv ˈsʌmbədi
words.us: teɪk ðə stɑːrtʃ aʊt əv ˈsʌmbədi
words.ex: The bad news took the starch out of him and he became very quiet.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息让他失去了勇气，他变得非常安静。
words.en: To make someone lose confidence or vitality.

words.tr: phrase. 开始从事；喜欢；形成...的习惯
words.ex: He took to swimming every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他开始每天早上游泳来保持健康。
words.en: To begin to like someone or something; to start doing something as a habit or regular activity.

words.tr: phrase. 轮流做某事
words.ex: We take turns at doing the dishes every night.
words.ex_cn: 我们每天晚上轮流洗碗。
words.en: To alternately perform a task or duty with one or more people.

words.tr: 短语动词。轮流做某事
words.ex: The children take turns playing with the toy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们轮流玩这个玩具。
words.en: If two or more people take turns doing something, they do it one after the other several times.

words.tr: phrase. 轮流；更替
words.ex: The children take turns to play with the toy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们轮流玩这个玩具。
words.en: If people take turns doing something, they do it one after the other to ensure that each person has an equal opportunity to do it.

words.tr: phrase. 定居；居住；安家
words.ex: He decided to take up his abode in a small village.
words.ex_cn: 他决定在一个小村庄定居。
words.en: To settle in a place to live.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人交往；与某人混在一起（常含贬义）
words.ex: She decided to take up with a new group of friends.
words.ex_cn: 她决定与一群新朋友交往。
words.en: To become friendly or involved with someone, or to discuss something with someone in order to get their opinion or approval.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 19 基本动词 TURN

words.tr: phrase. 对...熟视无睹
words.ex: He saw the mistake but decided to turn a blind eye to it.
words.ex_cn: 他看到了那个错误，但决定视而不见。
words.en: If you say that someone is turning a blind eye to something bad or illegal that is happening, you mean that you think they are pretending not to notice that it is happening so that they will not have to do anything about it.

words.w: turn a deaf ear to sth.
words.tr: phrase. 对某事充耳不闻；故意不理睬
words.uk: tɜːn ə def ɪə tuː sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: tɝːn ə def ɪr tuː ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: He turned a deaf ear to their complaints and continued with his work.
words.ex_cn: 他对他们的抱怨充耳不闻，继续工作。
words.en: If you turn a deaf ear to something, you refuse to listen to it or pay attention to it.

words.tr: phrase. 对…充耳不闻；故意不理睬
words.ex: He turned a deaf ear to his friend's warning.
words.ex_cn: 他无视了朋友的警告。
words.en: If someone turns a deaf ear to something, they ignore it or refuse to listen to it.

words.tr: phrase. 背叛；使对抗
words.ex: He turned against his friend because of a big argument.
words.ex_cn: 他因为一次大争吵而背弃了他的朋友。
words.en: To change from being friendly or supportive to being hostile or opposed to someone or something.

words.tr: phrase. 使停止往前；往回走
words.ex: He turned back when he saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到狗时，他往回走了。
words.en: To go back in the direction you have come from, or to make someone or something do this.

words.tr: phrase. 上床睡觉；上交；告发；交还
words.ex: It's late, so I'll turn in now.
words.ex_cn: 很晚了，我现在上床睡觉。
words.en: To give something to someone in authority, especially a piece of work or something that is lost.

words.tr: phrase. （尤指车辆）在极小空间内迅速掉头；迅速改变方向或决定
words.ex: The car can turn on a dime, making it easy to drive in small spaces.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车能在很小的地方转弯，开起来很方便。
words.en: To change direction or plans very quickly and easily.

words.tr: phrase. 背弃；拒绝帮助；不理睬
words.ex: He turned his back on his friend when he needed help.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友需要帮助时，他却背弃了他。
words.en: To refuse to help or support someone or something; to abandon or reject.

words.tr: phrase. 背弃；拒绝帮助；转身离开（某人或某事）
words.ex: He turned his back on his friend when he needed help.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友需要帮助时，他却背弃了他。
words.en: If you turn your back on someone or something, you ignore them, leave them, or reject them.

words.tr: phrase. 对…嗤之以鼻；轻蔑地拒绝；看不起
words.ex: He turns his nose up at fast food.
words.ex_cn: 他看不起快餐。
words.en: If someone turns their nose up at something, they reject it because they think it is not good enough for them.

words.tr: phrase. 对…嗤之以鼻；蔑视；看不起
words.ex: He turns up his nose at healthy food.
words.ex_cn: 他看不起健康食品。
words.en: To show disdain or contempt for something by refusing to consider it.

words.tr: phrase. 出现；生产；结果是；关闭；朝外
words.ex: The weather turned out to be sunny.
words.ex_cn: 天气结果是晴朗的。
words.en: If something turns out a particular way, it happens in that way or has the result or degree of success indicated. If you turn out something, you produce or create it. If you turn out a light, you switch it off.

words.tr: phrase. v. （结果）成功；进展顺利；最终发展为
words.ex: We'll see how things pan out.
words.ex_cn: v. 我们来看看事情会如何发展。
words.en: To turn out or develop in a particular way; to succeed.

words.tr: phrase. 算出；解决；锻炼；进展（顺利）
words.ex: I can work out the answer with a calculator.
words.ex_cn: 我可以用计算器算出答案。
words.en: If you work out a solution to a problem or mystery, you think about it and find a solution. If you work out the answer to a mathematical problem, you calculate it. If a plan or situation works out, it happens or progresses in a particular way.

words.tr: phrase. 结果是；原来是；证实是
words.ex: The shy boy turned out to be a great singer.
words.ex_cn: 那个害羞的男孩结果是个很棒的歌手。
words.en: If something turns out to be a particular thing, it is discovered to be that thing.

words.tr: phrase. 改过自新；重新开始；洗心革面
words.ex: He decided to turn over a new leaf and stop smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他决定改过自新，戒掉吸烟。
words.en: To make a fresh start; to change one's behavior or attitude for the better.

words.tr: phrase. （某人若在世）会气得在坟墓里打滚（形容某事令人震惊或愤怒至极）
words.ex: If he saw what they did, he would turn over in his grave.
words.ex_cn: 如果他看到他们做的事，他会在坟墓里翻过身来。
words.en: If you say that someone who is dead would turn over in their grave, you mean that they would be very shocked or upset by something, if they knew about it.

words.tr: phrase. 调低；关小；拒绝
words.ex: Please turn down the volume, it's too loud.
words.ex_cn: 请把音量调低，太大声了。
words.en: To refuse or reject an offer or request; to reduce the volume, temperature, or intensity of something.

words.tr:
n. 返回；归还；
v. 返回；归还；
words.ex: The return of the train was delayed.
words.ex_cn: 火车的返回被推迟了。
words.en: To go or come back to a place or person. To give, send, or put something back to its original place or condition.

words.tr: phrase. 关掉
words.ex: Please turn off the light before you leave.
words.ex_cn: 离开前请关灯。
words.en: If you turn off a device or machine, you stop it from operating by pressing a button or moving a switch.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人骄傲自满；使某人得意忘形（常用于否定或警告语境）
words.ex: The praise made him turn his head and feel too proud.
words.ex_cn: 表扬让他变得骄傲起来。
words.en: To make someone feel proud or conceited.

words.tr: phrase. 令人作呕；使某人感到恶心或极度反感
words.ex: The smell of that food turns my stomach.
words.ex_cn: 那种食物的气味让我恶心。
words.en: If something turns your stomach, it makes you feel sick or disgusted.

words.tr: phrase. 开启；接通；发动；突击
words.ex: He turns on the light in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他打开了房间的灯。
words.en: To cause something to start operating, especially by pressing a switch or button.

words.tr: phrase. 翻转；移交；换台；营业额达到；反复考虑
words.ex: He turned over the pancake with a spatula.
words.ex_cn: 他用铲子把煎饼翻了个面。
words.en: To cause something to move so that a different side is facing upwards; to transfer or hand over something to someone else; to achieve a certain amount of business.

words.tr: phrase. 将某事物转化为自己的优势；利用某事物为自己谋利
words.ex: She managed to turn the situation to her advantage.
words.ex_cn: 她设法使局势对自己有利。
words.en: To use a particular situation or condition in a way that benefits oneself.

words.tr: phrase. （面对冒犯或伤害时）不报复，反而宽容忍让；源自《圣经》，比喻以德报怨
words.ex: When someone insults you, it's sometimes best to turn the other cheek.
words.ex_cn: 当有人侮辱你时，有时候最好选择不报复。
words.en: To respond to insult or injury without revenge and with patience and forgiveness.

words.tr: phrase. 反败为胜；扭转局势对付某人
words.ex: He managed to turn the tables on his opponent in the last few minutes of the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛的最后几分钟成功扭转了局势，反败为胜。
words.en: To reverse a situation so that you gain an advantage over someone who previously had an advantage over you.

words.tr: phrase. 扭转局势；反败为胜；使形势对调
words.ex: With a clever strategy, he managed to turn the tables on his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 凭借巧妙的策略，他成功地扭转了局势，反制了对手。
words.en: To reverse a situation so that you gain an advantage over someone who previously had an advantage over you.

words.tr: phrase. 扭转局势；使形势发生有利的转变
words.ex: The new policy helped turn the tide in the company's favor.
words.ex_cn: 新政策帮助公司扭转了局势。
words.en: To cause a complete change in a situation, especially to reverse a previously unfavorable situation.

words.tr: phrase. 回到；返回到
words.ex: He will return to school next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周将返回学校。
words.en: To go back to a previous state, place, or topic.

chapters.name: 第一部分 基本动词TURN补充词组

words.tr: phrase. 转身；（使）好转；（使）扭转局面
words.ex: He heard a noise and told me to turn around.
words.ex_cn: 他听到一声响动，叫我转过身来。
words.en: To change direction so as to face the opposite way; to change something bad into something good.

words.tr: phrase. 转身；改变方向；（使）转向另一边
words.ex: He turned about when he heard his name.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到自己的名字时，他转过身来。
words.en: To change direction or to change one's mind.

words.tr: phrase. （使）变成；成为
words.ex: The caterpillar turns into a butterfly.
words.ex_cn: 毛毛虫变成了一只蝴蝶。
words.en: To change or develop into something different.

words.tr: phrase. v. 背叛某人；突然攻击某人
words.ex: He suddenly turned on me and started shouting.
words.ex_cn: 他突然对我发火，开始大喊大叫。
words.en: To attack or criticize someone suddenly and aggressively.

words.tr: phrase. 故意哭出来；装哭（通常为博取同情或操纵他人）
words.ex: Don't turn on the waterworks just because you didn't get dessert.
words.ex_cn: 别因为没得到甜点就哭起来。
words.en: To start crying, especially in order to gain sympathy.

words.tr: phrase. 翻转；移交；换台；营业额达到；反复考虑
words.ex: He turned over the pancake with a spatula.
words.ex_cn: 他用铲子把煎饼翻了个面。
words.en: To cause something to move so that a different side is facing upwards; to transfer or hand over something to someone else; to achieve a certain amount of business.

words.tr: phrase. 把……变成某物；使……转化为某物
words.ex: She managed to turn her hobby into a successful business.
words.ex_cn: 她成功地把她的爱好变成了一个成功的生意。
words.en: To change something into a different thing or state.

words.tr: phrase. 突然出现；重新露面；调大
words.ex: He didn't turn up to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他没有出席会议。
words.en: To arrive or appear somewhere, often unexpectedly; to increase the volume or intensity of something.

words.tr: phrase. 使某物转向；扭转（局势、生意等）；使好转
words.ex: The new manager turned the company around in less than a year.
words.ex_cn: 新经理在不到一年的时间里使公司好转了。
words.en: To change a situation so that it improves or becomes successful, especially when it seemed unlikely to do so.

words.tr: phrase. （使）某事好转；扭转（局势、情况等）
words.ex: The company managed to turn around its financial situation.
words.ex_cn: 公司设法扭转了财务状况。
words.en: To completely change the direction or purpose of something.

words.tr: phrase. 回到；返回到
words.ex: He will return to school next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周将返回学校。
words.en: To go back to a previous state, place, or topic.

chapters.name: 第一部分 LESSON 20 基本动词 WORK

words.tr: phrase. 逐渐融入某事物；设法将某物加入或结合进另一物中
words.ex: He was determined to work into the company's top management.
words.ex_cn: 他决心要进入公司的高层管理。
words.en: To gradually and carefully add or include something in a larger thing or process.

words.tr: phrase. 像马一样辛勤工作；拼命干活
words.ex: He works like a horse to support his family.
words.ex_cn: 他像牛一样工作来养家。
words.en: To work very hard, similar to how a horse works.

words.tr: 短语. 像魔法一样奏效；非常有效
words.ex: The new medicine works like magic for her headache.
words.ex_cn: 这种新药对她的头痛非常有效。
words.en: To function or operate in a way that is remarkably effective, as if by magic.

words.tr: phrase. 从事于…；继续工作；设法说服；影响
words.ex: He works on his homework every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都做家庭作业。
words.en: To spend time repairing or improving something.

words.w: work one's fingers to the bone
words.tr: phrase. 拼命工作；辛勤劳作到筋疲力尽
words.ex: He works his fingers to the bone to support his family.
words.ex_cn: 他拼命工作来养家。
words.en: To work extremely hard.

words.tr: phrase. 通过努力工作完成（某事）；靠打工支付（学费等）；逐步克服（困难）
words.ex: He works his way through school by doing part-time jobs.
words.ex_cn: 他通过做兼职工作来完成学业。
words.en: To gradually make progress through something by working hard.

words.tr: phrase. 逐步使自己地位上升；获得晋升
words.ex: He started as a cleaner and worked his way up to manager.
words.ex_cn: 他从清洁工做起，一步步升到了经理。
words.en: To gradually progress or advance in a job, position, or status through effort and hard work.

words.tr: phrase. 算出；解决；锻炼；进展（顺利）
words.ex: I can work out the answer with a calculator.
words.ex_cn: 我可以用计算器算出答案。
words.en: If you work out a solution to a problem or mystery, you think about it and find a solution. If you work out the answer to a mathematical problem, you calculate it. If a plan or situation works out, it happens or progresses in a particular way.

words.tr: phrase. 最终结果是最好的；事情最终会朝好的方向发展
words.ex: Everything will work out for the best in the end.
words.ex_cn: 一切最终都会往最好的方向发展。
words.en: to result in a good or satisfactory outcome

words.tr: phrase. v. 安排进入；设法加入；把…穿插进去
words.ex: The manager will work in a new intern next week.
words.ex_cn: 经理下周会安排一名新实习生进入。
words.en: To include or introduce something into a larger whole, especially in a subtle or skillful way.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 逐步发展；激发（情绪）；费力完成；锻炼身体
words.ex: He worked up a plan to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他逐步制定出一个存钱的计划。
words.en: To develop or increase something gradually, or to make someone feel an emotion strongly.

words.tr: phrase. 殴打某人；彻底搜查某人；严厉批评某人
words.ex: The gang threatened to work him over if he didn't pay up.
words.ex_cn: 黑帮威胁说，如果他不还钱，就要揍他一顿。
words.en: To thoroughly examine or repair someone or something; to beat someone up.

words.tr: phrase. （尤指暴力地）殴打某人；彻底检查或处理某人
words.ex: He decided to work over sb. to achieve his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他决定孤注一掷以达到他的目标。
words.en: To treat someone roughly or to examine or repair something thoroughly.

words.tr: phrase. 将某物融入/掺入某物；设法把某事物加入到另一事物中
words.ex: She worked her way into the top management.
words.ex_cn: 她努力进入了高层管理。
words.en: To incorporate or mix something into another thing.

words.tr: phrase. 解决某事；算出；想出办法；锻炼身体（尤指通过运动）
words.ex: He can work something out with simple numbers.
words.ex_cn: 他能用简单的数字算出一些东西。
words.en: To find a solution to a problem or to calculate something.

words.tr: phrase. 通过正式渠道或程序处理事务；经由既定途径解决问题
words.ex: He decided to work through channels to resolve the issue.
words.ex_cn: 他决定通过正规渠道来解决问题。
words.en: To resolve a problem or achieve a goal by following official or established procedures.
